items.quote: So, this is, yes, definitely. So, this is just the first capacity as far as rubber is concerned and that is also in the first phase only. And the total capacity that we are planning for rubber is around 30,000 tons. That would come up in Q1 or Q2 this year.

items.statement: Blended tax rate guided at 17-18% for FY27 vs 15% in FY26 due to higher Indian tax rate on copper business
items.quote: So, tax rate for last year, it was around 15%. But since the business which is coming up like RMI and copper business, which is mostly in India and Indian tax rate is close to 25%. So, blended tax rate for going forward should be in the range of 17%-18%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% with EBITDA margin maintained and slight upward trend in EBITDA and net profit margin
items.quote: So, we expect the top line to be growing between 15 -20% around that time, and I'm again being conservative. But 15%, hopefully, yes. And the EBITDA margin would be maintained with the slightly upward trend in EBITDA as well as in the net profit margin.

items.statement: Cotton volume growth expected around 20% for FY27, paddy 20-25%, maize strong growth continuing
items.quote: We have maintained a conservative line on cotton, but I've always said that the cotton will be growing around 20%. It has proved what I made the statement last year, it has grown to 22%. As far as paddy is concerned, paddy has also grown beyond 20-25%.

items.statement: Minimal CapEx budget for plants and processing; strategy favors rentals over ownership; only land bank and vehicles as CapEx
items.quote: As a matter of policy, as a matter of strategy, Nath has not been investing much in CapEx. If you go through my balance sheet, so you will find that we have only land bank as CapEx, and we also have vehicles as CapEx because which we need for ensuring sales production and things like that.

items.statement: Uzbekistan JV contributed INR 15 crores in FY26, first revenue from international operations; Central Asia market ~USD 1 billion in 5-6 years
items.quote: FY26 marks the first year our Uzbekistan JV contributed almost INR 15 crores to our consolidated top line, a landmark achievement in our international expansion journey and a strong validation of our global growth strategy.

items.statement: Cotton-paddy combined portfolio now 58% of revenue mix, up from 52% in FY25; maize emerging as third pillar at 10.72%
items.quote: The cotton-paddy combined portfolio now accounts for 58% of our revenue mix, up from 52% in FY25, a testament to our steady market position in this critical crop.

items.statement: El Nino impact mitigated by geographic diversification, product portfolio across durations, and advance stock positioning at branches
items.quote: El Nino definitely has an impact on entire agriculture, and it affects us differently in different crops, different geographies. But what growth we are talking about is a balanced growth that we are talking about despite of El Nino.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; cash and bank balance INR 707 million; inventory build-up funded by working capital debt
items.quote: Cash and bank balance stood at INR 707 million. Inventory increased to INR 4,446 million, in line with our planned scaled up for the upcoming season, reflecting our confidence in FY27 demand.

items.statement: Next-gen cotton pipeline includes products better than Sanket and Jumbo; competition now in-house; production stability expected over 2-3 years
items.quote: We have a product 2020, which is either similar or better to Sanket. And we have so many other products which we don't want to disclose now. But, yes, definitely, we have better than Sanket and Jumbo.

items.statement: Plant Nutrition segment declined 18% due to China export restrictions; expected to normalize as supply-side pressures ease
items.quote: Plant Nutrition segment, the segment saw a decline of 18%. This is mainly due to China export restrictions, which disturb supply dynamics. We expect this to normalize in the coming year as supply-side pressure ease.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin of 10-12% sustainable in medium term with new alu-zinc line and export ramp-up
items.quote: we feel that an EBITDA margin of anywhere between 10% to 12% is possible and sustainable.

items.statement: Second color coating line (150k tons) and 7MW solar plant targeted for July 2026 commissioning, funded by debt-equity mix
items.quote: the second color coating line, which is going to commission in Q2 of FY '27 is roughly about INR65 crores. And the solar captive power plant, which is also going to commission in the Q2 of FY '27, the capital outlay is INR30 crores.

items.statement: Current order book stands at INR350-400 crores, largely from export customers, with customers ordering more in advance to build buffer
items.quote: our current order book is in the range of between INR350 crores to INR400 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to 6.84% due to Middle East conflict-driven cost spikes, but full cost pass-through achieved on new orders
items.quote: EBITDA for Q4 FY '26 stood at INR15.64 crores with an EBITDA margin of 6.84%. The year-on-year softness in Q4 margin was entirely attributable to the extraordinary cost escalation in energy and raw materials triggered by the Middle East conflict.

items.statement: Successfully passed through 100% of incremental energy, raw material, consumable and freight costs to customers in new contracts since April 2026
items.quote: all the new orders and the new contracts that the company has been entering into with long-term customers, both domestic and international, we have been able to pass through the entire impact of the incremental costs.

items.statement: Expects robust demand environment in H1 FY27 with strong order visibility from domestic and export markets, assuming no further global conflict escalation
items.quote: We expect the demand environment to remain robust. And with the normalization of energy and raw material costs, assuming no further escalation in global conflicts, our margin recovery in H1 '27 should be meaningful.

items.statement: Pre-painted steel share of total quantities sold rose to 80% in FY26 from 74% in FY25; alu-zinc line commissioned Dec 2025 adds 36% capacity to 180k tons
items.quote: Pre-painted steel, our highest value product now constitutes 80% of total quantities sold in FY '26, up from 74% in FY '25.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts, government policies, GDP growth, infrastructure spending, and project funding timelines identified as key risks to FY29 3x growth vision
items.quote: anything to do with government policies, external geopolitical conditions, GDP of the country, demand of the country, public sector and private sector projects in the country would -- all of these would define.

items.statement: No immediate fundraising plans; next project (cold rolling mill) targeted within FY28 but financial tie-up not yet finalized
items.quote: it is too early to comment whether we will be wanting to raise any fund from the market or not for this project.

items.statement: Solar plant to save INR7-7.5 crores annually in power costs, replacing 50-55% grid dependency; half benefit in FY27, full from FY28
items.quote: it has the potential to basically generate savings of between INR7 crores to INR7.5 crores per annum just in terms of power cost.

items.statement: New color coating line expected to add INR300-500 crores incremental revenue in FY27; alu-zinc line to reach 80-85% utilization in H2 FY27
items.quote: we can anticipate anywhere between -- let's say, anywhere between INR300 crores to INR500 crores, in that range, of incremental revenue from the new capacity being installed.

items.statement: Alu-zinc commands INR3,000-5,000 per ton premium over galvanized steel; sustainable EBITDA per ton superior but exact quantum depends on internal/external factors
items.quote: as a layman, I would say it's fair to assume that a premium of between INR3,000 to INR5,000 a ton is a ballpark that one can say is a fair premium over galvanized steel.

items.statement: Cold rolling mill (360k tons) and second alu-zinc plant (360k tons) targeted within FY28; could enable INR2,500-2,700 crores revenue at 80-85% utilization
items.quote: which has the potential to generate a revenue of anywhere in the range of INR2,500 crores to INR2,700 crores per annum.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio to be maintained at 1-1.5x, will not breach 2x even during capex cycle; net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.01x in FY26
items.quote: we will definitely not breach a level of 2x, and we'll strive to actually be anywhere in the range of between 1x to 1.5x.

items.statement: Targets 15%+ revenue growth and 15%+ ROCE/ROE on multi-year basis; aims for INR500 cr PAT to enter top 100 listed companies ex-BFSI
items.quote: We pretty much want to continue doing what we are doing with a 15% return profile. And with scale, that keeps us significant. I think that's very important to call out.

items.statement: Cash business IPO targeted within FY27, deferred due to geopolitical conditions; SEBI extended DRHP validity to Sept 30
items.quote: Hopefully, within FY27, and I think SEBI has facilitated that by extending the DRHP validity to September 30.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 4.6% in Q4 FY26; India Security ex-APS at 5.5%, FM at 5.5%, International stable at 3.8%; targets pre-COVID 6% level over time
items.quote: We are closing this year at 4.6%, 4.7%. This is with the impact of APS consolidation for the full quarter. The stand-alone segmental numbers without APS, India Security is at 5.5% EBITDA margin. FM is also at 5.5% EBITDA margin

items.quote: I think it is going to be -- I mean, it would be fair to say that the 50 bps margin gap is the synergy opportunity. items.quote: SIS has returned a total of INR250 crores to shareholders this financial year. items.statement: DSO improved to 63 days in Q4, down 4 days QoQ; best since 2023; ROCE 16.5% vs 14.3% YoY; operating PAT INR105.5 cr (2.4% margin)

items.statement: No new international markets planned; focus on India consolidation and solutioning; immigration laws prevent sending Indian security guards abroad
items.quote: As far as new markets is concerned, I think SIS is very focused on India at the moment. Our priority is consolidating market share and accelerating the solutioning aspect. So currently, there is no new international market that we are looking at.

items.statement: Reiterated revenue CAGR of ~75% over FY25-FY28 driven by Bokaro ramp-up and organic growth
items.quote: We reiterate our earlier guidance of a CAGR of approximately 75% over FY '25 to FY '28 period supported by the phased commissioning and ramp -up of Bokaro greenfield project along with continued organic growth across the existing business verticals.

items.statement: EBITDA and PAT CAGR guided at ~45% and ~40% respectively over FY25-FY28
items.quote: In line with the above guidance, operating EBITDA and PAT is expected to grow at a CAGR of nearly 45 % and 40% respectively over the same periods.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin to stabilize at 12-13% and PAT margin at 5-6% by FY28
items.quote: EBITDA and PAT margins are expected to gradually stabilize at around 12 % to 13% and 5% to 6% respectively by FY '28 as the benefits of integration scale and operating leverage begin to materialize.

items.statement: Bokaro greenfield project on track for phased commissioning starting Q1 FY27; cold trials by end of May, hot trials in June
items.quote: FY '26 has been a pivotal year operationally marked by strong progress on our greenfield downstream steel complex at Bokaro, which remains on track for phased commissioning starting quarter one FY '27.

items.quote: So on a total cost of INR803 crores, our debt -equity is at roughly 250 to 300 of equity and balance of debt.

items.quote: That's fair. That's fair. That's a fair assumption.

items.quote: So if you look at saleable products, it'll be the differences because the highest value add is the color coat. items.quote: But a lot of these products are not long gestation sales periods, you typically have an order to delivery gap of maybe about two weeks. So the order book kind of becomes a little moot. items.quote: So if you look at long -term averages, the spreads are fairly stable. There are short -term aberrations from time to time and in the steel industry , it's best not to focus on the short -term aberrations. I think long-term the spreads are positive.

items.statement: Targeting Bokaro working capital cycle of 30-40 days; all production under BMW brand; minimal B2C ad spend, focus on B2B
items.quote: So, we are targeting a working capital cycle of about 30 days in Bokaro. But I think it's fair to say between 30 to 40 days is comfortable.

items.statement: Base case IRR for Bokaro investment above 20%
items.quote: So, our base case for an investment is a 20%, so in this case it's safe to say it's above that.

items.statement: Blended ROCE expected to reach 15%+ post Bokaro commissioning
items.quote: So on a blended basis, we expect to reach 15 plus.

items.statement: Legacy business peak revenue estimated at INR800-900 crores at full utilization
items.quote: I think it's fair to assume between INR800 crores to INR900 crores.

items.quote: Last 4 years, I think our net worth has gone from about INR1,000 crores to INR3,000-plus crores. And basically, all of it from accruals. items.statement: Aim to increase wealth RM headcount in FY27; no specific number given

items.statement: FPD AUM target to increase from INR52,000 crores; no specific number given
items.quote: And coming to asset growth, I think we are close to about INR52,000 crores. And I don't have a number in mind, but we have to increase it.

items.statement: Depreciation increased 20% YoY due to investment in branches and technology
items.quote: Depreciation increased 20% on account of investment in branches and technology.

items.statement: Net interest spread roughly 4%; MTF interest income ~INR160-170 crores in FY26
items.quote: Net interest margin, 18% -- no, 18%, 19%, I think the net interest spread is roughly about 4%.

items.statement: FPD AUM grew from INR31,000 crores to INR52,000 crores; mutual fund assets from INR14,000 crores to ~INR21,000 crores; HNI segment ~INR12,000 crores
items.quote: We have seen a growth in our FPD assets because it was about INR31,000 crores, and it has now become about INR52,000 crores. And we have seen all-round growth, both in mutual fund and other assets also and including our fixed income assets.

items.statement: Short-term impact from RBI regulations effective July 1 on broking business due to increased working capital and margin requirements; cost of F&O trades to increase for clients
items.quote: My view is that there will be a short-term impact for sure because of increased working capital requirements and margin requirements. And then over a period of time, the market finds its own level and goes back to that trend.

items.statement: Income tax search under Section 132; notice for ~INR56 crores for block period April 2018-Feb 2025; appeals filed; no material adverse impact expected
items.quote: We have got a notice which for roughly -- for both IIFL management and IIFL facilities for roughly about INR56 crores combined for the block period from April 1, 2018 up to February 3, 2025.

items.statement: Closed capital credit opportunities fund; raised INR500 crores
items.quote: We launched -- we closed our capital credit opportunities fund. We raised about INR500 crores and this is basically a risk-adjusted higher kind of fund.

items.statement: Board evaluating opportunities for acquisitions, new projects to enhance shareholder value; no definitive event requiring disclosure
items.quote: As a company, the Board continuously evaluates opportunities to enhance shareholder value, whether it's in terms of potential acquisition, new projects and other such and combination.

items.statement: SEBI regulations on domestic mutual fund yields: impact marginal as effective yield already aligned with regulator suggestion
items.quote: Our opinion or our learning is that the impact will be marginal because already effective yield was plus/minus the yield as suggested by the regulator.

items.statement: Operational PBT down 22% YoY in FY26 primarily due to steep increase in employee costs to INR687 crores
items.quote: Operational PBT was down 22%, and that is basically -- primarily driven by increase in the employee expenses.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to stay 60%-65% through FY2027; operating leverage expected from FY2028
items.quote: On the CTI, I would always say that we will be between 60% to 65% till end of FY2027. FY2028 onwards, the operative leverage will kick in.

items.statement: SME/BLG growth to resume once West Asia crisis clarity emerges; targeting 28-30% growth in next two years
items.quote: Whatever happened, single-digit growth is given and hopefully we will be back to that 28%-30% growth range in the next two years.

items.statement: Plan to open 150 showrooms across Kalyan, Candere and new regional brand in FY27
items.quote: During the ongoing financial year, we plan to open 150 showrooms across Kalyan, Candere and the new regional brand.

items.statement: Recommend 10% SSSG for 3-5 year projections despite recent 20-30% actuals
items.quote: If you are trying to put a 3 to 5-year projection, I always recommend only putting a 10% SSSG, even though I don't have a reason for it.

items.statement: Candere to open 50-55 stores in FY27 similar to FY26
items.quote: So, it will be in the similar line of the last financial year, 50-55.

items.statement: India standalone PBT margin expected to stay in 5.5-5.6% range with possible slight improvement
items.quote: I think that is here to stay. And some -- again, I told you, some operating leverage can come in and stuff.

items.statement: Candere gross margins in mid-30s due to >70% studded ratio
items.quote: The gross margin store level Candere is in mid-30s because the studded ratio are more than 70%.

items.statement: April started very well with strong Akshaya Tritiya sales and encouraging wedding demand momentum
items.quote: As we speak, April has started off very well. And even with high basis, we have been able to grow.

items.statement: Gold price up 60-70% YoY; customers buy on budget not volume, shifting to lighter/studded jewellery
items.quote: Gold price have went up by about 60% -70% over the last 1 year. Customer does not have the money to spend 70% more than what he budgeted.

items.statement: Target non-GML debt-free in India by FY27 end, possibly by H1 FY27; INR300 cr remaining
items.quote: Yes. So, we want to make it a non-GML debt-free in the running financial year. And yes, if things go really well, we might do it by H1 itself.

items.statement: Interest cost to reduce by ~INR30 cr from non-GML repayment plus INR20 cr one-off tax interest
items.quote: Correct. You are correct.

items.statement: Asset disposal timeline: first set of INR180 cr collateral release before September 2026
items.quote: The time line set for the set no 1 asset disposal was before September of this year, which I think is going in the right direction.

items.statement: South expansion focused on metros (Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad); 13 stores opened in FY26

items.statement: Expect to outperform underlying industry growth by 1.5x to 2x in FY27 based on order book over 85% of forecasted revenue
items.quote: Based on our current strong performance, execution visibility and the current order book being over 85% of the FY27 forecasted revenue, we expect to outperform underlying industry growth by 1.5x to 2x in FY27.

items.statement: Target export revenue share of 14% to 15% of consolidated revenue by FY28
items.quote: We are working towards increasing share of exports in our consolidated revenue to 14% to 15% by FY 28, driven by deeper penetration in existing markets, entry into new geographies and the addition of new customers.

items.statement: Total capex of INR 260-270 crores over 3 years from FY26, with INR 80 crores spent in FY26 and balance in FY27-FY28
items.quote: So put together, there is an investment close to INR220 crores. Apart from that, we have the normal capex, which is around INR15 - 20 crores per annum. So on a 3-year basis, we could say INR260 crores, INR270 crores.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable EBITDA margin target of 27-28% with high growth trajectory
items.quote: But in the long term, I think that 27% - 28% sort of margins with a high growth trajectory is what you should expect from SJS.

items.statement: Skid assemblies capacity expanding from 6,000 to 15,000 units/annum by next two quarters; peak utilization 75-80%
items.quote: Currently, we have scaled our skid assemblies capacity from 2,000 units per annum to 6,000 units per annum, and we are on track to further expand the same by the next two quarter to 15,000 skids per annum.

items.statement: New annealing furnace facility targeted for commissioning by end of CY2026
items.quote: we are also investing in advanced manufacturing capabilities, including a new annealing furnace facility targeted for commissioning by the end of this year.

items.quote: we work on a long-term contract with our, with the suppliers with whom we have an exclusive contract. And they have given a pipeline for the entire year and then they break it down into quarterly POs.

items.quote: I would say to consider an average, I think INR3 lakhs to INR3.25 lakhs would be an average that we can consider in terms of the average selling price for skid assembly.

items.quote: I think at the peak utilization of the metal bellows, I think we would reach about INR80 crores at the top utilization, the maximum utilization.

items.statement: Hyd-Air FY26 revenue INR31.64cr; current utilization ~60%; plan to use capacity for internal high-end fittings/connectors for data centers and HVAC
items.quote: Hyd-Air's revenue in FY26 was INR31.64 crores.

items.statement: Income tax demand ~INR40cr (AY18-19) on loan waiver; company confident of reversal on appeal; assessment reopened due to time-bar issues
items.quote: We have already -- we had done the necessary disclosures in both our financials and our income tax return. So we are confident that this is something, which will be -- which would come in our favor in the appeal that we are going to file.

items.statement: US Section 232 tariff on products reduced to 10-15% range from mid-Feb 2026; no current tariff issues
items.quote: I think it's around 15%, but I will have to just double check. I think in the range of between 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Domestic sales grew ~40% YoY in Q4; domestic share rose to 31% from 26%; expected to increase further as skid assemblies are 100% domestic
items.quote: Domestic share has increased significantly. The reason being that the domestic sales has almost increased by about 40%.

items.statement: 16+ products under development focused on high-growth segments; 2 robotic welding lines commissioned for assemblies; metal bellows utilization <20% in FY26
items.quote: We are also strengthening our innovation pipeline with more than 16 products under development, which are primarily focused on high-growth segment.

items.statement: Guided 20% AUM growth, 20% profit growth, and 17-18% disbursement growth for short to medium term
items.quote: As we go ahead, we would continue with similar guidance of 20% AUM, 20% profit and 17% to 18% disbursement growth.

items.statement: Exit spread at 5.82%, guiding 8-10 bps YoY spread contraction; LAP mix increase can offset contraction
items.quote: We have always guided that our spreads year-on-year will probably see some contraction to the extent of about 8 bps to 10 bps.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost 7.6% in Q4 FY26, exit cost of funds 7.71%; expect status quo for 2-3 quarters
items.quote: If we are able to maintain 7.7% cost throughout the entire next year, I'll be very, very happy to be very honest.

items.statement: Demand remains stable, end-user driven by first-time homebuyers; PMAY and state-level projects supporting growth
items.quote: We believe demand in our segment will continue to remain stable and end user driven, supported by first-time homebuyers and increased penetration in underserved markets.

items.statement: LAP mix deliberately slowed to 24-25% of disbursements vs typical 28-29%; room to increase to 27-28% when conditions improve
items.quote: We did incrementally about 26% loan against property in Q4 FY26, and we want to maybe take it to about 27%,28% in the current quarter, and we'll wait out.

items.statement: No stress from West Asia conflict; bounce rates stable for 6 quarters, minimal NRI exposure, customers in essential commodities
items.quote: Fortunately, the last -- the current month, 3 cycles of bounce rates have not seen any trend whatsoever. Our bounce rates have been stable for the last 6 quarters.

items.statement: DA volume INR 1,725 crore in FY26; targeting 10-15% growth in DA volume for FY27
items.quote: Probably next year, we would be trying to grow that in the range of anywhere between 10% to 15% in terms of overall DA.

items.statement: ROA 4.4% and ROE 15.9% for FY26 (ex-Labour Law Code impact); Q4 ROA 4.8%, ROE 17.1%
items.quote: FY '26 ROA and ROE, again, without the impact of the new Labour Law code is 4.4% and ROE is 15.9%.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 1.08% (30 bps sequential improvement); collection efficiency >99.8%; Stage 2 assets improved 30 bps
items.quote: Asset quality remains pristine with gross NPA standing at 1.08%, a sequential improvement of 30 bps versus quarter 3 FY26. Collection efficiency continues to remain strong, above 99.8%.

items.statement: PLR reduced 15 bps in Feb 2026 per formula; 74% assets and 76% liabilities floating, enabling pass-through if rates rise
items.quote: The February rate pass on that we did of 15 bps was the impact that we had received over the financial year that we passed on as per our RPLR formula that we had.

items.statement: Employee count: 5,430 on-roll, 3,965 off-roll as of March 2026; ESOP cost INR 13.5 crore one-time in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Number of employees as at 31st March '26, on-roll was 5,400 and off-roll was 3,900 as compared to 4,600 on-roll last year and off-roll was 4,300 in March '25.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth projected at low to mid-teens with EBITDA margin expansion of 75-100 bps
items.value: low to mid-teen revenue growth; 75-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: In FY27, we project low to mid-teen revenue growth and as I have been explaining in the last meet and a few calls that I have had the privilege of addressing to you guys that EBITDA margin expansion will happen as committed between 75 to 100 basis points going forward, assuming stable regulations and macroeconomic cond

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR400-425 crores
items.quote: Yes. So I think we guide around that INR400 crores rough number. I think we'll broadly be in that range of INR400 - 425-ish crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin improved 80 bps to 19.4% despite higher R&D spend
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved 80 bps to 19.4% reflecting improved utilization and productivity gains. The EBITDA margin improvement is despite the increase in R&D investments during the year.

items.statement: Raw material price increases from Middle East conflict partially baked into guidance; 1-2 quarters inventory buffer
items.quote: I think given the nature of the business and especially some of the markets we are in, for most of the markets, we do have between one to two quarters of inventory. So at least for the next one or two quarters, we don't see much of an impact coming through.

items.statement: Domestic base business (ex-Zuventus) grew high single-digit to low double-digit organically in FY26
items.quote: Ex of the Zuventus impact for the full year would have been close to the 9% - 10% base business growth that we have been talking about, that we delivered even in the first 9 months.

items.statement: In-licensing contributes ~15% of domestic sales; focus shifting to organic growth and R&D launches
items.quote: In-licensing makes up for the domestic about 15% of our sales.

items.statement: ARV order book remains robust in Rest of World markets
items.quote: In the rest of the world markets, we expect sustained growth led by non-ARV pipeline and robust ARV order book.

items.statement: Middle East conflict driving solvent shortages, higher freight and insurance costs; industry-wide issue
items.quote: The solvents, where the prices have shot up, the solvents that we require for active pharmaceutical ingredients are not available and that is an industry-wide problem that we are facing. Even for that matter one must admit that the insurance cost and the freight cost have also gone up because of the longer route that i

items.statement: Europe business expected to grow at mid-teens CAGR over next 2 years driven by Amphotericin B scale-up
items.quote: In the near term, the growth, we do expect it to be stronger in Europe, especially as Amphotericin B gets launched. But yes, once it reaches the scale, so I think over the next 2 years, we do still expect mid-teens growth in the Europe business as a CAGR.

items.statement: Domestic industry growth expected at 8-9% in FY27; Emcure targets low double-digit growth
items.quote: I think we continue to expect industry growth to be around 8% to 9%, and for us, the target, is to grow faster than the industry – probably at low double-digits.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to remain around 60% for full year FY27
items.quote: I think for the full year, we do expect the GCs to remain around that 60% point.

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR1,054 crores due to Manx and Zuventus minority stake acquisitions
items.quote: Net debt as of March 31, 2026, stood at INR1,054 crores. The increase in debt over the last year has primarily been because of pay-outs for Manx and the Zuventus minority stake acquisition.

items.statement: Poviztra (semaglutide) showing promising uptake after April price cut; 1,000 reps promoting; rDNA biologic differentiator
items.quote: Poviztra, there's obviously a lot going for that brand. A, it's an innovative brand; B, it's an rDNA biologic versus the synthetic generics that have entered the market. Now with this price reduction, I think we have a real sweet spot in terms of the pricing vis-a-vis the generics.

items.statement: Zuventus restructuring caused Q4 domestic softness; April back on track per internal targets
items.quote: But it's starting to pay us dividends in the sense that for April, as the CEO mentioned, we are right on target in terms of our own internal expectations for Zuventus. So we're very happy with the progress that we're seeing, particularly over the last 45 to 60 days.

items.statement: Targets double-digit revenue growth over coming years supported by store expansion across established and emerging brands
items.quote: The achievements through this year and the momentum we gained provides a strong foundation to sustain double-digit growth over the coming years, supported by a robust expansion runway across both established and emerging brands.

items.statement: Projects steady-state retail like-to-like growth of ~7% for Lifestyle Brands
items.quote: My sense is a 7% like-to-like over a steady state period is what we should project in this business.

items.statement: Expects Van Heusen Innerwear to achieve at least one profitable quarter in FY27, steady-state profitability in ~6 quarters
items.quote: I do hope to be able to deliver on that. Of course, it will be the best quarter of the year, which will be a positive quarter, and then we will have to work towards making sure that every quarter works like that. So, I think it's about maybe six quarters away for us to be able to then say that it's steady state every q

items.statement: Emerging Business EBITDA margin to improve continuously from ~4% in FY26
items.quote: While you might be seeing a composite of different segments within this, individually, all of them will contribute to a continuous improvement. So, if you look at it from almost breakeven last year on Emerging Business EBITDA, we were able to get to a nearly 4% Emerging Business EBITDA. This number should keep improvin

items.statement: FY27 CAPEX guided at INR 250-300 crores, ~INR 200 crores for retail expansion including renovations
items.quote: About INR 300 crores. So, we will continue with that kind of momentum. There is still a lot of growth opportunities in the market, so we will continue to drive that.

items.statement: Added 300+ net new stores in FY26, ending with 3,348 stores across 4.9M sq ft in ~800 cities
items.quote: Through the year, store expansion gathered strong momentum, culminating in new stores addition of 300+, accelerated expansion supported by strong product market fit in new market and deeper penetration in existing one, reinforces confidence in the long-term opportunity, with momentum expected to sustain on the back of

items.statement: Reebok to add 40-50 stores per year for next few years; overall net store additions expected to be stronger in FY27 with fewer closures
items.quote: Network expansion will continue. 40-50 stores per year for the next few years should be par for course, unless we do more than that. That, I think, will continue.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of ~25% and PAT margin expansion of ~50 bps
items.value: 25% revenue growth; 50 bps PAT margin expansion
items.quote: For next year guidance, we can give at around 25% revenue growth and PAT margin expansion of around 50 basis points.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 10.6%, up 166 bps YoY; PAT margin 7%, up 209 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA grew to INR200.5 crore, with EBITDA margin improving by 166 basis points to 10.6% versus 8.9% in FY25. Profit after tax nearly doubled to INR132 crore, a growth of 91% year-on-year, with PAT margin expanding by 209 basis points to 7% up from 4.9% in FY25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance ~11.5% for FY27 to support 50 bps PAT margin expansion
items.quote: 10.6% to 11.5% or thereabouts in order for us to deliver at least a 50 basis point PAT expansion.

items.statement: Entry-level new laptop prices in India rose ~57% in 6 months (INR25,500 to ~INR40,000); internationally ~40% (USD315 to ~USD440)
items.value: India: INR25,500 to ~INR40,000; Intl: USD315 to ~USD440
items.quote: A typical entry-level laptop with 8GB RAM and 512GB SSD, which was selling in channel in India for around INR25,500 as on 1st December 2025, rose to approximately INR32,500 by January 1st and is selling today at close to INR40,000, which is an increase of nearly 57% in just six months. The story is similar in the inter

items.statement: IDC cut 2026 PC shipment forecast to -11% (from -8.9%), implying ~32M unit decline; vs expected +10% growth, a 55-60M unit demand gap shifting to refurbished
items.quote: IDC has further cut its 2026 PC shipment forecast to a decline of around 11%, a further decline from 8.9% that was projected earlier. In absolute numbers, this implies a reduction of roughly 32 million units in 2026 alone. But the real picture is even more striking. Under normal circumstances, 2026 was expected to be a

items.statement: Refurbishment capacity ~150K units/month; expanded facilities: Mumbai 1->2, UAE 3->8; headcount 2,148 (1,800 production)
items.quote: From the capacity standpoint, from the people that we have and from the space that we have, we have taken strategic space positions in the UAE as well as in India. In Mumbai, we had one facility which we expanded to two and in UAE, we had earlier three, now we have eight. So, from the capacity and the employee perspect

items.statement: Strategic inventory INR743 cr (Mar'26) vs INR490 cr (Mar'25); bought at lower prices, insulated from price correction; no capex/equity raise needed till 2028-29
items.quote: No, not quite, because if we have kept strategic position of inventory, they are bought at comfortable prices. We have not bought them at higher prices, let me assure you that. And yes, we are in a situation where we have bought inventory at lower prices.

items.statement: No operational impact from Middle East tensions; shipments by air uninterrupted; facilities running normally
items.quote: No, no, but let me assure you that the situation here is quite normal. The government of UAE has handled the situation pretty well, very high rate of interceptions, and our facilities have been up and running every single day. Our shipments happen by air, so those are also uninterrupted.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: 81% laptops, 19% others; Geography: India 33%, US 21%, Europe 20%, UAE 12%, RoW 14%
items.quote: For the full year, India revenue is about 33 odd percent, UAE is at about 12%, US is 21%, Europe about 20%, and the rest of the world is about 14%. So in a sense, US and Europe put together is at about 41%, India at 33%.

items.statement: New distributor partnerships (Ingram, Supertron) at minuscule revenue currently; advanced talks in Europe and US; channel credit 30-45 days to match OEM terms
items.quote: Distributors are very, very excited about this business. Their team, their channel partners are accepting this proposition in a very excited and positive way. And in terms of inventory what they are keeping is between 30 to 45 days of inventory that they usually keep. It's very much required for doing distribution the

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth outlook depends on summer season; too early to comment on full-year guidance
items.quote: As regards what growth we can expect for the next year FY'27, I think it is too early to comment. You already heard Mr. Thiagarajan that summer is just set in, and we would like to wait and watch because it entirely depends on how the summer actually plays out to predict for the year.

items.statement: ~13% price increase needed in RAC (5% BEE norms + 8% raw material/FX); ~8% realized so far, balance 5% in May-June billings
items.quote: It should have been around 13% price increase that is warranted. We would have taken until now the, you know very well, again, I'm repeating, the inventory was enough. The primary sale is beginning to pick up. For whatever primary had happened, we would have realized up to 8% out of 13% price increase, 5 more percentag

items.statement: RAC summer season started April 13; secondary sales strong; primary billing picking up; 25-30% Q1 volume growth possible if summer sustains
items.quote: I have always stated that the given there is price increase of I'm saying average you take at least 10% over last year, a good performance would mean anywhere between 25% to 30% over last year.

items.statement: Carried forward order book grew 10.5% YoY to Rs 6,923 Cr as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: Carried forward order book of March 31, 2026, grew by 10.5% to RS.6,923 Crore as compared to RS.6,263 Crore as of March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Data center MEP order book ~Rs 1,500 Cr at any point; market size Rs 3,000-4,000 Cr
items.quote: I told you that we estimate the market to be anywhere between 3,000 to 4,000 and our order book will be somewhere around RS.1,500 Crore.

items.statement: Margin pressure from commodity inflation (copper, plastics, electronics), FX volatility, Middle East supply chain risk, war-related cost increases
items.quote: With rising input costs and volatile exchange rates, there will be challenges in managing the margins. Further, the ongoing Middle East crisis can lead to a supply chain disruption and also dampen growth.

items.statement: Commercial AC outlook 8-10% growth in FY27 driven by manufacturing sector; projects driven by manufacturing and data centers
items.quote: In commercial air conditioning again last year which was impacted by the multiple factors, including GST in some way. The outlook continues to be around 8% to 10% kind of growth, and the growth is today driven predominantly by manufacturing sector.

items.statement: No plans to enter white goods (refrigerators, washing machines); focus on AC, refrigeration and geographical expansion
items.quote: We have as on date, the foreseeable future, we don't have any such plans at all. We will be focused on air conditioning and refrigeration. There will be geographical expansion, which we have begun. India itself is a very high-growth market. We have no plans whatsoever to get into white goods.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue growth guidance to high single-digit to low double-digit, driven by 50% volume and 50% pricing
items.quote: So earlier, we had given a guidance of a high single and now we want to revise it. We are seeing high single to a low double-digit growth because you've got some pricing coming in because of inflation.

items.statement: Targeting margin expansion in FY27 despite 10% inflation, via price hikes, premiumization, cost savings, and mix
items.quote: But as far as we are concerned, we want to increase the margins from last year to current year. So we would want to mitigate all the inflation through price increases and improve the margins going forward from here.

items.statement: Using shrinkflation on INR10/20 packs (LUPs ~30% of business) to pass on packaging cost inflation
items.quote: Other initiatives that we are taking is shrink inflation. So, all the INR10, INR20 pack, we are reducing grammage.

items.statement: Food & Beverages targeting double-digit FY27 growth; Coconut Water 100% YoY, targeting INR150-200 cr exit ARR; Culinary +30%
items.quote: I told you food and beverages, we pencilled a target for us for a double-digit growth because of the low base and on an assumption that season will play out in our favour.

items.statement: Oral Care +7% in Q4 (vs 2.5% category); Herbal toothpaste +30-40%, Meswak +11%, Red +6-7%, Babool +1-2%; expect double-digit in Q1
items.quote: I think we should come back in quarter 1 with very strong double-digit growth here led by Dabur Red, Meswak, Dabur Herbal.

items.statement: Added AFET line for coconut water; have surplus capacity and are augmenting further to support 100% growth
items.quote: We've already put an AFET line now, and we've got surplus capacity. So, we are bursting from scenes in terms of capacity, and we are augmenting capacity as we go on.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margin of 13-14% for FY27, consistent with historical range
items.quote: So like historically, we have been talking about 13% to 14%. I think that is what the endeavor is. This year also, I think we were in that range only. So definitely, we would be there, though our endeavor is always to go on higher end.

items.statement: Industrial channel price increases effective mid-April; auto OEM negotiations ongoing with retrospective effective dates
items.quote: In case of industrial, there is a good mix of OE as well as channel. Now when it comes to channel, like decorative, there also we announced the price increase and that new prices are effective mid-April itself.

items.statement: Decorative demand showed consistent uptick since November across verticals; auto demand strong with long waiting lists
items.quote: Since November, there has been constant uptick in the market, and I think that is a positive sign. And this trend is only improving.

items.statement: Industrial utilization at 70-75% with sufficient capacity; performance coatings targeting double-digit growth
items.quote: In case of industrial, I think in powder and industrial liquid coating, we have sufficient capacity. We should be operating about 70% to 75% as of now.

items.statement: Key risks: West Asia crisis causing supply chain disruption, crude oil surge, rupee depreciation increasing import costs
items.quote: Among risks, West Asia crisis leading to supply chain disruptions is one of the key risks that we see in this quarter, high commodity prices due to crude oil price surge and impact on downstream products, import cost surge due to rupee depreciation.

items.statement: Capex normal and in line with previous years
items.quote: When it comes to capex, the capex is more or less normal and in line with previous years.

items.statement: Targeting 25% year-on-year revenue growth for Aerospace & Defense segment, with existing plant supporting FY28 growth and Andhra greenfield ramping in FY29
items.quote: we are targeting a 25% growth year-on-year. And the first-year growth can be taken care by the existing plant. The second year will have to be taken care by Andhra.

items.statement: ~INR100 crore per year per business (Aerospace and Auto) for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: in each of the businesses, we will approximately be spending about INR100 crores each to build capacities, which will be consistent, yes.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14.5% in FY26 vs 15.9% in FY25; pressure from reduced non-operating income post demerger
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 14.5% in FY '26 versus 15.9% in FY '25. While operational performance remains strong, EBITDA margins faced pressure due to a reduction in non-operating income.

items.statement: Precision Technology & Auto EBITDA margin 13.4% in FY26 vs 11% in FY25; includes INR13 crore one-time land sale gain in Q2
items.quote: The EBITDA margin stood at 13.4% in FY '26 versus 11% in FY '25. The EBITDA margin improvement was also on account of higher sales volumes, favorable product mix but also included a onetime gain of INR13 crores from the sale of land in Q2 of FY '26.

items.statement: Raw material cost increases (titanium, aluminum alloys) being passed through with a lag; formal cost reduction program underway
items.quote: certain raw materials have gone up, but normally, these are passed through. So, there will be a lag. But in effect, the margins should remain where they are.

items.statement: Geopolitical supply chain disruptions (Gulf logistics blockades) accelerating domestic raw material localization for aerospace-grade alloys
items.quote: Q4 was specifically impacted by a contraction in aerospace-grade titanium and aluminum alloys following logistic blockades in the Gulf. These persistent inflationary pressures have accelerated a strategic pivot towards domestic input localization

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 50-75 bps over FY26 is a given and will be delivered
items.quote: No/ So 50 to 75, 80 bps is a given. I mean it's not an option. We will deliver it, number one.

items.statement: Top line will grow at double digits and EBITDA will grow ahead of top line in FY27
items.quote: But right now, we remain confident of delivering top line numbers and EBITDA ahead of top line, right? And top line, we will grow at double digits.

items.statement: India tea margins are now at target levels and will be maintained in FY27
items.quote: Roughly right now we are where we should be, and we'll aim to be in this ballpark.

items.statement: U.S. coffee margins will improve as coffee prices decline and inventory works through
items.quote: Right now, as we speak, it is $2.99 is what Arabica is trading at, which means in the next probably 2 months or so, you will start to see coffee margins climb up in the U.S.

items.statement: Tea costs are benign, trending ~5% above same period last year; pricing cuts taken to stay competitive
items.quote: Tea prices largely benign, right now trending about 5% ahead of where they were in the same period last year. But barring any unforeseen climate change, we should have largely benign tea cost.

items.statement: Coffee prices declining (Arabica at $2.99); margin expansion expected in U.S. as inventory clears
items.quote: Coffee prices coming down. Right now, as we speak, it is $2.99 is what Arabica is trading at, which means in the next probably 2 months or so, you will start to see coffee margins climb up in the U.S.

items.statement: Growth businesses to sustain ~30% growth in near term; Sampann grew 69% in Q4, 46% full year
items.quote: So therefore, the growth portfolio will continue to chug along at this 30% number, at least in the near term.

items.statement: Innovation-to-sales at 4.5% with 80 new launches; focus on Health & Wellness, Convenience, Premiumization
items.quote: Innovation-to-sales ratio came in at 4.5% with 80 new product launches during the year.

items.statement: Middle East shipping disruption hit March exports; LPG supply secured via dual burners/alternate suppliers
items.quote: The third piece is where if there is a fuel price increase and there is broad-based inflation, that is what should worry us.

items.statement: NourishCo exited at ARR INR170 crores (Food Services), INR100 crores (Vending, 8,000+ machines), INR30 crores (Pharmacy, 42,000 outlets)
items.quote: Food Services exited at ARR of INR170 crores, present in roughly 60 cities. Vending exited at an ARR of INR1,000 -- sorry, INR100 crores, and we have now about 8,000-plus machines.

items.statement: Starbucks India: 3rd consecutive quarter of positive same-store sales (+5%), 23 net stores opened, 502 total stores in 80 cities
items.quote: Starbucks, a good part is now -- this is the third successive quarter of positive same-store sales growth. Same-store sales growth of 5% and total Starbucks growth of 7%.

items.statement: Expects Q1 FY27 to be far better than last year due to improved yarn spreads and fabric price hikes
items.quote: going by the spread improvements which is looking like as of now, I think most of the most of the textile companies should do far better in the first quarter, including our company -- Vardhman

items.statement: Yarn spreads improved 40-50% from $0.60-0.65 to $0.90-0.95 per lb on better demand and aligned cotton costs
items.quote: with the price of 3.30 today, with this kind of a rupee, I mean $0.90, $0.95 spread is available, which four months back was only about $0.60, $0.65 US cents

items.statement: 90% of spinning modernization complete; performance fabric plant commissioned last year; 4th cotton fabric line commissioned but underutilized due to US tariffs
items.quote: almost 90% of the modernization got completed in this period and whatever is left, I think this current financial year next 6, 8 months we'll complete

items.statement: Yarn demand strong; China buying 30m kg/month vs 7-8m kg historically; Indian spinners sold 2-3 months forward on exports
items.quote: China is consistently buying about 30 million kg. So practically another 20 million kg demand came to India and Indian export started reaching or touching almost about 120 million kg plus

items.statement: US retail sales up 4-10% for brands; home textile and garment exporters running at 90-100% capacity utilization
items.quote: the first quarter numbers there's increase of the retail size increased from 4% to 10% of the various brands. The demand from USA is really good

items.statement: Spinners sold out for 2-3 months forward on export orders
items.quote: most of the spinners, they are sold for about two to three months in forward as of now as far as the export is concerned

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA hit by INR 57-58 crore mark-to-market forex loss due to sharp rupee move to 94.80 on March 31
items.quote: we provided a loss of about INR57 crores, INR58 crores in this quarter on that

items.statement: Garment capacity expansion underway to improve viability; no decision yet on large-scale garmenting push
items.quote: the first step is let's make it a little viable unit and in case we can make money on the expanded capacity also, then we'll look at it differently

items.statement: Optimistic on FY27; expects better year for textile companies driven by FTAs, improved raw material competitiveness, and demand
items.quote: I hope the next year should be better year for most of the textile companies including Vardhman and in the meantime, most of the industry very, very opti, has a optimism based upon all the FTAs

items.statement: Targets INR500 crore annual revenue in FY27, maintaining 5-7 year CAGR trajectory
items.quote: Our goal was to hit INR500 crores by last year, but because of divestment of diagnostics, we said we will try and get to those run rates by Q4.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to sustain in stable competitive range around 35-36% medium term despite 1-2% potential correction from input costs
items.quote: Vimta continues to maintain very healthy EBITDA margins, clocking about 35.8% in FY '26, which we believe are among the best in the industry even by global standards.

items.statement: Biologics margins expected around current EBITDA range initially, may improve with overseas traction
items.quote: Honestly, we think the margins should be around this region. Our expectation is that it will be it might be a percent or few percent here and there.

items.statement: New facility built for 4-5 year growth runway, utilization to ramp gradually over next 2-3 years
items.quote: The idea is to when we took up this project of expansion, the idea was to have a facility that can take care of our growth at least for the next four, five years.

items.statement: Biologics CDMO launched in FY27; infrastructure, people, systems ready; targeting first client wins this year
items.quote: FY '26 also marked a strategic milestone with our entry into biologics contract research and development services. The first year, which is this year, FY '27, will be about execution, learning, and building credibility.

items.statement: Pharma, food, electronics testing show good visibility; pharma shifting to large molecules; electronics boosted by defence indigenization
items.quote: What we see for our food, pharma, and electronics testing is that it's good visibility. These are going to be industries that will flourish in the future as well.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts increasing input costs and supply lead times; tariff uncertainties remain
items.quote: Impact of war is there on us. The cost of some input materials, consumables has gone up slightly. There is a slightly longer lead time for us in the supply chain.

items.statement: Biologics has good inquiries from Europe, India, US; finalizing products and modalities; expect closures soon
items.quote: We have good inquiries and we will be closing them soon. We have good traction from Europe, from India, a couple of them from US as well.

items.statement: Routine services face price competition; specialty services command premium; food testing becoming levelled ground
items.quote: For some services which are very routine, low technology, low science, those kind of services price competition will always be there. But then there are some specialty services where the scientific input is very critical.

items.statement: No near-term fund raise planned; INR650M cash sufficient for current needs
items.quote: As of now, we don't need anything from that kind of a method. If there is, then we will definitely share that news.

items.statement: US subsidiary approved for customer proximity, not tariff advantage; minimal tariff impact on services
items.quote: The purpose of undertaking this is to be closer to our customers because we have a sizable population there and also to give them greater confidence.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% CAGR over next 3-4 years as stretch but doable goal
items.quote: It's a stretch number, but definitely doable. And that's what we target each year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue driven by pre-clinical and seasonal food testing strength; some areas below expectations
items.quote: The prime drivers for Q4's good revenues are our pre-clinical and also food has done well, food testing, because Q4 tends to be a good quarter for food testing.

items.statement: War impacted food testing in last fortnight of March due to export/import disruptions at NFL Navi Mumbai
items.quote: There was an impact especially the last fortnight of March because we serve exporters and we also support import testing at the NFL in Navi Mumbai.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: high single-digit India volume growth, mid-teens constant currency international growth, double-digit consolidated revenue growth to cross INR 15,000 cr, high-teens EBITDA growth
items.value: INR 15,000 cr revenue; high-teens EBITDA growth
items.quote: We expect to sustain high single -digit volume growth in the India business in FY '27. items.quote: We expect our global NIM to remain in the range of 2.6% to 2.7% for financial year '26-'27.

items.statement: Guided slippage ratio below 1% for FY26; actual was 0.60%

items.statement: Guided credit cost below 0.4% for FY27

items.statement: Added 144 branches in FY26; plan to open 250 branches in FY27, primarily in Southern and Western regions
items.quote: We added 144 branches in FY '26 and plan to open 250 more in current financial year. These branches will be primarily in the Southern and Western regions.

items.statement: Corporate credit pipeline of INR1.18 lakh crore pending disbursement from INR4 lakh crore sanctioned in FY26
items.quote: The bank sanctioned over INR4 lakh crores in corporate credit lines during financial year '25-'26 with INR1.18 lakh crores still pending for disbursement.

items.statement: Domestic NIM 2.61% and global NIM 2.47% in Q4 FY26; expect Q-o-Q NIM improvement from Q4 levels
items.quote: We expect the margins to improve moving forward and our NIM to witness Q-o-Q increase from the level of Q4 '25-'26.

items.statement: Target RAM share 58% in FY27 (from 54%) and 60% long-term; corporate share to drop to 42% short-term, 40% long-term
items.quote: we want to bring that share down to, in the long term it is 40%, short term it is 42%, and in the RAM we want to bring it to 60% in the long run and around 58% in this financial year.

items.statement: ECL implementation from April 2027; floating provision INR2,045 cr and capital buffers deemed sufficient; no material impact expected on ROA >1%
items.quote: we have already kept more than INR2,000 crores, which already you have also mentioned, INR2,045 crores in precise. It is kept for the floating provision that can take care of my ECL requirements

items.statement: No wage revision provision in FY27; revision due Nov 2027
items.quote: The wage revision due itself is the 1st November 2027. So financial year '26-27, it doesn't impact at all.

items.statement: AS-15 actuarial gain of INR2,121 cr in Q4 due to bond yield hardening; employee cost dropped to INR3,747 cr from INR5,089 cr
items.quote: Total impact of, positive impact is INR2,121 crores.

items.statement: Expect Prestige & Above volume growth of 20% in FY27
items.quote: During FY27, we expect to grow our Prestige & Above portfolio volume by 20% and expect our EBITDA margin to expand by 125 basis points for the full year.

items.statement: Expect Luxury portfolio value growth of 25% in FY27 from INR 475 cr base
items.quote: We expect to sustain this growth momentum and deliver 25% [value] growth in FY27 in this portfolio.

items.statement: Expect Regular category volume growth of 3-5% in FY27
items.quote: for next year, we expect 3% to 5% volume growth in regular category.

items.statement: Capex guided at INR 150-175 cr for FY27, focused on internal capacity expansion and optimization
items.quote: The capex as I said will be in the range of INR 150 crores to INR 175 crores which will be largely on my internal capacity expansion and optimization, etc.

items.statement: Targets mid-teens revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: So again, this year, while we're looking at the mid-teens again, so we should see the mid-teen growth for this year as well in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Targets 1-2% EBITDA margin improvement in FY27
items.quote: We should look at about 1% to 2% improvement for FY '27 as well. That's our endeavor and we are positive we'll be able to deliver that.

items.statement: Targets 1-1.5% annual EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: Like in our previous calls also, we have guided that we typically target 1% to 1.5% kind of margin growth year-on-year basis. And we'll continue to drive that, focus on that.

items.statement: Plans INR20 crore capex for new Chennai office; annual admin capex INR20-25 crore
items.quote: So that will, of course, lead to some investments to the tune of INR20 crores. And otherwise, we remain pretty much, I would say, consistent in terms of our admin and facility capex is typically in the range of INR 20 crores to INR25 crores for a year.

items.statement: HRO order book 48% international as of March 31
items.quote: It's about 48% of my order book is on the international side.

items.statement: No significant decline expected from existing HRO clients in FY27
items.quote: For FY '27, we are not seeing any significant decline from our existing customer base employee headcount.

items.statement: FY26 constant currency revenue growth 6.3%; currency contributed 3.3%
items.quote: Yes. So 3.3% is the growth attributable to the currency depreciation and 6.3% is the growth attributable to the various efforts which the company has been making.

items.statement: HRMS V2 and PulseHR.ai AI platforms to launch in FY27; target INR3 crore annual efficiency gain
items.quote: By deployment of these platforms, we are looking at an efficiency of INR3 crores per annum on our Tech & Digital business.

items.statement: International BPM revenue 78% of CXM in FY26, up from 73%
items.quote: International business, which now contributes 78% of the total CXM revenue, the CXM is the BPM segment, on a full year basis, up from 73% last year.

items.statement: Diversity target 50% women; currently 47.9%
items.quote: Diversity and inclusion increased by 1.2% at 47.9%. We set ourselves a target of 50% and we're confident we'll be able to achieve this number.

items.statement: Revenue expected to reach INR 5,300-5,400 crores after capacity expansion to 1.3 million tons
items.quote: the overall revenue should go up to somewhere around INR 5,300 crores, INR 5,400 crores with that

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of around 20% after project completion and mining integration
items.quote: with the completion of the projects and with the mining integration, we should be somewhere around 20%

items.quote: this should commence production sometime in H2 of this financial year

items.statement: Mine development of INR 1,500 crores targeting completion by FY28
items.quote: the third part is the mines with a capex of somewhere around INR 1,500 crore. That is likely to be completed by FY28

items.quote: our EBITDA per ton, which has already improved meaningfully from INR 8,300 per ton in FY25 to INR 8,785 per ton in FY26

items.statement: Captive iron ore mines expected to improve EBITDA by ~INR 2,000 per ton once operational
items.quote: this to translate into an EBITDA improvement of approximately INR 2,000 per ton

items.statement: Solar capacity of 78 MW expected to save INR 30-40 crores annually in power costs
items.quote: there would be a total of about INR 30 to INR 40 crores that we are expecting as a saving yearly from these 78 megawatts of total generation

items.statement: Strong structural demand in UP and Gujarat markets with ~25% market share and brand premium
items.quote: we have got almost 25% of the market share, and we on top of that, we realize some premium over our peer group because of the branding what we have created for Gallantt

items.statement: Objective to reduce external sale of semi-finished products and channel more upstream output into finished TMT
items.quote: Our clear objective is to progressively reduce this proportion s by deepening integration and channeling more of our upstream products into finished TMT

items.statement: Current INR 3,000 crore capex to be funded from internal accruals; future medium-term plan may consider debt and equity
items.quote: Internal accruals remain our first preference. However, we will also consider debt and equity capital where appropriate, ensuring that growth is funded efficiently

items.statement: Home textile order pipeline at 180 days, strongest visibility ever, despite global headwinds
items.quote: The order pipeline today sits at 180 days, the strongest visibility we have ever had, and that has come despite global headwinds.

items.statement: Home textile exports ~60% of business, of which ~60% is US; servicing US customers directly after closing American Silk Mills subsidiary; US remains large export segment
items.quote: On the overall, if I have to give you a view, where exports is roughly in the home textile, 60% of our total business is around exports. And in that 60%, almost 60% is U.S. So we are servicing directly to the customers and not through the subsidiary.

items.statement: FY27 constant currency revenue growth guided at 10-13% and EBIT margin at 12.25-12.75%
items.quote: We are guiding to constant currency growth for FY27 to be in the 10% to 13% range, and we are guiding for EBIT margin band of 12.25% to 12.75% for FY27.

items.statement: Debt increased by INR 200 crores in FY26 vs INR 700 crores in FY25; cash flow healthy, debt expected to decline; 40-50% of cash flow paid as dividend, 50% used for acquisitions/growth
items.quote: Last year the debt had increased by around INR700 crores, while the current year the debt increase is INR 200 crores. So it has been come down, we have actually repaid.

items.statement: BFS demand centered on regulatory compliance, financial crimes, CX, cost efficiency with strong pull for AI/automation transformation; Healthcare payer timing shifts due to Medicare Advantage regulatory changes; CMT soft Q4 due to volatilit
items.quote: Demand remains centered on regulatory compliance, financial and economic crimes, customer experience, and cost efficiency, and we are seeing strong pull for our AI and automation-led, outcome-oriented transformation offerings.

items.statement: Shift to agentic operating model: revenue per employee up 12% over 2 years; revenue growth materially faster than headcount growth; attrition improved to 29.7% down ~6pp over 8 quarters
items.quote: Over the last two years, our revenue per employee has gone up by 12%. Our revenue growth over the last two years has been materially faster than our headcount growth and we expect that gap to widen as agentic operations scale.

items.statement: New commercial constructs: platform fee plus per-interaction pricing with outcome accountability; K-shaped growth dynamic where higher value per interaction drives greater volume allocation
items.quote: This is not a chatbot. It's a governed autonomous collector with outcome accountability through a platform fee plus per interaction pricing, where higher value per interaction can drive greater volume allocation, supporting a K-shaped growth dynamic.

items.statement: Targets export volumes of 220,000 units per month in Q1 FY27, up from 200,000 levels
items.quote: We are looking at moving the exports needle to 2,20,000 units per month this quarter, up from the 2,00,000 levels.

items.statement: FY26 capex was approximately INR 500 crores, split equally between ICE and EV investments
items.quote: Capex for the year was approximately INR500 crores, split equally between ICE and EV investments.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 20.8%, expects to hold margin flat sequentially in Q1 FY27 supported by currency, mix and operating leverage
items.quote: Sequentially, we look to hold margin flat, essentially supported by favorable currency, richer mix and operating leverage.

items.statement: Commodity cost inflation estimated at 3.5-4% of revenue for Q1 FY27; pricing actions taken to cover 40% of impact from April 1
items.quote: Taken together, we are currently estimating a material cost inflation impact of approximately 3.5% to 4% of revenue.

items.statement: Price hikes taken on April 1 roll back 30-40% of GST rate cut benefit to customers
items.quote: depending on the product group, the benefit which the GST rate cut had given to the customer, almost 30% to 40% of that could get rolled back.

items.statement: Chetak EV crossed 1 lakh quarterly retails for first time in Q4; March retails 50,000+; market share ~23%; C25 variant driving youth segment
items.quote: In quarter 4, Chetak crossed the 1 lakh retail mark for the very first time in a single quarter, the highest ever quarterly retails for the brand.

items.statement: Supply chain constraints impaired ability to service demand by 10-15% in April due to LPG shortage, manpower migration, outbound logistics
items.quote: Supply chain difficulties in terms of the LPG shortage, manpower availability and outbound logistics to overseas markets have impaired availability to service demand by about 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues in Middle East risk disrupting Gulf exports (5,000-6,000 units/month); commodity inflation volatile and event-driven
items.quote: this, despite the loss of business in the Gulf region, we are, of course, hoping that there will be no further disruptions due to the geopolitical issues in the Middle East.

items.statement: Aspiration to consistently deliver 20%+ AUM growth and outperform industry
items.quote: Our aspiration clearly is to consistently deliver 20% -plus AUM growth, largely to outperform industry.

items.statement: Target ROE in high teens over long term
items.quote: I think high teens is where our eyes are very clearly set on ROE.

items.statement: Confident to maintain spreads at 5%+ going forward
items.quote: We're very confident to maintain the spreads 5%+.

items.statement: Continue to guide credit costs below 25 bps on sustainable basis
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance on keeping credit costs under check and below 25 bps on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Opex to AUM ratio target below 3% over 2-3 years
items.quote: I think on a 2-to-3-year platform, yes. We are shooting for something below 3%.

items.statement: Steady state opex to AUM ratio expected at 2.75% at double balance sheet size
items.quote: We maintain that once we reach a double size of the balance sheet, it will be somewhere 2.75% opex to AUM ratio.

items.statement: Added 31 branches in Q4, total network 435 branches across 15 states
items.quote: During the last quarter, we added 31 branches, bringing our total network to 435 branches across 15 states.

items.statement: NIM expanded 44 bps Q-o-Q to 8.45% in Q4 FY26; FY26 NIM up 29 bps
items.quote: Our NIMs expanded by 44 bps sequentially to 8.45% during the quarter. NIMs improved by 29 bps overall in FY26.

items.statement: Cost of funds improved 62 bps in FY26; 73% of borrowing linked to external benchmarks for faster repricing
items.quote: We were able to deliver 62 bps improvement in overall cost of funds for FY26.

items.statement: Secured Rs. 975 crore (USD 108M) from multinational financial institution, largest NCD placement in company history
items.quote: During FY26, we also successfully secured commitment of ~Rs. 975 crores, USD 108 million, from a marquee multinational financial institution at a very competitive cost.

items.statement: Cumulative 125 bps repo cut improved affordability, creating strong tailwinds for affordable housing
items.quote: The cumulative 125 basis repo cut by RBI has improved affordability, creating strong tailwinds for the segment, which is affordable housing.

items.statement: No deterioration in asset quality seen in April; bouncing lower than previous month and previous year April
items.quote: In fact, bouncing in the month of April was less than the previous month. And this year, April is better than the previous year April.

items.statement: Focus on rebuilding direct sourcing muscle via CSC, website, app referral; indirect channels to continue as-is
items.quote: We just want to continue building our own strengths, which is direct sourcing through channels like CSC, develop our digital avenues, which is the website, our own app, which has a referral program.

items.statement: Risk-adjusted pricing optimization already started in FY27; early results seen without increasing risk
items.quote: As we speak, there is no better way to start a good deed than today. So, it has already started in the financial year.

items.statement: Target AUM of INR 6,500 crores by March 2027 (FY27 end)
items.quote: I spoke of, March '27, we are likely to exit at INR6,500 crores of AUM.

items.statement: Target disbursement of INR 500 crores/month for next 3-4 months, then INR 550-600 crores/month
items.quote: we want to retain at that level for at least next three-four months and then aim for about INR550 crores to about INR600 crores as we progress

items.statement: Cost of borrowings expected below 12.5% blended for FY27
items.quote: overall for the year, we believe it should be, below 12.5%.

items.statement: NIM contracted to 9.9% in Q4 from 11.1% in Q3 due to prior quarter borrowing costs
items.quote: NIM contracted to 9.9% compared to 11.1% largely on the impact of cost of borrowings which we have seen in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Yield improved to 22.8% in Q4 from 22.4% in Q3; incremental disbursement yield ~25.25%
items.quote: Yield for the quarter got positive impact because of this movement into better portfolio mix. So, it is at 22.8% compared to 22.4% in Q3.

items.statement: Opex target 7-8% of AUM in medium term; current INR 160 crores/quarter can optimize further without cutting corners
items.quote: in the medium term, it should come down to about 7% to 8% opex to AUM, and in the near term, can INR160 crores come down? That's what we are aiming for.

items.statement: Customer satisfaction score improved from 22% in Q3 to 71% in Q4; targeting 95% by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: our score, which was about 22% in Q3 has gone up to 71%. We are still not very happy, we are aiming for a 95% score either before the end of this quarter or early next quarter

items.statement: Merger with CFL subsidiary expected to complete in 5-6 months
items.quote: On the merger front, the process has begun, might take another 5-6 months, we are working on it.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Spread guidance maintained at 5% to 5.25% for FY27
items.quote: Our aim remains to deliver a spread at a portfolio level in our guided range of 5% to 5.25%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY27 at 30-40bps
items.quote: Guidance on the credit cost is the same. 30bps to 40bps.

items.statement: Plan to add 30-40 branches annually with broad-based expansion across new and existing cities
items.quote: Our branch strategy is to add about 30 to 40 branches every year. So that is what we are planning.

items.statement: Q4 NIM 5.9%, FY26 NIM ~5.7%; spread ex co-lending 5.3% with incremental borrowing cost at 7.6%
items.quote: Net interest margin for Q4 stood at 5.9%, while there was a modest sequential compression of 10bps, NIM remains robust and continues to reflect the strength of our business model.

items.statement: PLR cut 10bps in Jan; no further cuts planned near term; cost of borrowing ex co-lending down 10bps to 7.9%
items.quote: On the liability side, through proactive borrowing mix management, we were able to contract our cost of borrowing, excluding co-lending, by 10 basis points to 7.9%.

items.statement: Demand improved from Oct; April collections better than Apr'25 and Apr'24; no visible impact from Middle East crisis
items.quote: Early indicators from April demonstrate good collection outcomes compared to the same month in previous years. Fresh slippage % is lower than what was seen in April 2025 as well as April 2024.

items.statement: Housing 83%, LAP ~17%; co-lending 3.7% of AUM, yields 12-14% range, LAP yield 14-14.5%
items.quote: Our origination yield continues to be healthy at 13% with an 83% share of individual housing loans.

items.statement: Asset quality improved: 1+ DPD 4.7% (-60bps), 30+ DPD 3.2% (-50bps), Stage 2 1.4% (-30bps), GNPA 1.8% (-20bps); provision coverage 44.9%
items.quote: Our 1+ DPD is at 4.7%, down 60bps sequentially. 30+ DPD improved to 3.2%, down by 50 bps sequentially. Stage 2 reduced by 30bps to 1.4%. Gross Stage 3 improved to 1.8%, down by 20bps q-o-q.

items.statement: AI agents operationalized for income assessment and bank statement analysis; pilots in lead qualification, legal/tech evaluation, bureau analysis
items.quote: We have already operationalized proprietary AI agents for income assessment and contextual bank statement analysis.

items.statement: Co-lending disbursements doubled to INR307cr in FY26; book INR593cr (3.7% of AUM); issues to be resolved by May, normal run-rate from June
items.quote: In co-lending, disbursement for FY26 doubled, rising from INR153 crores in FY25 to INR307 crores in FY26.

items.statement: QIP of INR1,250cr completed Apr'25; CRAR 44.1% (Tier I 43.8%); net worth INR4,357cr; BVPS INR418
items.quote: Following the INR1,250 crores QIP completed earlier in Apr'25, our balance sheet remains very well capitalized.

items.statement: Cost-to-income 32% in Q4 (32.5% FY26, -330bps YoY); opex/assets 2.7% guided range 2.6-2.7%
items.quote: For FY26, the cost-to-income stood at 32.5%, an improvement of 330 bps y-o-y.

items.statement: Write-offs INR36cr in FY26; auction ~1,000 units/year (50-100/month)
items.quote: Total write-off has been – this year has been about INR36 crores.

items.statement: Management guides for ~30% steady-state growth in new insurance premium but historically beats this guidance
items.quote: We always guide about 30%, we always beat that guidance.

items.statement: Health insurance grew 68% YoY for full year FY26; term catching up fast; savings returned to growth after 3-4 weak quarters
items.quote: The new protection business in Q4FY26 was up for the year 57%, health at 68%, so even in this, 67% year-on-year protection story, health continues to be slightly ahead of the pack, which is a positive sign. But term is catching up fast.

items.statement: Paisabazaar turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26; expects significantly positive EBITDA in FY27 with operating leverage from stable fixed costs
items.quote: Paisabazaar, on an operating basis, is positive on EBITDA this quarter, and honestly, internally at least, we expect it to be significantly positive next year, so we actually expect quite a strong year from Paisabazaar.

items.statement: No active exploration of new growth opportunities or adjacencies at board or management level in last 3 months
items.quote: So, on both of them, today, we are not exploring, either as a board, or I can tell you as a Management, any other growth opportunity. We have not come across any in the last 3 months?

items.statement: PB Health (subsidiary) plans to raise capital but has not approached PB Fintech yet; PB Fintech holds 26-28% and has pro-rata rights
items.quote: Yes, PB Health is going to be raising capital. They will be close to that. They have not come to PB Fintech to raise capital yet.

items.statement: No regulatory communication on commission caps; only media speculation; management welcomes deferred revenue structures in life and lower EOM in health if implemented
items.quote: I haven't seen anything, neither have any of the insurance companies seen anything. I don't think most of the people in the regulatory have also seen anything. Only the media has seen it.

items.statement: POSP agent mix shifted dramatically: 83% of premium now from small agents (<₹20L revenue/year) vs ~50% a year ago; 99.5% of agents are small
