items.quote: 83% of the premium comes from the small agents now. If you look at the same number a year ago, that would have been close to 50-50 in terms of premium. So, I think our growth is despite the fact that we're cutting out a lot of the other part.

items.statement: Post-GST (Sept 2024), customers buying higher sum insured in health (majority now ₹10L+ vs <₹10L before) and attaching more riders in term; conversion rates also improved
items.quote: In health insurance, for instance, people are buying higher sum insured than they were buying earlier. So, if you look at the proportion of policies below ₹10 lakhs and greater than ₹10 lakhs, now a vast majority of policies are being bought which are ₹10 lakhs and above in terms of sum insured.

items.statement: PB Connect wholesale business shut down (was losing ~₹0.5 Cr/month); no profit impact; focusing on retail micro-agents only
items.quote: We have decided to stop the wholesale business, and it's a decision that we've taken, because we don't see any strategic value of that business. And, because we decided to stop that, you have seen a decline in the revenue. It has no impact on the overall profits. Like, maybe we were losing ₹0.5 Cr a month or something,

items.statement: Renewal revenue ARR grew 63% YoY to ₹1,126 Cr in Q4 FY26 (from ₹689 Cr); core driver of future profit growth alongside new business
items.quote: And for the quarter, this is at an ARR of ₹1,126 Cr, up from ₹689 Cr, so that's a growth of 63% year-on-year. And this is one of the key drivers, not the only driver, I must emphasize that the new business is also contributing to increasing profits and doing so very handsomely.

items.statement: Expect meaningful improvement in POSP growth next financial year; will be very aggressive on POSP expansion
items.quote: I think we should see a meaningful improvement in growth in the next financial year, and that's what I would look towards.

items.statement: PB Health acquired one operating hospital in Noida (₹150 Cr revenue, ₹20-30 Cr profit); second hospital in Central Gurugram going live by month-end; exploring more in Delhi and outside
items.quote: We've acquired one hospital, which is an operating hospital, makes about ₹20 -30 Cr of profit in a year, does about ₹150 Cr of revenue. So that's operational and running in Noida. Our next hospital is to go live in the next few weeks.

items.statement: PB Care+ preferred network now covers 500-600 hospitals; plan to take on O&M operations for some network hospitals under PB Health brand over next year
items.quote: Now, these will start to come together over the next one year, where you will see O&M operations. So, of this 500-600 hospital network, we will take on some of them and start operating them under the PB Health brand.

items.statement: Paisabazaar costs stabilized; expect significant operating leverage this year with ~30% more output from current employee base
items.quote: I think we'll see a lot of operating leverage, this year. The costs have stabilized, and I think the absorption of that will be much better.

items.statement: Stopped wholesale POSP distribution for one supplier in January; it was fluffy revenue without profits; core Paisabazaar business growing
items.quote: We stopped it in January. It takes 15 days to stop the business, after that, we are not doing that business. It was a meaningful part of the home loans part of the Paisa revenue. That's fine. It was kind of fluffy revenue in the sense it didn't really have profits.

items.statement: Health insurance grew 60%+ for 13 consecutive quarters; term insurance growth driven by internal execution; UAE business grew 3% YoY in March despite bombing and AWS outage, 10-12% for quarter
items.quote: In health, for the last 13 quarters, we have grown at 60%+; 60% growth over 4 years.

items.statement: Long-term policy proportion stable; 4-5 year policies increasing but overall multi-year premium share unchanged; POSP now 83% of premium vs 50% year ago
items.quote: If you look at the same number a year ago, that would have been close to 50-50 in terms of premium. So, I think our growth is despite the fact that we're cutting out a lot of the other part, and it's actually reducing year-on-year, but it's gone from about 50-50 to about 80-20 in terms of premium.

items.statement: Health insurance sustainability requires participation from regular claimers (co-pay, tiered networks) and value for non-claimers (wellness, OPD); industry costs becoming unsustainable without participation
items.quote: Without this participation, please appreciate the cost is going to become unsustainable for the industry; we're not doing this out of joy, we're doing this out of necessity.

items.statement: PB Health in late-stage conversations to raise capital; PB Fintech has pro-rata right but no obligation; PB Health has not used 30% of existing cash
items.quote: PB Health has no immediate requirement of cash. They have not even used 30% of the cash they had. But they are in conversations to raise capital, they are in late-stage conversations.

items.statement: PB Corporate grew 140% in Q4 on prestigious account wins in banking/financial space; still small but investing for growth; can be significantly more profitable than POSP at scale
items.quote: We had a great Q4 on the corporate side. We won some very prestigious accounts, which were with other brokers, which we were able to win, especially in the banking and financial space.

items.statement: Claims support expanding from 250+ cities to preferred hospital network (PB Care+) for red-carpet experience; 24/7 doctor consultation and ambulance via app
items.quote: The story now is actually shifting towards the PB Care+ that Yashish mentioned, where there is the preferred network, and if you go to that network, you will get preferential treatment.

items.statement: Target 15-20% EBITDA margin in 2.5 to 3 years from now
items.quote: EBITDA, we will maintain about two and a half to three years from now, that we should be able to get to those sorts of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Any new investments only in AI; focus on AI agents for merchant and consumer services
items.quote: Any new investment, only in AI.

items.statement: No impact from PPBL ban; remain committed to wallet license application with RBI
items.quote: I think, no impact. We did a press release on the system. And we remain committed.

items.statement: Agentic AI interface (Paytm Check-in) showing 7-8x better funnel conversion vs traditional tap workflow
items.quote: 7 times more people complete the funnel in an agentic workflow than a tap workflow.

items.statement: Expect significant operating leverage and EBITDA margin expansion over the next year driven by revenue growth acceleration and lower indirect expenses.
items.quote: if we are sitting here a year from now, we're confident that we would see, we'll look back and say there was significant operating leverage and EBITDA margin expansion as a result.

items.statement: Contribution margin expected between 55-60%, closer to 55% due to PIDF impact.
items.quote: contribution margins, we should expect between 55 to 60, but maybe more 55 to rather than 60, what was happening because of the PIDF impact.

items.statement: Payment processing margin growing faster; willing to accept lower device subscription revenue per merchant due to rising lending penetration.
items.quote: It is the case that payment processing margin is growing faster, and partly because payment processing margin is growing faster, but combined with the fact that our lending penetration is going up, we are okay to make a little bit less money on device subscription per merchant.

items.statement: No material capital investment plan for AI data centers; will rent compute capacity instead of building captive infrastructure.
items.quote: We don't have a material capital investment plan right now on the table or in plan.

items.statement: Merchant lending growth driven equally by base expansion, penetration increase, and ticket size growth (~15% each); TAM expansion into larger tickets may lift blended ticket size.
items.quote: historically, what we have seen is three primary drivers of growth. One is the expansion of the base. The second is the penetration rate. And the third is the increase in ticket size. And each one of these has been broadly similar. So roughly call it 15% give or take on each one of these drivers.

items.statement: Wealth and personal loans expected to become much bigger contributors to financial services revenue next year.
items.quote: we expect things like wealth and personal loans to be a much bigger contributor next year than before.

items.statement: Achieved 30-40% offset of PIDF impact in Q4 via sales and subscription revenue optimization; confident of near-full offset over time.
items.quote: we would be able to offset 30 to 40%. So I'm pleased to report that we did achieve that, and we're confident that over time we'll be able to significantly achieve a near full offset.

items.statement: DLG proportion in merchant loan disbursements broadly flat or slightly higher; amount flat; not a targeted metric.
items.quote: Proportion of DLG is broadly flat, maybe slightly higher. The proportion of loans that come with DLG is probably slightly higher. The amount of DLG is flat, flattish.

items.statement: Expect overall double-digit top-line growth in FY27; India Engineering to grow in mid-teens; aim to maintain current margin profile with endeavour to improve
items.quote: Lastly, I feel confident that the current financial year FY 2026 -2027, we should achieve an overall double-digit growth in top line, though the growth in India engineering would be little bit more aggressive, somewhat in mid -teens. We are also feeling confident that we should be able to at least maintain our current

items.statement: Advantek sales expected to grow at least 3x in FY27; bottom line to improve considerably
items.quote: I am happy to note that capacity utilization in Advantek is improving, and we should see the sale from this unit growing at least 3x in FY '27.

items.statement: Bushing business targets 25-30% growth in FY27
items.quote: In the current year also, we are having a very aggressive growth plan in tune of 25 % to 30% in this segment.

items.statement: Large-size cage segment expected to grow 15-20% in FY27
items.quote: We expect at least this segment to keep on growing in mid -teens without any problem, 15 % to 20%, no issue.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to improve 100-200 bps over 2-3 years
items.quote: Over the period of 2 to 3 years, our expectation is overall increase of 100 to 200 basis points in our EBITDA.

items.statement: India Engineering EBITDA ~22% in FY26; China EBITDA ~11% in FY26; Romania negative EBITDA; consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR270 cr in FY26
items.quote: Our India Engineering business has posted an operating EBITDA of around 22% in FY 2026, which is quite satisfactory.

items.statement: Commodity cost pass-through mechanism well-established; average 4-month lead period for pass-through to customers
items.quote: And on your questions for the pass -through mechanism, yes, it is very well-established pass-through mechanism with the customer. So as per the -- our agreed lead period, it automatically pass through to the customers. Different customers has a different lead period . But effectively you can say that on an average on f

items.statement: Europe demand showing slow sustained improvement; industrial sector strong globally; India automotive and industrial demand robust; wind not yet picked up in Europe
items.quote: So, last whole year, we are seeing demand has slowly improved over the year. And specifically for the Europ ean subsidiary also, the demand is continuing to improve. Right now, the indications are that it is all positive, growing.

items.statement: Input cost pressure from oils, lubricants, plastic cage materials; Europe inflationary pressure; logistics stable post Suez crisis
items.quote: I think there is definitely an impact on the cost side of it which we are trying to mitigate. I don't have a clear answer on that to what extent and where, but it is we are seeing the impact across the board on the input side of the, you know, specifically when we use some of the oils, lubrication things in the in our

items.statement: Targeting upwards of 20% revenue growth on consolidated basis for FY27 with margin appreciation expected
items.quote: Therefore, our guidance for FY '26 -'27, we are targeting upwards of 20% revenue growth on a consolidated basis. Margin appreciation is also expected going forward, led by the increasing contribution of our corporate segment and the gradual scaling of our higher -margin emerging verticals.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1,220 crores standalone and crosses INR2,500 crores on consolidated basis as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: As of 31st March 2026, our order book in hand stands approximately INR1,220 crores. And this is considerably high given the work that we have done last year. So, our position on consol basis is much better and crosses even INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: Board approved 100% acquisition of Citelum India Private Limited for smart lighting and urban infrastructure entry
items.quote: I'm happy to share that the Board has approved the 100% acquisition of Citelum India Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of the French government, marking our foray i nto the smart lighting and urban infrastructure space.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 13 bps to 6.54% in FY26; PAT margin up 106 bps to 5.16% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin is 6.54%, an improvement of 13 basis points over FY '25, reflecting operational efficiency, better operational leverage and improvement in business mix.

items.statement: RFP participation increased from 5-6 corporates in FY25 to 30-31 in FY26, indicating growing corporate demand
items.quote: I would also like to highlight that our RFP participation has significantly increased from just 5 to 6 corporates in FY '24, '25 to around 30 or 31 in the financial ye ar 2025, '26.

items.statement: Corporate segment margin profile has increased post-pandemic; able to command better pricing due to service delivery efficiency
items.quote: The margin profile of the corporate sector also has increased over the period of time that we saw, which in the post -pandemic era. So -- and of course, it depends on the service delivery capability.

items.statement: Q4 revenue declined 12% YoY due to selective bidding (INR180 crores not pursued) and government tender delays; working capital increased with new contracts
items.quote: INR180 crores worth of business, we had decided we had taken a step not to go and bid aggressively and chasing revenue. Therefore, we had a major shift in our bidding philosophy to focus on projects which give us better margins.

items.statement: Waste management qualification targets scaling from 480-500 TPD to 800-1,000 TPD over next 18 months
items.quote: Under CBS guidelines, our qualification allows us to bid for projects of approximately 480 to 500 TPD, which is tons per day, by the end of the current fiscal. We are targeting to scale this qualification to 800 to 1,000 tons per day over the next 18 months.

items.statement: Government segment awarded 17 new contracts in FY26 and 2 in Q4 FY26 with profitability-first approach
items.quote: The government segment recorded 2 new contracts awarded during Q4 FY '26 and 17 new contracts awarded on a full year basis, reflecting this measured and profitability-first approach.

items.statement: Debt-equity comfortable at 0.22; loan and advances at INR146.45 crores expected to reduce meaningfully near term
items.quote: Our debt equity remains comfortable at 0.22. This is a short-term working capital impact that is very typical on the business that is scaling rapidly, and we expect this to correct itself as our new contracts stable.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR1.50 per equity share (face value INR10) for FY26
items.quote: I am happy to share that Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR1.50 per equity share of face value of INR10 for the financial year '26, subject to approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Taskmaster B2C platform revenue INR46 lakhs in FY26; no 2-3 year guidance given as still in pilot phase
items.quote: Currently -- the Taskmaster currently has -- it is a start-up. So, it has posted a revenue of about INR46 -- in this year, INR46 lakhs. We are building it.

items.statement: Bioenzyme technology commercialization under pilot projects with VPRC; no fixed commercial cost or timeline yet
items.quote: Currently, as you know, we have a strategic association with VPRC, Vishnu Prasad Research Center, in Chennai. And we are doing various pilot projects with their enzymes. So, this is -- we're already running these pilots in Mira -Bhayandar and Vasai Virar gar bage dumps.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at minimum 15% with renewable sector contributing 20-25% of total revenue
items.quote: For Financial Year '27, we are guiding 15% minimum revenue growth with renewable sector contributing close to 20% to 25% of the total revenue, further building up our diversification.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance sustained at 11-12.5% range
items.quote: EBITDA margins expected to sustain between 11% to 12.5% and order inflow guidance of minimum INR5,500 crores.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow reached INR 11,332 crores, significantly exceeding INR 5,000 crores guidance
items.quote: Total order inflow for the year stood at INR11,332 crores, significantly surpassing our annual guidance of INR5,000 crores for Financial Year 26.

items.statement: Cost escalation compensated by authorities on monthly basis per new government circular
items.quote: The increased cost is already compensated by the department; they already come up with the circular for compensating the escalation part and earlier it was linked to 3 months and now it has been linked to monthly basis.

items.statement: Standalone debt-to-equity at 0.2x and consolidated at 0.6x as of March 31, 2026
items.quote: Our standalone debt-to-equity stood at 0.2x as on March 31, 2026. On a consolidated basis, it stood at 0.6.

items.statement: Unencumbered cash INR 166 crores and FDR INR 75 crores as of March 31, 2026 (corrected figures)
items.value: INR 166 crores cash, INR 75 crores FDR
items.quote: We have an unencumbered cash lying in our bank on 31st March, which is close to INR266 crores, and unencumbered FDR close to INR146 crores (It was erroneously mentioned that the unencumbered cash and unencumbered FDR stood at INR 266 crores and INR 146 crores, respectively. The actual figures should be read as INR 166

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-30% with order book expected to reach 275-300 crore in 15-20 days
items.quote: I will only tell you why we are conservative and giving you the estimates of 20 to 30 to 40 percent. We are entering the new year with 199 and in 15 days time you will see the numbers going to upwards of 275 to 300 crores.

items.statement: Accepted tighter margins in data centre, solar, semiconductor projects to build credentials; expect gradual margin expansion as segments mature
items.quote: From a strategic standpoint, we made a conscious decision to accept relatively tighter margins in data centre orders, solar orders, and semiconductor projects to establish credentials and build a strong pipeline of orders.

items.statement: Strong demand in solar (23 active hot leads), data centres, semiconductors; non-pharma sectors seeing multi-year investments
items.quote: We are about 23 solar active hot leads available, number one. Number 2, we have Waree reference getting established. We have Satvik and Gupin getting established. IMR will add more to those names. And there is a very beautiful large order which is about to happen.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA 23.16 crore (28.31% YoY growth); standalone EBITDA down 21.5% to 12.96 crore due to strategic investments
items.quote: From a financial standpoint, in FY26, we reported a consolidated total income of 221.72 crores up 46.93% year on year from 150.90 crores last year, with a EBITDA at 23.16 crores, growing 28.31% year on year from 18.5 18.05 crores.

items.statement: Management projects 35-40% revenue growth for FY27 and targets EBITDA margin of 10-10.5%.
items.quote: We grew about 40% last year in terms of revenue, and we have historically mentioned that we will be looking for 40% growth for the next two years. So, yes, the projected revenue growth is about 35% to 40%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin sweet spot is 10-10.5%; Q4 adjusted for INR 5 cr ECL provision was 10-10.2%.
items.quote: No, so we would maintain an EBITDA of around 10 % to 10.5%. That is our sweet spot, and we will keep our consistent growth and numbers in the area.

items.statement: Targets Contract Manufacturing revenue share of 55-60% and Services share of 9-10% in FY27.
items.quote: I think it would be a fair assumption. We will be looking to target about 55% to 60% contribution from Contract Manufacturing and Services I think somewhere around 9% to 10% that we have really maintained historically as well.

items.statement: Plans to invest INR 25-50 cr in FY27 for capacity deposits across vendor and customer side.
items.quote: We will look to invest more in this financial year, maybe about INR 25 crores to 50 crores, depending on the opportunities that we get.

items.statement: Current asset base provides revenue predictability of INR 6,000+ cr over next 5 years; annual capacity of 9 MT (INR 900-1,000 cr).
items.quote: The current asset base actually gives us a revenue predictability of more than INR 6,000 crores for the next five years.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 crucial; aims to lock in 85-90% of annual top-line and bottom-line visibility in Q1.
items.quote: Our aim is in Q1, we should be able to predict around 85% to 90% of our top line and similarly of the bottom line as well.

items.statement: Raw material cost inflation is fully passed through; steel price changes do not impact profitability.
items.quote: For us, it is a clear pass -through. Our business model is such, if steel is sold at 90,000 and if the market is at 95 ,000, so for us, it is a complete pass -through.

items.statement: Took additional INR 5 cr expected credit loss provision in Q4 FY26 as conservative measure on receivable risk.
items.quote: We have taken an additional expected credit loss of about INR 5 crores. This is in line with taking a more conservative approach in terms of the receivable risk that we generally take in our balance sheet.

items.statement: Secured INR 30 cr working capital sanction; targeting INR 100-150 cr total facilities to bridge payables-receivables gap.
items.quote: We got a INR 30 crores sanction from one of the banks, and this is what we have mentioned before also that we will be going for about INR 100 crores to INR 150 crores of working capital facilities.

items.statement: Asphalt revenues grew 88% QoQ to INR 30 cr in Q4 FY26; active customers doubled to 28; margins 18-20% net profit possible.
items.quote: Revenues from asphalt increased to INR 30 crores in Q4 2026, growing 88% sequentially. More importantly, active customers in this category nearly doubled during the quarter to 28 customers.

items.statement: Targets peak Contract Manufacturing utilization of 75-80%+ in FY27; current annualized utilization 65-70%.
items.quote: We will be looking to reach a peak utilization of more than 75% to 80% in this financial year itself.

items.statement: Operating cash flow to PAT ratio currently ~1:2; targets ~1:1.5 in FY27.
items.quote: Currently we are at about 1 :2, somewhere around that, and I think the next year we will be looking to be somewhere around 1 :1.5 maybe.

items.statement: DAAS execution pipeline strong with 12+ active projects and INR 1,800+ cr GDV under execution.
items.quote: Our DAAS execution pipeline remains strong with currently about 12 plus active projects and about INR 1800 plus crores of GDV under execution.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved to 66 days in FY26 from 110 days; expects to sustain or improve further.
items.quote: The net working capital days further reduced to 66 days in FY26 from 110 days a year ago.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected to cross INR 1,000–1,050 crores with SessionM acquisition closed
items.quote: With the acquisition having closed, we are comfortable that revenues will cross INR 1,000–1,050 crores in FY27.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 25–30% for core organic business
items.quote: We at steady state we'll be at like a 70% gross margin. We spend about 15% to 16% on tech, we spend a similar amount on sales and marketing, we spend about 5% to 7% on G&A. So, net-net, this should be a 25% to 30% steady-state, probably more, EBITDA margin business.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin at 19%; full year FY26 at 14.7%
items.quote: We closed Q4 at a 19% adjusted EBITDA margin. A good improvement from last year. For the full year again, we had a pretty good 14.7% margin.

items.statement: Organic platform NRR 114% in FY26; inorganic NRR 94%; blended 110%
items.quote: Overall NRR for the inorganic side was 94%, and overall that brings you to an average of 110% between the organic and the inorganic pieces.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 contribution margin exit rate at 4%, up 170bps QoQ; 145bps one-time logistics headwind from Q2/Q3 FY26 now behind
items.quote: So that one-time logistics disruption is kind of behind us. And hence, going forward, the baseline from contribution margin perspective is the 4% Q4 exit rate that we have.

items.statement: Contribution margin improvement driven by ad revenue growth and fulfillment cost reductions including lower failed deliveries and COD mix shift
items.quote: We will keep reducing on a long-term basis the cost to serve a customer and we will kind of operate, with a certain margin structure from fulfilment cost perspective.

items.statement: Meesho Mall contribution margin lower than core marketplace during investment phase; focus on onboarding brands and selection over margin maximization
items.quote: So the contribution margin would be lower than the core marketplace, primarily because right now in the investment phase our goal is to on-board a lot more brands.

items.statement: First-year user frequency doubled over last 3 years due to pricing, assortment, AI improvements; long-term frequency potential much higher vs China benchmarks (~100x)
items.quote: Almost a doubling of frequency has happened from a baseline perspective in the last three years.

items.statement: Prepaid mix increase lowers logistics cost (better delivery rates, no cash handling); cost savings passed to consumers as lower prices
items.quote: The movement from cash on delivery to prepaid transactions has been improving the cost structure that we have.

items.statement: Meesho Mall scaling for affordable brands (value packs, national/regional/D2C brands) targeting mass India, not just premium; strong early traction
items.quote: Meesho Mall is not just focused on the premium customer. I think it's going to be focused on anyone who cares about value. So, it's going to be mass India.

items.statement: Ad product adoption growing: >2/3 of GMV-weighted sellers active; advertised catalogs up >40% YoY; ROAS industry-leading multiples
items.quote: The number of catalogs or products which are now live on kind of ads has improved significantly on a Y-o-Y basis, more than kind of 40%.

items.statement: NMV/GMV ratio ~58.8% in FY26 (stable 58-60% last 3 years); NMV based on delivered non-returned orders
items.quote: I think roughly the NMV to GMV ratio has been between 58% to 60% for the last three years. I think for FY2026 as well the number is about 58.8% to be specific.

items.statement: Seller concentration decreasing; Pareto seller count increasing rapidly per DRHP disclosures
items.quote: The concentration on sellers continues to kind of reduce as we have more and more sellers who kind of become active as well as larger on the platform.

items.statement: FY27 credit growth guided at 1-2% above industry growth
items.quote: We expect our credit growth to be 1% or 2% over the industry growth.

items.statement: FY27 NIM guided at 3.75-3.80% for full year
items.quote: With respect to margins, we expect that NIMs to be in the range of 3.75% to 3.8% for the full year, though we are at 4% plus at the exit quarter of this year.

items.statement: FY27 ROA guided at 1.7-1.8% for full year
items.quote: Given the current macroeconomic environment and the anticipated effects on the net interest margins discussed earlier, we expect the ROA for the full year to be between 1.7% to 1.8%.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost expected below 1%
items.quote: Credit cost, I can think around less than 1% we can think of.

items.statement: FY27 GNPA <1.5%, NNPA <1%, slippages <1% of asset book
items.quote: GNPA is expected to be less than 1.5% and net NPA to be less than 1% for the full year. Slippages would be expected to be below 1% of the asset book.

items.statement: FY27 cost-to-income ratio guided below 50%
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio would be below 50% as we have been continuously planning, and we'll endeavor to retain that way.

items.statement: FY27 LCR to be maintained at 115-120%
items.quote: LCR would be maintained around 115% to 120%.

items.statement: Fixed rate loan book increased from 23% to 29% of total advances in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our fixed rate loan book, which was at 23% in the total book at the end of December has now increased to 29% at the end of March '26.

items.statement: Working capital utilization down 2-3% across sectors; lower disbursements in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We started seeing the lower level of utilization in the working capital. 2% to 3%, it is down across the sectors, many sectors, it is there.

items.statement: INR163 cr one-time prudential provision for sectors exposed to geopolitical tensions (textiles, ceramics, fertilizers, chemicals, granite/quartz)
items.quote: We have provided prudentially INR163 crores, I repeat INR163 crores is a onetime towards sectors identified that may get affected due to ongoing geopolitical tensions.

items.statement: Management refrains from giving FY27 presales guidance due to approval uncertainties; FY28 INR 15,000 cr target may slip to FY29
items.quote: I would really refrain from giving any -- I mean, any kind of guidance, you know better than that how indeterminate it is, whatever guidance we may give.

items.statement: FY27 construction spend guided at INR 1,200 crores
items.quote: This year, we should be spending INR 1,200-odd crores for construction.

items.statement: Adequate cash for land acquisitions with INR 1,000 cr mutual funds and INR 1,300 cr cash/RERA balances; partnerships with global players for large deals
items.quote: We have almost INR 1,000 crores of mutual fund balances at a consol level. And we also have almost INR 1,300 crores of cash and RERA balances.

items.statement: BD pipeline of ~INR 60,000 crores being pursued; MMR share ~INR 35,000 crores
items.quote: Overall, I could say roughly about INR 60,000 crores of projects we are at this point, kind of pursuing.

items.statement: Land bank GDV of INR 70,000-72,000 crores; ~INR 31,700 crores launched, 70-75% sold
items.quote: we have about INR 70,000 crores, INR 72,000 crores of GDV today, of which about -- how much is launched about close to 30,000.

items.statement: Launch timelines dependent on environmental/NGT approvals; Niyaara Tower C approval 'touch and go' may spill to Q3
items.quote: Approvals are largely based on two things. One is the environmental and the NGT. So those are pretty indeterminate things.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA guidance of Rs.400 crore derailed by pricing pressures; management declines to give new EBITDA number due to volatility
items.quote: The only challenge what we find is the Rs.400 crores number which we had communicated as a part of a couple of years plan, that actually gets bit derailed because of the pricing pressures which we are seeing both in the commodity segment and more importantly on the specialty segment.

items.statement: Net debt of Rs.71 crore to become net cash positive in FY27 with Rs.130 crore scheduled repayment
items.quote: See, our scheduled debt repayment for next year is again Rs. 130 crores. So, obviously we will be debt-free, because we have Rs. 71 crores of net debt. So, net debt obviously will be debt-free.

items.statement: Next growth capex focused on specialty/niche chemicals; holding back announcement until geopolitical uncertainty clears
items.quote: The CAPEXES which will come for growth predominantly as of now our thought process is to make it in the specialty segment or in the niche segment with related chemistries. So, as and when we are just a bit comfortable with this geopolitics we will announce and inform all our stakeholders.

items.statement: Solar power expansion paused awaiting regulatory clarity on TANGEDCO banking rules and geopolitical stability
items.quote: We are waiting for a clarification on that because entire dynamics will depend on extent to which we are able to offset the renewable over the TNEB rates.

items.statement: Specialty EBITDA margin contracted 6% to 30% in FY26 due to 22% C-PVC realization drop with no commensurate PVC input price reduction
items.quote: Despite volume increase in both C-PVC and SIOP, the significant reduction in NR by 22% in C-PVC with no consumerate reduction in PVC input prices resulted in PVC-C-PVC spread contraction and consequently margins.

items.statement: Basic chemicals EBITDA margin improved to 3.5% from 1.3% driven by better utilization and renewable energy benefits
items.quote: The basic chemical margins improved to 3.5% over 1.3% last year.

items.statement: Caustic soda Q4 realization ~$350/t; current Q1 realization north of $400/t due to Southeast Asia supply disruptions
items.quote: In Q4 I think it was around $350. And as we talk in Q1 the realization is in the north of $400.

items.statement: Soda ash import price currently ~$250/t; prices healthy due to reduced Iran/Russia imports and higher freight
items.quote: See, today the import price is in the vicinity of about $250.

items.statement: C-PVC spreads have recovered to pre-war levels after March PVC price spike; normalization expected in coming quarter
items.quote: The spreads have improved. It has gone back to the pre-war. What has happened is that that there was a spike in the PVC prices in the month of March. So, pass-over was not happening in the CPVC.

items.statement: Caustic soda demand dip from paper/textile sectors but no production curtailment; alumina demand very strong
items.quote: Yes, there has been a demand dip because of the lower offtake from the sectors that you have mentioned, but there has been no production curtailment because of the demand dip that we have seen.

items.statement: Synthetic rutile margin improvement driven by shifting export mix away from China to higher-paying ex-China customers
items.quote: When we are exporting into China, we do not get those prices. When we export into our existing customers who have been taking ex of China, their prices are better off.

items.statement: VCM feedstock supply from Middle East paused due to Gulf War; procuring at higher cost difficult to pass through to PVC prices
items.quote: Because of the gulf war that supply which has been the closest logistically is not coming. So, our contracts were all put on pause. So, to tide over the situation, we are procuring the feedstock. There has been no issue in production, but it is coming at a high cost which we are finding it difficult to pass on in our f

items.statement: Record FY26 volumes in C-PVC (50kt capacity), SIOP and synthetic rutile; C-PVC capacity expanded from 20kt to 50kt commissioned on time, within budget
items.quote: We achieved our highest ever sales volumes in C-PVC, synthetic iron oxide pigment and synthetic rutile.

items.statement: Current quarter expected to be slightly better or equivalent to Q4 FY26; KPIs are EBITDA, revenue, positive cash flow, working capital control
items.quote: the current quarter is going to be slightly better or equivalent to last quarter. And our KPI remains EBITDA, revenue and positive cash flow.

items.statement: Knitting expansion of 92 crore under execution adding printing capacity; modernisation capex for old asset replacement ongoing; no major new capex planned
items.quote: we are having ₹92 crores of expansion in our knitting business. We are adding printing as one of the segments. So, as a result of this new CAPEX, we may also add EBITDA in the 3rd and 4th quarters

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 7.1% in FY26 from 4.8% in FY25 (231 bps expansion); Q4 FY26 margin stable at 7.4% QoQ, up 115 bps YoY; target double-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: EBITDA stood at ₹327 crores, from ₹233 crores, registering a strong growth of 40.5% year-over-year, with margins improving to 7.1% from 4.8%, an expansion of 231 basis points.

items.statement: Knitting expansion expected to improve EBITDA by 3-4% from current levels once fully implemented in Q3 FY27
items.quote: once this is in place, we are definitely expecting EBITDA improvement by 3% to 4% in the current levels.

items.statement: Gas cost significantly increased in April after Gulf War disruption; availability restored but cost remains elevated until geopolitical situation normalises; lag in passing cost increases to denim customers
items.quote: availability of gas is there, but the cost has significantly gone for upward revision. So, that is a challenge, and we expect this to resolve.

items.statement: Board approved preferential issue of 24.7 lakh Convertible Warrants (~36 crore) to promoter group LNJ Textile Advisory LLP in April 2026
items.quote: our Board of Directors in April approved a proposal for the infusion of equity through the preferential issue of 24.7 lakh Convertible Warrants, which are equivalent to almost 36 crore

items.statement: Capital allocation disciplined with focus on projects offering 1-3 year payback, particularly modernisation and productivity improvement
items.quote: capital allocation would remain disciplined, with a strong focus on capital expenditure projects that offer shorter payback periods of one to three years, particularly in the area of modernisation and productivity improvement

items.statement: Core business organic growth target of 16-18% YoY maintained for FY27
items.quote: As you know, during the last couple of quarters, as part of GREAVES.NEXT strategy, I have said that our growth ambition in the midterm is between 16% to 18%. So, we continue to hold that.

items.statement: Core business EBITDA margin target of 13-15% maintained as business scales
items.quote: Once again, we have said that we will maintain 13% to 15% EBITDA margins as we scale the business.

items.statement: Capex of INR 500-700 crore over next 5 years focused on product development, capability enhancement, and international expansion
items.quote: So, after the revamp of the strategy and launch of GREAVES.NEXT, we earmarked INR 500 crores to INR 700 crores of CAPEX. This CAPEX will be focused in three major areas.

items.statement: Secured single largest institutional order worth INR 35 crore for end-to-end genset delivery including long-term maintenance
items.quote: We also secured our single largest institutional order worth INR 35 crores. This covers end-to-end delivery, including supply, installation, commissioning and long-term maintenance.

items.statement: Aftermarket grew 35% YoY in FY26; retailer onboarding target of 3,000 by FY27 from ~350 currently
items.quote: We accelerated the retailer engagement, onboarding approximately 350 retailers with a clear roadmap to scale this to 3,000 by FY '27.

items.statement: Energy Solutions outlook strong supported by infrastructure growth, industrial expansion, and reliable power demand
items.quote: The overall outlook for India's genset market remains strong. This is supported by infrastructure growth, industrial expansion and an increasing demand for reliable power.

items.statement: Commodity cost pressures in aluminum, copper, platinum; passthrough mechanism activated in Q1 FY27
items.quote: However, there is a passthrough mechanism, which we have already activated in Q1. So, therefore, we do see some recovery on account of price.

items.statement: Greaves Finance AUM at INR 521 crore as of March 2026; group cash balance healthy
items.quote: The Greaves Finance Limited, the total asset under management for the financing business stood at INR 521 crores as on March '26. Our balance sheet continues to remain strong with a healthy cash balance.

items.statement: Expects 5-10% volume growth in FY27, with top-line growth higher due to elevated prices
items.quote: We expect that the next year will be like a normal year, which is about 5% to 10% growth rate, but there is too much uncertainty in the future.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR 80-90 crore for completion of Dahej project and maintenance
items.quote: So around -- it will be around INR80 crores to INR90 crores.

items.statement: Management believes margins have bottomed and expects improvement in FY27, though sustainability uncertain
items.quote: But we are optimistic that I think we have seen the bottom. So probably the margins going forward will be a little better than what we have experienced in the last year.

items.statement: Ammonia cost doubled from ~INR 50/kg to over INR 100/kg; finished goods prices raised to protect margins
items.quote: Going forward, yes, like ammonia, as you said, we were in the region of about INR50 a kg and now we are over INR100 a kg.

items.statement: Pharma demand stable (50-60% of sales); agro demand uncertain due to monsoon/El Nino concerns
items.quote: Well, at the moment, we haven't seen anything, but there is a little bit of concern that they could be affected, not pharma as much as agro because they expect this monsoon also with the El Nino and all, there is some concern.

items.statement: Methylamine faces overcapacity with new entrant Aarti; ethylamine capacity sufficient for 4-5 years; acetonitrile capacity adequate for 2+ years
items.quote: Methylamines, there is an overhang of capacity because a new player has come in. So there's RCF, Balaji, Aarti and us now. So there is a bit of overcapacity of methylamines

items.statement: Ammonia supply disruption risk persists due to war/Hormuz Strait; short-term contracts only; green ammonia 3-5 years away
items.quote: It will take some time for the industry to sort the supply chain out, maybe another 3 months, maybe 6 months for it to stabilize. Hopefully, by that time, all this Hormuz Strait will be opened out

items.statement: Balaji adding 18,000 TPA acetonitrile capacity; Chinese competition easing but still present; anti-dumping duty benefit only from late FY26
items.quote: Balaji putting up a new acetonitrile plant. Yes, of course, it can happen, and will ultimately make the competitive material.

items.statement: FY26 volume and value flat (+/-1%); prices down ~1%, volumes down ~1%
items.quote: It's been basically flat volume and value, plus-minus 1% either way prices have dropped 1% and volume has probably dropped 1%. So the combination is about 2% drop.

items.statement: Capacity utilization 60-85% across plants; sufficient headroom for growth without new capex
items.quote: On an average, we must be having between 60% and 85% capacity utilization, and that we continue to get enough raw material to keep there.

items.statement: Expect healthy volume growth in FY27 above industry average due to low base from FY26 decline
items.quote: we certainly look forward to a positive growth. And it should be in access to the industry average because we had a bad year last year. So, for us, it is a low base on which we have to grow this year. So, we expect healthy growth over last year.

items.statement: Capex on hold; will evaluate after first two quarters of FY27 before deciding on further expansion
items.quote: No, we are putting CAPEX on hold because we have already invested for all the developments and we will observe first two quarters as I told you last time before we decide for the further CAPEX plans.

items.statement: Building products margin 14-18%; agriculture margin 8-10% depending on season
items.quote: Normally, agriculture would have about 8% to 9% margin, or 10%, it depends on time of the year, while building product offers from 14% to 18%.

items.statement: May see inventory gains in Q1 FY27 due to volatile petrochemical prices from geopolitical issues
items.quote: going forward in Q1 also, as things are very volatile today, it is difficult to predict. But still, we may see some advantage on inventory side.

items.statement: Agriculture and building product demand back to normal after initial war-related disruption
items.quote: Demand for agriculture and building products were impacted immediately after the war broke out because of the sudden very high increase in the raw material and finished goods prices. But now they have settled. So, demand is again back to almost average normal.

items.statement: Expanding CPVC capacity; OPVC not on agenda; CPVC offers better margins and is focus for growth
items.quote: CPVC we are expanding. OPVC is not on our agenda at this moment.

items.statement: Government withdrew import duty on PVC and polymers until end of June due to war-related supply challenges
items.quote: Government of India has withdrawn import duty on PVC and all other polymers till the period of end of June up to 1st July.

items.statement: Trade receivables declined to INR 28 crores from INR 48 crores due to reduced institutional sales in Q4
items.quote: our outstanding are mostly towards institution. And you must have seen in the Q4, we have reduced our institutional sales as per our projections given to you. So, this is why the outstandings have declined.

items.statement: Targeting substantial revenue increase in FY27 and aim to reach INR 1000 crore revenue target previously guided
items.quote: we should be able to aim substantial increase over last year. And we will definitely target towards our guidance. That is what we had said earlier.

items.statement: Second manufacturing plant timeline undecided; will wait for first two quarters of FY27 to decide
items.quote: No. As I said earlier in the question, we will wait for first two quarters to make up our mind when and how, where.

items.statement: Loan growth target of 15-16% for FY27, matching industry if higher
items.quote: we are still aiming to get between 15% and 16%. But if the industry were to do higher than that, we will match industry.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 TCV deal signings reached $208 million, up 3% sequentially, marking second consecutive quarter above $200 million
items.quote: We've signed deals worth $208 million TCV during Q4, which is 3% higher than what we signed in Q3 of FY '26.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 18.5% (+30 bps QoQ); FY26 full year margin at 16.3% (+333 bps YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q4 increased to 18.5%, which is an expansion of 30 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin expected to be upward of 15% as investments in sales, AI, and leadership will erode margins from current 18.5% level
items.quote: I continue to believe, that our steady state margins that we should expect is going to be upward of 15% and there will be an erosion from where we are today, obviously, because of these investments.

items.statement: Sales team strength to increase 30-40% YoY by mid-FY27 with significant hiring already completed in US and Europe across verticals
items.quote: By the middle of FY '27, I reckon that our sales team strength would have gone up by 30% to 40% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Demand environment remains soft and volatile with clients delaying decisions due to macro uncertainty, trade, tariffs, and geopolitics
items.quote: the demand environment has been quite challenging, marked by a lot of uncertainty and added to it the developments related to trade, tariffs and geopolitics have made the situation even more volatile

items.statement: Revenue shifting from traditional services to AI-led outcome-based deals causing near-term revenue deflation but expected to catch up in future quarters
items.quote: what happens in an AI deal is we have to commit to the savings and underwrite some of the savings right up front, which is why you see revenue deflation in the immediate and the medium term

items.statement: Walking away from low-margin non-strategic deals cost ~200 bps of FY26 growth; productivity benefits from AI deals passed upfront to clients
items.quote: at least 200 basis points of growth roughly went away because we walked away from low-margin, non-strategic deals

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin included ~340 bps one-off benefits (170 bps forex + 170 bps provision reversals) not expected to repeat in Q1 FY27
items.quote: the forex tailwind gave us a 170-basis point benefit. And the other items that I talked about gave us another 170 points benefit. So it's about a 340-point benefit that we got in the fourth quarter

items.statement: ETR elevated in FY26 due to US federal tax provision and Labor Code changes; expected to normalize to historical levels from FY27
items.quote: The elevated ETR due to incremental U.S. tax, as I had called out on our earlier calls, was limited and will be limited to FY '26, and we expect ETR to settle closer to our historical ETR level starting FY '27

items.statement: BFSI spending stable but shifting from traditional to AI-related work; no increase in overall pool size observed
items.quote: We don't see an increase in spending. We see the spending to be pretty much even, only the shift that I spoke about from traditional services to new age services

items.statement: Expects lower EBITDA percentage margins in Q1 and Q2 FY27 due to crude oil inflation, but higher revenue growth and absolute EBITDA to remain reasonably good
items.quote: This quarter and next quarter, I expect some pressure on EBITDA percentage margin, but we are seeing upside in a variety of other areas. We're seeing pricing growth higher than what we thought we get.

items.statement: Indonesia expected to deliver mid-single-digit volume growth and high single-digit value growth going forward
items.quote: So, I think what we will get in Indonesia is kind of mid-single-digit volume, high single-digit value going forward.

items.statement: Africa business expected to deliver strong performance in FY27 with FMCG growth compounding
items.quote: I expect Africa performance to be quite strong, on Monday, we'll explain to you that there are some underlying drivers in FMCG, which are driving bulk of the growth in Africa, and those will continue to compound in FY27.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 21.7%, standalone margin at 24.7%
items.quote: In Q4, at a consolidated level, revenues grew 11% in INR terms on the back of 6% underlying volume growth. EBITDA grew by 10%, with operating margin at 21.7%

items.statement: Price hikes taken in April: soaps +5%, detergents +6-7%, household insecticide +4-5%
items.quote: In soaps, we have taken our prices by 5%. In detergents, we have taken up prices again by 6% or 7%, which is now a meaningful part of our business, maybe 7%. In household insecticide, we have taken up prices again by 4%, 5%.

items.statement: Blended raw material inflation currently 7-9% at USD 100-105 Brent and 4,500 MYR palm oil
items.quote: I think we put that out in our result 7% to 9% is what we're seeing.

items.statement: India standalone delivered 8% underlying volume growth and 10% sales growth in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our standalone business delivered an excellent quarter, driven by 8% underlying volume growth and 10% sales growth.

items.statement: Indonesia delivered 4% underlying volume growth for second consecutive quarter
items.quote: In Indonesia, I think even last quarter, we had about 4% volume growth. And this quarter also, we had 4% volume growth.

items.statement: Crude oil at USD 100-110 creates 6-7% inflation spread across all categories, may pressure margins for 3-4 months
items.quote: if this oil remains USD100 to USD110, that's what we expect and that to for a few months because it USD100, USD110 as we had spent in the pre-note is not something that we can't price up for over 3, 4 months.

items.statement: El Nino risk may impact household insecticide in Q1 but benefit soaps and Indonesia
items.quote: if the predictions of El Nino are right, there will be impact and Q1 will be a difficult quarter for HI because for a good quarter when it's hot and reasonably wet, actually, it's reasonably good for Q2 and Q3 should be okay.

items.statement: State-of-the-art pet food plant commissioned in Nashik, volumes shipping
items.quote: We've set up a state-of-the-art plant in Nasik, and we've shipped our volumes from there.

items.statement: Godrej Fab ARR at INR 500 crore GSV (INR 450 crore NSV) in Q4, broken even in Q4
items.quote: I think our ARR is about on GSV terms, about INR500 crores in quarter 4 and maybe INR450 crores in NSV terms. So, it's very, of course, internally look at our gross sales value is about INR500 crores.

items.statement: Revenue presentation changed from Q4 FY26: customer-related spends netted off revenue per ICAI EAC opinion, no impact on EBITDA, PAT, cash flow
items.quote: The impact is straightforward, revenue from operations and the corresponding lines within other expenses both reduced by the same amount period after period. There is no impact whatsoever on absolute EBITDA, PAT, profit after tax, total liquidity, or cash flow.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin at 20.1%, up 276 bps YoY and 180 bps QoQ; EBITDA net of RSU expense at 19%
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA, adjusted for RSU expenses and non-recurring costs, stood at INR 115.7 crore or $12.6 million, which is an EBITDA percentage of 20.1%.

items.statement: Management maintains EBITDA margin guidance in 17%+ range; Q1 at 20.1% includes FX benefit, core margin ~19%
items.quote: We have continued to maintain our margins in a very healthy range, as we had guided in the +17% margin, kind of a range.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month ACV wins increased to $82.5M from $76.5M last quarter, showing positive deal momentum
items.quote: We had $76.5 million of ACV on a TTM basis last quarter. We are reporting $82.5 million of ACV wins this quarter.

items.statement: AI-driven demand expanding; ~29% of revenue from AI/AI-enabled services; strong deal momentum in SDLC, modernization, business workflows
items.quote: approximately 29% of our revenue today comes from AI and AI-enabled services.

items.statement: Fixed-price revenue mix rising from ~10% in 2024 to ~15-16% in 2025; shift toward outcome-based pricing with AI transformations
items.quote: Last year, as in 2024, has already probably changed to maybe closer to 15% or 16% in 2025, and we believe that it will continue to move in the favor of fixed price as we go along.

items.statement: Deliberate bench investment in AI/data talent (~2-2.5% utilization dip to 80.5%) to build COE and EXIQO AI studio
items.quote: there's a deliberate decrease in utilization as a result of which, for creating that COE and the deliberate bench on both data and AI talent, thus bringing our utilization down to about 80.5%.

items.statement: Frontier model vendors (Anthropic/OpenAI) partnering with PE to target mid-market; seen as validation of people-centric AI approach, not pure tool play
items.quote: It validates that AI is fundamentally a people problem, not a tools problem. Because if it was only tools, then those frontier companies have already released the tools.

items.statement: No formal forward guidance provided; high confidence in organic and combined growth trajectory; EBITDA maintenance expected
items.quote: while we don't provide any forward guidance and flavors, but very high confidence that both organically, as well as combined entities, we are on the right trajectory for doing what we promised to our investors to continue to grow the organization.

items.statement: Novigo acquisition fully integrated; restated annual revenue ~$21-22M vs original $32M due to accounting policy alignment (gross to net)
items.quote: That restated will stand at about $21-$22 million a year.

items.statement: Token costs for client delivery borne by client (100% pass-through); internal token costs for training/R&D absorbed by company
items.quote: token cost for output delivered to the client is usually, I would say, in almost 100% cases borne by the client, either they provide us subscription to the front end model that they are subscribed to, or we would do it, but we will pass on the costs.

items.statement: New CRO Farooq Ahmad onboarded (Bay Area, 30 yrs tech experience) to strengthen North America tech sales and go-to-market
items.quote: we recently onboarded Farooq Ahmad as our Chief Revenue Officer. He is going to be leading our sales engine, strengthen the go-to-market approach, and lead the key growth initiatives across key markets, especially focusing on North America in the tech space.

items.statement: SG&A dropped to INR 91.4 crore from INR 114.3 crore QoQ due to AR provision reversal; normalized run-rate ~INR 110-115 crore
items.quote: SG&A expenses decreased by INR 22.9 crore from INR 114.3 crore in last quarter to INR 91.4 crore this quarter. This is mainly due to reversal of conservative AR provision on account of realization in this quarter.

items.statement: Middle East crisis impacted Novigo in Q1; expected to be behind them, contributing to positive growth ahead
items.quote: They obviously were also impacted by the Middle East crisis to some extent in Q1. So, that hopefully will be a thing behind us, and then that will contribute to positive growth in that front as well.

items.statement: P&A segment targets 50% total growth by FY29; no piecemeal FY27 guidance given
items.quote: we are totally committed to delivering the F '29 objective, which we said that we are going to ultimately work towards managing a 50% total growth on our P&A portfolio, and we are totally committed to that.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA per liter guided at INR5-7 for FY27, same as FY26 range
items.quote: INR5 to INR7 is our guidance for the EBITDA per liter. That's the range in which it will remain for the year.

items.statement: Bulk alcohol annual volume guidance ~200 million liters; growth expected on top from UP capacity
items.quote: INR20 crores is our annual guidance. And on top of that is UP. So yes, there is going to be growth on top of the INR20 crores.

items.statement: No immediate need for external fundraise; internal accruals and debt optimization to fund FY27 plan
items.quote: this year, we do not see a need to achieve the business plan given some of the operational improvements and leverage we've been able to get.

items.statement: Annual debt outflow reduced from INR67 cr to INR14 cr projected for FY27, unlocking INR53 cr liquidity
items.quote: we have systematically reduced our annual debt outflow from INR67 crores per annum to just INR14 crores projected for FY27. This action alone unlocks INR53 crores of direct liquidity in the coming year.

items.statement: Blended interest rate reduced by 50 bps through refinancing and treasury management
items.quote: Through this refinancing and broader treasury management, we have driven down our blended rate of interest, combining all forms of borrowing by a full 50 basis points.

items.statement: Ethanol and ENA export orders visible; Q4 exported 3.7 million liters ENA
items.quote: In Q4, we started this journey and exported 3.7 million liters.

items.statement: Ethanol demand expected to stay strong due to higher blending mandates and flex-fuel push
items.quote: Over the last few months, we've seen oil marketing companies, Government of India start preparing towards higher ethanol blends. And I believe flex fuel mandates for new cars is also on the angle. So overall, ethanol demands are going to be quite strong going forward.

items.statement: P&A revenue grew 27% YoY to INR164 cr, volumes up 31% to 1.19M cases in FY26; underlying growth ex-Delhi 58%
items.quote: When we isolate and remove the Delhi anomaly from the data, our P&A business grew at an exceptional 58% year-on-year.

items.statement: Regular & Others FY26 revenue INR900 cr (+4%), volumes 15.7M cases, EBITDA INR158 cr (+12%); portfolio reset in WB & Haryana complete
items.quote: For the full year FY26, revenue was INR900 crores, up 4% with volumes at 15.7 million cases and EBITDA delivering a 12% expansion to INR158 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical-driven cost pressure on glass, PET, logistics; mitigation underway, impact expected modest
items.quote: we have quickly geared up and a lot of efficiency measures are already up and about. While we see that there will be an impact, but the way we see most of the impact, we should be able to neutralize.

items.statement: Bihar prohibition policy monitored; first-mover advantage if market reopens due to existing manufacturing footprint
items.quote: We are actively monitoring the legislative landscape and policy regarding prohibition. If or when that market reopens, the first-mover advantage should be significant because we have a fully operational footprint in the state.

items.statement: Q4 manufacturing inventory buildup from ENA shift and permissions delay to liquidate in Q1 FY27
items.quote: This inventory buildup will get liquidated in Q1.

items.statement: P&A segment revenue target is INR500 crore by FY29, not INR1,000 crore
items.quote: The number for P&A is INR500 crores, not INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA guidance maintained at INR5-7 per liter regardless of ethanol/ENA mix
items.quote: Our guidance remains between INR5 and INR7 a liter regardless of ENA or ethanol.

items.statement: R&O margin target 16-18%; Q4 at 18% seen as high end, expect slight decline due to UP mix
items.quote: Our target in this space is 16% to 18%. So it will be a little bit lower than that for sure.

items.statement: Rajasthan price increase of INR30 per case secured for FY27; no increase in UP or Haryana yet
items.quote: This year also, we've got a price increase in Rajasthan to the extent of INR30 a case.

items.statement: UP and Rajasthan combined grew 7% in FY26; expect higher growth in FY27 driven by UP brand launches
items.quote: Rajasthan plus UP last year give us 7% growth. I believe in the coming year, Rajasthan plus UP will give us higher than 7% growth.

items.statement: Bulk volume target well over 20 crore liters in FY27 (20 crore from existing units + ~2 crore from UP)
items.quote: Well over 20 crores will be the target for this year.

items.statement: West Bengal re-entry timing uncertain; license shift in progress, relaunch with new portfolio planned
items.quote: In West Bengal, our license is in process, and it's very difficult to commit a particular quarter when everything gets kicked off and signed off.

items.statement: Equity capital raise put on hold; expansion funded from internal cash flows; residual cash to repay debt
items.quote: The plan for capital raise -- equity capital raise has been put on hold. We are able to manage our expansion based on our internal cash flow.

items.statement: Net debt at INR627 crore as of Q4 FY26; R&O working capital 5-6 days; interest cost expected INR14-15 crore/quarter post-refinancing
items.quote: So the net debt business for the company is at INR627 crores. That's the net debt.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR170-180 crores, higher due to AI-led tech investments
items.quote: For the next year, the capex is estimated at roughly around INR170 crores, INR180 crores.

items.statement: Store expansion guidance maintained at 13-15% area addition annually, net of 1-2% closures
items.quote: The guidance for the next year remains the same at 13% to 15% area addition every year, net of 1% or 2% mistakes that may need closures year-on-year.

items.statement: Yarn prices up 10-15%, translating to 5-7% apparel cost increase; passing 1-2% to consumers, absorbing rest
items.quote: So definitely there is a rise of almost 10% to 15% in the yarn prices, which effectively converts to almost 5% to 7% in the apparel prices. With some negotiation in certain products, we have to absorb 1% to 2% to the cost of the future deliveries.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment healthy but crude-led inflation across basket (60-65% need-based) may pressure spending; minimum wage hikes provide some offset
items.quote: So the consumer may find it difficult to manage their inflation and that could be a reality. And that is what we are caring about, that all of our consumers who are largely need-based consumers whose their income, but one respite we are able to see is the increase in minimum wages.

items.statement: Polyester mix 70-75% in forward/winter season vs ~50% cotton in summer; shifting to kurta sets from kurtas to improve ASP and fashion mix
items.quote: But when we are moving towards the forward season and the winterish season, the polyester mix goes up. That is why your polyester mix would be around 70%, 75% of the total sourcing that we are doing in the forward period.

items.statement: Crude oil up 30-35% driving yarn cost up 8-9% and garment cost 3-4% for polyester-heavy products; supply chain disruptions from gas issues and labour shortages in Bengal/Tamil Nadu
items.quote: What is the level of because if the overall crude prices that we see has grown by almost 30%, 35%, it has translated to almost cost of 10% -- 8% or 9% in yarn cost, and which has resulted into 3% to 4% of apparel or garment cost.

items.statement: Targeting rent expense at 6-7.5% of sales (currently ~8%) as new stores planned at lower rent ratios; pre-COVID was 4.5%
items.quote: So I think we should be hovering and then we should be comfortable around say 6%, 7% to 7.5% and 7% is the ballpark figure which we want to come up with.

items.statement: Medium-term ROC target 18-20%+ (currently ~14.5%); LimeRoad marketplace profitable at CM3 high single digits, losses cut 70% YoY
items.quote: So I think we have been always working towards acquiring around 15% to 18% of ROC giving. So right now we are around 14.5% we want to go to 18% and then maybe 20% and above 20%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26: 24% total sales growth, 12% LTL (10th consecutive quarter), 29 new stores, 92 net additions FY26; Unlimited South 28% revenue growth, 63% EBITDA growth
items.quote: Quarter 4 has been a great growth quarter for us, with actually our highest ever quarterly new store additions as well as good like-to-like same-store sales growth, leading to a total sales growth of 24%.

items.statement: Labour cost pressure emerging from Haryana/Noida region wage hikes; competitive intensity rising but market share gains possible from weaker peers
items.quote: I see there are constraints in terms of the overall inflation, overall labour cost also going up because what happened recently in Haryana, or Noida and all of this certainly has led to a little bit of -- could lead to a little bit rise in the labour cost.

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guided at 20-25%, NIM 12.8-13.2%, cost-to-income 33-35%, credit cost 3-4%, ROA 4-4.8%, ROE 16-20%
items.quote: For FY27, we are guiding an AUM growth of 20.0-25.0%, NIM of 12.8-13.2%, cost to income of 33.0-35.0%, credit cost of 3.0-4.0%, ROA of 4.0-4.8%, and an ROE of 16.0-20.0%.

items.statement: Microfinance portfolio growth assumed at 10-12% for FY27, with 6-8% of MFI customers graduating to retail finance annually
items.quote: So our assumption is around 10-12%.

items.statement: Retail finance share of AUM expected to reach 24-25% by end of FY27, up from 18.1% in March 2026
items.quote: It should hit somewhere around 24-25%.

items.statement: Mortgage loan branches expected to breakeven at INR 800-1,000 Crore book size; currently operating ~120 dedicated retail branches
items.quote: For mortgage loan products, the standalone retail finance branches, we should see them achieving breakeven as we near maybe INR 800 Crore to INR 1,000 Crore of mortgage book from the retail finance branches.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance widened to 3-4% for FY27 to absorb potential macroeconomic effects from global issues; April collections trend holding at Q4 levels
items.quote: The broader range, what we have picked from 3.0-4.0%, it is primarily to take into account all these evolving externalities, because we need to see how, what is going to be the actual fallout of the global issues.

items.statement: Digital adoption accelerating: Grameen Mahi app active users 11.2 Lakh (25.4% of borrowers); digital collections rose from 14% to 22% YoY; tech processes 30 Lakh transactions/day
items.quote: Our customer app, Grameen Mahi, onboarded 8.4 Lakh borrowers in FY26, taking the total active base to 11.2 Lakh customers, representing 25.4% of our borrower base. The proportion of digital collections increased YoY from 14% in Q4 FY25 to 22% in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Expects mid-double-digit revenue growth in FY27 with 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: We are reasonably confident of sustaining mid double-digit growth in fiscal '27 with 30 to 40 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: Online B2C expected to sustain 20%+ growth rate going forward
items.quote: Yes. for us, online B2C, like I said, continues to remain solid, and we expect that over the years, this should continue to be at 20% plus.

items.statement: Gross margin target of high-50s percentage over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We have directionally been working on delivering towards the high 50s, and that's what we will go towards the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Plans 1.5 lakh net sq ft retail space addition in FY27
items.quote: So we expect to drive about 1.5 lakhs net square feet addition over the next fiscal year across our portfolio.

items.statement: India revenue ~4% currently, expected to double in FY27; targeting dominant role as India becomes 2nd/3rd largest auto market

items.quote: There will be a pre-buying that will happen in the second half of 2026 And we believe that the truck business will pick up a little bit. The European market as well as North America market is likely to pick up in the second half of 2026.

items.statement: ESG commitment: Net-zero by 2050 (internal target pre-2040), >40% carbon footprint reduction by 2030, signed science-based targets
items.quote: And we have actually signed up with science based targets now And we are committed to being a net- zero organization by 2050. But there is an important milestone that we will hit in 2030, which is reducing our own carbon footprint by more than 40%.

items.statement: India revenue share currently 4%, expected to increase substantially as market becomes third largest globally
items.quote: Right now, we are about 4% of our revenues are from India and they will increase substantially. The share will go up and we do believe If it is going to be the third largest market.

items.statement: China revenue share similar to India at around 4%
items.quote: We would not like to talk about that, but it is similar to India

items.quote: Roughly, we will grow 30% this year, but for the next two years or next three years, in that case, the number will have to grow up 3 to 4X is the understanding correct?

items.quote: The 10% wallet share, it will increase by 20%. In the immediate future, right? It will not move from 10% to 20% of their wallet share. It will increase by 20% this year

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected in mid-teens percentage assuming current aluminum prices

items.statement: Stationary engine order book of $100 million finalized, targeting revenue by FY29-30

items.quote: On FY 2027 itself, we are not very clear about the capex as today because we have taken some interim requirements. But September we have to decide on the capex even for FY 2027.

items.quote: And also, on the aluminum price reset or the aluminum price pass-through, we have been very clear with the customers. Where aluminum price pass-through is not there, then we are declining to supply.

items.quote: Frankly speaking, we are focusing on value-added products like casting and machining. We are not interested really to do only the casting portion.

items.quote: For the Bhiwadi plant, it will be at the highest single digit or maybe even double digit, but at the Hosur plant it will be single digit because still it's ramping up.

items.quote: I think when we reach across $1 billion and then we slow down the capex and then it is an smaller portion of the installed capacity, then the margin should improve.

items.quote: I think it will be 2 to 3 years' time. It is also a little sensitive towards aluminum prices, but I would say that at the current aluminum prices, I think 2 to 3 years we should be there.

items.statement: Targeting cost-to-income ratio of 67-68% for FY27

items.statement: Targeting credit cost of 70-80 bps for FY27

items.quote: I would look at anywhere between 1.25% for the portfolio overall put together

items.quote: And if I tell you the latest number, the AUM is INR 2,250 crore. It has grown in line with my overall AUM growth and the gross sales, net sales, SIP book, everything has been reasonably great.

items.statement: FY27 regular capex expected lower than FY26's INR 25 crore, excluding potential Chandon estate acquisition
items.quote: We expect regular capex in FY '2 7 to remain lower than the FY '26 levels as well, excluding the proposed asset purchase agreement with Chandon, which again, Rajeev highlighted we expect to conclude in H1 of FY '27.

items.statement: Quietly optimistic about YoY margin improvement starting FY27 after moderation in FY26
items.quote: I think we've already moderated to a large extent. And I think I'm quietly optimistic that we will start to see now improvement in margins going forward. Of course, that is always dependent on growth.

items.statement: Demand improved across key markets in Q4 FY26; Maharashtra and Karnataka showing visible improvement after corrective actions
items.quote: Encouragingly, our two largest markets, Maharashtra and Karnataka saw visible improvement in demand trends. I'm especially pleased to say that after the corrective action we took earlier in the year, Karnataka now seems to be looking much better moving forward.

items.statement: Elite & premium share grew to 79% of own brands in Q4 FY26 from 75% in Q3; The Source range grew 35% in Q4, 20% for FY26

items.statement: Plans to increase wallet share by 2% annually, adding INR11,000 crore from existing customers and INR4,300 crore from 5.5 lakh new customers over four years
items.quote: In the next four years, we will increase our wallet share with the customer at 2% per annum, and we will disburse through that wallet share increase around INR11,000 crores to these customers.

items.statement: Targets 53% JLG and 47% non-JLG portfolio by 2030, with MSME individual loans at 33%, LAP at 10%, retail secured at 3%
items.quote: By end of 2030, we will have 53% portfolio in JLG loans and around 47% portfolio would be in non-JLG products, which would be MSME, Muthoot Small Enterprise Loans, which is the individual loans, around 33%.

items.statement: Expects further NIM improvement in FY27 as yield changes from H2 FY26 flow through
items.quote: The benefit of that is started coming, but the more benefit will be getting to us in the next financial year. So there is a clear momentum in terms of improvement in revenue.

items.statement: Developed NatCat insurance product to insulate portfolio from climate risks like floods and cyclones
items.quote: We have developed a product which are natural calamity product, insurance product, NatCat, through which we ensure that even if there are floods or cyclone, our portfolio is insulated from there.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 credit cost at 3.5% vs 9.4% in FY25; Q4 credit cost at 2.8%, lowest in seven quarters
items.quote: For the full year we are at 3.5%. But if you look at in the previous year, we were at almost 9.4% full year credit cost. So the credit cost is also now stabilizing with like I highlighted 2.8%.

items.statement: Interest rate risk flagged as key uncertainty; policy rates may rise slightly over next six months from current 5.25%
items.quote: The anticipation is for the next six months the rates might not change much, but the only thing, the risk is that it can increase a little bit.

items.statement: Targets INR1,000 crore profit by FY30 with 5% ROA and 20%+ ROE
items.quote: Yes, your interpretation is correct. Yes.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced to 10.27% from 11% previous year; incremental borrowing cost at 9.9%
items.quote: We were at 11% in the previous year. Currently, we are at 10.27%. And if you look at the incremental cost of borrowing whatever we have borrowed in the last 12-month period, the effective cost is around 9.9%.

items.statement: Target to increase NCD/ECB share of borrowing from 22% to 40% by 2030
items.quote: What we are trying to build is that going forward, we wanted to bring this 22% by 2030 to almost 40%.

items.statement: Credit cost at 2.8% in Q4 and 3.5% for full year, lowest in 7 quarters, down from 9.4% previous year
items.quote: We are at 2.8% in Q4 and for the full year we are at 3.5%. But if you look at in the previous year, we were at almost 9.4% full year credit cost.

items.statement: Added 80,000 new clients in Q4; strategy focuses on existing client deepening and new client acquisition
items.quote: So in Q4, we have brought in another 80,000 clients into the Muthoot Microfin ecosystem.

items.statement: Borrowed INR9,537 crore last financial year; 62 financial institutions; INR700-800 crore free funds; contingency funding of INR2,000-3,000 crore
items.quote: In last financial year, we have borrowed almost INR9,537 crores, and that too in a very difficult market.

items.statement: Diversification improved to 83:17 (microfinance:other) from guided 85:15; individual loans at zero delinquency; gold loan and LAP scaling
items.quote: In terms of our diversification strategy that we were talking 85% to 15%, we are at 83% to 17%.

items.statement: Hybrid underwriting model with 1,800+ credit officers; AI-enabled credit appraisal memo; centralized + decentralized approach
