items.statement: In-house IT team of 100+ professionals; ISO 27001:2022 certified for 3 years; multi-cloud infrastructure; AI/ML ready environment; 10 agentic AI use cases identified
items.quote: We have a strong in-house capability of more than 100-plus people are strong IT professionals are working on our environment.

items.statement: Liquidity risk managed via board-set thresholds, ALCO committee, treasury management, and independent risk evaluation
items.quote: Going forward, the liquidity risk governance process that built enable us to manage all financial obligation and financial requirement at all times without any disruption, even at stress scenarios.

items.statement: Guides 20% AUM CAGR focusing on qualitative, sustainable growth over high-speed expansion
items.quote: So that's why I think we have calibrated, we kept our growth rate at 20%. Yes, even if the guardrails are removed, I think we will continue to follow the same practice

items.quote: We are already at 12% NIM, we are looking at 13.5% to 14% NIM expanding.

items.quote: As of March 31st, we have a total debt of about INR 90 crores. And our investments and cash bank balances are INR 160-odd crores.

items.quote: Employee benefit expenses include certain provisions of approximately INR 14 crores which relate to long -term incentive plan, pending litigations based on external legal advice and higher gratuity and leave encashment obligations arising from policy changes. items.statement: Rajpat Logistics subsidiary expected to add 25% revenue on top of current ~INR400 cr base within 2-3 years
items.quote: I can definitely say that Rajpat will add another 25% from that. Apart from -- growth in the airspace logistics, it will happen.

items.statement: Targeting ROCE of 15%+ from Rajpat Logistics subsidiary business
items.quote: And we are expecting a upward of 15% in return on capital employed from that business, ROCE.

items.statement: Expect rate increases to drive growth more than volume in FY27 due to hardening rates from geopolitical situation
items.quote: What will be -- more rate will be increased more than the volume definitely because the rates are getting hardened.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 profit before tax crossed INR10 cr milestone, up 34% YoY to INR10.30 cr
items.quote: We have achieved the profit -- in fact our profit grew by over 34% year-on-year to INR10.30 crores. Profit before tax is INR10.30 crores.

items.statement: Air freight segment profit increased to INR11.26 cr in FY26 from INR8.53 cr in FY25
items.quote: Accordingly, segment profit, segment air freight division profit increased to INR11.26 crores in FY 2025-26 compared to INR8.53 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: International air freight rates increased ~15% since March 2025 due to geopolitical supply constraints

items.statement: No immediate plans for warehousing or asset-heavy capex; current operations yield higher ROCE than warehouse business
items.quote: Our current operations are giving us more ROCE than if we venture into the warehouse operation. So that is the process going on but never say never.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict causing supply issues and rate hardening, but company maintains momentum with 60+ airline relationships
items.quote: Unfortunately, there is -- supply issues are there. But since we have -- we are operating with more than 60 airlines.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR0.40 per share (30% of PAT) for FY26
items.quote: The Board has also recommended a final dividend of INR0.40 per equity share for 2025-2026. It is basically 30% of our profit after tax.

items.statement: Actively pursuing redevelopment of non-core property with adjacent landowners; meeting scheduled next week to maximize value
items.quote: As early as next week also, we're going to have a meeting for that only. And rest assured, we are actively pursuing that matter.

items.statement: Rajpat Logistics to operate asset-light trucking model for select top corporates with minimal receivables risk
items.quote: We are an asset light company, and we will continue to be an asset light company. So, we will not own any trucks, but we will leverage our network.

items.statement: Expects 10-14% growth in international business for FY27, possibly up to 15%
items.quote: Yes, we expect 10 to 14% growth in our international business this year, as per our current business plan. Last year there was 4% growth, this year we expect 10 to 14%. Maybe even 15%.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR 120 crores, including land acquisition
items.quote: No, it'll be closer INR 120 crores and the reason for that is we're also looking at land.

items.statement: Total announced capex of INR 240 crores over next 18 months (INR 200 crores projects + INR 40 crores land)
items.quote: So I mean, you know, you need to factor all that in that it's a total announcement of 240 crores.

items.statement: Major capacity enhancement projects commissioning from June-July 2026 through Q1 2028; partial benefits from current quarter
items.quote: We expect commissioning of major enhancement projects starting from June -July and continuing through this financial year and beyond up to the first quarter of 2028.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 19.5% from 18.3% driven by structural initiatives
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 19% year-on-year to INR267 crores and margins expanded to 19.5% from 18.3% in this financial year.

items.statement: Targets maintaining EBITDA margin consistently between 18-21% over next five years including industrial business
items.quote: Will it average out to what we have over the next five years? Will it pan out and be in line with our aspirational goal of maintaining profitability consistently between 18% and 21%? Yes.

items.statement: No internal risks identified; well-positioned to navigate external challenges with strong management and owner-driven governance
items.quote: I mean, nothing beyond what other companies or the environment faces , as we don't have any internal risk whatsoever.

items.statement: Domestic business resilient despite global challenges; export demand impacted but international business grew 4% in FY26
items.quote: While export demand was impacted, NRB and its subsidiaries remain more resilient than many of those around us. Our international business did grow over the previous year to a little over 4%.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by over INR 20 crores despite significant sales growth; position considered close to optimal
items.quote: Nevertheless, we believe that there was and will continue to be scope for improvement, and our inventories at the end of the year were in fact lower by over INR20 crores, even though our sales rose significantly.

items.statement: Loan growth guidance raised to 12-14% for FY27 from previous 11-13%
items.quote: The loan growth earlier we had given a guidance of 11 to 13 %, now we are upsizing that to 12 to 14 %.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance raised to 10-12% for FY27 from previous 9-11%
items.quote: Deposit growth guidance for the last year was 9 to 11 %, that we are improving to 10 to 12 %.

items.statement: NIM guidance maintained at 2.75-2.95% for full year FY27
items.quote: The NIM guidance has been 2.75 to 2.95% for the full year.

items.statement: ROA guidance maintained above 1% for FY27
items.quote: ROA, as we always say, the ROA is going to be more than 1 %

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance maintained at 1-1.25% for FY27
items.quote: the slippage ratio we continue to maintain at 1 to 1.25 % considering the geopolitical issue

items.statement: Credit cost guidance set at less than 0.60% for FY27
items.quote: The credit cost for the full year is going to be less than 0.60%.

items.statement: Plan to raise Rs 6,000 crore via AT-1 and Tier 2 bonds in FY27
items.quote: we are going to raise Rs. 6000 crores in the form of AT-1 or Tier 2 in this financial year.

items.statement: Enabling provision for Rs 8,500 crore equity capital raise over 2-3 years up to FY28
items.quote: we have enabling provision of raising almost Rs. 8500 crores of equity capital over a period of 2-3 years. That is still FY28.

items.statement: ECLGS scheme expected to enable Rs 12,000+ crore disbursement to MSMEs
items.quote: Based on the 20% of that, we are expecting Rs. 12,000 plus crores is the impact which you can disperse because of the ECLGS scheme.

items.statement: No immediate impact from West Asia conflict on portfolio; monitoring international book closely
items.quote: As of today, I don't see in terms of number any impact. But we are mindful of any impact that may come because of geopolitical issue directly on the domestic book and also on the international book.

items.statement: Loan growth guidance upsized to 12-14% for FY27 from previous 11-13%.
items.quote: The loan guidance we are upsizing from the earlier guidance of 11 to 13% to 12 to 14% considering our performance.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance upsized to 10-12% for FY27 from previous 9-11%.
items.quote: The deposit growth is from 9 to 11% earlier, it has been upsized to 10 to 12%.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY27 set at 2.75-2.95% accounting for IT refund volatility.
items.quote: The NIM, we achieved 2.89% this quarter, but we are slightly looking at a probable repricing of asset liability while projecting at 2.75 to 2.95 % for the full year.

items.statement: ROA guidance maintained at above 1% for FY27.
items.quote: The ROA continue to have more than 1 % and that is what we had earlier guidance also continue to have the same guidance.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance maintained at 1-1.25% for FY27.
items.quote: The slippage ratio also we still keep it at the same level of 1 to 1.25 %

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained below 0.60% for FY27.
items.quote: and the credit cost below 0.60%.

items.statement: Plan to raise Rs 6,000 cr via AT-1 and Tier 2 bonds in FY27.
items.quote: We have also announced this time that we are going to raise capital in the form of AT-1 and Tier 2 to the extent of Rs. 6,000 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for Rs 8,500 cr equity raise valid till FY28.
items.quote: Earlier, we announced equity raise of almost Rs. 8,500 crores to be as enabling provision to raise FY 2028.

items.statement: ECL final guidelines impact aligned with earlier ~18 bps estimate; quantification after one quarter of implementation.

items.statement: Rs 1,500 cr floating provision created in Q4 FY26 for balance sheet buffering; not linked to ECL.

items.statement: Expects overall business growth of 14-16% for industry and IOB in FY27
items.quote: We do hope that 14 % to 15% to 16% growth for overall industry, not only for IOB, is very much feasible and we can do better than that.

items.quote: Yes, 3.2, I think. Global it is 3.21, domestic it is 3.32. We expect to maintain at this range between 3.30 to 3.35.

items.statement: Plans to front-load entire ECL requirement of ~Rs 3,000 crore by April 2027

items.statement: Targets Rs 3,600 crore recovery from NPAs in FY27

items.statement: Cost of deposits fell to 4.97% in FY26 from 5.08% in FY25

items.quote: Cost to income came down by 220 bps and it stood at 44.94 as of 31st March 2026 when compared to 47.14 as of 31st March 2025.

items.statement: SMA ratio improved to 4.92% in Mar'26 from 6.70% in Mar'25; no West Asia stress seen
items.quote: March '25 our SMA percentage to total credit used to be 6.70 last year. And as in March '26, it came down to 4.92%. So, SMA front is no challenge.

items.statement: RAM (Retail, Agri, MSME) constitutes 83% of domestic advances; will remain priority
items.quote: RAM will be our priority going forward also. Retail, Agri, MSME and why because I will say that we are having 3500 branches almost and they are spread across the geography.

items.statement: ROA guidance for FY27 is >1%
items.quote: Bank can deliver that. That is why we have given it our return on asset more than 1%.

items.statement: PSLC income expected around Rs 3,000 crore in FY27
items.quote: It is 3,000. It will be around 3,000.

items.quote: For the last year the number was 1,204 crores digital transaction. Prior to that that was 940 crores.

items.statement: NIM improved 9 bps QoQ to 2.54% in Q4 FY26; full year NIM 2.51%
items.quote: In this quarter, our NIM improvement was 9 basis point.

items.quote: We had raised because our retail term deposit even after raising was much cheaper than the bulk deposit rate.

items.quote: Total requirement will be 10,000. And it can be staggered to 4 years. And our profit is in the range of 19,000 to 20,000 crores. So, bank is in a very, very good position to absorb the entire in the first go itself.

items.quote: If the need be, if need required, we will go for capital raising. And since it has not moved to the board, once board permissions, then I will share it with you. I think within couple of months, we will share that number with you.

items.statement: Target RAM:Corporate mix of 60:40 (currently 59:41); retail to drive RAM growth
items.quote: We endeavour to reach at 60-40. 59 RAM and 40 corporate.

items.statement: Proposed dividend 210% of paid-up capital (Rs 4.20 per share)
items.quote: We are proposing a dividend of 210 percent of paid up capital and our share face value price is 2. So, the proposed dividend is Rs. 4.20 per share.

items.statement: FY27 performance to improve progressively with meaningful new product scale-up in H2
items.quote: As we look ahead to FY '27, we expect to increasingly benefit from the foundations that have been laid with performance improving progressively as the year unfolds, especially as our new products scale up meaningfully in the second half.

items.statement: Malaysia DP Line 2 operational soon; DS doubling by end FY27; minor debottlenecking in Bangalore
items.quote: The DP has happened. The Line 2 has is getting qualified as we are speaking and will get operational soon. DS, the drug substance doubling will happen towards the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Biosimilars EBITDA margin 26% in Q4 FY26, up from operating leverage and mix
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at ₹720 crores, representing growth of 33% on a year-on-year basis. This translates into an EBITDA margin of 26%.

items.statement: Generics EBITDA margin 8% in Q4 FY26, up ~300bps QoQ on volumes and operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA stood at ₹75 crores. EBITDA margins were at 8% , improved nearly 300 basis points over Q3 of this fiscal, driven by higher volumes and operating leverage.

items.statement: Biosimilars revenue grew 12% YoY in Q4 FY26 to INR2,756 cr; FY26 revenue up 16% YoY like-to-like
items.quote: Biosimilars revenue for Q4 FY '26 stood at ₹2,756 crores, representing a 12% year-on-year increase, driven primarily by advanced markets.

items.statement: Yesintek (ustekinumab) US market share ~20% per IQVIA Feb data; strong formulary placement
items.quote: We've seen tremendous success with our biosimilar ustekinumab, which continues to gain market share. And in fact, if you've seen the IQVIA numbers as of February and the overall market is close to a fifth already.

items.statement: Insulin Aspart (Kirsty) US commercial ramp-up in H2 FY27; 100% share in closed-door networks
items.quote: We're looking to expand that to the commercial play in the second half of this fiscal year '27. So, watch this space, we will keep you posted on how Aspart ramps up in the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Net debt reduced from >$1.5B (Mar'25) to $1.1-1.2B; all free cash flow to debt reduction
items.quote: If you remember in March '25, including structured instruments, we had, in fact, more than $1.5 billion of net debt. That's down to $1.1 billion now. So, it will hover between $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion subject to working capital.

items.statement: Ongoing capex of ~INR1,100 crores to commercialize in H2 FY27, adding 35M meters fabric and 22,000 tons spinning capacity.
items.quote: As regards to the present ongoing capex, the plan is progressing very well. It is expected to commercialize in second half of FY '27.

items.statement: Renewable power capex (75 MW including PPAs) expected operational by H2 FY27; targeting 50-55% of power needs from renewables.
items.quote: The renewable power capex is also progressing as per schedule and expected to be operational in the second half.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 124 bps QoQ to 15.17% on improved realization, efficiency and cost savings.
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 15.17% against previous quarter margin of 13.93% and Q4 '25 margins of 14.30%.

items.statement: Yarn spreads increased from INR110/kg in Q3 to INR120-125/kg currently; fabric prices improving with a lag.
items.quote: The last quarter spreads were about INR110 a kg and now it is about INR125 -- around INR120 to INR125, depending on different counts.

items.statement: Export demand steady at ~100M kg/year; management expects 5-10% incremental international demand from China.
items.quote: We can think about a slight increase, maybe about 5% to 10% going more towards -- because of the increase in demand coming in from China.

items.statement: Domestic and export demand both improved in Q4; FTAs with UK and EU expected to drive strong order inflows and sourcing diversification to India.
items.quote: Already various customers from Europe have started inquiring and planning to diversify their sourcing from India, looking into these FTAs.

items.statement: Revenue expected to grow 30-35% from current levels driven by capex (INR1,000+ cr incremental revenue) and 5-7% price normalization.
items.quote: We expect that we should be -- from here onwards, we should be easily able to add 30% to 35% of our -- to our existing revenue numbers.

items.statement: West Asia conflict increased sea freight 75-80% to Europe and transit time by 2 weeks; most freight passed on via FOB sales.
items.quote: Sea freight cost, there is an increase, especially for the Europe, there is an increase of about 75% to 80% increase in comparison to what was there in the month of February.

items.statement: Industry requesting permanent removal of cotton import duty; government dialogue ongoing but no timeline committed.
items.quote: We have been requesting the Finance Ministry as well as Textile Ministry and Agriculture Ministry to remove the duty for complete forever.

items.statement: Peak total debt expected at INR1,900-2,000 crores post capex; funded via internal accruals and debt at blended cost ~6.5%.
items.quote: Our peak debt -- means our peak debt depends upon our working capital, but our normal total debt, we are expecting to be less than -- in the range of about INR1,900 crores to INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Fabric revenue share 22% (woven ~18%, knitted ~4%); new capex fully integrated for finished fabrics to improve value-added mix.
items.quote: The new expansion is completely integrated. And whatever capacity we are putting on the woven side is also for the finished fabrics.

items.statement: Renewable energy savings expected at INR30-35 crores in FY27 and INR50 crores annually once fully operational.
items.quote: During this year itself, we expect that we will have a saving of around INR30 crores to INR35 crores.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed guidance to double AUM, income and net profit over the next three fiscal years (FY27-FY29).
items.quote: Yes, absolutely. So we last quarter showcased how we are going to do it and this quarter on a full year basis, we have reaffirmed the guidance, so we are sticking with the same guidance for the upcoming three fiscal years.

items.statement: NIM target maintained at 6.5% for FY27 despite achieving 6.83% in FY26.
items.quote: We continue to say that we are going to maintain the same 6.5% sort of a NIM level even in the upcoming financial year as against the 6.83 that we are doing, so our target remains the same and we hope you overachieve the NIM in the upcoming financial year too.

items.statement: Added 427 new touchpoints in Q4 FY26, taking total network to 5,299 across 22 states.
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 427 new touch points, taking our total network to 5,299 touchpoints across 22 states, comprising 422 branches, 3381 distribution points and 1,496 business correspondents.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing moderated to 10.22% in FY26, supporting NIM expansion.
items.quote: At the same time, our cost of borrowing moderated to 10.22%, reflecting continued progress in liability optimization and funding diversification.

items.statement: AUM grew 17% YoY to Rs 61,009 million; disbursements for Q4 FY26 stood at Rs 13,440 million.
items.quote: Our Assets Under Management increased to Rs.61,009 million, registering 17% year-on-year growth, reflecting steady expansion across income generation loan and MSME lending segments. Disbursements for the quarter stood at Rs.13,440 million indicating sustained borrower demand and healthy sourcing momentum.

items.statement: Demand for small-ticket credit remains healthy and broad-based across micro-entrepreneurs and small businesses in Tier-3/4/5 geographies.
items.quote: Demand for small-ticket credit remains healthy and broad-based, supported by working capital needs of micro-entrepreneurs and small businesses, rising economic activity across informal and semi-formal segments and the growing acceptance of formal credit channels even in India's Tier-3, 4, and 5 geographies.

items.statement: No concentrated exposure to exporters affected by Middle East tensions; LCC segment may face some difficulty but Paisalo not impacted.
items.quote: We do not have any large concentrated exposure on any of our borrowers, which are largely dependent on getting proceeds from there. So from that point of view, we are considerably better looking.

items.statement: Completed maiden ECB issuance of USD $15 million; achieved dual AA stable rating.
items.quote: We completed our maiden ECB issuance of USD $15 million, a historic milestone that reflects growing international investor confidence in Paisalo's credit story and opens a new and diversified avenue of long-term funding. We also reinforced our credit standing through dual rating of AA stable.

items.statement: Headcount reduced 3% in FY26 despite AUM growth and branch expansion, indicating productivity gains from AI/tech investments.
items.quote: Despite meaningful expansion in our branch network and strong double-digit AUM growth in FY26, headcount was down 3% during the year, an early but tangible sign that our technology and AI investments are translating into real productivity gains and a more efficient cost structure.

items.statement: Co-lending with SBI: one method expected live in Q1 FY27, second by end of Q1 or early Q2 FY27.
items.quote: One of the methods we are expecting it to get live within this quarter itself while the second process we are awaiting the bank's confirmation on their compliance of the RBI circular. So I am expecting that the second one also should get live in by the end of the quarter one of the new fiscal year or early next quarter

items.statement: Actively scouting for inorganic growth opportunities and partners.
items.quote: Yes, we have that on the plans. We are actively scouting for opportunities and partners to help us in the same.

items.statement: GNPA and NNPA improved to 0.76% and 0.61% respectively in Q4 FY26; collection efficiency at 98.5%.
items.quote: Asset quality remained healthy and stable during the quarter, with GNPA and NNPA improving to 0.76% and 0.61% respectively, underscoring the strength of our underwriting and collection framework.

items.statement: FY27 entered from position of strength with sustained demand, improving funding efficiency, pristine asset quality and robust risk framework.
items.quote: With sustained demand across our core segments, improving funding efficiency, pristine asset quality and a robust risk and operating framework, Paisalo has entered FY27 from a position of strength.

items.statement: Targets maintaining EBITDA margin around 24% for FY27
items.quote: So, we believe that the maintaining of this number, this margin should be achievable.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR 140 crore used to buy rented properties for printing presses and offices
items.quote: Largely with this money is going into buying out the existing properties, what we have rental.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 66 bps to 28% on like-for-like basis excluding election impact
items.quote: EBITDA margin expansion of 66 bps to a robust 28% in FY 2026.

items.statement: Newsprint cost averaged INR 49,000/ton in Q4 FY26, up from INR 48,000/ton in FY25
items.quote: In quarter 4, this number has become INR49,000 and going forward, we believe this number will further go up maybe by 6% to 8% going forward in the quarter 1 itself.

items.statement: Expects newsprint prices to rise 6-8% in Q1 FY27 based on forward orders
items.quote: In the Q1, we believe this should -- this may -- actually not may, this has already gone up by 7%, 8% because we have the forward order with us.

items.statement: April 2026 ad revenue showed double-digit growth; real estate, jewelry, healthcare grew double-digit in FY26

items.statement: Core four apparel brands EBITDA margin at 7.8% in Q4 FY26, targeting double-digits over next two years
items.quote: The core four brands' revenue was INR1,667 crores with an EBITDA margin of 7.8%, which is without these new businesses. So, the core brands are actually quite okay at 7.8% and we will endeavour to take it to double-digits over the next two years' time

items.statement: Premiumization strategy to shift mix toward wool and linen, but rising raw material prices may limit gross margin improvement
items.quote: on the one hand we are going for premiumization, on the other hand raw material prices are up. So, we think overall we should still look at some gross margin improvement, but it may not be humongous because there are tailwinds and there are headwinds both

items.statement: Strategic shift toward premiumization (wool, linen, premium garments) and casualization (smart casuals, polos, denim) across segments
items.quote: For FY '27, our strategic growth pieces include premiumization across all segments, i.e., shift towards wool in suiting; linen in shirting, and more premium category of garments in branded apparel. The second lever that we are going to push is casualization

items.statement: Monitoring US-Iran conflict impact on crude prices (>$100), energy costs, and freight; below-average monsoon (92%) may hit discretionary spending
items.quote: We are closely monitoring from Raymond the US-Iran conflict, which has kept brent crude prices hovering over $100. And leading to increased energy, raw material prices, and freight costs. Domestically, we face the dual challenge of extreme heat waves affecting multiple states and below-average monsoon forecast at 92%,

items.statement: Net working capital improved from 87 to 77 days in FY26, targeting <70 days in FY27 through debtor and inventory management
items.quote: We will also be working on the inventory and we are actually targeting less than 70 days of working capital, sorry, yes, less than 70 days of working capital in the next financial year

items.statement: Plan to add 100 gross EBO stores in FY27, net addition of 30-40 after closing underperforming stores
items.quote: We plan to add a gross of about 100 EBO stores in FY '27; however, we will continue to exit underperforming stores during the year and we think the net increase would be 30 to 40 this year

items.statement: Sleepwear business exited, removing ~INR20 crores annual EBITDA drag
items.quote: It's about INR20 crores was the annual drag. So, that we should get back, but this year to do that we have had to take some provisions

items.statement: Renewable energy target: increase from 5-6% in FY26 to 25% by 2030; Scope 1&2 emissions reduction target 15% by 2030
items.quote: On renewable energy, we are on track to increase our renewable percentage between 5% to 6% this year from our baseline of FY25, and we remain on track to increase this to 25% of our total energy requirement by 2030. items.quote: The segment reported a revenue of INR342 crores in Q4 FY26 as compared to INR248 crores in the same quarter previous year, reflecting a growth of 38% Y-o-Y. items.statement: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 22-25% (3x GDP) and ROA target of 3%+ with mid-to-late teens ROE over 8-10 quarters
items.quote: Our sense is we should be able to grow business at about three times of GDP, so look at anywhere between 22% to 25%, and that's our commitment to the Street on a forward-looking basis unless we see something massive.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost guidance of 2.7-2.8% after FLDG benefit and management overlay
items.quote: And going forward also, we would expect the credit cost to be in the range of 2.7% to 2.8%, that is what is the plan projection.

items.statement: NIM improved 25bps YoY to 9.4% in FY26; further expansion expected as D2C mix rises from 59% to targeted 65%
items.quote: Pertinent to highlight as the mix continues to improve from 59% to targeted 65%, you will see some bit of expansion in NIMs.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds at 8.6% in Q4FY26; overall CoF at 8.5% for FY26; expect to hold 8.5-8.6% in FY27 with shift to 40% fixed-rate borrowings
items.quote: I think we will definitely not see a reduction in the cost of fund, but we will be able to hold on to the numbers that we have demonstrated this year. So, maybe we will not see any further reduction, but I think 8.5% to 8.6% is something we'll be able to hold

items.statement: Household consumption expected to reach $3.4T by 2030 from $2.4T in 2024, creating significant credit opportunities
items.quote: Our sense is that the household consumption is further expected to reach about 3.4 trillion by 2030, creating significant credit opportunities across the consumer consumption ecosystem.

items.statement: D2C business grew 39% YoY to INR 9,800 Cr (59% of AUM); consumer finance at INR 5,000 Cr+, MSME at INR 3,691 Cr (43% YoY), rural at INR 1,009 Cr
items.quote: Our AUM has grown by about 22% on a year-on-year basis and about 10% over the previous quarter to reach INR 16,594 Cr, outpacing the industry, reflecting the sustained momentum and growth driven by direct-to-customer business which now accounts for 59% of our total assets under management.

items.statement: MSME LAP portfolio has 100% registered mortgage; average ticket INR 11-15L; exposure to conflict-affected sectors <2% of book; calibrated growth since Feb 2026
items.quote: So, on the potential conflict, the entire MSME universe, and between gas, petrol, chemicals, pesticide, all of that is less than 2% of our book

items.statement: Rural finance credit cost improved to 1.3% in Q4FY26 from 6.7% in FY25; GNPA at 4bps; 84% MFI book under CGFMU; X-bucket collection 99.6%
items.quote: The credit costs have consistently improved quarter-on-quarter to reach 1.3% in Q4 FY26, with full-year credit cost declining from 6.7% to 4.9% in FY26.

items.statement: Placement volume INR 11,834 Cr in FY26; placement fee income up 22% YoY to INR 31 Cr; credit fund AUM INR 3,092 Cr with INR 38 Cr fees
items.quote: Our placement volume for FY26 was INR11,834 crores, with placement fee income growing by 22% year-on-year to INR31 crores.

items.statement: Added 66 branches (net) in Q4FY26; 17 new MSME branches and 64 rural branches in FY26; rural network now 342 branches
items.quote: We have added 66 branches and merged two branches during the quarter.

items.statement: Net NPA 0.6%, GNPA 1.2% in Q4FY26; Stage-2 assets declined to 1.5% from 2.6% in Sep'25; 100% provision on 90+ DPD unsecured loans
items.quote: GNPA and NNPA improved quarter-on-quarter to 1.2% and 0.6% respectively.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 22.6%; debt-equity improved to 3.1x from 3.9x; tangible net worth INR 3,896 Cr (13% YoY); liquidity surplus INR 1,250 Cr
items.quote: Capital adequacy remains quite strong at 22.6%, well above the regulatory requirement, giving us ample headroom to grow the balance sheet over the next two to three years.

items.statement: Created INR 66 Cr management overlay for macro/geopolitical uncertainty; RBI FLDG clarity in Feb 2026 removed need for extraordinary provisions
items.quote: As a prudent measure, company created a management overlay for potential unforeseen events given the current macroeconomic environment and what we are witnessing in the West Asia.

items.statement: Targeting 1.5 GW generation and 10 GWh BESS commissioning in FY27
items.quote: So we are targeting 1.5 gigawatts of projects in this financial year, right, and around 10 gigawatt hour of battery.

items.statement: Committed total capex of INR12,475 crores including INR6,445 crores incurred and INR6,030 crores purchase orders
items.quote: In terms of capital deployment, we have committed total capex of INR12,475 crores, which includes capex incurred of INR6,445 crores during the year and purchase orders aggregating to INR6,030 crores.

items.statement: Won 301 MW FDRE projects in Q4, under construction portfolio at 5.1 GW, total portfolio 8,071 MW requiring ~17 GWh BESS
items.quote: we won 301 megawatt peak power FDRE projects with SECI during the quarter, expanding our under construction portfolio to 5.1 gigawatts and total portfolio to 8,071 megawatts, which will also require installation of around 17 gigawatt hour BESS.

items.statement: Focus on FDRE/peak power with BESS; plain solar hardest to sell; 10 GWh BESS target alongside 1.5 GW generation
items.quote: Upcoming future operational capacity is expected to have an operating battery portfolio of around 10 gigawatt hour, along with 1.5 gigawatts of contracted generation capacity

items.statement: Secured INR15,000 crores financing for under-construction projects; refinanced INR3,300 crores operational debt at 150 bps lower; WACD 8.4%
items.value: INR15,000 crores new, INR3,300 crores refi
items.quote: During the year, we secured financing of around INR15,000 crores for various under construction projects. And refinanced debt amounting to INR3,300 crores for various operational projects, resulting in reduction of rate of interest of the refinance projects by approximately 150 basis points.

items.statement: Quick commerce contribution margin breakeven targeted in current quarter (Q1 FY27)
items.quote: reiteration of our guidance of achieving breakeven in the current quarter

items.statement: Food Delivery medium-term growth guidance of 18-20% and steady-state EBITDA margin of 5%
items.quote: we have continued to guide two things there. One is a medium-term growth of 18% to 20% and an EBITDA margin of steady state 5%.

items.statement: Quick commerce contribution margin improved ~5.5 percentage points over last year
items.quote: we would have moved it massively by close to 5.5 percentage points over the last year itself

items.statement: Noice private label is contribution margin positive but not margin-maximizing
items.quote: having said that it is margin positive

items.statement: No immediate store additions needed; focus on operating leverage from existing store utilization
items.quote: we don't see the necessity to add stores necessarily over at least the next few quarters considering the current utilization that we have

items.statement: Quick commerce MTU additions may face headwinds from low AOV/low frequency base; focus on retention and repeat
items.quote: our MTU will still face slight headwinds on the base that are low AOV and low frequency

items.statement: Differentiation strategy via private labels (Noice) and brand partnerships (Triply) to upgrade assortment across categories
items.quote: You will, actually, in the next couple of months, see a host of such examples pop up across the Instamart app

items.statement: SNACC operations shut down in Q4 FY26; closure costs impacted platform innovation P&L
items.quote: this was the quarter that we also shut down SNACC operations. A large part of the cost that you see in that P&L is related to the SNACC operations getting closed.

items.statement: Expect to achieve contribution margin breakeven in Q1 FY26 (April-June quarter)
items.quote: And now that April is behind us, we are pretty confident of being able to achieve that.

items.statement: Exited March at 110 bps contribution margin vs 180 bps quarterly average; Q1 FY26 breakeven implies ~100 bps improvement from March exit rate
items.quote: while 180 basis points was the average for the quarter, we exited the month of March with 110 basis points.

items.statement: Top city already at 3% positive contribution margin and EBITDA breakeven at city level
items.quote: our top city, for example, is already operating at 3% positive CM. And at the city level, it's already breaking even at an EBITDA level.

items.statement: EBITDA profitability timeline withdrawn; will be a choice made later depending on market forces
items.quote: I think EBITDA profitability will be a choice that will be made at a later point in time and again, depending on how the market forces play out.

items.statement: Capex to significantly come down from last couple of years as warehousing expansion phase largely behind
items.quote: we expect the capex numbers to significantly come down from the last couple of years.

items.statement: Recent capex of ~INR195 cr/quarter largely on warehousing for Tier 2 markets to reduce middle mile and improve serviceability
items.quote: Largely on the warehousing investment. As we have overall increased the geographical footprint, there are these Tier 2 markets where we see the need to open warehousing.

items.statement: MTU net additions slowed to 0.5M/quarter due to deliberate churn of low-AOV users; expect healthy MTU movement after 2 more quarters of churn
items.quote: a large part of that user growth reduction that you have seen is the users that we have deliberately churned out from the platform.

items.statement: Non-grocery share in quick commerce near 30%, targeting 30-40% range to retain high-frequency benefits
items.quote: We hit the early 30s. We expect this number to be somewhere in the range of 30%-40%.

items.statement: Stopped No Fee experiment in third week of January; roughly half of NOV/GOV improvement from that, rest from structural reduction in consumer incentives
items.quote: we stopped the No Fee experiment sometime around the third week of January. So that gain came through. So roughly half of the gain came through because we stopped the No Fee experiment.

items.statement: Take rate up 50 bps QoQ on GOV basis; NOV take rate flat at 19.2% due to consumer-side monetization (less incentives, delivery fees) and halving low-AOV order mix
items.quote: it's 50 basis points pickup if you look at our take rate, Vivek.

items.statement: Marketing spend elevated at ~INR700-715 cr/quarter due to competitive intensity from 6-7 players; hard to estimate when it will drift down
items.quote: It's going to be extremely hard to guesstimate that, where does the market structure evolve, how competitive does it get before it settles down.

items.statement: LPG crisis in early March caused <0.5% price increase on platform; navigated via analytics, demand spreading, and supply configuration; situation easing
items.quote: We can see that on our platform, which is not significant and it's less than 0.5%.

items.statement: Quick commerce mid-term NOV target INR1 lakh crore in 3-6 years; growth to come from frequency recovery, NOV/user increase, and user acquisition acceleration after churn phase
items.quote: the guidance is for INR1 lakh crore in NOV in probably 3 to 6 years.

items.statement: Cash from operations remains negative (~$400M annualized) due to heightened capex (now moderating) and cyclical working capital changes; expect sequential improvement
items.quote: Some of the working capital changes are cyclical, and you should expect us to sequentially improve that in the coming year.

items.statement: Targeting similar revenue growth in FY27 as FY26's 87% increase
items.quote: we saw the scale that we had last year and we're targeting the same kind of growth this year as well on our revenue moving forward

items.statement: FY27 revenue split guided at 50% aerospace & defense, 50% non-aerospace & defense
items.quote: The breakup in the split of revenue, I would say is 50% aerospace and defense and 50% non-aerospace and defense for the year '26-'27

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 17-22% for FY27 with improvement expected
items.quote: I've always said the margins will be between 17% to 22%. We are definitely going to show an increased margin this financial year

items.statement: Strategic agreements of ~INR3,000 crores and confirmed POs of ~INR715 crores as of date
items.quote: Today, our revenue visibility is stronger than at any point in the company's history, supported by strategic agreements aggregating approximately INR3,000 crores. As on date, the company's total order bookings stand at around INR715 crores of confirmed POs

items.statement: Received orders aggregating ~INR570 crores during FY26
items.quote: during the year, we received orders aggregating approximately INR570 crores, further strengthening execution visibility

items.statement: Space and semiconductor segments targeting 300-400% revenue growth in FY27 vs FY26
items.quote: for both the space and the semiconductor this year we're looking at a significant growth. We're looking at close to a 300% to 400% growth on our revenue from the previous year

items.statement: Leasing additional 210,000 sq ft facility near existing operations for space and semiconductor programs
items.quote: we have taken a strategic decision to lease an additional facility of approximately 210,000 square feet in close proximity to our existing operations instead of constructing a new facility

items.statement: FY27 delivery target of roughly 5.5 million sq ft
items.quote: We have a target of delivering roughly 5.5 million square feet in FY '27.

items.statement: FY27 launch sales target of 20-25% at launch, expecting INR 1,800-2,000 crores from new launches
items.quote: We plan to achieve, as we do in all our launches, approximately 20%,-25% sales at launch and that is the target we have for this year also.

items.statement: Net debt to equity ratio will be lower than 2x in FY27, absolute net debt not to exceed March 2026 level of INR 8,100 crores
items.quote: However, we would attempt to reduce it marginally at the absolute level, but not substantially. So, our debt-to-equity ratio for FY'27, we will be, of course, issuing a proper guidance a little later, but it will be lower than 2x for sure.

items.statement: Refinanced INR 3,500 crores debt since listing, achieving 120 bps reduction in blended cost of debt and INR 125 crores annualized savings
items.quote: Since our listing, we have leveraged our strength and strengthened our market position to refinance approximately INR 3,500 crores of debt. These results are tangible. We have achieved an interest rate delta of 3.5% of these facilities, leading to a 120 basis points drop in our overall blended cost of debt, total debt.

items.statement: Plan to refinance another INR 1,300 crores in coming quarter
items.quote: We expect to refinance another around INR 1,300 crores in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Total future inflows across portfolio approximately INR 57,000 crores including ongoing projects (INR 27,000 crores) and ready-to-move/forthcoming launches (INR 30,000 crores)
items.quote: In addition, our ready-to-move-in projects and forthcoming launches together add approximately INR 30,000 crores, so total future inflows across the portfolio is about INR 57,000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin 30%, Q4 margin 36%; new project margins 20-25% at revenue level, 25-30% cash flow level
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 1,022 crores, reflecting a 30% margin.

items.statement: Robust walk-ins and conversions in April 2026 despite geopolitical concerns; Worli project sold INR 400 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Till now, our walk-ins have been robust in April also. As the lifecycle of our projects are at maturity and mid-level, we are seeing a good robust walk-ins yet and conversion, we do not see an issue till now.

items.statement: Construction cost escalation 2-4% but manageable given sales value; geopolitical situation being monitored
items.quote: The construction costs have increased, but it is 2% to 4% of the construction cost and it should not have an impact on us looking at the total value of sales.

items.statement: Unsold inventory in ongoing projects INR 22,000 crores; expected to monetize over 4-6 years with new launches adding INR 7,000-8,000 crores annually
items.quote: So, what will happen, it is always an overlapping situation. This Rs. 22,000 cr inventory will get added by around INR 7,000 crores to INR 8,000 crores during the year itself. So, that will take it to around INR 30,000 crores. So, this entire INR 30,000 crores will get liquidated, most part of it, over a period of next

items.statement: Cash balance INR 1,062 crores as of March 2026, less than 20% locked in RERA accounts
items.quote: Today our cash balance as of March'26 has been around INR 1062 crores. Out of which not more than 20% is locked into the RERA account.

items.statement: Expects steady-state EBITDA margins of 15-16% going forward
items.quote: So going forward, if you say, we expect our EBITDA to be similar to around 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Committed INR39.53 crore via purchase orders for greenfield expansion as of March 2026
items.quote: As of the end of this March, we have already committed INR39.53 crores via purchase orders of our greenfield expansion project.

items.statement: Total capex for new 35,000 MT facility is INR76 crore excluding land
items.quote: So the total capex for the new capacity is about INR76 crores and this is without the land.

items.statement: Trial production at new Vizianagaram plant expected Nov-Dec FY27, commercial production from Q4 FY27
items.quote: So, we look at commencing with trial productions in November or December of FY27 and commercial production from Q4 of FY27.

items.statement: Targets 15% capacity utilization at new plant in FY27, 65-70% in FY28, 85-90% thereafter
items.quote: So I think we should look at somewhere around 15% of capacity utilization in FY27. Then in FY28, we are looking at 65% to 70% of capacity utilization and then reaching at 85%-90% utilization rate by the next fiscal.

items.statement: New plant peak revenue potential INR475 crore at 85% utilization; existing plant expects 20-22% revenue growth
items.quote: So, our peak would be about INR475 crores at a 85% utilization rate.

items.statement: 78% revenue from repeat institutional customers; unable to onboard new customers due to capacity constraints
items.quote: However, I would like to share that our revenue is -- repeat revenue is coming nearly 78% from our existing customers, which highlights that there is a very high demand for our product in the market and we are not able to cater to new customers.

items.statement: H2 FY26 margin compression due to RCN price spike, forex (~10.5% depreciation), and shipping disruptions
items.quote: While H2 saw some margins compression due to a spike in raw cashew nuts prices, forex, and global shipping disruptions, we maintained a double-digit EBITDA margin for the full year.

items.statement: Initiating currency hedging and longer-term shipping contracts to mitigate forex and freight cost risks
items.quote: We are already talking to the banks for the hedging mechanism so that we can hedge some currency risk. And then we are already talking to the shipping lines to do some longer-term contracts so that we can also hedge some of our shipping cost.

items.statement: Whole kernel recovery improved to 70:30 (wholes:pieces) after technology upgrade in Nov 2023
items.quote: Yes, so our wholes recovery as compared to pieces recovery is now at about 70:30. 70 being wholes and 30 being pieces.

items.statement: No firm orders for new capacity yet; institutional customers give only 1-3 month visibility
items.quote: So, actually we don't have any existing orders because these institutional customers, they give you visibility only for -- the visibility ranges from one month to sometimes three months, so we are still away from that period.

items.statement: Royal Mewa brand grew 6.5x in FY26; marketing focus on digital/social media without compromising margins
items.quote: Furthermore, our brand Royal Mewa is no longer just a pilot project. It grew over 6.5 times this year.

items.statement: IPO raised INR74.45 crore; INR57 crore allocated to new facility, INR10.42 crore to general corporate purposes
items.quote: Our successful IPO through which we raised INR74.45 crores is being primarily utilized towards setting up of our second processing facility in Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh.

items.statement: Expects historical revenue growth rates to continue in FY2027; no specific revenue guidance provided
items.quote: We do not have specific revenue guidance at this point in time, but we expect that our historical revenue growth rates are a good indication of where we should be growing in the next year as well.

items.statement: License-driven revenue to grow from 3% to 20% of total revenue by 2030, driving gross margin expansion
items.quote: We want to take that license driven revenue from 3% to 20% by 2030, and which will be quite significant in terms of also margin expansion.

items.statement: Output/outcome pricing carries 5-7pp higher gross margin vs input-driven; license pricing carries 25-30pp higher
items.quote: there is a 5- to 7-point difference between input-driven pricing versus output-driven, outcome-driven pricing. 5- to 7-point of additional gross margin are there in output and outcome compared to input and there is a 25-to-30-point difference between that and the license-driven gross margin.

items.statement: R&D investment increased 48% YoY to INR 212 crore in FY2026 (4.1% of revenue expensed); total R&D spend 6.4% of revenue
items.quote: In FY2026, we spent INR 212 crore on R&D investments, 48% higher than the previous year. Out of this INR 212 crore, INR 134 crore, or 4.1% of the revenue, was expensed in the P&L.

items.statement: Qure.ai now has a phenomenal order pipeline and very strong order book as of April 2026, expected to recover and exceed prior performance
items.quote: And today, as of April 2026, Qure is sitting on a phenomenal order pipeline and a very, very strong order book. They are not just going to recover from all the setbacks from the last year, but do even better than that.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 93bps YoY in FY2026 driven by mix shift to output-based contracts, price increases, productivity (+218bps) and weaker rupee (+179bps), offset by merit increases (-304bps)
items.quote: Gross margin for the FY2026 expanded by 93 bps year-over-year to 46.8%. Again, three drivers: First, 218 bps from change in mix of engagement moving more towards output-based contracts, price increases, and productivity improvements. Second, 179 bps from weaker rupee. Third, 304 bps of negative impact from annual merit

items.statement: Q4 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 22.1% (+189bps YoY); FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 17.6% (+20bps YoY) despite 96bps SG&A increase from growth investments
items.quote: For the FY2026 adjusted EBITDA was 17.6% versus 17.4% in the previous year. While our gross margin expanded by 93 bps, growth investments in relationship management for key clients and opening new offices led to 96 bps uptick in SG&A as a percentage of revenue versus the previous year.

items.statement: Repaid long-term debt in April 2026 using IPO proceeds (INR 957 crore); company is now debt-free with INR 2,052 crore cash
items.quote: In April, we used these proceeds to repay our long-term debt as we had committed at the time of the offering. Fractal is now debt free.

items.statement: Net revenue retention 117% for FY2026 (112% in Q4); NPS 78 for year (81 in Q4); 59 clients with $1M+ revenue vs 53 prior year
items.quote: Net revenue retention at 117% for the year and 112% for Q4. Our clients are not just buying more from us, they are positioning us as central to their AI transformation.

items.statement: Expects 25-30% same-store sales growth (SSG) for FY27, driven by existing SIS stores and new EBOs.
items.quote: I am expecting 25% to 30%, but if gold prices shoot up just like last year, it again can match with the previous year's SSG growth.

items.statement: Expects top-line revenue growth of 25-30% for FY27, primarily driven by SIS SSG and new store additions.
items.quote: I expect top-line growth also to get maintained around 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Plans to open 15 new EBOs over 24 months using IPO proceeds; 1 store already opened, 6-7 in FY27, remaining in FY28.
items.quote: Out of these 14, 6 to 7 will take place in current financial year and remaining will be in next financial year. Because we have mentioned in DRHP, RHP prospectus that this is a project for 24 months' period.

items.statement: EBO capex estimated at INR20-25 crores per store; INR287 crores from IPO proceeds earmarked for store expansion and working capital.
items.quote: When it's a EBO which we are setting, it requires around INR20 crores to INR25 crores per EBO. So that expansion will have better numbers at lower capex.

items.statement: No order book disclosed; business is B2C retail with no order backlog.
items.quote: We are doing exclusively diamond jewellery only. We have got no mix of the plain gold jewellery or anything.

items.statement: Sees structural demand tailwinds: rising incomes, urbanization, shift to organized/branded jewellery, and growing diamond acceptance across occasions.
items.quote: Backed by these favourable tailwinds along with our differential business model, strong parentage, and scalable retail strategy, we believe PNGS Reva is well-positioned to capitalize on this opportunity and deliver sustainable long-term growth.

items.statement: Product mix: 60-70% lower ticket (entry/everyday), 20-25% medium, 10-12% high-ticket bridal/occasion wear. Average bill size INR1.2 lakhs in FY26 (up 41% YoY).
items.quote: As far as current year ending for which we are referring the results, that is FY26, the average bill size value or average order value is INR1,20,000. Y-o-Y growth is 41%.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds not seen as long-term threat due to lack of resale value; natural diamonds viewed as wealth/inheritance assets.
items.quote: So with our buyback policy, natural diamond has got rarity and increasing value over a period, so I am not thinking that is a threat for me.

items.statement: No equity dilution expected for next 2-3 years; growth funded via internal accruals (INR64 cr added this year) and existing debt headroom (INR150-200 cr unused sanctions).
items.quote: I don't primarily expect any dilution of the equity, but after getting settled by 2030, I will be expanding out of the borrowings in future.

items.statement: Inventory turnover at 1.31x in FY26; expected to stabilize at 1.25-1.35x despite new EBO additions due to SIS SSG offset.
items.quote: Hardly, this means this is 1.31, if that were the case, it would fall between 1.25 and 1.35.

items.statement: Marketing spend ~3-4% of top-line annually; INR2 cr per new EBO spread over 12-18 months for BTL/ATL/social media.
items.quote: And brand as such we will be spending around 3% to 4% every year on the top-line.

items.statement: Gold price increases may compress gross margin % but absolute margin rupees maintained; no hedging due to high MCX cost, relies on natural hedging (same-day cover) and surplus gold recycling.
items.quote: Gross margin percentage basis it may contract, but in absolute value, it will get maintained. And as a person, I more believe in the absolute value rather than percentage.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 18.5-20% with sequential quarterly improvement, H2 stronger
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY '27, supported by our ramp-up of new launches and investments that we've made across our manufacturing facilities and ongoing expense optimization initiatives.
