items.quote: So we believe that there will be double -digit growth in top line in Crop Protection segment, which will have a better profitability going forward than quarter 4.

items.statement: FY27 Pigments revenue guided at INR500-600 crore with EBITDA margin much better than 3.3%
items.quote: So this segment would be in the range of -- in the top line point of view, it will be in the range of somewhere INR500 crores to INR600 crores. But from the profitability, which was in the last financial year, we were in the range of 3.3% from EBITDA point of view. We see this year it will be much better than the last

items.statement: FY27 dividend planned with Board approval based on better revenue and profitability
items.quote: In FY 27, we believe that we will have better revenue and better profitability. And based on that, in this financial year, FY27, with the Board approval, we'll try to provide a reasonably good dividend to the investors.

items.statement: FY27 capex limited to routine INR35-40 crore, no significant capex
items.quote: So as far as the capex is concerned, there won't be any significant capex in the current financial year. Only the routine capex to the tune of about INR35 crores to INR40 crores will be there.

items.statement: Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc approved; commercial production starts Kharif season at Sanand with no new capex
items.quote: Commercial production of these products are expected to commence during the Kharif season this year.

items.statement: TiO2 plant suspended due to sulphuric acid >INR30/kg (was <INR5) and high utility costs; awaiting DGTR anti-dumping decision in 1-2 months
items.quote: Currently, the sulphuric acid price is more than INR30 per kg, which used to be below INR10. In fact, in the normal time, it used to be below INR 5.

items.statement: Geopolitical war (US-Iran) caused raw material cost spike; sulphur/sulphuric acid prices uncontrolled until Strait of Hormuz reopens
items.quote: We believe that -- let's hope the war ends very soon, Strait of Hormuz opens up very fast, and that will bring down the sulphur and sulphuric acid price to the reasonable levels.

items.statement: FY26 standalone EBITDA grew 27% YoY to INR228.7 crore; consolidated EBITDA margin 8.1% vs 6.9%
items.quote: In FY26, on standalone basis, revenue stood at INR 2,091 crores, up by 4% Y -o-Y, and our EBITDA grew by 27% Y-o-Y to INR228.7 crores.

items.statement: Crop Nutrition segment expects significant top-line and bottom-line growth over next 2-5 years with better profitability
items.quote: And going forward for the next 2 to 5 years period, we see significant growth happening in the Nutrition segment with better profitability.

items.statement: FY26 debt repaid ~INR160 crore; standalone debt INR528 crore (0.30x D/E), consolidated INR722 crore (0.47x D/E)
items.quote: In FY26, we have made a debt repayment of approximately INR160 crores.

items.statement: Amalgamation of Kilburn Chemicals and Meghmani Crop Nutrition filed; voting on June 6 for operational/financial synergies
items.quote: The scheme of amalgamation which we have filed and the Court has already directed to have the voting on June 6.

items.statement: Ended FY2026 with Rs.2,000 Cr order book; all fixed-fee models, no transaction-fee contracts; includes marquee wins from SBI, ICICI, HDFC securing 85% of FY2027 target
items.quote: We end FY2026 with a solid order book, not only from size, which is Rs. 2,000 Crores, but even if we say so, it is high quality wins. None of these deals is linked to any transaction fee linked contract. All of them are fixed fee models.

items.statement: FY2026 capex Rs.350 Cr (up from Rs.100 Cr in FY24/25); includes tech investment Rs.40 Cr (1.6% of revenue) and Rs.15 Cr in gig delivery model
items.quote: In FY2026, in the middle of the storm, we upped our capex spend significantly to drive higher growth in the coming years, and we have invested Rs.350 Crores of capex in FY2026.

items.statement: Q4 FY2026 EBITDA margin improved 280 bps QoQ to 19% EBIT margin; full-year FY2026 EBIT margin contracted 360 bps to 15.6%; targeting 25% EBITDA margin in FY2027
items.quote: Overall EBIT margins in Q4 have gone from last year Q4 was 22.6%, they dipped to 15% in Q3 and have come back up to 19% in Q4 of this year. For the full year EBIT margins for FY2026, they have contracted by 360 bps from 19.2% to 15.6%.

items.statement: Seeing banks shift from cash dispensers to recyclers (cash acceptance, video KYC, card issuance); 6,000-7,000 ATMs in RFP pipeline mostly fixed-price or product purchase; consumption weakness risk Rs.50-70 Cr if currency supply dip persists
items.quote: In FY2027, we know the 6,000 to 7,000 units that we see in different stages of bank RFP pipeline planning are mostly all either product purchase and with subsequent services outsourcing or will be a fixed price outsourcing deals.

items.statement: Board approved Rs.168 Cr buyback (~3% equity) at Rs.340/share; post-buyback cash balance Rs.650 Cr retained for growth; CEO not participating
items.quote: With clarity on our capital needs and our cash balance of Rs. 650 Crores, the board has approved Rs. 168 Crores buyback, roughly 3% of our outstanding equity shares, at Rs.340 price point.

items.statement: FSS acquisition to close end of Q1 FY2027; will consolidate managed services (move from #5 to #3), enable cross-sell to mid-sized private banks, shift contracts to fixed-fee; Securens acquisition closed and accretive in FY2027
items.quote: In Q4, we signed our contract deal with FSS for the managed services business. This not only helps us consolidate the managed services segment, but more importantly for CMS, it allows us an entry into midsized private banks for cross-selling.

items.statement: Targeting 13-14% services revenue CAGR over next 4 years (vs 12% past 4 years); three platforms target Rs.20,000 Cr TAM; Q1 FY2027 revenue run-rate target Rs.650 Cr
items.quote: Over the next four years, we see our opportunity to accelerate this growth to a 13% to 14% CAGR, which is more in line with our historical growth of 15% CAGR.

items.statement: Guided for 20-25% EBITDA margin
items.quote: we are guiding for a 20% to 25% EBITDA margin

items.statement: Executable order book stands at INR 697 crores as of 31 March 2026
items.quote: our executable order book as of 31 March , 2026 stands at approximately INR 697 crores

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin was around 30%
items.quote: this quarter, we had done around 30% EBITDA margin

items.statement: Kavach opportunity is large, long-duration and strategically important
items.quote: The Kavach opportunity is large, long -duration and strategically important for us

items.statement: Railway payments are well streamlined with no bad debt risk, just cycle timing
items.quote: railway payments are very well streamlined. There is absolutely no issue in railway payments. It's just a cycle and a process

items.statement: Order execution cycle typically 18-24 months, aiming to maintain similar growth trajectory
items.quote: typically, what we have seen is until now, we have seen an 18 to 24 month order execution cycle

items.statement: Zero-emission mobility is a strong pillar with active traction in NTPC and other inquiries
items.quote: Zero-emission mobility is a very strong pillar of this strategy because it can significantly improve overall energy efficiency

items.statement: Mainboard migration in process, no specific timeline given
items.quote: we are in the process. It's just a matter of -- very difficult to give a timeline to it. But we have already been on the journey

items.statement: Semiconductor project substructure work to start July 2026; production in 24-30 months from July
items.quote: Our target is to start the substructure work from July. And broadly, it should 24 to 30 months from that time.

items.statement: Logistics cost impact INR14-15 crores in Q4; transport cost up INR100-120/ton in Feb, INR200-220/ton by March
items.quote: On a weighted average basis across the quarter, probably around INR14 crores to INR15 crores was the impact because of the higher logistics cost.

items.statement: Industrial salt volume 1.1M tons in Q4 (-7.2% YoY) impacted by 120k tons customer deferrals and 250k tons logistics issues; full year 4.2M tons (+22% YoY)
items.quote: Volumes were impacted by nearly 120,000 tons due to customer deferrals on account of the US-Iran conflict and around 250,000 tons of shipments we could not complete because of the logistics issues.

items.statement: Idealis Mudchemie: Gujarat plant production-ready awaiting approvals; Nagri plant redefining product roadmap; expect lean H1, ramp in H2 FY27
items.quote: We expect to have a fairly lean first half of this year in terms of Idealis Mudchemie, but we expect that the second half will start getting to a larger ramp.

items.statement: SOP plant reengineering underway; plant trials expected Q1 FY27, higher production H2 FY27
items.quote: This program is currently underway, and we expect to complete plant trials in the first quarter of this year and go into a higher level of production in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Standalone cash INR37 crores, consolidated INR55 crores as of March 31, 2026
items.value: INR37 crores standalone, INR55 crores consolidated
items.quote: Yes, just stand-alone cash, cash equivalent bank balances, INR37 crores and consolidated is INR55 crores.

items.statement: Three strategic priorities: consolidate core salt/bromine, scale derivatives/oilfield/SOP, invest in advanced materials (batteries/semiconductors)
items.quote: As we look forward, I think we have established three clear strategic priorities for the company. The first one is to consolidate the core salt and bromine business. Secondly, to scale up our derivatives, oilfield and SOP businesses...

items.statement: OSAT revenue expected at INR250-300 crores and PCB at INR300-400 crores in FY27, first year of operations.
items.quote: I'm sure and certain we will do a good number of PCB of around INR300 crores to INR400 crores, and OSAT of around INR250 crores to INR300 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated order book remains strong at over INR9,000 crores, diversified and non-cancellable.
items.quote: Our order book continues to be stronger at INR9,000 crores plus.

items.statement: Railway Kavach margins expected north of 30%, higher than current consolidated margins.
items.quote: And the margins are going to be north of current 30% plus.

items.statement: Targeting 30% of total revenue from new product development (NPD) and value-added solutions in coming years.
items.quote: Our goal is to steadily increase the contribution of NPD-led and value-added solutions to nearly 30% of the total revenue in the coming years.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions (West Asia conflict) caused last-minute customer deferments and supply chain delays, impacting near-term revenue recognition.
items.quote: Near-term top line performance did not fully meet market expectations, primarily due to geopolitical disruption, especially the West Asia conflict, which led to last-minute customer deferment, supply chain delays and product timing shift.

items.statement: Core EMS working capital days improved significantly from 83 days (FY24) to 53 days (FY26); standalone EMS cash flow turned positive INR250 crores vs INR65 crores prior year.
items.quote: On a like-to-like basis, we would like to bring it to your attention that the core EMS business has demonstrated a significant improvement in the efficiency as committed earlier with the working capital days reducing from 83 days in FY '24 to 53 days in FY '26.

items.statement: EV segment grew 28% in FY26 despite largest 2-wheeler customer dropping 90% volume; new product launches underway.
items.quote: You can see our growth in the EV segment this year is about 28% growth despite the fact that one of our largest customers in 2-wheelers has dropped the production significantly by about 90%.

items.statement: OSAT order visibility over INR25,000 million for next 5 years; PCB demand pipeline robust with customers requesting additional capacity.
items.quote: In OSAT, the order outlook for both the current year and the medium term remains strong with revenue visibility of over INR25,000 million over the next 5 years.

items.statement: FY27 net square feet addition target at least 20% above FY26 (~100,000 sq ft)
items.quote: But at least for now, we should be able to expect at least 20% more than last year's square feet addition.

items.statement: FY27 SSSG expected similar to slightly better than FY26's 3%
items.quote: So, we do anticipate a similar to a little bit better SSSG numbers than we've achieved this year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected to exceed FY26's 13.1%
items.quote: But broadly, if I have to give you, it should be more than the guidance that more than what we achieved last year '25-'26.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target 17.5%-18% vs FY26 15.76%
items.quote: And our target, with the plan of action on expansion and Varamahalakshmi format it should be possible that we should at least be in the 17.5% to 18% range this year.

items.statement: FY27 store expansion focused on Karnataka (Kalamandir) and Andhra/Tamil Nadu (Varamahalakshmi Skills), ~60-40 split Kalamandir:Varamahalakshmi
items.quote: Broadly, I think we should implement approximately in the range of 60-40 between Kalamandir and Varamahalakshmi format this year.

items.statement: Gross margin maintained at ~42% despite new formats; FY27 target to hold gross margin
items.quote: One of the top high priority KPIs for us is to maintain the gross margin irrespective of the fact we are coming with the newer formats and lesser gross margin stores.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin impacted by ~INR4 cr bonus (2 bps) and ad spend timing; FY27 EBITDA expected at full-year FY26 level +50 bps
items.quote: Otherwise, we should be able to expect a decent EBITDA about the full year EBITDA plus at least 50 basis points in the next year.

items.statement: Wedding calendar FY27 has 5-10% more dates than FY26, spread across quarters
items.quote: I think in terms of the absolute number, we have around extra days than compared to last year. So yes, I think more than 5% to 10% of extra dates is what we have compared to last year.

items.statement: Varamahalakshmi + Valli formats drove FY26 growth; Varamahalakshmi now 52% of sales
items.quote: 52% of the overall thing. So, the component of Varamahalakshmi is increasing in the overall pie.

items.statement: KLM format declined ~3% in FY26; 9,000 sq ft reduced for margin improvement; revival plan underway
items.quote: So, KLM, I think the decline has been around low-single-digit, about 3% or so is the overall decline for KLM format.

items.statement: Company debt-free; internal accruals sufficient for FY27 expansion and next 2-3 years; no borrowing planned
items.quote: Since the company is totally debt-free and the company has enough resources for completing the entire expansion with the internal generation, there will not be any further borrowings this year.

items.statement: Inventory per sq ft reduced from INR11,533 to INR10,480; continuous optimization balanced with sales
items.quote: We have reduced the inventory per square feet by around INR1,000. What was around INR11,533 has come down to INR10,480 or so.

items.statement: Store payback: Varamahalakshmi 8-9 months; maturity to avg EBITDA margin 1.5-2 years; Kalamandir slightly longer
items.quote: Varamahalakshmi format will give a payback within 8 to 9 months, whereas to reach the EBITDA margins to get the store mature, it will be approximately 1.5 years to 2 years.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 18-20% with quarterly order inflows of INR450-500 crore
items.quote: We've targeted around 18% to 20% growth. So in similar fashion, our quarterly revenue will be increasing in that fashion. And our order booking will be also growing in the similar speed of around INR450 crores to INR500 crores every quarter.

items.statement: Order book of INR1,514 crore as of March 2026, 63% exports, 37% domestic
items.quote: As of 31st March, 2026, our order book stood at INR1,514 crores, providing strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters of this approximately 63% is from exports and 37% from the domestic market.

items.statement: New Kandla facility on 7 acres near port, commissioning in 9-10 months for ultra-large tanks up to 500 tons
items.quote: We have acquired approximately 7 acres of land near the Kandla Port on a 30-year lease basis, the facility is expected to be commissioned within approximately 9 to 10 months.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 23.8%, within guided 21-24% range; margins vary quarterly due to product mix
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin is 23.8% for FY '26, remained in line with or better than the guidance provided earlier, demonstrating disciplined execution despite headwind arising from the U.S. tariffs.

items.statement: Strong demand across geographies; primary constraint is logistics/supply chain, not market slowdown
items.quote: The key takeaway is that demand fundamentals remain robust across the geographies. The primary constraint continued to be logistics and supply chain related challenges rather than the slowdown in the market demand.

items.statement: Project orders now >60% of order book vs 30% earlier; standard products growing slower
items.quote: My product mix is changing. My standard tanks is reducing, and my non-standard orders are increasing. If you see earlier, it was just 30% project orders. Now we have more than 60% project orders in our order book.

items.statement: Expect INR1,200 crore of current INR1,514 crore order book to execute in FY27
items.quote: Order book of or pending order of around INR1,514 crores. So out of that, at least INR1,200 crores will be executed this year.

items.statement: Expecting more high-value aerospace orders in Q1-Q2 FY27 similar to INR200 crore Q4 order
items.quote: We are expecting more high value orders in Q1 FY '27. This order is a direct outcome of our proven execution capabilities and reinforces the growing confidence that global aerospace players have in INOX India's engineering expertise.

items.statement: LNG storage demand increasing due to Qatar supply disruption; need for standby tanks at fueling stations
items.quote: People are asking for at least 2 tanks, 1 standby tank for their consumption so there is no stock out. Because these stations are directly connected with people.

items.statement: Chinese LNG tank imports blocked by PESO regulations; no Chinese shop has PESO approval
items.quote: There is a regulation in India called as a PESO, which governs the incoming flow of such tanks. And there is no shop in China, which is approved by PESO as of today.

items.statement: ITER repeat orders expected INR50-60 crore annually for next 5+ years
items.quote: So on an average, going forward, at least INR50 crores to INR60 crores we should get on a regular basis for next at least 5 years.

items.statement: Data center liquid nitrogen cooling MoU with European OEM; R&D stage, 6-12 months for prototype
items.quote: We have signed an MoU with European company to jointly develop liquid nitrogen-based cooling solution for the data center. This is currently an early-stage R&D led initiative and we expect meaningful development over the next 6 to 12 months.

items.statement: Cochin Shipyard order: 6 LNG tanks of 800 cu.m, INR85 crore, execution over 2-3 years
items.quote: We got 6 tanks order for the 6 ships of around 800 cubic meter tank. The order value is around INR85 crores, and we have to complete between 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Management declined to provide FY27 revenue or profit guidance due to recent gold duty changes and PM appeal uncertainty
items.quote: I think in the scenarios like this, we would really not give out the guidance for this year. Not that we are not optimistic for it or anything, but let us reserve this guidance.

items.statement: Surat and Rajkot large-format stores targeting Q2 FY27 opening; two mid-format stores in Gandhinagar and Maninagar also planned this calendar year
items.quote: Both the showrooms are targeted to commence operations by quarter 2 of FY27.

items.statement: Each new large-format store requires INR125-150 crore inventory; funding via debt, internal stock transfer and profits — no equity dilution planned
items.quote: We anticipate about INR125 crores to INR150 crores of inventory for each store.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 233 bps to 14.44%; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 11.19% (+63 bps YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA margins improving to 14.44% and expansion of 233 basis points.

items.statement: Retail gross margin ~12-14%; Wholesale ~7-8%; Job work ~6-8%; B2B vs B2C OPM difference ~3%
items.quote: Retail would be around 12% or 14% GP. Wholesale will be around 7% to 8% GP. B2B will be around 6% to 7% and 8% GP.

items.statement: Inventory carried at 20-25% below current gold price; exploring Gold Metal Loan (GML) for new store inventory
items.quote: We have our weighted inventory at about 20% to 25% lower than the current market price.

items.statement: April 2025 sales very good; consumer demand steady in occasion wear ahead of wedding season; daily wear may pause but occasion wear resilient
items.quote: April has been very good.

items.statement: Recent customs duty hike and PM appeal to defer gold buying — impact uncertain; management monitoring ground-level consumer reaction for 1-2 months
items.quote: Certainly, I think these restrictions are not advantageous, but up to what level there is an impact is crucial.

items.statement: Targeting peak debt/equity of 1:1.2 to 1:1.5 for FY27; current equity ~INR300 cr; no equity dilution for store expansion
items.quote: We want to keep the debt levels at 1:1 ratio ideally or 1:1 point, maybe leverage to 1.4, 1.5.

items.statement: Total value of merchandise sold FY26: INR1,251 cr (Retail INR408 cr, B2B INR843 cr); job work volume down but value up due to gold price
items.quote: The total amount of value of merchandise this year that we have sold is INR1,251 crores.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity utilization ~50-55%; no manufacturing capex needed for 2-3 years as gold price rise boosts rupee capacity
items.quote: The capacity utilization is approximately 50% or 55%.

items.statement: Trade receivables spike to INR56 cr due to IIJS Bangalore exhibition and early Akshay Tritiya; now normalized to ~30-day wholesale cycle
items.quote: 24th of March, there was an exhibition in Bangalore, IIJS Tritiya. And, of course, because of exhibitions, there was a spike in sales.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY28 organic revenue target of US$400 million with ~40% EBITDA margin
items.quote: we're also using the opportunity today to reaffirm our long-term guidance of FY '28, which is a US$400 million of organic revenue with around 40% of EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Expect strong FY27 with sequential quarter-on-quarter improvement driven by capacity expansion and commercial launches
items.quote: we are confident of a strong FY '27 and also reiterate our FY '28 guidance of US$ 400 million revenue and 40% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: US$100 million capex program on track; second DDC line installed and undergoing qualification, available for commercialization in Q2 FY27
items.quote: As a part of the US$ 100 million capex which we are doing, the new line which has been installed already a couple of months back is currently undergoing qualification and will be due for availability for commercialization in the next quarter.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA INR919 million, up >5x sequentially; margin expanded 1,550 bps QoQ on higher CSA revenues
items.quote: the Q4 EBITDA reported was INR919 million, which is more than 5x sequentially and the margin expanding by 1,550 basis points quarter-over-quarter, reflecting a strong operating leverage on our higher CSA revenues.

items.statement: Completed 49 regulatory/customer audits in FY26 including surprise FDA inspections at two sites (EIRs received); renewed EU GMP at two sites; received ANVISA approval
items.quote: We saw the year successfully completing 49 regulatory and customer audits, and these include who's who. In fact, we had surprise FDA inspection during the year at two of our sites, and we completed both successfully getting the EIRs.

items.statement: Added ~400 people at flagship site; expanded US front-end, operations and quality teams to support FY27/28 growth
items.quote: We have our flagship site where thanks to all the expansion project, we have added almost 400 people, which is where the bulk of our growth is going to be coming. We have also expanded and deepened the strength of our other organization, whether it is in front-end in the US or whether it is in operations and in quality

items.statement: Targeting 50%+ ROCE in medium term; working capital elevated for launch preparation but expected to normalize in FY27
items.quote: we believe we've got a very good foundation in place and very excited about what lies ahead for us in FY '27 and '28. We expect to scale meaningfully, building towards the 50% plus ROCE expectation that we have for ourselves during the medium term.

items.statement: Management expects to continue store expansion without slowdown despite macro challenges, targeting long-term consumption growth
items.quote: We will continue. We will not slow down our expansion at all because we are very excited about the long-term consumption story in this country and it is our hope and belief that these issues are not permanent in nature and they will go away.

items.statement: FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin improved 60bps to 10.2%, Q4 margin 8.8% vs 8.2% YoY; PAT margin 6.5% vs 5.9%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for full year was INR 1,321 crores, which is a growth of 27.8% over last year, and the adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.2% vis-a-vis 9.6% of last year.

items.statement: Monitoring macro/geopolitical developments closely; higher crude prices and currency depreciation could fuel inflation and impact demand; greater sensitivity to poor harvest/rural income
items.quote: We are specifically monitoring the macro environment very closely and the evolving geopolitical developments, and navigating the situation with agility.

items.statement: Quick commerce expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities with 1.3 crore registered users; small format stores (13 total) delivering same per sq ft EBITDA and ROCE as large format
items.quote: Our quick commerce operation expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities in the country, and our registered users on quick commerce grew to 1.3 crores people.

items.statement: Marketing campaign achieved 1.6 billion Instagram views (top 10 ever); will continue investing in brands to attract younger customers and improve aspirational quotient
items.quote: Our new campaign has now been seen 1.6 billion times on Instagram, which makes it among top 10 campaigns on Instagram ever.

items.statement: Exploring new formats/categories at early stage to address 50% unserved retail market; legacy stores constrained for new categories due to volume growth
items.quote: We are looking at, if there is an opportunity for some different formats, which will help us get to more consumers and customers in the country. It's at a very early stage...

items.statement: Q4 GM compression due to seasonal clearance promotions ahead of spring/summer season and intentional promotion intensity to capture consumption uptick
items.quote: The most dominant reason was the fact that we were entering spring/summer. And typically, in the quarters before our biggest season, we try and get rid of as much old stock as we can...

items.statement: Expects 40-42% CAGR for next 4-5 years minimum, building on 38-40% historical CAGR
items.quote: I feel that this growth momentum should continue next five, six years, and we should be able to grow at around 40%, 42% for next four or five years minimum.

items.statement: Targets INR360-400 crore revenue for FY27
items.quote: Between INR360 crores to INR400 crores is our target to invoice this year.

items.statement: Expects to maintain 24-25% EBITDA margin in FY27, with expansion from FY28 as greenfield ramps
items.quote: This year also we should be able to maintain around 24%, 25% EBITDA. This year we will be increasing some expenses on the new factory also. But from next year onwards, we will see gradual increase in the profitability.

items.statement: Order book at INR400+ crore as of March 31, 2026, providing 1-2 year visibility
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, our order book stood at over INR400 crores, INR400 crores plus, providing healthy execution visibility over the next one to two years.

items.statement: Greenfield to add 5,000-7,000 units annual capacity for high-value RIP/RIS products up to 550 kV
items.quote: The new facility is expected to add approximately 5,000 to 7,000 units of annual capacity, focused on high-value RIP, RIS products with gradual ramp-up over the next few years.

items.statement: Plans fundraise of INR100-110 crore (approved up to INR150 crore) for 550 kV testing, brownfield expansion, and working capital
items.quote: Around INR100 to INR110 is what we are eyeing. And that will be mainly for the capex for the increased production range up till 550 kV and the testing infrastructure.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 260 bps to 25.7% driven by scale, price recovery, supplier negotiation, currency hedging, and export/retrofit mix
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 25.7% compared to 23.1% in FY25, a growth of almost 260 basis points. This reflects our continuous focus on maintaining margin discipline even during a phase of accelerated growth.

items.statement: Has pass-through arrangements with customers for commodity, currency, and input cost escalations
items.quote: There is an arrangement with the customer that we would also be transferring that price rise to them. And they are able to give it to us.

items.statement: Customers giving 24-36 month blanket orders; demand strong across OIP, RIP, and high-current segments
items.quote: Today the situation is the transformer companies are giving us blanket orders for the next 24 to 36 months and they want us to prepare our side for those all delivery execution.

items.statement: Sukrut Electric acquired; targets INR150-160 crore revenue in 4-5 years (5-6x from INR25-26 crore in FY26)
items.quote: Sukrut, we assume that in next four to five years, we should be able to cross at least INR150 to INR160 crores of revenue. And presently it is around INR25 crores, INR26 crores revenue financial year '26.

items.statement: Export target: 20%+ of revenue in 2-3 years; USA subsidiary operational, EU/UK partnerships active, customers awaiting greenfield readiness
items.quote: Our target would be that eventually in next two to three years, we at least do 20% plus from exports.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-40% and PAT growth at 50-60%
items.quote: For FY27, our initial outlook indicates revenue growth of approximately 30% to 40% and PAT growth of about 50% to 60%.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR230 cr including INR65 cr for ANDA acquisition; FY27 capex guided at INR200 cr
items.quote: FY' 27, we are expecting around INR200 crores taken together.

items.statement: 51 approved ANDAs covering 150+ strengths; 20 launched, 30 to launch over next few quarters; 27 molecules with 60+ strengths in development
items.quote: Out of the approved product portfolio, 20 ANDAs have already been commercially launched, while an additional 30 approved ANDAs covering over 100 strengths will be launched over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Emerging markets EBITDA margin at 18-19% in Q4, expected to sustain at 20-21% in FY27
items.quote: As I stated in my opening remarks, last quarter our EBITDA margin stood at about 18% to 19% on emerging market. As we add another INR10 crores, INR20 crore, INR30 crores, INR40 crores of revenue as we move forward, I think the margin will sustain at 18%, 19%, maybe add another 100 basis points to 200 basis points. So m

items.statement: Emerging markets FY27 revenue projected at INR180 cr; 4,000+ products under registration
items.quote: So, in the emerging market, we anticipate that next year our projection is about INR180 crores of revenue that we are looking to get from emerging markets.

items.statement: Regulated markets 83% YoY growth in FY26; CDMO-CMO ~47-48% of revenue, own products ~50-53%
items.quote: I think CDMO and own product are almost the same, which we continue continue to do around 50% to 53% of our own product, and 47%, 48% of CDMO-CMO taken together.

items.statement: Guidance conservative due to external uncertainties (shipping, US inflation); may revise after 1-2 quarters
items.quote: So we have decided to be a little conservative. Let us wait for one or two quarters. Let us see how things settle in the world.

items.statement: INR100 cr unutilized IPO funds to be deployed for sterile manufacturing development over next couple of years
items.quote: So that INR100-odd crores of IPO fund is for a specific purpose that is already been given in our DRHP. So, we plan to start the operations for that particular purpose within this year.

items.statement: Apnar Pharma acquisition: FY27 revenue INR80-100 cr; 2-3 year target INR180-200 cr
items.quote: So, for the full year, we expect Apnar to give us about INR80 crores to INR100 crores of revenues from that particular plant.

items.statement: US business 3-4 year target INR2,500-3,000 cr revenue; accessible market ~$1B for approved products
items.quote: As a company, we are building at least INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores of revenue just coming out of the US in the next three to four years' timeframe.

items.statement: Amerisyn JV FY27 revenue budgeted INR50-80 cr with ~40% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We feel this year, probably we'll do about INR80 crores to INR100 crores of revenue from that JV, maybe a little conservatively, maybe INR50 crores to INR70 crores. That's what has been budgeted between say INR70 crores, INR80-odd crores on an average basis. We feel we'll be able to achieve that with decent profitabili

items.statement: Expects compound AUM growth of 30-35% annually over medium term
items.quote: we expect a compound growth of AUM at around 30% to 35% annually over the medium terms

items.statement: Expects PAT growth of 40-45% in current year FY27
items.quote: PAT expected growth at around 40% to 45% in current year

items.statement: Branch breakeven at 7-8 months with INR1.5-2 crore loan book
items.quote: So around INR1.5 crores to INR2 crores is the range where we come up with the breakeven point

items.statement: NIM expanded to 11.26% in FY26, expects similar or higher levels
items.quote: NIM expanded to 11.26%, reflecting improving lender confidence, better pricing discipline, and gradual improvement in our funding profile

items.statement: Sees structural opportunity in secured MSME lending across Tier 2/3 markets
items.quote: The broader environment of secured MSME and retail lending in India continues to remain structurally favorable

items.statement: 82% AUM from Rajasthan, 11% MP, 7% Gujarat, expanding in UP and Maharashtra
items.quote: 82% is from Rajasthan, around 11% is from MP, and 7% is from Gujarat and rest is from other states

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.13%, Net NPA 1.09% with 49% PCR on Stage 3; LTV 35-38% on NPA
items.quote: Gross NPA stood at 2.13% and net NPA stood at 1.09% as of March '26

items.statement: Branch network grew to 176 across 6 states; 18 new branches added in FY26
items.quote: Our branch network increased to 176 branches across six states, reflecting our continued investment towards strengthening distribution reach

items.statement: ROE 13.7% in FY26; targets sustainable ROE above 12-12.5% medium term
items.quote: in the medium terms I can say that we believe that it will be above 12%, 12.5% on a minimum side

name: Sri Lotus Developers and Realty Ltd

items.statement: FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crores with 55-60% revenue and PAT growth
items.quote: we are confident of achieving our FY27 guidance of pre -sales in the range of INR1,800 crores to INR2,000 crores, along with revenue growth of 55% to 60% and PAT growth of 55% to 60%.

items.statement: H1 FY27 launch of 3 projects with INR2,500-3,000 crores revenue potential
items.quote: we expect to launch three projects in H1 FY2027, Lotus Aquaria in Prabhadevi, Lotus Trident, and Lotus Sky Plaza in Andheri, with a combined revenue potential of over INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Six planned launches with estimated GDV of INR5,000-5,500 crores
items.quote: we have a strong pipeline of six planned launches, Lotus Aquaria, Lotus Trident, Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino, and Lotus Odyssey, with an estimated GDV of INR5,000 crores to INR5,500 crores.

items.statement: Added 9 new projects in FY26 with cumulative GDV of INR8,500-9,000 crores
items.quote: During FY26, we added nine new projects with a cumulative GDV of approximately INR8,500 crores to INR9,000 crores, significantly strengthening our development pipeline.

items.statement: Marketing spend less than 1% of revenue, margins expected to sustain guided range
items.quote: So marketing spend as I said, it would be even less than 1%. But against that, we will be having our lot of direct customers also. So that will take care about not paying other commissions. So margin we are very confident that it will be in the same range what we have guided.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions may cause 1.5-2.5% total project cost increase, but NRIs/HNIs viewing Mumbai as investment destination
items.quote: there would be some inflation and some cost rise. But that cost increase in totality of the project will not be more than about 1.5% to 2.5%.

items.statement: Commercial and ultra-luxury residential both seeing extremely strong demand across micro markets
items.quote: Commercial is doing extremely well across all the micro markets and residential in ultra-luxury also has a very strong demand.

items.statement: Pricing strategy maintains 10-25% premium over competitors in all micro markets
items.quote: And as you know our pricing in any micro market we are about 10 to 20, 25% higher than any other competitor.

items.statement: No import component in supply chain, insulated from geopolitical supply chain issues
items.quote: Fortunately, we do not have any import component in our supply chain. So we are in a way insulated with the geopolitical issues.

items.statement: Ghatkopar project (INR600 crores GDV) at final Supreme Court hearing, conclusion expected this year
items.quote: So it is around INR600 crores GDV project.

items.statement: Board approved 50% dividend payout for FY26, promoters waived entitlement for reinvestment
items.quote: the Board has approved a dividend payout of 50% for FY26. In line with its long-term growth vision, the promoter group has voluntarily waived its dividend entitlement for FY26.

items.statement: Collections expected to improve significantly in Q1-Q2 FY27 as projects move from basement to superstructure
items.quote: the collection once the superstructure will start, the collection will be improved. So the collection will be much better in this quarter and next quarter.

items.statement: Targeting to double FY26 revenue to INR 3,000+ crores in FY27, with 120,000-140,000 pump installations and INR 600-1,000 crores from rooftop
items.quote: We are eyeing around 1,20,000 to 1,40,000 pump. With that we are looking through around INR 2,200 crores to INR 2,400 crores business if we talk about the numbers. And from the roof-top we are eyeing around INR 600 crores to INR 1,000 crores in range between. So, like with all together, we are eyeing around INR 3,000 C

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 710 crores as of date, including INR 350 crores from Magel Tyala Phase 4 and post-April 2026 orders
items.quote: As on date, order book stands INR 710 crores. This is what the order book we have right now.

items.statement: Expecting INR 1,400 crores total order book by end of Q1 FY27 from Magel Tyala Phase 5 (INR 350-400 crores) and Smart Scheme (INR 300-400 crores) plus existing INR 710 crores
items.quote: INR 700 crores business already in hand plus this both together INR 700 we are expecting. So, INR 1,400 crores order should be there for the -- before the quarter 1 get ends.

items.statement: Committed to maintaining double-digit EBITDA and PAT margins; FY26 EBITDA margin was 20.44%, PAT margin 13%
items.quote: See, even last call also I said two-digit margin. Right now also I would say that two-digit margin we would like to keep it.

items.statement: Demand remains strong; Q4 shortfall due to rainfall and raw material delays in late March, not demand slowdown
items.quote: See, demand is still there. Demand is not at all a question. It was slightly delayed due to the -- some raw material delay, but we able to cope up, I believe.

items.statement: FY27 revenue mix: majority from pumps and rooftop, with potential entry into megawatt-scale EPC and long-term BESS opportunities
items.quote: Definitely there it will be having part of the roof-top, sizable number from roof-top, and we are slowly going towards the EPC of the megawatt scale as well.

items.statement: Asset-light model maintained; no manufacturing capex planned; INR 100 crores fixed asset addition is corporate office purchased to secure bank limits via property collateral
items.quote: For the getting the bank limits, we have fixed deposits to be given. That fixed deposit has been transfer into the asset. So, instead of fixed deposit is better to have the asset.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility mitigated via 3-6 month forward price freeze agreements with 2-3 suppliers per component occupying 30-50% of their capacity
items.quote: My vision is always remain that, you know, whenever I take the order, I get clarity, okay, this margin I will have. So, I go and I freeze the price on the day one for my 3-month, 6-month supply side.

items.statement: Monthly installation capacity now at 15,000+ systems; inventory days reduced to 21 days targeting just-in-time; working capital days expected to remain at 140-150 days
items.quote: We have reached to the 15,000 plus monthly installation capacity right now. I have developed that much bandwidth for us.

items.statement: DCR cell supply secured: 875 MW long-term contract signed previous year with prominent supplier for PM Surya Ghar Yojana requirements
items.quote: We have long-term contract. Already we have sign for the current financial year is 875 megawatt with one of the prominent supplier in the country.

items.statement: Market share: ~9% of national PM-KUSUM Component B installations, >15% in Maharashtra; Magel Tyala Phase 4 contributed INR 350 crores order
items.quote: If you take the past number of the GK Energy's contribution in the whole business of the PM-KUSUM which is got installed 10 Lakh plus pump, there itself you can see it is close to two-digit, around 9% is what the country side we have contribution.

items.statement: Worst-case FY27 revenue INR 2,500 crores if PM-KUSUM 2.0 fails; best case INR 3,000+ crores; management confident scheme will proceed as win-win for discoms and farmers
items.quote: So, worst case we are talking about INR 2,500 crores revenue and the best case can be INR 3,000 crores revenue if the PM-KUSUM 2.0 is not delayed.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 remains 2% to 4% of revenue, consistent with prior years
items.quote: So, we expect FY27 also our guidance would remain similar, 2% to 4% of revenue .

items.statement: Indonesia order of 70,000 units: product homologated, first shipment on the seas, ramping up deliveries rapidly
items.quote: I'm pleased to tell you that we already have the product homologated in Indonesia, and our first shipment is already on the seas.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin 13.9% (+130 bps YoY), 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA margin; FY26 EBITDA margin 13.2% (+550 bps vs FY23)
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded steadily through the year and exited Q4 at 13.9%, up 130 bps YoY. This is the 11th consecut ive quarter of double-digit EBITDA margin delivery.

items.statement: Commodity headwinds ~100 bps impact in Q4, significantly higher in Q1; took 2% price increase in April but not passing full cost to protect demand
items.quote: we have taken a 2% price increase in the month of April, but we have decided to not pass on the entire commodity increases and we will work on the cost levers

items.statement: Demand fundamentals intact: April industry volumes healthy double-digit growth, e-way bills +19% YoY in March, +12% in April; diesel price key monitorable
items.quote: April 2026 continued in positive territory at a 12% YoY growth, which, in our view, is a reliable proxy for the underlying freight activity.

items.statement: Non-cyclical revenue CAGR running at 2.7x cyclical CAGR; Q4 ASP drop due to higher van volumes and no electric bus sales, not discounting
items.quote: Over the period, non -cyclical CAGR is runn ing at 2.7x the cyclical CAGR. We've been deliberately building this mix, and this is now showing up meaningfully in the numbers.

items.statement: Iveco deal closure expected Q2 FY27; financing via bridge loan with subsequent refinancing, equity and debt options open
items.quote: our initial plan for financing is going to be through a bridge loan and subsequent refinancing at this point of time, all options are open. So we've kept both equity and debt still open.

items.statement: Iveco regulatory approvals: all secured except financial regulatory approvals from France and Spain; FDI approvals received
items.quote: All approvals have been secured. What is pending is only the finance regulatory approval, which is from France and Spain. All FDI approvals have already been received.

items.statement: Replacement cycle: ~40% of HCV volumes from large fleets replacing after 4-6 years; scrappage center inflows remain low as trucks change hands for lighter duty
items.quote: I would say that at least probably 40% of the volume was related to these large fleet owners replacing their trucks with new ones.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected to continue at ~8% annually until new Pune plant commissions in 2028
items.quote: So, the growth will continue to be in the range of I believe we have forecasted around 8%. So, we expect that growth to continue.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 adjusted PBT margin at 11.5% vs 13.1% in Q3 FY26; decline driven by adverse OEM mix shift and higher bonus accruals
items.quote: If you remove both of them, then the previous quarter, that is Q3 '26, would have been 13.1% and the current quarter would have been 11.5%.

items.statement: Management expects ~50% CAGR revenue growth going forward, with FY27 revenue definitely above 150 crores.
items.quote: Revenue, definitely yes. We don't want to commit to a specific PAT figure yet, but we will try to achieve the best possible results.

items.statement: No large order book; sales orders are maximum 7 days, allowing flexible pass-through of raw material price changes.
items.quote: In sales, we don't have much of an impact because we don't carry a huge order book. Our orders are for a maximum of 7 days, so we are able to pass on any increase or decrease to the customer.

items.statement: EBITDA margin may fluctuate slightly from 39.49% due to formwork entry (lower margin) and steel scaffolding growth, but absolute EBITDA will grow via higher topline.
items.quote: The 40% margin might fluctuate slightly, but overall, we will be growing. We will try to maintain this range. Because even in formwork, our model is a little different from the rest of the market.

items.statement: Aluminum price increase of 40-50% benefits inventory holdings; sales pricing is flexible with 7-day order book allowing full pass-through.
items.quote: Over time, with a 40-50% increase in aluminum prices, that benefit has been quite large and is not yet fully reflected on the books.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting from 43% rental/47% sales to ~40% rental/60% sales in FY27 due to formwork (mostly sales) and steel scaffolding growth.
items.quote: In the current financial year, the contribution from sales will likely increase due to formwork. We are expecting a ratio of roughly 40% rental and 60% sales.

items.statement: Formwork production to start by end of June 2026; FY27 target 30-40 crores revenue, aiming to be top 3 player in few years.
items.quote: We hope that by the end of June, our production will start. In the first year, we have set a modest target of 30-40 crores. From next year onwards, we will be increasing this segment multiple fold.

items.statement: Bad debts <2% over 6 years; dedicated 10-12 person collection team; advances of 1-3 months rental taken from new customers.
items.quote: In the last 6 years, our bad debts have been less than 2%, which is very low compared to industry standards. We have a dedicated team of about 10 to 12 people for receivables.

items.statement: Annual asset scrap loss of 2-3 crores expected as regular business occurrence from damaged/lost scaffolding at sites.
items.quote: Yes, it is a regular part of this business.

items.statement: Company will take on debt to fund FY27 capex; currently net cash ~4-5 crores, debt-free; debt typically retired within 3 years.
items.quote: Yes, debt will increase. Given the speed at which we plan to grow, debt must increase. While there will be a one-time spurt in debt, we usually retire it within 3 years.

items.statement: Expanding warehouse network from 500km to 250km radius; adding 4-5 yards annually (Surat/Bharuch, Cochin/Trivandrum, Goa planned).
items.quote: We normally add four to five yards every year. We are planning for a yard in Surat or Bharuch very soon. We are also planning one in Cochin or Trivandrum to cater to Kerala, and one in Goa.

items.statement: TAN production estimated at 160,000-170,000 tons in FY27 assuming 9 months operation
items.quote: So, let's assume that we have got about nine months production to be very conservative. So, we are saying that we have roughly about 1,60,000 - 1,70,000 tons of production would be possible.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at Rs 500 crores including TAN balance and routine Rs 170-180 crores
items.quote: The total put together should be around Rs. 500 crores balance, I mean, Urea and TAN put together.

items.statement: New urea plant (1.3 MT) brownfield cost estimated at Rs 9,500-10,000 crores
items.quote: The price is INR 9,500 crores to INR 10,000 crores. That is the upper bound as far as brownfield projects are concerned.

items.statement: Complex fertilizer stocks secured till July-August 2026 via strategic early purchases
items.quote: Secondly, as far as Chambal is concerned, we did make some strategic purchases, very big, early in the beginning of the year, and we are covered at least till July-August in terms of our stocks.

items.statement: Urea business operates on cost-plus basis; higher gas costs passed through via subsidy
items.quote: So, if you understand this business, it is basically a cost-plus kind of business. So, government recognizes the cost and therefore, in terms of higher prices of gas, except for that impact on working capital, we are able to pass on the cost to the government in the form of subsidy, increased subsidy.

items.statement: Current gas cost around USD 18.5 per MMBtu for Q1 FY27
items.quote: Currently, what I understand, it is USD 18 plus, USD 18.5 plus. It may be around the same number.

items.statement: TAN market demand growing at 6-7% annually; market currently short due to Russian export curbs
items.quote: And it is a healthy growth, I would say, given that we are already at 1.2 million tons or so of demand. So, if you are saying 6%-7% growth, we are talking about 70,000 tons per year, add on year to year, that kind of number.

items.statement: Crop protection, specialty nutrients and biologicals revenue grew 30% YoY to Rs 1,203 crores in FY26 with 23.5% EBIT margin
items.quote: For FY '26, the segment delivered strong performance revenues increasing by 30% year-on-year to INR 1,203 crores as compared to INR 926 crores in FY '25, and EBIT margins remained healthy at around 23.5%.

items.statement: Biologicals volumes up 30% and revenues up 57% in FY26; 14 new crop protection products planned for FY27
items.quote: The biological business continued to scale up well, with robust increases of about 30% in volumes and 57% growth in revenues, reflecting increased farmer adoption of sustainable agricultural solutions.

items.statement: Phosphatic fertilizer availability constrained by logistics (28-29 ships stuck at Hormuz), not production
items.quote: We have many ships, about 28 or 29 ships, which are stuck up in the Hormuz. They are carrying material. They are loaded up there and so on. So, it is more a question of logistics than production.

items.statement: G-3 urea profitability clarity expected in a month; new regime starts Dec 1, 2026
items.quote: Too premature to give you any guidance on this, but it is moving. That much I can say, because we are to be in this regime from December 1st onwards.

items.statement: IMACID JV P2O5 capacity expansion to 7 lakh MT by Dec 2026; sulphuric acid capacity expansion in FY27
items.quote: The increase in P2O5 production capacity from 5 lakh metric tons to 7 lakh metric tons is expected to be implemented in December 26. Further, Sulphuric acid capacity is also being increased, which is expected to be implemented a year ahead in FY '27.

items.statement: Final dividend of Rs 6 per share recommended, total Rs 11 per share for FY26
items.quote: Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of Rs. INR 6 per share, totaling to Rs. 11 per equity share for FY '26.

items.statement: Crude steel production target of 22.5 million tons for FY27 including 0.6 million tons RINL volumes
items.quote: Our capacity is 21 million tons, and we are targeting to produce 22 million tons. I think it is 22.5 million tons so far as our target is concerned for '26-'27.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR15,000 crores for FY27, rising to INR18,000-19,000 crores in FY28 and INR20,000-25,000 crores annually thereafter
items.quote: Guidance for '26-'27 is INR15,000 crores. And since our expansion projects are ongoing in different, different plants. So in '27-'28, the capex figures will be in excess of INR20,000 crores.

items.statement: Expansion projects at IISCO (INR35,000 crores, 4.5 mt), Bhilai (INR30,000 crores, 3.5 mt), and Bokaro (INR18,000 crores, 3 mt) with major spend from FY28-29
items.quote: capex of IISCO is around INR36,000 crores -- maybe INR35,000 crores. And Bhilai, which is yet to be announced is around INR30,000 crores, and Bokaro is somewhere around INR18,000 crores, something like that.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve further in FY27 due to firm steel prices, rupee depreciation, and cost reduction efforts despite higher coking coal costs
items.quote: With the coal price remaining in range bound -- coal prices remaining on the higher side range bound actually, we hope that the margins will continue to improve further.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 NSR: Longs INR53,400/t, Flats INR51,000/t; April-May NSR: Longs ~INR57,600-57,800/t, Flats ~INR56,000-56,700/t
items.quote: In quarter 4, NSR of -- average NSR of long products was INR53,400 and flat was INR51,000. When we compare this with April, NSR of long products is INR57,600 and NSR of flat is INR56,700.

items.statement: Coking coal procurement cost rose from INR18,200/t in Q4 to INR21,000/t in April and INR21,800/t in May; blended consumption impact lower due to 30-day stock
items.quote: Coking coal, when we look at actually in quarter 4, the coking coal average price is INR18,200, which has gone up in April and May. April average price is INR21,000 and May average price is INR21,800.

items.statement: Demand muted in Q1-Q2 FY27 due to seasonal destocking; expected to pick up from Q3 onwards
items.quote: Generally, demand remains muted in quarter 1 and quarter 2, as all of us have seen, on the back of more sales in quarter 4. So there are events of destocking in quarter 1.

items.statement: Rail price revision for FY25 to be finalized in FY27; impact uncertain (could be positive or negative); no arrears in FY26
items.quote: So far as '26-'27 is concerned, we can't say anything about whether we'll get an advantage from rail price revision or we'll get a negative on rail price revision.

items.statement: Wage revision effective Jan 1, 2027; provision to be made in Q4 FY27 based on government guidelines; cost over and above current employee cost guidance
items.quote: As I told clearly, actually, government notification, etcetera, will come regarding pay revision. And after that, we'll make a provision in quarter 4 of next year, '26-'27.

items.statement: Employee count reduced by 3,400 to 49,752 as of Apr 1, 2026; further reduction of 3,400-3,500 per year expected in FY27-28 plus VRS targeting 500-1,000
items.quote: So as on 1st April 2026, the numbers are 49,752 as compared to 53,159 opening of this year. So a reduction of around 3,400 numbers.

items.statement: Iron ore production target raised to 56 million tons in FY27 from 38 million tons in FY26; aiming for 80 million tons; no major lease renewal issues except Chiria
items.quote: Last year we produced 38 million tons, while this year, we have kept a target of 56 million tons, out of which some quantity will be sold. And going forward, we are trying to ramp up to 80 million tons.

items.statement: Salem stainless steel plant: targeting yield improvement from 84% to 90% at CR mill, LPG to PNG conversion, cheaper power, and slab imports to utilize spare capacity
items.quote: So in CR mill, where the yield right now is only 84%, 83%, we are trying to increase it to 90%. We have taken a couple of other actions like replacing LPG with PNG.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 11-13% low double-digit range for long term; EBITDA growth expected slightly ahead of revenue growth
items.quote: If you look at our full year growth, Mihir, it is 13%. And we've so far guided to a low double-digit growth in the range of 11% to 13%. And for a longish period of time, we will hold on to the same guidance.

items.statement: Raw material supply secured until at least mid-July with weekly inventory expansion; no volume impact from Middle East crisis in Q4
items.quote: We've made sure that availability is adequately covered till at least at this point in time till middle of July, and we continue to increase that on a weekly basis. So therefore, on availability, we are in a strong position.

items.statement: Middle East crisis affecting raw material availability and cost; supply secured till mid-July; proactive price increases implemented weekly; competitive advantage seen for market share gains
items.quote: The crisis has affected both the availability and cost of our key raw materials. We are proactively navigating the situation with a clear and structured approach. We are prioritizing supply security for our customers while ensuring that cost impact gets fully passed on.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.52x; ROCE improved 96bps to 19%; Thailand greenfield investment $5M; sustainable tubes 38% of sales; EcoVadis Platinum rating achieved
items.quote: Strong EBITDA and PAT performance, combined with healthy cash flow generation have enabled a further deleveraging of our balance sheet with net debt to EBITDA improving to 0.52x. Return on capital employed also improved to 19%, expanding by 96 basis points.

items.statement: Management declined to provide FY27 guidance for revenue, margins, order inflow, capex, working capital or net debt due to macro uncertainty; will revisit after Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We have decided not to give any guidance for FY27. However, we will revisit this decision, maybe when we will have -- we have some clarity after conclusion of the first quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR 83,004 crore as of 31 March 2026, up 16% YoY, highest ever; book-to-bill ~4x across seven verticals.
items.quote: Our consolidated order book as of 31st March '26, stood at INR 83,004 crores, which is about 16% increase over the last year, and highest in the company's history.

items.statement: Standalone order backlog INR 72,259 crore; subsidiary order backlog INR 10,745 crore.
items.quote: Standalone order backlog is INR 72,259 crores, and for a subsidiary company, it is INR 10,745 crores.

items.statement: Standalone segment-wise order backlog: Buildings INR 22,740 cr, Transportation INR 15,320 cr, Water & Railways INR 10,400 cr, Electrical INR 13,800 cr, Irrigation INR 4,950 cr, Mining INR 6,750 cr.
items.quote: Buildings, it is INR 22,740 crores. Transportation, INR 15,320 crores. Water and Railways, INR10,400 crores. Electrical, you can take INR 13,800 crores. Irrigation, you can take it as INR4,950 crores and mining, INR6,750 crores.

items.statement: JJM (Jal Jeevan Mission) total order book INR 26,000 crore; executed INR 20,142 crore; balance INR 6,181 crore as of 31 March 2026.
items.quote: The overall order book, what we have received for the JJM projects, including groundwater, surface water is INR26,000 crores. We have already executed projects up to INR 20,142 crores, leaving a balance of INR6,181 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex plan INR 500 crore (INR 100-150 crore for mining equipment, INR 350-400 crore regular replacement/refurbishment).
items.quote: FY27, the capex plan is INR500 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin 8.44% vs 9.21% YoY; consolidated EBITDA margin 8.83% vs 9.07% YoY.
items.quote: At the stand-alone level, we achieved an EBITDA of 8.44% for Q4 FY26 as against 9.21% of the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: 74% of contracts have escalation clauses; management unsure if price increases will be fully covered; potential material availability/logistics issues.
items.quote: About 74% of the contracts, we have escalation clauses. But I'm not very sure whether the increase in the prices will completely get covered under the escalation clauses. There may be some impact.

items.statement: Prospective project pipeline ~INR 2.5 lakh crore; active bidding continues based on risk/reward; INR 1,700 crore orders already bagged in April FY27.
items.quote: We continue to see a very interesting pipeline of prospective projects. If I were to put a number, this number would be close to INR 2.5 lakh crores.

items.statement: Smart meter SPV debt closed at 9.15%; working capital facilities adequate, utilisation <80-90%; access to commercial paper and invoice discounting below 8%.

items.statement: Vizag Urban Infra outstanding INR 291 crore; expect full recovery of INR 250-291 crore in FY27.

items.statement: FY27 cost transformation savings target ~Rs 7,100 cr vs FY26

items.statement: India volume growth at least 2 Mt YoY in FY27 driven by Kalinganagar ramp-up

items.quote: In India we expect 1Q to be about Rs. 6,000 /t higher than 4Q. In UK, we expect it to be about £80/t higher in 1Q compared to 4Q and in Netherlands we expect it to be about €80/t higher in 1Q compared to 4Q.

items.statement: Downstream target 50-60% of volumes; Tubes to 4 Mt, Wires to 1 Mt, double Packaging & Colors
items.quote: We feel that we can do much more in color-coated steels. We were in some sense limited by the JV and that's why we bought out the BlueScope share and we plan to double the size of the Colors business also in the next 12-24 months. So, I think we want our downstream businesses to at least be about 50-60% of our volume.

items.quote: We would like to run more on spot. We have made a small step in that direction with a floating -- with a floating rate -- part floating rate charter on one of our vessels. That will start this month sometime.

items.quote: Our NAV continues to move higher, moving by about INR 200 between end of December and end of March. And we've also declared our highest ever quarterly dividend of INR 11.70 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR35.10 per share.

items.quote: we have pencilled in almost additional ₹100. So we are factoring around ₹225 to ₹250 per tonne kind of a price increase on account of both fuel and as well as miscellaneous expenditure.

items.quote: we do expect a strong demand growth in both Telugu states of AP and Telangana. Yeah, we do expect anywhere between 5% to 10% growth in Tamil Nadu. Karnataka, we expect a 5% growth for the coming year.

items.quote: what we do except is off of 30% kind of a margin as a minimum in that business line.

items.quote: Net of expenditure, we are likely to receive around ₹3.5 crores per acre. And we have around 100 acres. So we were expecting ₹350 crores spread over two years' time.
