items.statement: Consolidated blended EBITDA margin target of 18-20% achievable in FY27
items.quote: On a blended level, we would always look at getting to an easy EBITDA of around 18% to 20%, and that's what we are heading to. I think it's not too far from now.

items.statement: CCT EBITDA margin expected to reach ~15% as business scales
items.quote: So going forward, I think comfortably, we should be at EBITDA of 15% more or less.

items.statement: $7M capex already deployed in CCT post-acquisition for capacity expansion
items.quote: In fact, after the acquisition also, the Fineotex has already done a capex of around $7 million.

items.statement: CCT order book described as very strong with Q4 as baseline for growth
items.quote: Right now, what has been experienced in the quarter four is something, which is the base what is already done. But already, as I see even now and going times, I think the order book is too strong enough even to comment right now.

items.statement: Q4 consolidated EBITDA margin at 14%, targeting 18-20% blended steady state
items.quote: So, all along, Fineotex has been proven for operational efficiencies in the last 15 years of being listed. Always, our EBITDA margins have been minimum in any of the quarters of, let's say, 60 quarters of being listed, Fineotex EBITDA have always been minimum 18% to 28% on the general level.

items.statement: Oil & Gas specialty chemicals now 55-60% of revenue vs textile at 35-36% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: At the moment, almost oil is 60%. Oil Specialty Chemicals is contributing to almost 55% to 60% in terms of value and revenue for the quarter 4.

items.statement: Cash on books >INR300 crores post-acquisition, funding organic/inorganic growth
items.quote: Right now, we are looking at certain more opportunities. And so there is a good cash -- cash on bank in Fineotex is more than INR300 crores even as we speak after doing the acquisition and things like this.

items.statement: Additional 25% stake in CCT to be acquired from founders in Jan 2028, taking ownership to ~79-80%
items.quote: So, yes, we have already signed with the founders that further 25% has to be sold by them to Finotech's in January '28. It's part of the agreement. So that's about it. So that is going to add us to almost 79% or 80%.

items.statement: Doubling CCT manufacturing capacity underway with machines ordered and installing
items.quote: In the line with increasing demand outlook and strong customer traction in the US oilfield chemicals market, we are now in process of doubling the manufacturing capacity in CrudeChem.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated top-line growth targeted at low double-digit range
items.quote: This will translate into an overall top line consolidated growth to be in the low double-digit range .

items.statement: International generic business expected to grow low to mid-teens; API business high single to low double-digit
items.quote: The international generic business are also likely to grow at a decent amount by low to mid-teen range and the API business to grow in the high single or low double -digit growth.

items.statement: India business aims to reach market growth rates with focus on specialty brands
items.quote: We expect the India business to improve and growth momentum and hope to be closer to market growth with a renewed approach to strengthen focused brands.

items.statement: U.S. business expected to grow 10-15% in INR terms; ROW 15%+; API ~10%; India at market growth
items.quote: I expect the U.S. business to grow between 10% to 15% at least. The ROW will continue the growth at 15 -plus percent. API will be closer to the 10% growth. And India, we hope with some changes, we will get to market growth.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crores for capacity, debottlenecking and replacement
items.quote: We expect capital expenditure for the year to be in the range of INR300 crores to INR350 crores, primarily towards capacity, debottlenecking and replacement capex.

items.statement: Core EBITDA margins expected to improve and offset U.S. branded business drag; target to return to ~20% EBITDA margin over 2-3 years
items.quote: As I mentioned, at some point, we would go back up to the 20% kind of EBITDA margins over a 2 , 3 year period. And I expect that this year, it's going to be a good year that we will start seeing improvement in the margins as well.

items.statement: Pivya branded business drag estimated at 100-150 bps in FY27, to be offset by core business leverage
items.quote: From a modeling point of view, I would take about 100 to 150 basis points of impact coming from Pivya, from the branded business in U.S.

items.statement: API pricing remains premium; solvent cost increases not yet passed on but inventory buffers mitigate near-term impact
items.quote: Have we passed it on? No, it's still not a materially big issue for us. As you know, we generally do carry a higher bit of inventory, and that's helped us out right now.

items.statement: No major easing assumed in pricing pressure, competition or supply chain volatility for FY27
items.quote: We are not assuming any major easing in pricing pressure, competition or supply chain volatility.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing and licensing deals for F2/F3 already generating revenue; contribution expected in FY27
items.quote: No, it's already started. Some of the licensing and some of the contract manufacturing is in progress. So we'll see part contribution from that in FY '27 itself.

items.statement: Peptide portfolio has 5-6 molecules; 2 filed, rest in progress; capex for peptide facility already completed
items.quote: We've got a couple. The portfolio is about 5 to 6 that we had. Two of them are filed already and the rest are going on.

name: S H Kelkar and Company Ltd

items.statement: No full-year FY27 guidance given due to raw material and geopolitical uncertainty; confident on normal Q1 and Q2 with secured pricing, supply contracts, and inventory
items.quote: I think this is a very, I would say, difficult question to answer. We are faced with an uncertain future on what is the raw material supply situation, what is the pricing and inflation as a result of the Iran -USA standoff. And given that, we are not really in a position to give you a full-year view. I think quarter 1

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin target of 13-13.5% for H1 FY27; minimum floor of 12-13% adjusted EBITDA
items.quote: We believe that we have taken adequate steps to keep close to this number at least for the first half of this year and we will wait and watch and see and take corrective steps as necessary to ensure that we do not fall below the 12%, 13% EBITDA level which we want to keep as a minimum.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to be maintained at 42%+ for H1 FY27 despite inflationary pressure
items.quote: We will see that the margin continues to be under pressure, but we will be able to maintain 42% and thereabout for the first half of the year.

items.statement: Raw material inflation running 12-13%+ across the board; company passes on increases via 2-3 month inventory cycles and frequent price communication
items.quote: I think the inventory prices are going up, it is very difficult to put an exact number, but upwards of 12%, 13% plus. Pretty much across the Board, there is inflation in operations, in power and fuel, and we expect further inflation on these operating parameters.

items.statement: Exited ~Rs 35 crore (Rs 50 crore annualized) of low/negative-margin business via one-time sale to protect margins amid RM inflation
items.quote: We have transitioned out of Rs. 35 crore, which is roughly translating about Rs. 50 crore of annual business, which was low-margin or negative-margin in the new environment. We have transitioned out of that business with a one -time sale to these clients.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~Rs 140 crore, front-loaded in first two quarters; Almere (Netherlands) fully operational, Vanavate (Maharashtra) expected in coming months, Vashivali rebuild by Q3 FY27
items.quote: FY27 capex will be around Rs. 140 crore of capex. This is all the capex, most of it is in front-ended first two quarters.

items.statement: Gross debt ~Rs 851 crore end-March; may rise temporarily in next 3-6 months for inventory build-up; target to reduce debt 10% per year thereafter; borrowings to remain around Rs 800 crore mark in FY27
items.quote: Gross debt end of March we had a Rs. 851 crore and temporarily we do see that it is going to go up a little bit because we are just ensuring a supply security and, in that bargain, we might have to build some inventory. But when you look at a long -term horizon for sure that we are expecting every passing year we shoul

items.statement: Overall industry demand muted in high inflation; company expects to gain market share and deliver normal growth vs market slowdown
items.quote: I think yes, overall demand will be muted. I do not see the same kind of growth rate as is normal years. Demand will be muted. There will be a transition phase probably first half of the year while the demand the new sort of post-inflation scenario plays out. The overall industry level growth rates will come down, but

items.statement: Europe capacity doubled with Almere factory + Germany CDC; targeting double-digit growth restoration; US CDC at $1M contracted revenue, 4-year organic breakeven vs 5-6 years inorganic
items.quote: We have now the new capacity in Europe that will allow us to grow rapidly and restore the double-digit plus growth rates that we want to achieve in the next few years because we have doubled our capacity and I think we can grow that business aggressively.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (Middle East, Iran-US) driving raw material price volatility and supply risk; 40% RM directly crude-linked, 30% indirectly; rupee depreciation gives ~3-3.5% revenue boost but margin pressure from dollar loans
items.quote: The broader environment continues to be fluid, evolving geopolitical developments and supply-side dynamics globally. However, our strong customer relationships, diversified presence, and improving operating platform positions us well to navigate these uncertainties and capitalize on the emerging opportunities.

items.statement: Creative Development Centres (Germany, Manchester, US) cost Rs 80-85 crore/year opex; treated as capex-like with 3-year breakeven; total investment ~Rs 500-600 crore including past capex
items.quote: So, at this point we have the new initiatives last year which we have started in Germany, Manchester just came on stream this year and the US which came on stream last year. So, three centres which is almost Rs. 70 crore, to Rs. 80 crore of cost per year in opex are also of the nature of capex and they will start gener

items.statement: Confident of hitting Rs 300 crore+ consolidated EBITDA in FY27 (at least FY25 level) despite FY26 slip
items.quote: I am actually confident that we will hit the Rs. 300 crore plus EBITDA for this year. Very much so for the first half where we have more visibility, but I am confident that we can do better than '25 or at least at the '25 level for this year.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle ~140 days; expected to remain elevated until inflation stabilizes due to higher inventory strategy
items.quote: So, the cash conversion cycle is around 140 days at the moment. We see that remaining like this till the time that the inflation sort of steady becomes a steady state because in the high inflation we are keeping higher inventory levels.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR650-700 crore, PAT INR100 crore; FY28 revenue INR800-850 crore; FY29 revenue INR1,000 crore with 30% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain confident of achieving our FY27 goals of INR650 crores in revenue and INR100 crores PAT in FY27, while continuing our journey toward long-term aspiration of INR1,000 crores revenue by FY29.

items.statement: FY27 revenue could exceed INR650 crore by up to INR50 crore if LatAm registrations accelerate
items.quote: So, we believe that INR650 crores is a very, very achievable number, but this number could increase considering if we get more registrations or queries from the ministry and the registration happens in the timely manner. So, probably this number could go plus/minus -- sorry, not minus but plus INR50 crores.

items.statement: Total capex INR260-270 crore for hormones, oncology expansion, biosimilars clinical trials, R&D and BE; INR46 crore spent in FY26, INR90 crore planned FY27, INR90-100 crore FY28
items.quote: So, sir, for hormones, oncology expansion, biosimilar with clinical trials and the R&D and the bioequivalence what we have to do, all these four projects roughly the capex was around INR260 crores to INR270 crores, out of which INR46 crores capex we have already done in FY26. So, FY27, we would do roughly around INR90

items.statement: Unit 6 hormones capex INR65 crore, 50% spent in FY26, targeting WHO GMP and commercialization in ROW before November
items.quote: So, roughly around INR65 crores of capex was to be done and roundabout we have already spent 50% of the total capex in FY26. So, we believe that before November, we'll try to get the WHO GMP and do the commercialization in the ROW market.

items.statement: 55 submissions made in FY26, ~10 approvals received, 6 more expected in H1 FY27, all 55 by end CY27; 25-30 new submissions planned FY27
items.quote: So FY26, we made total 55 submission, sir, out of which we got roughly around 10. And in Q1 and Q2 FY27, we might get six more. And all these 55 registration we will get before end of calendar year '27. And we are in the process of making 25 or 30 more submission this financial year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue expected INR150-160 crore (similar to Q4 FY26), Q2 INR160-170 crore, Q4 target >INR200 crore; quarter-on-quarter growth 15-20%
items.quote: So, probably the Q1 for FY27 will be the same as Q4 of FY26. It will be around INR150 crores -- between INR150 crores to INR160 crores. But the second quarter of FY27, we believe the numbers would increase to INR160 crores, INR170 crores. So, I think quarter-on-quarter, there will be increase of 15% to 20% increase in

items.statement: FY27 standalone revenue target 30-40% growth over FY26 INR7,005 cr; EBITDA margin target 11-12%; order inflow target INR10,000-12,000 cr
items.value: 30-40% revenue growth; 11-12% EBITDA margin; INR10,000-12,000 cr order inflow
items.quote: FY27 revenue target from -- if we look at FY26 number, we mentioned it will be a 30% to 40% growth from this number. So we're in line with that because we have the order. The order book is very healthy right now at almost INR28,000 crores. So we are very confident of the revenue that we should be able to get. That's wh

items.statement: Order book stood at INR 1,432 crores as of 31 March 2026 on consolidated basis
items.quote: Our order book as of 31st March stood at INR1,432 crores on a consolidated basis providing strong visibility for future growth.

items.statement: Management expects to continue growing at similar or accelerated pace in FY27 and beyond backed by large ticket orders due this financial year
items.quote: We will continue to grow at a similar rate, in this particular financial year and the subsequent financial year backed by the size of the order book that we are going to have.

items.statement: Unit 3 Phase 1 civil work complete, machinery received and installation underway; Phase 2 civil work in progress
items.quote: Unit 3 civil work is already complete for phase one. So, phase two civil work is still taking place. Some of the machinery, which we have ordered, we have already received those machinery and installation process going on.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 114 bps to 24%, PAT margin expanded 185 bps to 12%
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 114 basis points to 24% in FY26, while PAT margin expanded by 185 basis points to 12% in FY26.

items.statement: Serious entry into land systems including armament electronics, fire control systems, battle tanks, ICVs, artillery platforms, vehicle-mounted counter-drone systems with trials in upcoming quarters
items.quote: FY26-'27 will mark our serious entry into key defense domains including armament electronics, fire control systems, and battle tanks, infantry combat vehicles, and artillery platforms, vehicle-mounted counter-drone systems with trials scheduled in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Expecting DAC approval for large Navy order for mines/torpedoes any moment; also pursuing export opportunities with customer audits underway
items.quote: We are expecting the DAC approval any moment. As and when we receive, we'll definitely keep you posted, but this is something which is going to happen very shortly.

items.statement: IDL Explosives undergoing transformation, currently loss-making but operational losses reduced significantly; margin guidance from Q3 FY27
items.quote: For last few years, IDL was loss making, but there's the huge transformation as I already told you that we have started by taking up the initiatives, and the operational loss, we have reduced significantly at both EBITDA levels and at different levels of the balance sheet.

items.statement: TNT (500 tons) and HMX (50 tons) capacity for industrial explosives; larger defense explosives expansion DPRs under preparation
items.quote: The capacities are not limited to that. For higher capacities for the defense explosive requirements, you know -- and you know, we would be doing a very large expansion. So, the DPRs are have -- are getting ready.

items.statement: Standalone revenue growth was 36% in FY26 vs 45-50% guidance due to delayed customer approvals; management expects to bounce back and maintain similar momentum
items.quote: Certain projects which we expected to be, you know, executed in the last quarter of, you know, previous financial year, that couldn't happen because of the certain approvals, you know, which got pending actually from our customer.

items.statement: Additional acquisition by subsidiary Apollo Defence Industries expected to complete before end of FY27, subject to NDA
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that an additional acquisition by our subsidiary Apollo Defence Industries Private Limited is expected to be completed before end of this financial year, which will significantly complement our organic growth.

items.statement: Received lifetime DPIIT license covering UAVs, INS, radars, torpedoes, mines, ATGM, decoys, chaffs/flares, aerial bombs, rockets, missiles, loitering munitions enabling full platform penetration
items.quote: We have received a DPIIT license covering UAVs, INS systems, radars, torpedoes, underwater mines, ATGM, decoys, chaffs and flares, aerial bombs, rockets, missiles, and loitering munition. This is a remarkable achievement, which are a lifetime license for the company.

items.statement: Inventory holding days improved in FY26; further improvement expected as production orders increase and in-house test facilities come online
items.quote: As and when these production orders keep hitting, and then the revenue starts recognizing, I think the inventory levels will slowly come down.

items.statement: Addressable market for mine variants alone estimated at INR 4,000-4,500 crores immediate market size; aerial bombs also sizable opportunity
items.quote: Only these variants of mine alone would be a cumulative, you know, a market, you know, in very immediate market size of something like INR4,000 crores to INR4,500 odd crores.

items.statement: R&D expenditure at 8% of revenue (INR 72 crores) in FY26 with zero R&D attrition; developed Mini Torpedo, sensor suits for UAVs, FOG-based INS systems
items.quote: We made the highest investment in R&D within the industry during FY26 with R&D expenditure amounting to 8% of revenue, which is around INR72 crores in absolute terms.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume growth expected at higher end of 6-8% range; EBITDA per metric ton at higher end of INR19,000-21,000 range
items.quote: Q1, we are looking that you'll be able to -- we'll be delivering close to the higher end of the volume guidance range of 6% to 8%. And EBITDA as well at the higher end of the range of INR19,000 to INR21,000 metric tonne.

items.statement: Full year FY27 guidance conditional on Q1 conditions persisting; no formal FY27/FY28 guidance given due to geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: If the current scenario continues the way it is, that's my rider. If nothing -- it may not improve, but it's not worsen. If this is the situation what we have in Q1 continues, I think we'll also be able to deliver that for the full year.

items.statement: No new growth capex commitments for FY27; only routine/replacement capex and some WIP capitalization expected
items.quote: I don't see any growth capex given what -- there may be some work in progress that will get capitalized. But nothing new commitments that we are seeing in this year other than certain brownfield that we do or we may do some routine capex, replacement capex.

items.statement: FY26 full year EBITDA per metric ton at ~INR19,000; Q4 FY26 at INR20,114/MT vs INR21,715/MT in Q4 FY25
items.quote: On a full year, we were at around INR19,000.

items.statement: AMET region demand expected to improve from Q1 FY27 as supply disruptions ease; no fundamental demand destruction
items.quote: So you're talking about degrowth that happened 15%, majorly was supply-led, very clearly, which should start getting taken care from the Q1 of this year.

items.statement: Raw material prices (petchem, oleochemicals) up significantly; pass-through to customers with lag; no weekly price changes possible
items.quote: Now everything has gone up significantly. In fact, petrochemical prices -- base feedstocks have gone up much more than the oleochemical feedstock prices.

items.statement: EPC project revenue not material in FY25/FY26; bulk of revenue recognition expected in FY27
items.quote: Bulk of it will be in this financial year.

items.statement: U.S. specialty pipeline reinitiated post tariff reversals; strong growth potential in premium specialty products
items.quote: Our specialty pipeline in the U.S. has been reinitiated post tariff reversals, and we are seeing encouraging traction and strong growth potential in premium specialty products.

items.statement: Launched Galsoft Lumithic, next-gen mild surfactant for cosmetics; self-thickening, amino acid-based, suited for sensitive applications
items.quote: We further advanced our innovation agenda with the launch of Galsoft Lumithic in in cosmetics Paris, a next-generation mild surfactant which is self-thickening, amino acid-based surfactant that simplifies formulation.

items.statement: Management declined to provide specific revenue or EBITDA outlook for FY27 and FY28, focusing on quarter-over-quarter improvement instead.
items.quote: We will not give any outlook at this point. I would like to believe that the good performance in this quarter is a start to many such good quarters. But at this point in time, my priority and my team's priority is going to be just dig our heels in here and try to do better quarter-over-quarter.

items.statement: Base business operates at 26% EBITDA margin and 54% gross margin; consolidated Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin was 16% at INR 61 crores.
items.quote: It operates at 26% EBITDA margin with gross margins of 54%.

items.statement: No greenfield or brownfield capex planned; focusing on incremental debottlenecking projects to unlock capacity for high-margin products.
items.quote: We are not planning to take up any greenfield projects. There's no big capex that we're going to invest. In our existing facilities itself, we have around 30% capacity available. So, I think it's going to be all about how smartly and wisely we can use this capacity for our high-margin products.

items.statement: Base business has a healthy order book driving strong utilization across facilities; no one-off spot orders or inventory restocking benefits.
items.quote: On the base business, Sajal, we have a very healthy order book, and you've seen that in our numbers as well. So I'm very encouraged looking at this order book and the utilization across our facilities that there is a strong performance, and it is not factors outside our control that are really favoring our business.

items.statement: Developed markets contribute 75% of sales; base business momentum driven by new customer acquisition, geography expansion, and share of wallet gains.
items.quote: Business contribution from our developed markets, which is our mainstay, continues to be at 75% of overall sales.

items.statement: Ibuprofen business recorded negative EBITDA; board appointed bankers to evaluate strategic options (sale or conversion to multiproduct facility), decision expected in H1 FY27.
items.quote: Our Board has appointed bankers to evaluate strategic options for ibuprofen, and we expect this process to finish in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Vizag facility mothballed since 2024, incurring INR 12-15 crores annual fixed costs; future use depends on ibuprofen strategic decision.
items.quote: However, we have certain fixed cost expenditure for the Vizag site which is INR12 crores to INR15 crores annually.

items.statement: No further capital raise planned after rights issue; internal target to become debt-free (including working capital debt) by FY29.
items.quote: We also concur with kind of similar views. So we have an internal target of making Solara debt-free by FY '29.

items.statement: Top 15-20 products contribute ~75% of revenue across ~70 commercialized products; no single molecule dependency.
items.quote: Roughly, we have commercialized close to 70 products in the entire portfolio, what we sell currently, of which roughly top 15 to 20 products has a mix of close to 75% of the entire business.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization ~70% in base business (ex-ibuprofen); 30% spare capacity available for growth without major capex.
items.quote: If you look at our capacity, we are currently using around 70% of our capacity. So, there is enough capacity -- there's around 30% capacity left that we can utilize.

items.statement: Debt reduced by ~INR 158 crores in FY26 (21% reduction); INR 113 crores from rights issue first call, INR 45 crores from operational cash flows; targeting ~INR 503 crores by end May 2026 after second call money.
items.quote: We have been able to reduce our debt by roughly INR158-odd crores during FY26, which actually signifies close to 21% reduction in the debt during the year, out of which INR113 crores came off from the first call money of rights, which we had in May '26. And then balance INR45 crores were actually paid off from our oper

name: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd

items.statement: AUM target to cross INR5 lakh crore in H1 FY27; steady growth thereafter with replacement of low-margin railway assets by higher-margin diversified assets
items.quote: So going forward, we expect that in the year FY27, the magic figure of INR5 lakh crores for AUM, we should touch sometime in H1, maybe early to that, let us see.

items.statement: FY26 sanctions INR74,000 crore (vs guidance >INR60,000 crore); disbursements INR35,000 crore (vs guidance ~INR30,000 crore); key deals include DFCCIL refinance INR10,000 crore and HURL refinance >INR12,000 crore
items.quote: Against what we gave the guidance of INR60,000 crores, we crossed the mark or we reached the mark of nearly INR74,000 crores for the year in terms of sanction of assets. And against the guidance of INR30,000 crores for disbursement, we could do around INR35,000 crores.

items.statement: Tax-free status for 5-7 years due to accumulated depreciation; PBT=PAT; new metro leasing to replenish depreciation shield
items.quote: On tax, we have enough depreciation kind of thing in our kitty. So this company will remain tax-free with the kind of already accumulated depreciation that we have for next 5 to 7 years.

items.statement: FY26 PAT record INR7,000+ crore; net worth INR56,000+ crore; AUM net growth to INR4.85 lakh crore from flat INR4.6 lakh crore; Q4 PAT flat due to provisions/CSR but revenue up 9%
items.quote: We have crossed the magic figure of PAT of INR7,000 crores this year. Our net worth is consistently growing from INR52,000-odd crores, now it is INR56,000-odd crores plus.

items.statement: Management expects 25-30% year-on-year revenue growth for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: So with the current trend that is going on, we are quite optimistic that this trajectory of growth that has been witnessed in past few years should keep continuing. But our sense is that it could be more than 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Order book consistently revolving at INR3,000+ crores providing multi-year revenue visibility
items.quote: Our order book remains robust, revolving consistently over INR3,000 crores, providing multiyear revenue visibility and reinforcing confidence in our long-term growth outlook.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be maintained at 44-45% year-on-year with minor variation
items.quote: So EBITDA would be -- remain on growth trajectory only. And probably what we believe is we should be able to maintain EBITDA of 44%, 45% year-on-year. It may vary 1% or 2% here and there, but no major movement.

items.statement: Strategic priorities: PEC contracts, higher capacity drilling rigs (2,000 HP), and offshore fleet expansion
items.quote: See, if we talk about top 3 priorities, of course, PEC is one. Second priority for us is higher capacity drilling rigs. And third priority definitely to add a fleet into offshore segment as well.

items.statement: PEC contracts have free gas price mechanism; higher gas prices increase order book value
items.quote: Yes, definitely. Because in PEC, we are having a free gas price mechanism. And as you rightly said, with increase in gas price, this order book can increase upward.

items.statement: New 2,000 HP drilling rig capex estimated at INR100-120 crores, funded through internal accruals and debt
items.quote: So our primary estimate is the rig can be of around INR100 crores or INR100 crores to INR120 crores, but that depends on the availability of equipment as well.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of INR500-600 crores submitted; new PEC tender (15-year) recently received but not yet bid
items.quote: It's close to around INR500 crores, INR600-odd crores.

items.statement: Dolphin Offshore expected FY27 revenue of INR150 crores with ~60% EBITDA margin on single asset
items.quote: But with the single assets which we are already operating, we are expecting top line of around INR150 crores from this financial year and the current FY27 with EBITDA of almost 60%.

items.statement: QIP plan cancelled due to improved cash flows
items.quote: No. So we have decided not to go ahead with QIP.

items.statement: Long-term vision: company could double in 3-5 years given government push and market share in onshore services
items.quote: But barring that, now that government has a great move, on this sector, it won't be surprised company could even get double in next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Management expects to sustain EBITDA margins in the 30-32% range going forward despite geopolitical uncertainty.
items.quote: However, we remain confident in the strength of our business fundamentals and our ability to sustain EBITDA margins in the range of 30% to 32% going forward.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR 540 crores, fully funded by internal accruals, focused on Solapur greenfield and R&D.
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we plan to incur a capex of about INR540 crores, which includes carryover commitments from FY26 as well as fresh capital investments. Importantly, this entire capex will be funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Solapur Phase 1 (370 KL BI block, 120 KL API block) expected operational in Q2 FY27; initial utilization 40-50%.
items.quote: Solapur Phase 1 is progressing as planned and is expected to be operational in Q2 of this year.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 360 bps to 33.6%, highest in history, driven by mix, cost management, and operational efficiency.
items.quote: We delivered EBITDA margins of 33.6%, expanding by 360 basis points, highlighting the inherent strength and operating efficiency of our business.

items.statement: Price erosion of ~5.5% on non-GPL, non-CDMO base business; raw material (solvents) and freight costs rising but largely passed through to customers.
items.quote: So on that, the price erosion is about 5.5% is what we have seen on the non-GPL, non-CDMO.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility across regulated markets; non-GPL revenue grew 13% YoY in FY26; chronic therapies 67% of revenue.
items.quote: Our revenue for the year stood at INR2,552 crores, registering a 6.9% year-on-year growth and in the non GPL business leading the momentum with 13% growth.

items.statement: Non-GPL contribution rose from 59% (FY22) to 71% (FY26); CDMO share increased from 6% to 7%; high-potency API pipeline advancing (12 validated).
items.quote: This is reflected in the strong and consistent performance of our non-GPL segment, whose contribution to the overall business has steadily increased over the years from 59% in FY 22 to 71% in FY 26.

items.statement: CDMO recovery from Q3 FY26; 4th/5th projects ramping; targeting 2 new CDMO deals in H2 FY27.
items.quote: So CDMO, the fourth and fifth project have kicked in really nicely. There's some revival even on the earlier projects. And so we expect that CDMO will continue this momentum. As far as new projects go, we hope to close 2 new deals in the second half early second half of this year.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts (war) creating supply chain constraints, elevated logistics/energy costs; Dahej fire caused INR 20 cr loss (booked in other expenses).
items.quote: From an expense perspective, yes, we have booked a loss due to fire in our other expenses to the extent of INR20 crores.

items.statement: R&D spend at 3.6% of sales in FY26; expected to rise to ~4% over next 1-2 years, focused on flow chemistry, HPAPI, pellets/granules, CDMO.
items.quote: As far as settling down, I don't think we'll cross 4%, right? We'll probably be at 4% in the next year or 2. And then it should settle down.

items.statement: Asset turnover may dip below 2x temporarily as Solapur/brownfield capacity comes online, but expected to recover as utilization ramps.
items.quote: I mean it would temporarily go down below 2 as well, right? But it would come back up once the utilization picks up, like I explained earlier.

items.statement: Net debt-free with INR 782 cr cash (Mar'26); generated INR 984 cr operating cash over 2 years, invested INR 472 cr capex, paid INR 61 cr dividends.
items.quote: As of 31st March 2026, our cash and cash equivalents stood at INR782 crores, with capex for the year being INR306 crores.

items.statement: Forex gain of INR 31 cr for FY26 (INR 11 cr in Q4) due to rupee depreciation; net exporter benefits.
items.quote: For the entire year on the P&L, we have seen a net gain of about INR31 crores on the P&L. There is about INR11 crores of gain that we have booked for Q4.

items.statement: Expects 15-17% revenue growth in FY27 and high-teen growth in FY28, excluding potential recovery of lost US business
items.quote: for fiscal 2027, what we expect as on date is maybe a mid-teen growth, 15% to 17% growth, something like that. And again, same kind of growth would be there or maybe a bit on a higher -- a high-teen growth in the fiscal 2028.

items.statement: Expects US order flows to resume meaningfully from Q1 FY27 as tariffs normalize
items.quote: With duties now normalizing, we expect U.S. order flows to resume meaningfully from Q1 of current fiscal, that is FY 2027.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR 30-40 crores minimum plus maintenance capex; broadly INR 50 crores per year for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: there would be there a minimum INR30 crores to INR40 crores bare minimum capex plus maintenance capex, etcetera, that would require for a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Monthly dispatch schedule of INR 115-125 crores for H1 FY27; expects INR 160-165 crores incremental revenue in FY27 from order book ramp-up
items.quote: on an average, INR115 crores to INR125 crores dispatches planned for this first half on a monthly basis.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 51.5% in FY26 from 49.4% in FY25 due to product mix shift and raw material management; expects normalized gross margin range of 49-53%
items.quote: our gross margin expanded meaningfully from 49.4% to 51.5% in fiscal 2026, reflecting the positive shift in product mix towards higher-value machine auto components and a better raw material management.

items.statement: Expects operating EBITDA margin not less than 20.5-21% on conservative basis, with potential improvement from scale benefits
items.quote: I expect on a conservative way, operating EBITDA would not be less than 20.5%, 21% kind of thing. And with the incremental growth, further it may improve because maybe I'll be getting the benefit of scale of economy and fixed cost absorption.

items.statement: Quarterly raw material cost pass-through with majority of overseas customers; half-yearly with a few customers
items.quote: With the majority of our overseas customers, we have a quarterly pass-on for the raw material cost. Maybe with a couple of customers, it's on a half yearly base kind of thing.

items.statement: Container availability delays of 2-3 weeks and extended transit times; managing with premium payments and inventory buffering
items.quote: there is a delay of maybe two to three weeks on availability of container and maybe a bit of extended transit days also. But we try to manage our inventory at warehouse and consignment stock.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of 1 crore shares at INR 180/share (INR 180 crores); promoters not participating; considering dividend but preserving cash for capex and uncertainties
items.quote: In April 2026, our Board approved a buyback of 1 crores shares at INR180 per share, aggregating to INR180 crores. The promoters /promoters group has chosen not to participate, ensuring that full benefit of this buyback flows directly to all public shareholders.

items.statement: Fully settled Right of Recompense obligation of INR 101 crores on March 31, 2026; now debt-free with no legacy obligations
items.quote: In March 2026, precisely on 31 st of March 2026, Rolex Rings has honored its Right of Recompense obligation in full, making total payment of INR101 crores to our consortium lenders.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 62-63%; forging equipment at 80-85% utilization in certain product ranges requiring capex
items.quote: My utilization is almost same what we had, as you have seen that my top line is almost at same -- this thing. So, we are in the range of 62% to 63% of utilization of my available or achievable capacity.

items.statement: Expect 200-225 net new stores in FY27, with KFC contributing 100-110 stores
items.quote: We expect to add approximately 200 to 225 net new stores in FY27 as DIL. KFC is expected to contribute 100 to 110 stores of these additions with the balance being driven by Costa Coffee, Biryani By Kilo and international businesses.

items.statement: Merger with Sapphire Foods on track for completion by end of current fiscal year
items.quote: We continue to expect completion of the merger by end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Tech-driven changes to be managed within existing budgets including Yum! charges
items.quote: we will be able to manage all the tech-related changes within our existing budgets, including whatever charges we pay to the Yum!.

items.statement: Ended FY26 with 2,256 system stores, net addition of 217 stores over last 12 months
items.quote: We ended FY26 with a system store count of 2,256 stores, representing a net addition of 217 stores over the last 12 months.

items.statement: KFC brand contribution margin improved to 17.0% in Q4 FY26, up from prior year
items.quote: Brand contribution grew nearly 20% year-on-year to reach INR 99 crore with brand contribution margins improving to 17.0% for the quarter.

items.statement: KFC menu price increase less than 0.5 percentage point on portfolio basis in recent quarter
items.quote: There was a very small correction. So, on a portfolio basis, I would say it was maybe less than 0.5 percentage point.

items.statement: International business grew 20% YoY, crossed INR 500 crore quarterly revenue for first time
items.quote: As a result, the international business grew 20% year-on-year and crossed INR 500 crore in quarterly revenues for the first time.

items.statement: Shifted KFC promotional focus from online to dine-in channel to drive store traffic and SSSG
items.quote: we have shifted the focus now more to dine-in and more to the dine-in customers. And therefore, we are tailoring the offers and the price points and the promotions to make sure that the dine-in customers are attracted

items.statement: Gas crisis continues in parts of country, monitoring closely; mitigating via electrical equipment evaluation
items.quote: The gas crisis continues to be an issue in some parts of the country, and we are still not fully out of it. We are monitoring the situation very closely and continue to effectively manage the situation.

items.statement: Discontinuing Tea Live brand in India and Thailand next quarter after testing
items.quote: Having tested Tea Live in India and Thailand, we have decided to discontinue the brand, and the same will happen in the next quarter.

items.statement: New leadership team largely in place by next quarter including CTO, CMO, COO hires
items.quote: I am happy with the progress made and feel very confident that we will be able to largely have the new team in place by next quarter.

items.statement: Pizza Hut SSSG -3.7% in Q4 but improved sequentially; ADS stable at ~INR 30,000/store/day
items.quote: While SSSG was at minus 3.7%, the SSSG performance improved on a sequential basis, with ADS remaining stable at ~INR30,000 per store per day.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 29-30% and PAT margin 19-20% for FY27
items.quote: We hope to keep margins stable between the 29% to 30% EBITDA margins as well as in the PAT around 19% to 20%.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR3,000-3,500 million for Site 5 and new R&D site
items.quote: The total capex for financial year '26 was INR3,838 million and the capex expected for financial year '27 is INR3,000 million to INR3,500 million.

items.statement: Remaining capex across Site 5 and R&D expansion ~INR1,500-1,600 crores over next 4 years
items.quote: It will be approximately all put together, the Site 5 is the major site and the Site 1 where we are expanding the R&D. So all put together, it will be approximately INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores, all in next 4 years.

items.statement: 3 new LSM products (2 pharma, 1 agro) from Site 5 to commission by May-end/early June; validation done, orders in hand
items.quote: There are 3 new large-scale manufacturing products, 2 in pharmaceutical and one agrochemical from Site 5, which will be commissioned by May end or starting of June 1st week. Validation batches are done and orders are already in hand.

items.statement: LSM pricing up >20% YoY and 18% QoQ in Q4; sustained in April-May; medium-term sustainable
items.quote: Pricing has been exceptionally strong over 20% year-on-year and 18% quarter-on-quarter in Q4. We believe this pricing environment is sustainable in the medium term.

items.statement: No demand disruption from oil market conflict; steady demand across products; no hoarding
items.quote: We have seen a steady demand in all our products as such. So there is no hoarding of material happening in this instance during this war.

items.statement: Target 70% revenue from CRAMS+CEM, 30% LSM over next 3-4 years; currently 55% CRAMS+CEM
items.quote: We are very confident of achieving our vision of 70% of revenues coming from CRAMS and contract exclusive manufacturing business models by fiscal year '30.

items.statement: Fire at external warehouse near Site 1 on Mar 11 '26 caused INR70M inventory provision; Site 2 fire claim settlement expected by end Q1 FY27
items.quote: Further, a provision for loss of inventory on account of fire at an external warehouse near Site 1 on March 11, '26 a mounting to INR70 million has been provided in Q4 of financial year '26.

items.statement: Debt to increase by INR200-250 crores in FY27 as QIP funds deployed; sequential drawdown
items.quote: Approximately by end of financial year '27, you can expect INR200 crores to INR250 crores additional in the debt, not more than that.

items.statement: Site 5: 4 of 16 blocks built, 2 ready for commercial production; 4 more blocks excavation started; 20 blocks total across Site 5 and Site 5+
items.quote: We have already completed the construction of 4 blocks. Two blocks are already ready to run. So water trials and solvent trials are ongoing. I think we'll have a good news very soon when we start the commercial production on 2 production blocks.

items.statement: Semiconductor materials: Phase 1 target 400 tonnes at $40-50/kg; opportunity seen tripling by 2030
items.quote: We are looking at producing on the first phase of 400 tonnes of particular set of molecules and where the average price would be $40 to $50 per kilo.

items.statement: Expecting margins to bounce back to previous levels in FY27
items.quote: No, no, we'll bounce back to our previous levels.

items.statement: Total portfolio 7.5 lakh sq ft with 4.92 lakh sq ft booked and 2.40 lakh sq ft available inventory
items.quote: Our total project portfolio consists of 7.5 lakh square feet, out of which 4.92 is booked and 2.40 lakh available inventory.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with capital employed around INR 80-90 crores as of March 31
items.quote: It will be upwards around INR80, INR90 crores.

items.statement: Dombivli hospital expected to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of 2 years of operation (calendar year end 2027-28)
items.quote: 2 years of operation, calendar year '26, we have started. So, calendar year end of, '27, '28, you should expect it.

items.statement: Dombivli EBITDA burn estimated at INR2-3 crores per month on average for the full year
items.quote: So, we have said between INR2 crores to INR3 crores a month on an average for the whole year.

items.statement: Total expansion pipeline of ~1,700 new beds across 4 greenfield projects at average cost of INR1.5 crores per bed
items.quote: Across the 4 hospitals in this cycle, from Dombivli all the way to BKC, the 1,700 beds will come up at an average cost of around INR1.5 crores per bed.

items.statement: FY26 capex deployment of ~INR500 crores for Dombivli, BKC land payment, Pune and Mira Road projects
items.quote: we deployed around INR500 crores in capex this year, Dombivli, BKC land payment , and ongoing Pune and Mira Road projects.

items.statement: Remaining 75% of BKC land cost to be paid in FY27
items.quote: It should be paid in this financial year. Everything will be paid in this financial year.

items.statement: Internal accruals over next 4-5 years plus debt at under 3x EBITDA expected to fund all announced projects
items.quote: Our current view is that the internal accruals over the next 4 -odd years, combined with debt at under 3 times EBITDA, should be sufficient to fund everything that we have announced.

items.statement: Pune South on track to open in calendar year 2028; Mira Road excavation expected to begin by end of 2026
items.quote: Pune South is on track to open in calendar year '28, as we had committed. Mira Road has completed its architectural drawings and is undergoing regulatory clearances. We expect excavation to begin by the end of the year.

items.statement: Key cost risk is depreciating rupee increasing capex costs; consumable costs linked to global supply chains being monitored
items.quote: On the cost side, the only thing that I am watching out for very keenly is the depreciating rupee and the cost of capex, so that is kind of a national reality.

items.statement: Insurance revenue share at 55.4% of total revenue; government revenue at 1%
items.quote: The insurance revenues now make up 55.4% of our revenue mix, while government stands at just 1%.

items.statement: Thane occupancy ~75%, Pune ~65%, Indore 45-50% for FY26
items.quote: For Thane, the occupancy has been around 75%; Pune, close to 65% and Indore is between 45% and 50%

items.statement: Indore Phase 2 expansion (111 beds) to be considered once occupancy crosses 60%
items.quote: Once the occupancy crosses 60% or near 60%, then we will think about the next phase of bed addition.

items.statement: FY27 launch target set at over INR150 billion GDV
items.quote: we are estimating that we'll do new launches in excess of INR150 billion

items.statement: FY27 sales target set at near INR100 billion
items.quote: we expect to do sales which are nearing INR100 billion

items.statement: FY27 revenue recognition and collection targets set at INR50 billion each
items.quote: Completion and collection go hand-in-hand and hence, we've kept a target of INR50 billion for both of these metrics

items.statement: FY27 PAT guidance between INR1,000-1,500 crores
items.quote: The number for the current year, I think, should be in between INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores

items.statement: JV with RMZ requires INR3,500-4,000 crores total capex over 4-4.5 years, Signature Global share ~INR1,500-2,000 crores
items.quote: about 5.5 million square feet, you should assume capex in the range of about INR3,500 crores to INR4,000-odd crores should happen by both the parties put together over the next 4 to 4.5 years

items.statement: Launched portfolio of 21+ million sq ft with GDV over INR30,000 crores; total portfolio 40 million sq ft with GDV over INR70,000 crores
items.quote: Put together, the GDV of both these sets of projects crosses INR700 billion, INR70,000 crores of GDV is there in between these 2 subsets of the portfolio

items.statement: FY26 gross margin ~30%, EBITDA margin 9-10%
items.quote: We generated a gross profit margin of about 30%, EBITDA margin of 9% to 10%

items.statement: Realizations crossed INR15,000/sq ft in FY26, up 20%+ YoY; expect normative inflationary increases in FY27
items.quote: per square foot realization crossed INR15,000 mark, which is, of course, a 20% plus realization on a per square foot basis vis-a-vis the previous year

items.statement: Global headwinds uncertain; NGT restrictions and excessive rains caused completion slippage in FY26
items.quote: There are certain global headwinds right now. No one can predict how that's going to pan out for the country or for the region

items.statement: Net debt reduced to near zero (~INR2 billion); operating cash flow INR21 billion in FY26 allocated to BD, debt reduction, approvals
items.quote: net debt is actually down to a near 0 level. It's just 2 billion, could have been positive or minus 2

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY27 maintained at 17-20% including new capacity ramp-up from H1
items.quote: At consolidated level with the planned capacity expansion and the current demand trends, we expect revenue to grow by 17% to 20% in FY27. It's the same guidance that we had in the previous call.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR250-275 crores for capacity expansion across moulding, writing instruments, wooden pencils and land development
items.quote: Therefore, despite the current geopolitical and regulatory uncertainties, we have lined up a capex plan between INR250 crores to INR275 crores for FY27.

items.statement: Implemented 4-5% price increase via scheme/discount rationalization across products; further gradual MRP hikes planned if inflation sustains
items.quote: As a first step, what we've done is – wherever we could believe we could rationalize our channel margins or we could rationalize the schemes and discounts, we've taken that step, which has resulted in about 4% to 5% increase, which has been passed to consumer, and this is across different products, not any specific SKU

items.statement: Office supplies growth driven by ball pens and highlighters; wooden pencil capacity expansion planned after long gap
items.quote: Along with ball point pens, as you rightly said, another category within the office supplies broad category was highlighters, again, a product which we launched towards the end of last financial year. That product category has also done well.

items.statement: West Asia conflict driving crude-linked raw material inflation (40% direct, 30% indirect exposure); currency volatility; near-term margin pressure
items.quote: A significant portion of our input basket is directly linked to crude derivatives, which makes cost trends especially sensitive and highly volatile to the developments in the West Asia conflict.

items.statement: Uniclan FY26 revenue INR203 crores (23% growth), EBITDA margin 8.6%; targeting 20% growth and 10% EBITDA margin long-term
items.quote: FY26 on a full year basis, we've done a revenue of around INR203 crores at Uniclan. This represents close to -- for Uniclan, this represents close to a 23% growth over their base year revenue. In terms of margins, the margins have been around 8.6%.

items.statement: 45-acre facility first building completion June 2027, commercial production end of Q2 FY27; total built-up area to double over 3 years
items.quote: As a part of the phased development of our 45-acre facility, the first building is on track for completion in June 2027 with commercial production expected to commence towards the end of Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Seven SpA JV formation expected to complete before end of June 2026; SKIDO revenue grew 60% YoY in Q4 to INR4.5 crores
items.quote: In terms of our JV formation with Seven SpA, we are in the process of formation of the joint venture entity, and this should be completed before the end of June 2026.

items.statement: Distribution reach targets 225,000 directly serviceable stationery stores out of 300,000-350,000 universe; cross-sell via Uniclan kirana network
items.quote: So, our universe to target would be about direct target, direct reach about 225,000 stationery stores. And by that time, I think our distribution through Uniclan in the general merchant outlet would have also reached a substantial point, which is basically into Kirana stores.

items.statement: FY26 capex INR292 crores vs guided INR225-250 crores; increase due to strategic land acquisitions near Umargam and Jammu
items.quote: The company totally spent around INR292 crores in FY26 towards these objectives. As a part of the phased development of our 45-acre facility, the first building is on track for completion in June 2027 with commercial production expected to commence towards the end of Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Targets Critical Power exports to reach 20% of revenue in FY27 from 15% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are really trying to increase that to 20% in FY '27, and this rise of 10% to 15% in Quarter 4 is just a trajectory on that journey

items.statement: Targets INR 50 crore BESS revenue in FY27 from pilot stage
items.quote: this year, we have kept an internal target of scaling from pilot stage orders to north of INR 50 crores of business

items.statement: Standalone gross margin expanded to 27% in Q4 FY26 driven by richer EVSE mix and fewer low-margin lithium batteries
items.quote: Standalone gross margin in Q4 expanded to 27%, an improvement, significant improvement year-on-year, driven by a richer EVSE mix, fewer lower margin lithium batteries

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin reached 10.6% in Q4 FY26, up 148% YoY
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 29.9 crores at a margin of 10.6%, up 148% year-on-year

items.statement: BharatNet project margins slightly lower in Q4 due to fixed government contract pricing amid commodity cost increases
items.quote: because of the fixed nature of pricing in these government contracts some slight low, the contribution margin in Q4 is slightly lesser than in Q3 because of some of the price increases due to geopolitical situation

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR972.9 cr, EBITDA INR97.9 cr, PAT INR68.6 cr; Q4 revenue INR286.2 cr (+27.6% YoY), EBITDA INR26.8 cr, PAT INR18.9 cr
items.quote: For FY26, the revenue stood at INR972.9 crores, EBITDA stood at INR97.9 crores, and the PAT stood at INR68.6 crores. For the fourth quarter, we saw continued momentum across all our key customer segments, with revenue for Q4 at INR286.2 crores, up 27.6% year-on-year, EBITDA at INR26.8 crores, and PAT at INR18.9 crores.

items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 commissioning targeted in H1 FY27; brownfield debottlenecking at Naidupeta to complete by Dec 2026; combined capacity to exceed 115,000 MTPA by 2029
items.quote: We continue to target the commissioning of Phase 1 of the zinc oxide production as per plan. Once operational and stabilized, the Dahej facility will become a pivotal contributor to our overall capacity build-up and also to our growth plans.

items.statement: Very healthy order book and demand projection for May-June; June projections almost at par with April-May
items.quote: even as we speak the months of May, June, we have a very, very healthy order book and a very healthy demand projection. So, currently we are not witnessing any slowdown from the tire industry and what we hear that the demand for tires is quite strong in the market and even our projections what they have given for the m

items.statement: Current EBITDA margin 10-11%; target blended margin 13-14% with higher value-added products from Dahej; Q4 margin 10.26% impacted by 150bps from energy/raw material spike in March
items.quote: So, you see our current EBITDA margins are usually in the 10% to 11% range, and as we've mentioned before, higher value-added products would help increase the blended margins to the 13% to 14% range.

items.statement: All incremental costs (raw material, energy, freight) from March transparently passed on to customers effective 1st April 2026; pricing directly linked to LME with direct pass-on model
items.quote: In line with our long-standing pricing philosophy, all of these incremental costs, including higher freight, energy, and other ancillary costs, have been transparently passed on to all our customers with effect from 1st April 2026 itself.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict disrupted supply chains in March (Middle East import freeze, Europe shipment delays); secured raw material via scale, balance sheet, supplier relationships; temporary ceramic plant shutdowns in Morbi due to gas shortag
items.quote: There is no denying the fact that the war has impacted virtually every industrial supply chain across the world, and zinc dross, our primary raw material, has been no exception. However, this is precisely the kind of environment in which JGC strength comes to the fore.

items.statement: Solar Phase 1 at Naidupeta commissioned in FY26 (~INR2 cr capex, 3-3.5 yr payback); further renewable investments planned at Naidupeta and Dahej; export contribution 10-15% of sales; zinc oxide is 3.5-5% of tire compound by weight, 1-1.5% o
items.quote: we've spent roughly about INR2 crores or so in the solar power project and the payback period for the project is about three to three and a half years. So, the return on the capital employed is fairly high and it also leads to significant reductions in the energy cost.

items.statement: Consolidated top-line growth guided at mid-teens for FY27
items.quote: Overall, we expect the top line growth at a consolidated level to be in the range of mid- teens at the backdrop of higher investment in further scaling up ICONiQ White, arrest de-growth of the other 3 millennial brand and establishment of super premium to luxury portfolio of ABD Maestro.

items.statement: P&A category volume growth guided at high teens by FY28
items.quote: Through a combination of above, we expect P&A category to grow at high teens by FY28.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be at least equal to FY26 level of 14.4%
items.quote: The guidance that we are giving is that the FY27 overall margins, we should be hold on to the FY26, if not better it.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target raised to 18% by FY28
items.quote: Our guidance was 17% EBITDA margin by FY28. If you would notice, we have increased by 100 basis points to 18%, and we will stay with that guidance.

items.statement: Gross margin target of 48-50% over next 3 years
items.quote: From a level of 45% it would be my endeavour that over the next 3 years, we take it to 48% to 50% because gross margins in the alcobev space in India are still very low.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target to cross 20% over next 3 years
items.quote: Premiumization is the name of the game. EBITDA margin, hopefully with a 50% gross margin, I think should cross the 20% mark easily over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Return on capital target of ~25% over next 3 years
items.quote: The return on capital, which is a prudent capital allocation that I see should be in the region of 25% over the next 3 years.

items.statement: P&A volume contribution target >50% and value contribution 70-75% in 3 years
items.quote: The Premium and above segment, I believe that it should cross the 50% mark as far as volume is concerned. And as far as value is concerned, it should be between 70% to 75% mark.

items.statement: Phase 1 & 2 backward integration to add ~300 bps EBITDA margin by FY28 and ~100 bps by FY29
items.value: 300 bps by FY28, 100 bps by FY29
items.quote: Phase 1 and Phase 2 initiatives are expected to contribute approximately 300 basis points towards EBITDA margin enhancement by FY28, and an incremental margin improvement of nearly 100 basis points by FY29.

items.statement: UP bottling plant to eliminate ₹27 franchise fee per case in H2 FY27
items.quote: Our bottling unit that we are planning to put in UP, we have fairly large volume base there now. The ₹27 franchise fee will not be applicable. This will happen sometime in H2.

items.statement: ICONiQ White achieved 10.7 million cases in FY26, running at 12M+ cases ARR
items.quote: Continued success of ICONiQ White, which crossed a significant milestone and recorded sales of 10.7 million cases during FY26 and continues to be one of the fastest-growing millennial spirit brands globally.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 163 bps to 14.4%; standalone EBITDA margin expanded 267 bps to 15.5%
items.quote: We reported highest ever EBITDA of ₹568 crores, a growth of 25.8% over last year EBITDA of ₹451 crores, and EBITDA margin expanded by 163 basis points to 14.4%.

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth in CDMO for H1 FY27 with API prices at current levels; domestic branded formulations targeting IPM-level high single-digit to low double-digit growth; international branded formulations targeting double-dig
items.quote: At least for the H1, we see a strong volume growth and the API prices, I think, should remain at current levels. So that's how we look at the CDMO segment. The domestic marketing we talked about, we should be targeting an IPM level low single digit -- high single digit, low double-digit kind of growth in the domestic A

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR222 crores; FY27 capex target is INR300 crores, including expansion of oral solid facility.
items.quote: FY26, we did a capex of INR222 crores. And this year, we are targeting to keep our capex to INR300 crores. That's the target for our capex.

items.statement: FY27 revenue projected between Rs 2,150-2,200 crore, up from Rs 1,898 crore in FY26
items.quote: I think we are projected 15%, but I think we should be somewhere between Rs. 2,150 crores to Rs. 2,200 crores, which is very good.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target of Rs 2,500 crore reaffirmed
items.quote: And Rs. 2,500 crores for 27-28 as projected some years ago.

items.statement: Gujarat PEB plant Phase 1 operational by July 2026, Phase 2 by year-end; Andhra heavy structure plant Phase 1 by July-August 2026, Phases 2-3 accelerated to end of FY27
items.quote: As promised, both the pre-engineered building plant in Gujarat will be in play by July this year, and the heavy structure plant will also be in two phases in July and August. That will make it 40,000 tons and the plan currently is to add it to 60,000 tons by next November or December.

items.statement: Order book stands at over Rs 1,700 crore, up Rs 40-50 crore from last disclosure; Rs 102 crore order announced recently to be booked next quarter
items.quote: Our order book is over Rs. 1,700 crores right now compared to what it was in April. It is Rs. 40 crores, Rs. 50 crores higher than what it was last time we declared it. After that, as you know, we have announced another Rs. 102 crore order that we have received, but that will go into the next quarter.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin steady at 9.3% despite provisions and extra costs
items.quote: The total revenue for FY '26 is Rs. 1,898 crores compared to Rs. 1,453 crores, a growth of 31%. EBITDA Rs. 176 crores from Rs, 136 crores, 29% growth, very healthy. EBITDA margin steady at 9.3% in spite of these provisions that we had to make and the extra costs we had to incur.

items.statement: Pipeline 1 (orders finalizing within 60 days) at Rs 800-900 crore; Pipeline 2 (orders finalizing in 2-7 months) at Rs 3,500 crore; no slowdown seen
items.quote: Pipeline 1 would be about Rs. 700 crores to Rs. 800 crores, where orders would get finalized within the next 60 days. That would be approximately Rs. 800 crores to Rs. 900 crores currently. So, those are very serious at a serious stage. And Pipeline 2, where we have already bid for jobs, and we think it will be between

items.statement: Dividend of Rs 12.5 per share (125% of face value) recommended for FY26
items.quote: the directors have recommended a final dividend as of last year, Rs. 12.5, 125% of the share value.

items.statement: FY28 revenue guidance of Rs 2,500 crore includes HSS segment contribution
items.quote: See, HSS segment, we were not going to give a very major figure in anything because till we get into the market and till we start selling and till we see, like they say, the taste of the pudding is in the eating. items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% maintained, HSS contribution to be revised after plant commissioning
items.quote: You see, if everything goes in order, I think this year, we should be able to sell about 10,000 to 12,000 tons because the production will happen in July by the time we get into commercial production supply.

items.statement: Gujarat HSS plant Phase-1 commercial production by July 2026, Phase-2 to follow shortly after
items.quote: Trial production Wil start in June, and commercial production will start by July. We are very much on track, except that we lost that one month in the beginning.

items.statement: Fundraise via QIP or other route in next 2-3 months primarily for HSS plant Phase-2 and 3 acceleration
items.quote: We are going to raise funds. As we said, we are exploring, while we did take approval for QIP, we are exploring as to what s the best way to raise the fund when we require it.

items.statement: Order book at Rs 1,700 crore as of 30 April 2026, executable in ~9 months, primarily PEB
items.quote: Rs. 1,700 crores. As of 30th April 2026, it is Rs. 1,700 crores? Yes. To be executed in about 9 months, yes.

items.statement: FY27 PAT margin expected at 7-7.5%, similar to current levels despite growth investments
items.quote: Yes, 7% to 7.5%. Yes, net. By what, we don't know.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target >10% long-term, currently ~9.3% (9.7% ex one-offs), driven by value-chain move and productivity
items.quote: I think the chances of being on the upside is very high, that we should grow. And that is the target. I mean, 9%, 9.5%, 10%, I don't think is a very good margin for a company which does all that we do.

items.statement: Steel price volatility averages out over 4 quarters; each job uniquely priced with forward cost estimates
items.quote: We don't have an automatic formula that just price everything at Rs. 60 or Rs. 70. No. We price every job as a unique individual job, where we see what are the materials required?

items.statement: Export revenue target Rs 100 crore in FY27 (currently Rs 30-35 crore in hand), North America JV to ramp over 1-1.5 years
items.quote: If [ were to make a very wild guess, I would say that our aim should be to get at least Rs. 100 crores of orders. In export, that would be our aim.

items.statement: Key risk is manpower shortage at sites and plants; addressing via better worker care, automation and robotics
items.quote: I think the biggest challenge that India will face, and then of course everybody will face, is the manpower. So, I think how well prepared we are to pick up that challenge.

items.statement: Tax rate normalized to ~25% from FY27 after one-time 27% hit in Q4 FY26 due to Section 145A method change
items.quote: But going forward, it will be back to normal. So, instead of, say, 25% tax as we should have paid or 24% we paid last year, I think it went up to about 27%.

items.statement: Working capital improvement focus: tightening payment terms, higher advances, milestone-based collections for large orders
items.quote: So, we are also tightening up the processes at the time we are taking orders to make sure that the payments come faster and the customers do meet their milestones.

items.statement: Sixth PEB plant land acquired; combined PEB capacity Rs 3,000 cr + HSS Rs 500 cr by FY27-28 end
items.quote: We have bought the land recently for the second PEB plant, if we want to have it. We bought the land last month next to our existing land.

items.statement: Management does not provide specific growth guidance; growth is an outcome of profitable customer acquisition
items.quote: We generally don't give growth guidance I think this is we've typically helped you guys to plot how to look at the business, how it will scale, etc. But we have decided not to give guidance on our numbers.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin stabilized around 31% in Q4 FY26 vs peak 36% in Q1 FY26 due to stepped-up investments in growth businesses
items.quote: I think we peaked in terms of profitability say back in say Q1 of FY26 almost 36% of say adjusted EBITDA margin and now we have sort of stabilized around 31% odd.

items.statement: Vehicle finance business expected to exit investment mode and start generating cash flows by end of FY27
items.quote: Vehicle finance business probably by the end of this financial year would no longer be in the investment mode and would start probably churning cash flows which will also enable us to move that into a core business kind of a trajectory from a narrative perspective.

items.statement: Vehicle finance assets managed by partners at ~600 crores; ~10% on Blackbuck's own books for new experiments and partner onboarding
items.quote: Close to 600 crores is the assets managed by our partners overall in our books. About 10 percentage is basically on our books.

items.statement: Tolling GTV grew 27% YoY in FY26 vs industry NETC CV growth of 16%, driven by product and distribution strength
items.quote: The GTV of tolling for us in the last full year grew at about 27% on a year-on-year basis in a very matured and penetrated industry largely driven by a strong product play and a distribution play.

items.statement: AIS telematics device sales doubled in Q4 FY26 driven by mandates across 10 states and strong distribution
items.quote: The sales of the AIS vertical doubled during the last quarter which was largely driven by mandates and largely driven by a strong distribution and a product play.

items.statement: Super loads mature hubs (Bangalore, Hyderabad) show strengthening unit economics; 10 new cities growing faster than established ones due to network effects
items.quote: Our mature or let's say our first hubs of Bangalore and Hyderabad, we continue to scale, continue to double down and these continue to show signs of strength from a unit economics from a scale perspective.

items.statement: Growth businesses are contribution margin positive on every order; EBITDA-level losses due to scaling investments in manpower, technology, and AI
items.quote: So, most or all our businesses across regardless they are new or experiments or whatever we are always contribution margin positive. We make money on every order we do so if orders scale our profitability converges.

items.statement: OMC loyalty program suspension temporarily impacts fuel business; similar hiccups occurred before and resolved
items.quote: One small narrative on that which is a very direct impact is as you know that we have a fuel business which is basically built on top of the loyalty program which OMC's work on and they have suspended their loyalty program temporarily.

items.statement: MLFF tolling framework remains prepaid (99%+ payments prepaid); Blackbuck exploring acquirer-side participation opportunities
items.quote: Whatever offline information we've received we believe 99% plus of the payments are prepaid.

items.statement: FY26: Total income ~715 crores (+55% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA ~190 crores (+84% YoY), PAT 160 crores (first full year profitability), Free cash flow ~185-190 crores
items.quote: On a Gross Income level we've done close to about 715 crores in total income which is growth of about 55% on a year-on-year basis. On a EBITDA basis we have done close to 190 crores which is a 84% growth on a year-on-year basis. This is our first full year of profitability at a PAT level. We have done 160 crores in PAT

items.statement: Monthly transacting customers grew 13% YoY to 8.2 lakh; power users (2+ services) grew 22% YoY; daily app engagement ~45 minutes
items.quote: We grew in our transacting customers by 13% on a year -on-year basis to close to 8.2 lakh monthly transacting customers across the whole year. Users who use more than two services who are our power users, we've compounded at 22% year on year.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated EBITDA target north of INR 500 crores
items.quote: I would say that we did a consol EBITDA of about INR 280 crores FY26. We are looking at north of INR 500 crores for the FY27 EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Punjab Phase 2 expansion targeting commissioning by end of FY27

items.quote: As such after the Phase 2, if you realize we still have the cotton expansion that is coming up in MP where we should be on the ground post the monsoons.
