items.statement: Technical yarn capacity doubling at Silvassa from 9,000 to 18,000 MTPA, commissioning by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: As communicated earlier, we are progressing with the doubling of our technical yarn capacity at Silvassa from 9,000 metric tons per annum to 18,000 metric tons per annum, which we believe will further strengthen our position in higher value textile applications.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improvement expected in FY27 as Punjab stabilizes and product mix improves
items.quote: We anticipate this will translate into stronger operating margins, better absorption of depreciation and interest cost and healthier free cash flow generation over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Punjab facility gross margins expected to improve substantially from Q2 FY27 as supply chain settles and value-added mix increases
items.quote: Yes, see once we ramp up fully, I mean we are ramped up fully, but once we settle the supply chain and the product line-up everything, you will from the second quarter FY27, you will see the substantial change in that.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through underway after war-related volatility; polyester spreads cautiously constructive
items.quote: But because whenever there is a high volatility, it becomes a little difficult to pass on immediately, which stabilizes over a period of time. That is exactly what happened and we have passed on now in the process of passing on the entire hike of raw materials.

items.statement: Domestic yarn demand robust post-war volatility; long-term structural drivers from man-made fiber shift remain intact
items.quote: Demand scenario, the last quarter after the war, yes, downstream people also because of the volatility in the crude prices and the raw material prices were a little disturbed. But they are back to base and we see very robust demand coming in now also.

items.statement: Peak gross debt at INR 1,500 crores; targeting INR 100-125 crores annual repayment with no major new debt planned
items.quote: This is our peak gross debt level and we are expecting a payouts of close to INR 100 to INR 125 crores every year. And we don't plan to take any big debt in the near future.

items.statement: Gas cost at Silvassa up 50-60% but only 6-7% of operational cost; Punjab uses agri-waste unaffected by gas prices
items.quote: As far as Silvassa is concerned, yes, we use gas for heating. There definitely the cost of gas has gone up by about 60%, 50% to 60% of the cost of gas. So that is affecting our cost of heating at Silvassa but not at the Punjab facility.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR350 cr: INR90 cr for pump/motor automation & capacity; rest for solar module expansion to 2.1 GW + backward integration
items.quote: By the end of this year, I think we will infuse around INR350 crores of total capex this year in FY27.

items.statement: SteriPort capacity expansion from 6.6 crore to 12 crore bottles/year expected operational by 20th June 2026
items.quote: With utilization levels remaining healthy, we are now expanding capacity from 6.6 crore bottles per year to roughly 12 crore bottles per year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 24-25% for FY27 driven by SteriPort expansion (27% margin) and solar savings
items.quote: The new product line is expected to have about 27% EBITDA margin only for SteriPort. So combining the new and the existing, on an average basis we will be expecting between 24% to 25% EBITDA margin going forward.

items.statement: PAT margin expected to improve from 5% to 8-9% as debt repayment reduces finance costs
items.quote: Once we leverage in the current year then going forward, it will be improving by at least 3%.

items.statement: Polymer prices up 60-70%; price increase of INR 1.25-1.75/bottle (5-6% on selling price) implemented with no resistance
items.quote: We are witnessing roughly 60% to 70% increase in input cost, both the grades: polyethylene and polypropylene. And the impact per container would vary from roughly INR1.25 to INR1.75.

items.statement: SteriPort contributes 42% of revenue; SVP portfolio (inhalation, preservative-free ophthalmics) contributes 20% of SVP revenue
items.quote: Our SteriPort platform, a product that continues to gain strong traction in the market, contributes nearly 42% of the revenue from operations.

items.statement: No long-term contracts with hospital chains; pricing is one-sided favoring buyers, but price increases passed through immediately
items.quote: In Indian context, the contracts typically tend to be one-sided. If we enter into a contract with a hospital chain like say, Apollo, if it favors them then they will trigger all the covenants, but if it is working against them then probably they would stop buying from you.

items.statement: Debt reduced from INR 234 crores to INR 204 crores post March 2026; 90% borrowing now at single-digit rates; further INR 30-40 crores debt replacement planned
items.quote: We should still be able to replace around INR30 crores to INR40 crores of debt with lower interest rate in next six months also.

items.statement: No annual order book; export visibility 3-6 months; exports 39% of FY26 revenue (up from 32% in FY25)
items.quote: In year '25-'26, our total export was around 39% of the revenue.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 120-125 days currently, targeting 110 days; receivables improved due to early payments ahead of price hikes
items.quote: Our current working capital cycle is about 100-plus days. To be precise, it will be ranging between 120 to 125 days and we expect it to go about 110 days in near future.

items.statement: PLA plant to be commissioned in Q3 of this year; future expansions possible in about 15 months.
items.quote: 15 odd months is very possible. 15 months is very possible. And we look to commission in the third quarter of this year.

items.statement: PLA project capex revised to INR3,080 crore; lacto-gypsum gypsum board plant approved at Kumbhi.
items.quote: we had an investor call on the PLA project post our fundraise, which was going to revise capex at INR3,080 crore.

items.statement: Board approved INR450 crore preferential share issue; promoters subscribed INR193 crore, no dilution.
items.quote: the Board has approved raising of INR450 crore through issue of preferential shares to fund the capex as well as general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Aspiring to 35% EBITDA margin on PLA; incentives are below EBITDA and not counted in guidance.
items.quote: we had earlier stated that we are aspiring to make 35% of EBITDA margin. The incentives are largely in the form of capital subsidy and interest subvention.

items.statement: No ethanol price revision for juice and B-heavy routes in three years despite higher cane costs; expects revision now.
items.quote: the problem is the absence of revision of ethanol prices under the juice and B-heavy route for the last 3 years, despite higher cane costs and operational expenses.

items.statement: UP sugar prices broadly Rs 41-42/kg; expects prices steady and gradually rising on low closing stock.
items.quote: In UP, prices have broadly remained in the range of Rs. 41 to Rs. 42 per kg. We believe prices would remain steady and gradually probably inch up based on the data points given to you on the closing inventory.

items.statement: Government looking at raising blending beyond E20; E85/E100 draft notification out for public comments.
items.quote: And for E85 and E100, automobile companies are ready with the prototype. Government has also come out with the draft notification for public comments.

items.statement: FY26 ethanol output about 27 crore liters; existing capacity can reach 34-35 crore liters.
items.quote: For Balrampur, in the year gone by, that is FY26, we produced around 27 crore liter of ethanol. And with our existing nameplate capacity, we can reach around 34 crore- 35 crore liters of capacity.

items.statement: Industry has ethanol overcapacity; government addressing it by pushing demand beyond E20.
items.quote: At the industry level, definitely there is an overcapacity. To address that, government is coming out how to increase the demand by way of going beyond E20, E85, E100.

items.statement: Crop yield uncertain due to fertilizer availability; honest assessment only after September, best in mid-August.
items.quote: If you want an honest answer to this question, do not ask anybody before September. But yes, if there is a negative tenor to the crop yield, probably some rainfall quantum etc, best assessed in August, mid-August.

items.statement: Rising crude lifts fossil-based plastic and PLA prices, favorable for the company.
items.quote: owing to the current crude price rise, the PLA prices have moved north and that is good for us.

items.statement: PLA plant built to handle multiple grades and applications; barrier properties and food safety validated.
items.quote: Our plant is built well to handle different grades, different applications, etc.

items.statement: PLA customer offtake agreements nearing finalization; customers await commercial production before switching suppliers.
items.quote: Because everything is nearing finalization, and to give you, you know, let it get finalized. We are very near to everything.

items.statement: Government mandate on non-plastic expected sooner than later, not six months away; central, UP and customer fronts progressing.
items.quote: We are hoping that it will be sooner than later. No, I am not looking at 6 months from now.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance retained at more than 15%
items.quote: So, we are retaining our revenue growth of more than 15%. So definitely, we are going to have more than 15% as a revenue growth for '26-'27.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance set at more than 28%
items.quote: EBITDA margins will be more than 28%.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow guidance of more than INR 55,000 crores including QRSAM
items.quote: The order inflow we are expecting this year more than INR55,000 crores. That includes, of course, QRSAM, which we are expecting very soon.

items.statement: FY27 R&D investment target of around INR 2,200 crores
items.quote: So, this year, we have targeted a value of around INR2,200 crores investment in R&D.

items.statement: FY27 capex target of more than INR 1,200 crores with 20%+ growth
items.quote: And same thing is the capex also, again, 20%-plus growth. So, we are targeting more than INR1,200 crores as a capital investment for this year.

items.statement: New technology programs will bring higher margins due to increased value addition
items.quote: Firstly, let me tell you, margins should be better only when new technologies comes in because new technology means more value addition.

items.statement: QRSAM contract expected to be signed by June 2026 with first production model within 18 months
items.quote: So, we are confident that in next 1, 1.5 months, it should be over. Worst case, it may slip by 1 more month. So, we are not expecting more than that delay as of today. And regarding the program, once we sign the program within 18 months, we are supposed to give the first of production model.

items.statement: Export order book at USD 96 million; targeting export share growth from 4-5% to >10% over 4-5 years
items.quote: We have around USD96 million order book for this year and subsequent year. Some of the orders are to be executed in 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Expects improved profitability and top-line growth in Chemicals for the year.
items.quote: And for the year at least, we see that we should have improved profitability and also top-line growth.

items.statement: Hopes to more than double performance chemicals business this year.
items.quote: And we are hoping, that I'm not projecting, but we are hoping for in excess of doubling this business this year and maybe continue, if we continue to do our projects well, continue to maintain that momentum for years to come.

items.statement: Expects Potable Spirits EBIT margin to be maintained and improved via premiumization.
items.quote: So, I would imagine that there is no reason for us to believe that we should be able to maintain these margins and in for the effort that we put in mix, we will try and improve it.

items.statement: JV share of net profit expected to improve drastically.
items.quote: So this year, which you are seeing that INR46.42 crores share of net profit from the JV, I think that will improve drastically.

items.statement: Plans to sell 24% more JV equity in FY29, making Chemicals debt-free.
items.quote: And as I have already told that in '28-'29, we are going to sell out 24% more equity as per the agreement.

items.statement: Ennature Biopharma may not see significant EBITDA improvement this financial year.
items.quote: So, this is broadly in terms of nicotine, I mean, I would say, the business right now is in the focus, but in terms of the EBITDA improvement, we may not see the significant improvement in this financial year, but definitely the investment and the growth and the customer acquisition what we're doing right now is going

items.statement: FY26 capex ~INR830 crores, mainly two grain distilleries (Gorakhpur, Kashipur) ~INR400 crores.
items.quote: Actually, there are two distilleries largely, which are the main capital expenditure. One is the grain distillery in Gorakhpur, and one is the grain distillery in Kashipur. So, basically, out of whatever amount you are saying, about INR400 crores is out of these two distilleries capitalization.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 15.5%, up 162 bps; PAT margin 6.9%, up 84 bps.
items.quote: EBITDA has been INR654 crores, which is up 24.5% over last year. And the EBITDA margin itself is up to 15.5%, up 162 basis points.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 17.1%, up 5 bps; including other income ~20.8%.
items.quote: In EBITDA terms, it is INR167 crores, which is up 13.3%, and the EBITDA margin at 17.1%, is up five basis points.

items.statement: Grain prices stable/lower; mid-last year ~INR24/kg, last quarter ~INR21-22/kg.
items.quote: And the grain prices have been stable, and if I may just state to you, in the middle of last year, grain prices were running close to INR24 a kilo. And then in the last quarter of last year, they were running close to between INR21 and INR22 or, INR21 plus minus.

items.statement: Government may increase ethanol blending beyond 20% and promote flexi vehicles.
items.quote: And there are discussions with increasing talk about securing India's energy, reducing forex outflows, of probably increasing it beyond 20%.

items.statement: Potable Spirits: IMFL ~25% of pie, IMIL ~75%; focus to grow IMFL premium.
items.quote: Approximately 25% of the pie is towards IMFL and 75% towards India Made Indian Liquor. But we have definite focus to improve the IMFL part of it without losing focus of the IMIL part.

items.statement: War impacts exports to Middle East (e.g., New Park oilfield chemicals) and raises feedstock costs/availability.
items.quote: And as far as exports is concerned, it has impacted us adversely because for big customers like New Park, where we send our oilfield chemicals largely to the Middle East, that business is largely on hold.

items.statement: Prepaid INR804 crores debt in Q4, funded by INR467 crores equity and cash flow; saves INR20 crores interest.
items.quote: One point is that the company has prepaid almost about INR804 crores in this quarter, which has been funded by INR467 crores through equity issue, which we did in November '25 and rest of the funds has been put in through the cash flow.

items.statement: FY27 cement demand growth expected at about 6%.
items.quote: Overall, we see that FY26-'27 cement demand is going likely to grow at about 6% or so.

items.statement: FY27 capacity addition estimated at 45-50 million tons, down from 64 million tons last year.
items.quote: So '26 -'27 estimated to be about -- again, our estimation is about around 45 million to 50 million tons, right? Last year, it was about 64 million tons.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected at INR1,500-1,700 crores.
items.quote: We expect total capex in FY27 to be around INR1,500 crores to INR1,700 crores

items.statement: FY28 capex expected close to INR2,000 crores.
items.quote: and close to INR2,000 crores in the next year when we would be also taking up the -- we have already started, but it will ramp up the land acquisition and the project in Kutch and Nagaur.

items.statement: FY29 capex expected at INR1,000-1,500 crores.
items.quote: and maybe INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores in the FY '29.

items.statement: Durg expansion (including grinding units) expected by end of FY28.
items.quote: We are expecting the Durg first to come by FY28 towards the end of that year, FY28.

items.statement: Northeast project expected one year after Durg, around FY29.
items.quote: And one year later, the Northeast project should also be there and followed by the greenfield there thereafter.

items.statement: Kutch project expected by FY30.
items.quote: Kutch is for sure FY30.

items.statement: Confident to achieve 30 million ton capacity by 2030.
items.quote: So, we are reasonably confident that we'll achieve 30 million ton by 2030.

items.statement: Aim to reduce EBITDA per ton gap with leaders by INR50-75 in FY27.
items.quote: And I'm sure that it is going to reduce at least by another INR50 to INR75 for sure.

items.statement: Energy cost expected to rise by at least INR300 per ton and packaging cost by INR80-100 per ton.
items.quote: Energy costs are expected to rise by about at least INR300 and packaging cost about INR80 to INR100 per ton, and that is going to impact maybe in coming quarters because of this geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 cost inflation expected at INR100-130 per ton, with INR300 impact in Q2.
items.quote: But this quarter, definitely, I see somewhere around maybe INR100 to INR120 or INR130 a ton.

items.statement: April demand was better; May initially sluggish but improving from May 15 onwards.
items.quote: April was better. May initially, it was sluggish because of combination of reasons. And of course, I think there was a big uncertainty around this geopolitical conflict also and that has got rubbed on the cement industry as well. But May 15 onwards, I see a little bit green shoots in demand in the month of May.

items.statement: Blended cement ratio was 62% in FY26; plan to improve to 65%.
items.quote: If I improve blended cement ratio, which was 62% last year, if I take to 65% and 94% of clinker utilization to about around, let's say, 97%, 98%.

items.statement: Top line should grow to INR4,000-5,000 crores with exports contributing more than current share.
items.quote: So overall, as you rightly mentioned the forecast with the domestic market growth, export and all other initiatives that we are taking up, the top line should grow in the order of rough order of INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores with export being a large -- better than the current contribution what we have today.

items.statement: Phase 1 and 1A capacity expansion to be completed by end of December 2026.
items.quote: So as we committed to you, the Phase 1 and I would say, Phase 1 and 1A, that's what we call is that capacity will be completed by end of December '26.

items.statement: Next phase of capex investment to be finalized in next 6 to 9 months based on domestic and export outlook.
items.quote: And then that's what we were telling to earlier question that in next 6 to 9 months, we'll be coming and forming up our next phase of capex -- capex investment based on both the domestic and export market outlook.

items.statement: Capex spend in upcoming year expected to be similar to last year's INR70 crores.
items.quote: So, we'll be almost similar range of capex spend will be there in the upcoming year as well.

items.statement: Industry expected to remain 400,000+ units in FY27, with Q1 and Q2 typically softer.
items.quote: And the next year as well, we are expecting it to be 400 plus.

items.statement: Australia subsidiary CODB is about 500K-600K per month, to reduce further after eliminating warehousing.
items.quote: As of now, the CODB is about 500K or 600K per month, which includes significant warehousing, rental costs and all, which would also further reduce once the warehousing costs have been eliminated.

items.statement: Water heater launched in FY26; revenue to grow with wider geographic spread and full product suite.
items.quote: it was a launch year. So the revenue wasn't anything to write home about. But in the coming year, we are sort of going to -- it's a long haul. It's going to be a long process. And in the years to come, we will sort of work our way up the revenue chain.

items.statement: No pricing pressure despite cost pressure; gross margin maintained at 46% consolidated.
items.quote: gross margin on a quarterly consolidated basis was about 46 % in line with year before despite there has been major turmoil and summer -related disturbances. So neither there has been a pricing pressure, and despite cost pressure, we have due to a variety of strategies and initiatives, maintained that.

items.statement: US business sales in FY26 were about ₹45 crores; potential is at least ₹140 crores.
items.quote: In FY '26, U.S. business sales was about ₹45 crores. I don't have the EBITDA margin handy right now, but by and large, it is in line with our domestic business.

items.statement: Passing on cost increases; only 10% achieved, remaining 90% over next two quarters.
items.quote: So, we are at 10% as we talk. So, 90% has to be achieved on realizing this price. So, it will happen over next 2 quarters, this quarter and next quarter.

items.statement: Revenue to outgrow market; no specific percentage guidance provided.
items.quote: I don't think we can give you a percentage guidance either on the bottom line or the top line. I can tell you we will outgrow the market.

items.statement: Capex to be 8-10% of revenue, similar to prior year.
items.quote: Similar lines 8%, 9%, 10%.

items.statement: Rail expansion capex of INR120+ crores; production to start by November-December 2026.
items.quote: So yes, we are roughly at INR120-plus crores for capex. Last week I was in Jamshedpur. So we should be able to produce by November this year, so by November this year.

items.statement: Bharuch plant utilization to reach 70% by July-August 2026.
items.quote: I think with the PPAPs going on, we should be July, August, we should start seeing utilization of about 70%.

items.statement: Demand stable across key segments; not a concern.
items.quote: So overall, for me, the current top three worries, demand is not a worry.

items.statement: Cost escalation and pass-through is top priority risk.
items.quote: Cost escalation and passing it on, obviously, is our top priority, ramping up Bharuch new plant, PPAP is second.

items.statement: Order book healthy; core domestic and export CV bullish.
items.quote: And the order book is healthy. So, core domestic and export commercial vehicle is pretty much bullish.

items.statement: Process industry and distribution to grow faster than rail and mobile.
items.quote: But to your direct answer, definitely process distribution, these are going to be strong growth followed by rail and -- followed by mobile and rail.

items.statement: Manufactured vs traded mix to remain around 65:35 for next 2-3 years.
items.quote: So, I would say that 65%-35% might be there for next 2, 3 years, easy, but the pie will keep on increasing.

items.statement: Board approved merger of Timken GGB with Timken India for synergies.
items.quote: the Board has approved the merger of Timken GGB with Timken India Limited. This will help drive operational synergies, improve effectiveness and reduce, obviously, overall cost.

items.statement: Bharuch plant generated INR80 crores revenue in FY26; Q4 alone ~INR60 crores.
items.quote: So for the full year, it was almost INR80 crores revenue coming out of the new plant.

items.statement: GGB entity Q4 revenue INR16.6 crores, PBT INR4.6 crores (32% margin).
items.value: INR16.6 crores revenue, INR4.6 crores PBT
items.quote: So GGB if you look at the results which we have announced for the quarter, the revenue was INR16.6 crores and the profit before tax was INR4.6 crores.

items.statement: Domestic business targeting 10% volume growth for FY27.
items.quote: So on the domestic business, we are working towards the 10% volume growth year-over-year.

items.statement: Domestic realizations expected to improve 2-3% in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: I think another 2% to 3% improvement in average realization will be seen in quarter one in the domestic front.

items.statement: Edible oil business expected to see healthy double-digit growth in FY27.
items.quote: So we'll see a healthy double-digit, I would say, growth in the category this financial year.

items.statement: Export demand expected to double once Middle East war settles.
items.quote: So once the war is settled, I think the exports will double up in next six months because there has been a big gap as far as food reserves are concerned.

items.statement: Middle East inventory replenishment expected as logistics improve.
items.quote: Inventory levels in several Middle Eastern markets have reduced over the last few months due to shipment disruptions and therefore, we expect demand replenishment as logistical stability improves.

items.statement: Unsold rice inventory has 8-9% margin potential at current prices.
items.quote: And the stocks which are lying with us, which are unsold. So I do not talk about the unsold, there is a very good margin. There is a margin of around 8% to 9% as far as the prices are concerned.

items.statement: Middle East buyers accepting higher freight costs due to limited alternatives.
items.quote: Despite this elevated logistics and insurance cost, buyer across the Middle East have broadly accepted the higher freight environment, largely because there are currently limited alternatives available to maintain continuity of food supplies in the region.

items.statement: Potential deficient monsoon could tighten paddy availability and support prices.
items.quote: However, any meaningful weather disruption could tighten paddy availability and support stronger price realization in the coming season.

items.statement: Branded non-basmati growing at 4x overall domestic business rate.
items.quote: The non -basmati trajectory is particularly noteworthy from INR197 crores to I NR271 crores in a single year, growing at nearly 4x the rate of the overall domestic business.

items.statement: Company hedges 80% of export sales to manage forex risk.
items.quote: As far as the devaluation of the currency is concerned, we have a policy in the company to book 80% whatever we sell.

items.statement: Dividend of 450% of face value approved, subject to AGM approval.
items.quote: A dividend of 450% of face value translating into INR103 crores has been approved by the Boa rd and is subject to shareholder approval in the upcoming AGM.

items.statement: Inventory of 530,000 tons rice equivalent as of March 31, 2026.
items.quote: So in rice equivalent terms, as of March 31, we were carrying about 530,000 tons of inventory.

items.statement: Net bank borrowings negative INR789 crores as of March 31, 2026.
items.quote: Net bank borrowings, including treasury investments was at a negative INR789 crores as of March 31, '26, as against a negative INR405 crores last year.

items.statement: Real estate Samalkha land parcel under evaluation for warehousing or monetization.
items.quote: Regarding the Samalkha District Panipat land parcel, we continue to assess various monetization and development options.

items.statement: Management aims to reach 17-18% EBITDA margin in the next couple of years, excluding Comfort Click.
items.quote: I think there are no new numbers. We've talked about in the next couple of years, we hope to get to our 17-18. Now we have without Comfort Click. So those numbers stay and we focused on getting there.

items.statement: Comfort Click business became EPS accretive in Q4 FY26 and is expected to remain so for the next two years.
items.quote: As far as Q4 is concerned, on Comfort Click business itself, we have become EPS accretive.

items.statement: Comfort Click gross margin is above company average and has improved post-acquisition.
items.quote: On the gross margin front, I think even on the portfolio at Comfort Click, we have improved our gross margin. And the Comfort Click gross margin is over indexed to the company's gross margin.

items.statement: Operating leverage will play out on the entire business excluding Comfort Click, which is a variable spend business.
items.quote: As far as operating leverage is concerned, it is likely to play out on the entire business ex - Comfort Click, because as we told earlier also that Comfort Click is largely variable spend business.

items.statement: Domestic business grew 1.7% in Q4 FY26; skin and hair care grew 39.7%, food and nutrition grew 9.4%, seasonal brands declined 9.8%.
items.quote: Within the domestic business, the seasonal brands declined by 9.8%, whereas the skin and hair care brands registered a growth of 39.7%, and food and nutrition brands grew by 9.4%.

items.statement: Organized channel saliency improved to 30% in FY26 from 24% in FY25, driven by premiumization and modern trade/e-commerce growth.
items.quote: The domestic business continued to witness a steady shift towards organized channel, with saliency improving to 30% in financial year '26 from 24% in financial year '25, driven by premiumization as well as strong growth in modern trade and e-commerce channels.

items.statement: Quick commerce contributes 7-8% of total domestic business and ~45% of e-commerce; company is fit-for-purpose across channels.
items.quote: So overall, online - sorry modern trade plus e -commerce, organized trade is about 30% of our domestic business. Quick commerce will be 7%-8%.

items.statement: RiteBite Max Protein expanded into RTD beverage, ghee jaggery bars, and Korean flavor chips to widen consumption occasions.
items.quote: Under the RiteBite Max Protein franchise, we expanded its offering with the launch of Max Protein Ultimate Protein Boost Ready -to-Drink beverage, Max Protein Roots Ghee Jaggery Bar and Korean flavor chips with multiple flavors.

items.statement: Glucon-D entered performance hydration segment with Recharge in liquid and sachet formats; initial response encouraging.
items.quote: Under Glucon-D, we entered a performance hydration segment with the launch of Recharge across two formats, liquid in orange and green apple flavors, and sachets in orange and lime flavors, targeting active and health-conscious consumers. Initial response has been encouraging.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY27-28 will be in the 25% bracket; FY27 will be a mix of cash tax and deferred tax asset utilization.
items.quote: So FY 27- 28 will be in the 25% bracket. But 26-27, it will be kind of cash plus deferred tax asset used. So the mix of two.

items.statement: No plans to divest slow-growing categories; capital allocation is appropriate across brands.
items.quote: I think our allocation of funds are appropriate to the brand. So I don't see any major changes. I think all brands have appropriate funding required. So there's no other plans or any other changes to the business.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at ~INR 1,750 crore, split into sustaining and growth capex.
items.quote: For FY27, we have planned a total capital expenditure of approximately INR 1,750 crores, comprising of around INR 650 crores towards sustaining capex and around INR 1,100 crores towards growth capex and balance towards land acquisition.

items.statement: New greenfield EV powertrain plant in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar with INR 550 crore investment, commissioned by Q2 FY28.
items.quote: The project involves a total estimated investment of INR 550 crores to be funded through a mix of debt and equity. Capital expenditure will be phased over the next 2, 3 years with the facilit y expected to be commissioned by second quarter of FY 28.

items.statement: New 2-wheeler lighting order with annual peak value ~INR 450 crore, SOP in H2 FY28.
items.quote: A key highlight during the quarter was the receipt of a significant new order for unserved models, with an annual peak value of approximately INR 450 crores for the supply of 2-wheeler lighting products, with SOP scheduled in second half of FY 28.

items.statement: New seating export orders with annual peak value ~INR 390 crore from 3 Europe/North America CV customers, supplies from FY28.

items.statement: Additional sunroof order with annual peak value ~INR 85 crore, total sunroof order book over INR 350 crore.
items.quote: Further strengthening our order book, we secured an additional order wi th an annual peak value of estimated to be INR 85 crores, taking the total sunroof order book potential to over INR 350 crores.

items.statement: Discussing with customers to shorten price adjustment cycle from half-year to monthly/quarterly due to abnormal commodity and labor cost inflation.
items.quote: So we have been discussing with our customers, how do we cut our price adjustment cycle? Can we cut half year to monthly, if possible, quarter to monthly ? items.statement: Labor cost increase in Haryana and Gujarat expected to impact ~INR 200 crore; working to mitigate with customers.
items.quote: So the impact is obviously quite significant. It's almost like a couple of hundred crores for what we call Haryana and Gujarat. But still, there are some more which we expect to come on.

items.statement: Near-term moderation in alloy wheel penetration due to customer vehicle mix shift to entry-level models and steel wheel adoption.
items.quote: From a demand standpoint, we are seeing some near-term moderation in alloy wheel penetration in our customers. items.statement: Exports from India expected to cross INR 1,500 crore in next few years from ~INR 600 crore last year.
items.quote: So this INR 600 crores, coupled with all the significant new business wins what we have shared, definitely in next few years, we do expect this to cross INR 1,500 crores mark based on what we know now.

items.statement: INR 2,500 crore fundraising is an enabling resolution, no specific plan currently.
items.quote: So Neel, if that's the only question, I'm assuming, this is only an enabling resolution we take every year. Even last year, we have done it. And this is a mix of all the instruments. It is not necessarily equity. It also covers NCDs and some other borrowings.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 24-25% at current market levels.
items.quote: And FY '27 guidance, see at current market level, we should be able to do somewhere about 24%-25% at EBITDA levels, at current market levels.

items.quote: Yes, including the balance of CRM, balance of your battery storage and little bit of solar, you can consider CAPEX of close to about INR 1,500 crores to INR 2,000 crores for FY '27.

items.statement: Healthy six-month order book for RR Ispat rolled products.

items.statement: Mining cost guidance INR 3,000-3,200 per ton for FY27; reduction expected from Q3-Q4.

items.statement: High-grade pellet mix to improve from Q3 FY27 post-monsoon as mining ramps up.
items.quote: But that will happen from Q3 onwards as the mining production starts going up post-monsoons.

items.statement: BESS first line commissioning by March 2027; FY28 output 5-6 GWh, scaling to 17-18 GWh by third year.

items.statement: BESS business margins currently 12-13%, conservative estimate 7-8%.

items.statement: CRM complex first line commissioning by end Q4 FY27/early Q1 FY28; FY28 utilization 50% (3-3.5 lakh tons), FY29 90%.
items.quote: We are hopeful to commission the first line by end of Q4, early Q1 in next financial year. And that is why we have taken a very conservative guidance of 50%, which is at about 3-3.5 lakh tons of CRM complex for FY '28.

items.statement: Merchant pellet players solely dependent on market iron ore may face margin squeeze.
items.quote: But there will be a challenge to merchant pellet players who are solely dependent on market for purchase of iron ore. We can definitely see a squeeze in margins for them.

items.quote: So, from FY '25 perspective, you'd see a quarter -on-quarter growth in quarters. But if you look at it historically, it will again be a back -ended H2 year for us.

items.statement: Margins expected to remain stable around 25% EBITDA, with mix-driven fluctuations.
items.quote: I'm very comfortable with our margins of what is 25% plus EBITDA. And sometimes it will go higher, sometimes it will go a little lower.

items.statement: No margin impact from commodity price increases due to rate contracts and pass-throughs.
items.quote: But we do not see that impacting both our supply chain procurement or therefore, our margins.

items.statement: Enquiry book nearly doubled to 18 GW for product segment; India up 100% to 7 GW.
items.quote: And that enquiry book for the product segment of 18 GW is, of course, nearly double of what it was in FY '25. The Indian market itself has also increased in its enquiry book by about 100% odd over this past year to about 7 -odd GW for us.

items.statement: U.S. subsidiary had ₹8 crore loss in FY26; expected to be profitable or breakeven in FY27.
items.quote: Though the full year itself, as you will see from the annual report when it's out and the subsidiary accounts still had a loss of about ₹8 odd crores in that subsidiary. In the coming year, we anticipate not only for that to reverse, but for it to be profitable, largely driven by greater execution.

items.statement: Receivables at ₹6.39 billion; expected to remain high in FY27 due to back-ended execution.
items.quote: receivables at the end of March 31, 2026, stood at ₹6.39 billion, primarily reflecting the execution profile of certain large projects as well as the billing, which was skewed towards the end of March, which will be liquidated in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Exports expected to exceed domestic in FY27; U.S. Aftermarket to contribute more to revenue.
items.quote: So as Mr. Nikhil said, we are looking at Aftermarket contributing more to the revenue in FY '27. Some of the product orders might take some time to execute, but we are quite confident that the conversions will be good.

items.statement: FY27 gross margin improvement target of 40-50 bps YoY; EBITDA margin improvement target of 50-75 bps YoY
items.value: 40-50 bps gross margin; 50-75 bps EBITDA margin

items.statement: Mid-single-digit revenue growth outlook for FY27; profit growth targeted at close to 10%
items.quote: we're maintaining mid-single-digit growth outlook for the current year and then close to about 10% or so plus broad growth in the profits.

items.statement: Capex during FY26 reduced by more than half compared to FY25, reflecting disciplined capital allocation
items.quote: Capex during the year was almost reduced by more than half compared to FY 2025, reflecting disciplined capital allocation.

items.statement: BCG-led cost transformation (Project PULSE) targeting ₹40-50 crores annual procurement savings and similar opex savings; AI-enabled digital platform being institutionalized
items.value: ₹40-50 crores procurement savings; similar opex savings
items.quote: As I recall, we had foreseen on that annually about ₹40 crores to ₹50 crores, we should be able to save in our procurement and a similar number in our opex as well. So I think we are well on track.

items.statement: Top 10 customers expected to grow 7-8% in FY27; new verticals in North America to drive growth above average
items.quote: across our top 10 clients, we should see growth more in the vicinity of about 7-8%, slightly lower than the average. It is the new verticals that will fire the growth. It is in North America, that would be firing the growth.

items.statement: New vertical investments reduced 27% in FY26 to ~₹120 crores; targeting ₹80 crores in FY27 and ₹50-60 crores recurring annually thereafter
items.quote: We've actually brought it down by 27%, and we had said we will be able to bring it down to about ₹80 crores in FY 2027. We remain positive that we will be able to bring it to ₹80 crores, beyond that ₹50 crores to ₹60 crores every year is going to be a recurring investment.

items.statement: Expects 6-7% tonnage growth in FY27 with at least 2% sequential quarterly growth
items.quote: In terms of volume growth, we are expecting to grow at least around 6% to 7% for the full year basis. And we are expecting that at least around 2% quarterly growth on a sequential basis even for the financial year '27.

items.statement: No exposure to bus business; promoter has separate bus company
items.quote: Currently, we are not into bus business. This company is -- the promoter and another company is having the bus business.

items.statement: Western DFC not a risk as commodities carried not linked to railway services

items.statement: Targets year-on-year EBITDA growth of over 20% for FY27.
items.quote: So we will be able to maintain year-on-year EBITDA growth of over 20% for FY27.

items.statement: Expects positive headcount on both half-year and full-year basis in FY27.
items.quote: However, on a half year basis as well as a full year basis, we will be positive.

items.statement: Targets bottom-line growth upwards of 20%.

items.statement: Entered FY27 with about 20,000 open positions, 15-20% higher than same point previous quarter.

items.statement: Enterprise segment margin outlook is flattish; relies on operating leverage.

items.statement: ABS capacity expansion of 12 lakh units per annum, SOP September 2026.
