items.statement: Targets INR500 crores revenue, requiring over 30% growth over next 4-5 years.
items.quote: In short, the target is INR500 crores, and we feel we are getting into a position with our new products also getting accepted in the market to grow at a higher rate compared to our previous few years where we grew in the mid-20s.

items.statement: SaaS business targeting approximately 35% ARR growth.
items.quote: For our SaaS business, we are targeting an ARR growth rate of approximately 35% and we expect the SupTech business with a combination of one-time revenues plus recurring revenues to move a at a lower rate, but there could be surprises as we go forward.

items.statement: SupTech business expected to grow at lower rate than SaaS, with possible lumpy revenues.
items.quote: And we see the SupTech platform going at a good clip, may not be matching the SaaS growth revenues. But here, there is the possibility of getting lumpy revenues as well.

items.statement: Aims to remain EBITDA positive while growing business, balancing customer acquisition costs with SupTech profits.
items.quote: We don't want to be doing this in EBITDA negative mode. We want to make sure that we remain EBITDA positive and still grow the business.

items.statement: Sales and marketing spend at 1.1-1.2x net ARR, may increase slightly but not indiscriminately.
items.quote: We are at about 1.1, 1.2 levels. We might go a little higher than that, but we don't want to be spending indiscriminately.

items.statement: Prolonged Middle East crisis could delay SupTech pipeline, potential impact post June.
items.quote: It is possible that a prolonged Middle East crisis might have a possible adverse impact on the SupTech pipeline. Having said that, so far, we have not seen any indications along these lines, but it will be fair to factor in this possibility if the crisis goes well beyond the first quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: SaaS business predominantly Europe and U.S. focused, sees no significant impact from Middle East crisis.
items.quote: On the SaaS business part, which is enterprise-oriented business, we don't see much of an impact, because our SaaS business is predominantly Europe and U.S. focused and to some smaller extent, India as well.

items.statement: Expanding SupTech product suite with risk-based supervision, licensing, and decision management modules.
items.quote: We are also expanding this product suite to offer more end-to-end features for the regulatory customers, which include risk-based supervision, licensing and decision management and a few other modules as well.

items.statement: Cash at INR155 crores, net worth INR200 crores, book value INR98 post TaxTech divestment.
items.quote: Post the TaxTech divestment, our balance sheet has strengthened considerably and cash right now in the books is at around INR155 crores as on March 31st, while the net worth has moved to INR200 crores from INR76 crores as at March 31st, 2025, and the book value has gone up as well to about INR98 from INR37.

items.statement: DataTech business spun off into subsidiary for sharper focus.
items.quote: Now, we also mentioned in our press release that our fledgling DataTech business, we have spun off in the subsidiary to give it sharper focus.

items.statement: MSME loan facilitation pilot started February, 3 lenders onboarded, early stage.
items.quote: The loan facilitation we have rolled out starting from February on a pilot basis. Now we are slowly increasing the number of lenders, and we are also reaching out to MSMEs in a calibrated fashion.

items.statement: Internal target for MSME monetization earlier than a couple of years.
items.quote: Our internal target is a little bit earlier than that.

items.statement: Days receivable comfortable at 75-80 days, may improve with enterprise SaaS growth.
items.quote: Yes. I would say that 75 to 80 days is what we would be comfortable. But if the enterprise SaaS revenues really gallop going forward, it could further improve, but we need to wait for that.

items.statement: Exploring inorganic opportunities in adjacencies to enhance RegTech footprint, disciplined approach.
items.quote: We'll be open to evaluating opportunities, particularly in adjacencies that could enhance our RegTech footprint. Early days, but we are just on a wait-and-watch mode, even now.

items.statement: Standalone FY27 revenue guidance of INR 875-950 crore, excluding battery chemicals.
items.quote: We remain confident of achieving revenues in the range of INR 875 to INR 950 crore in FY27 on a standalone basis, considering full production from MPP-5 from Q2 FY26 onwards.

items.statement: FY29 consolidated revenue target of INR 3,700-4,200 crore.
items.quote: So, somewhere around INR 3,700 to INR 4,200 crore is the expected revenue by FY29 on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Dahej Phase 1 project budgeted at INR 428 crore, completion by February 2027.
items.quote: Under this updated schedule, the Dahej Phase 1 project is budgeted at INR 428 crore and is firmly on track for completion by February 2027.

items.statement: Pakhajan Phase 2 revised cost INR 1,367 crore, completion by March 2027.
items.quote: Concurrently, the revised cost for Pakhajan Phase 2 stands at INR 1,367 crore and expected completion is by March 2027.

items.statement: FY27 capex outflow expected around INR 800 crore.
items.quote: FY27 we would complete with the balance CAPEX which could be around INR 600 crore/INR 700 crore. Plus maybe about INR 100-odd crore in Neogen. So, total together at around INR 800 crore.

items.statement: ROCE expected to remain 18-20% even after revised capex.
items.quote: So, when we put together the revised model also, the return remains at 18% to 20% - 20% being the base target on the salt side and with electrolyte, as I said, we are finalizing it, but effectively we should be targeting 18% to 20% ROCE, even after the revised capex.

items.statement: Lithium salt prices from China still 20-25% lower than Neogen's long-term formula prices.
items.quote: Now the differential would be, if we look at our formula long-term price, so it would be around 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Electrolyte price expected $6-8 per kg at steady state, $7-9 with current lithium prices.
items.quote: Electrolyte also depending on the volume and the scale, we had, as you remember in the beginning, said around $8 to $10 and later on we had said around $6 to $8 per kg. So, we expect, currently it should be with the current lithium price somewhere around $7 to $9 per kg, otherwise $6 to $8.

items.statement: Domestic giga customer increasing capacity from 1 to 5 GWh, expecting significantly higher volumes.
items.quote: Within the first half, their capacity is increasing from 1 giga to 5 giga. The estimation that we have received from them will increase for the current year. We expect a significantly higher volume as compared to the last year.

items.statement: Organic Chemicals revenue split: bromine derivatives 40-45%, advanced intermediates 30%, organolithium and lithium balance.
items.quote: I think bromine derivatives was about 40-45% of the revenue. The advanced intermediates was about 30% of the revenue. The organolithium and lithium together were the balance.

items.statement: No liquidity concerns; additional equity and insurance proceeds sufficient for project completion.
items.quote: So, for us, there is not too much of a difference. Whatever insurance proceeds we are receiving on a regular basis and whatever balance also we expect to receive in a relatively shorter period of time. So, we are not concerned.

items.statement: Morita's $20 million equity contribution expected in H1 FY27.
items.quote: Our strategic partnership with Japan's Morita continues to progress well, and their planned equity contribution of $20 million towards the joint venture is expected during the H1FY27.

items.statement: Insurance claims received INR 140 crore plus INR 7 crore salvage; net receivable INR 203 crore.
items.value: INR 140 crore plus INR 7 crore salvage
items.quote: This brings our total cumulative on-account insurance claims received to INR 140 crore plus a salvage realization of INR 7 crore. Our net claim receivable stands at INR 203 crore, and we are working closely with insurers towards expediting the final settlement process.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected low to mid-teens, with India organic growth 8-9%.
items.quote: We expect revenue growth to be in the low to mid -teens, supported by OSAM's full year contribution, Africa continuing on its current trajectory, and an 8% to 9% organic growth in our India business.

items.statement: Maharashtra project to start commercial operations by end of FY27; INR180 crores capex planned for FY27.
items.quote: Maharashtra out of INR280 crores, INR20 crores we have spent in FY25, INR86 crores we spent in FY26 and balance INR180 crores we're planned to spend in FY27.

items.statement: Uganda greenfield expansion total capex budgeted around INR60 crores, to be completed by end of 2029.
items.quote: Total capex budgeted for this project is currently around INR60 crore s, including land as well as the plant. It will be executed in a phased manner and will be completed by year-end of '29.

items.statement: Targeting VAP contribution closer to 32-34%.
items.quote: This growth will be delivered by curd, paneer, and ice cream, and broadly we are targeting closer to 32% to 34% in terms of VAP contribution.

items.statement: Africa business expected to scale to 15-18% of consolidated revenue by FY28.
items.quote: We see Africa scaling towards 15% to 18% of consolidated revenue by FY28, supported by a Phase 2 expansion in Uganda, which will include pasteurized milk and milk products that will be sold in Uganda.

items.statement: Milk procurement cost in Q4 FY26 was INR41 per liter, up from INR38.7 in Q3 and INR37.4 in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: The average procurement cost in Q4 FY26 stood at INR41 per liter as against INR38.7 per liter in the previous quarter and INR37.4 per liter in Q4 FY25.

items.quote: Our average milk sales price for the quarter stood at INR58.4 per liter, which was INR57.7 per liter in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Expect margin recovery to begin in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: In Q4, represented a cyclical throw , we expect this to begin to recover in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Passed on around INR1 of inflation via sales price; expect procurement cost to reduce by another INR1.
items.quote: We have passed on around INR1 of the inflation in the sales recovery that we have already done, currently that we are doing. We're anticipating the procurement improves, we should get down another rupee or so will be coming down in the procurement price.

items.statement: Packaging material costs increased by 30% year-on-year, expected to remain elevated.
items.quote: So I think packaging material as a number has gone up by 30%. Most of the plastics that are there and we use a lot of the plastic, it's gone up by 30%.

items.statement: Effective tax rate to return to normal 25-27% range post favorable tax orders in FY26.
items.quote: Effective tax rate will return to the normal 25 to 27 range post completion of the favorable tax orders we received in FY26.

items.statement: Africa volume growth expected at 20% in current year; value around INR600 crores.
items.quote: The sustainable growth numbers in terms of volume we are confident of maintaining the 20% kind of growth numbers in the current year.

items.statement: Maharashtra procurement currently 3 lakh liters per day, targeting minimum 5 lakhs by end of FY27.
items.quote: So right now, the average procurement Maharashtra what we are procuring is 3 lakh average right now for the last couple of months onwards. So once season comes by end of this year, we are targeting minimum 5 lakhs.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance: 12-13% high visibility, targeting 18-20% with investments.
items.quote: we have a reasonable level of confidence in terms of high visibility pipeline and order book to deliver about 12% to 13% of growth

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 21-22% due to upfront investments in AI CoE and Databricks leadership.
items.quote: what we planned for is an EBITDA between 21% to 22% for the revenue growth that we will deliver primarily on account of some of these upfront investments

items.statement: Technology vertical expected to grow 5-8% YoY in FY27 after adjusting for losses.
items.quote: technology vertical for this year, our sense is that it should be between 5% to 8% growth on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Consumer vertical expected to grow 18-22% in FY27.
items.quote: Consumer should, our sense is right now, should grow anywhere between 18% to 22%.

items.statement: BFSI expected to grow at least 40% in FY27.
items.quote: BFSI, obviously, the growth rates for the next year will come down compared to the previous year. But our sense is they should grow at least at about 40% for the next year

items.statement: Databricks portfolio expected to grow 60%+ in FY27.
items.quote: the expectation is that the Databricks portfolio of work will continue to grow at about 60% plus.

items.statement: Largest tech account shrinkage was $6.5-7M; targeting 95% of last year's revenue from this client in FY27.
items.quote: the total value of shrinkage was closer to about $6.5 million to $7 million.

items.statement: AI-led projects have gross margins of 55-58% vs overall 50.8%.
items.quote: we are seeing that the gross margins on those projects are definitely higher at about 55% to 58%.

items.statement: No deflation in T&M pricing; clients pay more for AI work but expect higher productivity.
items.quote: there is no deflation on the way it works is that clients continue to engage our people. In fact, in many instances, they will be willing to pay a bit more.

items.statement: 28% of FY26 revenue from primary AI (traditional, generative, agentic) visible to clients; another 21% AI under the hood.

items.statement: Plan to increase fixed-bid/outcome-based contracts from 20% to capture AI productivity benefits.

items.statement: BFSI practice grew over 80% in FY26; ended year with ~$18M revenue.
items.quote: the BFSI practice grew in excess of about 80% compared to the year before.

items.statement: Confident of 25% growth in FY27, based on order book conversion and pipeline.

items.statement: INR120 crores allocated for organic growth in FY26, including government, IoT, and IP creation.
items.quote: So overall, what we have done the capital allocation in FY26 was INR120 crores for organic growth. This organic growth included the growth in the government business, it's included in the IoT business. It included in creating intellectual property.

items.statement: IoT-led EBITDA margin increased to 16% in FY26, targeting further expansion.
items.quote: So, let's hope that this -- over the course of year, I think we increased EBITDA from 14% to 16%. Last quarter, of course, Stellar was 33% -- but over the course of the year, that was the number -- and we are hoping to increase that 16% in this year.

items.statement: Government business expected to see significant growth in FY27 due to strong order book and pipeline.
items.quote: But we saw a strong Q4, that's the inflection point that we have seen. And so the government business itself should see a significant growth in this year.

items.statement: IoT business expected to see significant growth in FY27 and coming years with dedicated management focus.
items.quote: So as we keep growing IoT business and you will see a very good growth in the IoT in this year and the coming years because we have now a full clear management focused on growing the IoT business.

items.statement: Government receivables increased, but no bad debt and collections are strong.
items.quote: One of the reasons we are actually moving on two fronts in the government. items.statement: Final dividend of INR3.50 per share declared for FY26.
items.quote: The Board was pleased to express its gratitude to all the shareholders by declaring a final dividend for FY26 of INR3.50 per equity share of INR2 each at the rate of 175%.

items.statement: Aim to at least hold margins in FY27 despite input cost pressures.
items.quote: Our key focus in FY27 is on stepping up revenue growth while at least holding margins.

items.statement: Expect acceleration and step-up in growth in FY27 versus FY26.
items.quote: FY27, as we see today, short of any black swan events coming our way, we do see an acceleration and a step-up in growth of what we delivered in FY26.

items.statement: Robotics expected to reach INR 1,000 crores by FY30.
items.quote: we expect it to reach more than INR1,000 crores for us by FY30.

items.statement: Water purifier category growth expected to accelerate due to low penetration and rising awareness.
items.quote: Given the growing category awareness and like I said, the low penetration, we expect this category growth to indeed accelerate going forward.

items.statement: Input cost inflation may cause gross margin headwinds in FY27, to be mitigated through pricing, mix, and COGS actions.
items.quote: If input cost inflation sustains at current levels, there will be some gross margin headwinds in FY27 that we aim to mitigate through a series of actions across pricing, mix management and COGS initiatives.

items.statement: Capex increased from INR 55 crores in FY25 to INR 84 crores in FY26.
items.quote: This is despite a step-up in capex from INR 55 crores in FY25 to INR 84 crores in FY26.

items.statement: Service revenue growth expected to step up, driven by filters opportunity and AMC bookings.
items.quote: The step-up to a double-digit growth in service lies in unlocking this filter opportunity.

items.statement: No material impact expected from potential drought on water purifier business.
items.quote: We do not expect this to have a material impact on our water purifier business going forward.

items.statement: Robotics manufacturing to migrate to Dixon over next 3-4 months; localization progressive.
items.quote: as we come closer to September, you will start seeing the manufacturing and assembly migrate to Dixon over the next 3-4 months.

items.statement: Service revenue growth to step up in FY27, with some impact in FY28 due to multi-year AMC mix.
items.quote: the impact of that would come of our FY26 bookings growth would come in FY27. But you may not see the full impact yet because some of that revenue may come in FY28 because the share of our multiyear mix in our AMC bookings has gone up quite significantly.

items.statement: Confident of growing around mid-teens in FY27.
items.quote: We are confident that will continue to grow around mid-teens in FY27.

items.statement: Plans to invest around Rs. 400 Cr capex in FY27.
items.quote: For next year growth of mid-teens, we need to invest around RS.400 Cr which we shall be investing in this year also.

items.statement: Aims to maintain 13.1% EBITDA margin, excluding aluminium denominator impact.
items.quote: Overall we achieved EBITDA margin of 13.1% and except for the denominator factor. We will be able to maintain that EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Alloy wheels revenue expected at Rs. 90-100 Cr in FY27 and Rs. 220 Cr in FY28.
items.value: Rs. 90 - Rs. 100 Cr FY27; Rs. 220 Cr FY28
items.quote: FY27 we are expecting revenue of around Rs. 90 - Rs. 100 Cr and FY28 will be about Rs. 220 Cr.

items.statement: Aluminium price increases passed on to OEMs and aftermarket from April.
items.quote: Everything has been corrected April onwards and all these aluminium price rises which has happened in April also, they have been passed on to the customer both on the aftermarket front as well as to our OEM customers.

items.statement: Aluminium prices rose from 285 to 365, passed on to customers.
items.quote: The aluminium is abrupt. It rose, it has risen from 285 to even 365 the price, but the price has been given by the customer.

items.statement: OEM customers maintaining original production schedules, showing growth this year.
items.quote: As far outlook of the two-wheeler industry is concerned, our all our OEM customers they are carrying on with their original production schedules which shows a nice growth in this year also and none of the supplies have been affected by the raw materials or anything.

items.statement: Exports expected to grow 20% in FY27 if geopolitical situation reasonable.
items.quote: This year we are very confident of growing at 20%, provided the geopolitical situation remains reasonable, which we are as an optimist, which we feel that it shall be sorted out soon rather than later.

items.statement: Independent aftermarket grew 24.7% in FY26; expects good growth in FY27.
items.quote: Happy to share that our independent aftermarket has grown by 24.7% in FY26.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict and minimum wage hikes create input cost pressure; customers requested to compensate.
items.quote: Recent developments in geopolitical scenario and significant increase in minimum wages by some of the state governments has created an input cost pressure on the industry. The customers have been requested to support, and we are confident that all our prestigious OEMs will compensate this input cost escalation.

items.statement: Second captive solar plant of 11.55 MW expected commissioned in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Our second captive solar plant of 11.55 megawatt in Bikaner, Rajasthan is progressing well and is expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27, this reflects ASK's special focus on green energy.

items.statement: Strategic reduction in low-margin wheel assembly business complete; revenue nil from April 1, 2026.
items.quote: Another key update, strategic reduction in low margin wheel assembly business is now complete. From 1st April 2026, wheel assembly revenue will be nil.

items.statement: Bangalore plant reached 90% capacity utilization; Karoli at 65%.
items.quote: Very, very happy to share that Bangalore we have reached 90% capacity utilization that we set up last year, our 18th plant and the third plant in Bengaluru. The Bangalore all capacities are full now. In the Karoli plant, the capacities utilization is still 65%, that is the reason that we have made investment for the al

items.statement: Alloy wheel supplies to Japanese customer to start in H2; sunroof and cable JV supplies also H2.
items.quote: The alloy wheel supplies to the Japanese customer in the beginning of the H2, so this current year you'll see much higher capacity utilization in the Karoli plant also.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected orders 40,000-45,000 and consolidated revenue 500-550 crores, nearly double Q4.
items.quote: Looking ahead to Q1 FY27, we expect 40,000 to 45,000 orders and consolidated revenue of 500 to 550 crores, nearly double of the Q4 level.

items.statement: Gross margins to incrementally increase long term; short term commodity pressures and growth investments.
items.quote: And over the longer term also, we can actually expect gross margins to incrementally keep going up.

items.statement: Auto maintenance capex about ₹50 crores annually; no major capex for 1 million capacity.
items.quote: Vipul, again, I will tell you rule of thumb maintenance CapEx will be some ₹50 crores annually.

items.statement: Plans to expand Gigafactory from 6 to 20 GWh by next year, raising capital separately at cell entity.
items.quote: And we are actually going to be expanding that 6 to 20 GWh by next year, but only by raising capital separately at the cell entity, which also we have a lot of inbound interest from private equity players, given the leadership of this asset that we have created.

items.statement: Expects volumes to increase 10-20% in near term as delivery timelines improve.
items.quote: I actually expect as we improve our delivery timelines, volumes will go up another 10 -20% in the near term.

items.statement: Plan to transition full vehicle portfolio to own cells by September 2026; 15% already on Bharat Cells.
items.quote: And we plan to transition the full vehicle portfolio to our own cells by September 2026.

items.statement: Own cell production cheaper than imports; expect 10-15% advantage at 6 GWh scale.
items.quote: I do expect, as we scale up our Gigafactory towards the 6 GWh over the course of this year, we will get a 10%-15% advantage on building our own cell, including the operational overheads of the Gigafactory.

items.statement: OpEx to reduce to ₹100-120 crores per month in next couple of quarters.
items.quote: And we are further saying that in the next couple of quarters, we'll actually get our OpEx down to about 100 -120 crores a month; so further down while business rebounds.

items.statement: Consolidated OpEx expected to move towards approximately ₹350 crores over next couple of quarters.
items.quote: We expect OpEx to move towards approximatel y 350 crores. We actually spoke about in our last year Shareholders’ Letter also over the next couple of quarters, as the full benefit of 26 actions flow through.

items.statement: Expects ₹300-500 crores operating cash burn in FY27; positive after 20,000-25,000 orders/month.
items.quote: So, there will be about ₹300-₹500 crores of operating cashflow burn over the course of this year as the volumes go up. It could be lower if volumes rise faster.

items.statement: Asset base can support ₹15,000-20,000 crores annual revenue without meaningful incremental capex.
items.quote: Together, the asset base can support approximately 15,000 to 20,000 crores of annual revenue scale across Auto and Cell without needing meaningful incremental CapEx.

items.statement: Cell production to start in H2 FY27, reaching 6 GW by June-July 2027.
items.quote: So we believe that in the second half of the year beginning, we'll be able to start our cell production and then ramp up. So we are very, very close to our cell production start of 2.4 gigawatt.

items.statement: FY27 capex for expansion is about INR 1,700 crores, funded by debt and equity.
items.quote: So, for FY27, our capex requirement for this expansion is about 1,700 crores. So it will be a mix of debt -equity.

items.statement: FY28 capex for 6 GW ingot project expected INR 1,800-2,000 crores.
items.quote: So we see around 1,800 crore to 2,000 crore capex will be required in FY28 as well.

items.statement: Confirmed order book at 5.89 GW, about INR 8,000 crores, execution over 18 months.
items.quote: Our confirmed order book remains robust at approximately 5.89 gigawatt, as of March 2026, providing strong forward revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Margins to be stable and healthy in FY27, improving significantly in H2.
items.quote: So, overall, we see that the margins will be quite healthy and stable for FY27.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 margins to be softer due to war and commodity fluctuations.
items.quote: And we expect that the first quarter, because this war still continues. The first quarter will be a little softer, because there's high fluctuation, which is really extraordinary fluctuations both in, you know, the US dollars and commodities and oil prices, and all these are key components in manufacturing.

items.statement: Some orders allow cost pass-through, others require absorption due to fixed-price contracts.
items.quote: So it depends from order to order. For some of the orders, we will be able to pass on that, you know, change and for other, we will have to absorb some of some of that compression.

items.statement: Cell market is seller's market with high demand, especially retail segment.
items.quote: So it is more like a seller's market right now for solar cells , and there is very high demand in the retail segment, especially in the PM Surya Ghar and the KUSUM segment.

items.statement: Initially focus on retail segment for cells, then enter C&I and utility by Q3/Q4 FY27.
items.quote: So initially, we will be focusing on the retail segment, and we believe that because we have gone in with the same set of equipment and technical know -how, the technical staff will also be coming along with it. So we are very confident that we'll be able to stabilize our efficiencies in a very short period of time , w

items.statement: Commodity price increases, rupee depreciation, and war impact input costs and margins.
items.quote: So the major reasons for the decrease in EBITDA are, as you rightly mentioned, correct, because there was an increase in commodity pricing, which really impacted our input costs across the value chain.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio to remain between 1 and 1.5 times.
items.quote: Our current debt-equity is 0.65, but we feel that our debt -equity will remain at around 1.1 -- between 1 and 1.5 times ratio, not more than that.

items.statement: Encapsulant capacity expanded to 5 GW, with 5-10% cost savings from in-house production.
items.quote: The savings which we get from our internal manufacturing are between 5% to 10%, depending on, you know, what prices we are able to secure the raw material, but it gives us an added advantage.

items.statement: EPC revenue contribution was 3-4% of top line in FY26, expected to remain same in FY27.
items.quote: Our EPC contribution was about 150 megawatt, which is about 3% -4% of our bottom line. We only take EPCs that are profitable and have a high margin, because that is not our core business.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA per ton expected to stabilize at INR 30,000-32,000 on steady state basis.
items.quote: the management expects normalized EBITDA to stabilize at approximately INR32,000 to INR30,000 on a steady state basis.

items.statement: Copper value-added products to add INR 25-45 per kg EBITDA at current copper prices.
items.quote: it will be between additional per kg at the present price rate, I mean at the present prices of copper, would be between INR25 and INR45 per kg.

items.statement: Copper downstream project to increase EBITDA margin by 2-4%.
items.quote: Copper downstream project has potential to further increase the EBITDA margin from 2% to 4%.

items.statement: Lead volume growth expected 10-15%; copper growth double-digit, potentially above 15%.
items.value: 10% to 15% for lead; beyond 15% for copper
items.quote: lead will be in the range of 10% to 15%, but copper, because the recycling is increasing and the application is increasing and availability of scrap is increasing, therefore copper could be even higher.

items.statement: Total capex for FY27 around INR 115-120 crores across projects.
items.quote: this all put together plus the phase two of the copper value-added project will be around INR115 to INR120 crores.

items.statement: Plastic recycling unit capex around INR 15 crores, operational by Q3 FY27.
items.quote: The new unit is targeted to become operational by quarter three financial year '27 and will entail an estimated capex of around INR15 crores

items.statement: Antimony project capex around INR 20 crores.
items.quote: coming to antimony project, it will be to the tune of around INR20 crores.

items.statement: Ahmedabad JV project capex around INR 30 crores.
items.quote: the Ahmedabad project is estimated to be a number of around INR30 crores.

items.statement: Kuwait project capex around INR 30 crores.
items.quote: Then the Kuwait one with another INR30 crores.

items.statement: Copper cathode phase one commissioning expected Q2 FY27, phase two Q3 FY27, scaling to 1,500 TPM.
items.quote: we expect phase one commissioning by quarter two financial year '27 and phase two commissioning by quarter three financial year '27 respectively. Once phase two is completed, cathode capacity will scale up to 1,500 metric ton per month.

items.statement: Copper wire rod commissioning expected August 2026 with 600 TPM capacity.
items.quote: We expect commissioning by August 2026 with an installed capacity of 600 metric ton per month.

items.statement: Copper bus bar commissioning targeted September 2026 with 1,500 TPM capacity.
items.quote: commissioning is targeted for September 2026 with a planned capacity of 1,500 metric ton per month.

items.statement: Q4 margin compression due to geopolitical shipping disruptions and LME formula decline; expected temporary.
items.quote: EBITDA per ton witnessed temporary compression primarily due to two external factors.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR 210 crores, 45%+ growth over FY26.
items.quote: Our FY27 revenue target is INR 210 crores, a 45% plus growth on FY26.

items.statement: FY27 PAT expected around INR 24-25 crores on INR 210 crores revenue.
items.quote: So, it will be around INR 24-25 crores on INR 210 crores of business.

items.statement: H1 FY27 revenue outlook around INR 92 crores, H2 around INR 99 crores.
items.value: INR 92 crores H1, INR 99 crores H2
items.quote: Adding new recurring means and project work, H1 outlook is around INR 92 crores and H2 estimate is INR 99 crores.

items.statement: Entered FY27 with INR 159 crore assured recurring revenue at INR 13.5 crore per month.
items.value: INR 159 crores, INR 13.5 crores per month
items.quote: We entered FY27 with INR 159 crore in assured recurring revenue at INR 13.5 crore per month, a 35% MRR step-up before even we won a single new deal, if I don't consider any new deal in the current year.

items.statement: Current contracted base and visible pipeline of INR 190 crores for FY27.
items.quote: Current outlook based on contracted base and visible pipeline is INR 190 crores.

items.statement: FY27 margin recovery via higher-margin AI/security mix, utilization to 88%, operating leverage.
items.quote: Our FY ‘27 margin recovery plan is built on three levers. First, improving our services mix towards higher margin, AI and security work. Second, driving billable utilization from 84% towards 88%. And third, operational leverage as new hires reach full productivity.

items.statement: FY27 PAT margin expected similar to FY26, around INR 24-25 crores.
items.quote: See, we are targeting a 45% growth in our top-line revenue and equivalent increase in our PAT margin. So, that will be around the same, if not more.

items.statement: No cost escalation risk; AWS prices stable, hardware price inflation is a tailwind for cloud migration.
items.quote: No, there is no cost surprise.

items.statement: AI to be meaningful contributor in FY27 and primary growth engine from FY28.
items.quote: AI will be a meaningful contributor in FY27, and our primary growth engine from FY28 onwards.

items.statement: Targeting 5% of revenue from AI and cybersecurity combined in FY27.
items.quote: And our target for this year, both AI and cybersecurity put together, we are targeting about 5% revenue from this.

items.statement: No major manpower cost increase; INR 17 crore to INR 18.5-19 crore plus INR 1.5 crore new hires.
items.quote: Yes. So, there will be, on the existing manpower only, the INR 17 crore would, with the appraisals in place, it will go up to INR 18.5 or 19 crore. And then, there would be about a few, like I said, a few resources here and there, which would get added on.

items.statement: Dubai contract and gaming client exit removed INR 7.5 crores revenue; headcount added INR 6 crores cost.
items.value: INR 7.5 crores revenue, INR 6 crores cost
items.quote: The Dubai contract decision removed approximately INR 4 crores from the top line. The mandatory gaming client exit removed a further INR 3.5 crores. Together, that is INR 7.5 crores of revenue that was either foregone or withdrawn. Simultaneously, our headcount investment added approximately INR 6 crores in annual cost

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; global expansion to be funded by revenue from those geographies.
items.quote: So, we will start like that so that our initial cost of business acquisition is low and as we acquire more customers, as we build our revenue, we expect that revenue and the profit which gets generated from those particular geographies to fund our future expansion and growth in those regions.

items.statement: Debtor days improved from 72 to 62; FY27 target below 55 days.
items.quote: Debtor days, we have improved 14% from 72 days to 62 days with the FY ‘27 target below 55.

items.statement: Targets FY27 revenue of INR450-500 crores, with H1 target of INR200+ crores.
items.quote: Our target for this year is to achieve INR450 crores plus, and we are focused on that.

items.statement: Aims to become a INR1,000+ crore company in three years.
items.quote: maximum in three years we want to become a 1,000-plus company.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin above 15%, with potential 1-2% improvement.
items.quote: The target is to go above 15%, but it depends a lot on the situation and how price variations hit us.

items.statement: Aims for standardized EBITDA margin above 18% for CT PT products.
items.quote: But standardized we will almost want to work above 18% EBITDA.

items.statement: Current order book of INR237 crores plus INR125 crores fresh orders.
items.quote: We have approximately 237 crores orders. And we have already pre-ordered new add-ons of the 125 cr.

items.statement: Plans INR25 crores capex from IPO proceeds for machinery and facilities.
items.quote: Right now, our first target is the INR25 crores capex we mentioned during the IPO.

items.statement: Capex in SMC, FRP, and engineering units to enable revenue above INR750 crores.
items.quote: if our full-fledged, if we want, revenue above INR750 crores can come.

items.statement: Passes on copper and steel costs; takes short orders to manage resin fluctuations.
items.quote: For copper and steel, we pass on the costs because it depends on the situation at the time of supply.

items.statement: Includes 5% price escalation clause in orders to pass on fluctuations.
items.quote: if the fluctuation is like this, if it is more than 5%, then we will pass it on.

items.statement: Expects significant boom in utilities and electrical industry over next 5 years.
items.quote: for the next 5 years, there will be a significant boom in the industry because a lot of new infrastructure development is happening in India

items.statement: Shifts focus to higher-margin products like CTPT, busducts, and meter cubicles.
items.quote: we have started taking orders for products like CTPT, busducts, and meter cubicles, which are high-value items. These have much better EBITDA margins compared to SMC.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation causes raw material price fluctuations, impacting margins.
items.quote: Right now, it is a fluctuating market due to geopolitics.

items.statement: No immediate need for debt or equity; may consider after September based on situation.
items.quote: right now we have a cash fund because the IPO has just happened. So, according to that, right now, if we can maintain the working capital cycle better, then perhaps there will be no requirement this year.

items.statement: Working capital cycle sustainable at 40-45 days per government MSME rules.
items.quote: our cycle will either improve or stay at 40 to 45 days as per the government rules, the MSME rules.

items.statement: Expects 50%+ revenue growth in FY27, matching historical performance.
items.quote: Whatever historical performance we have shown in the last three fiscals, with the same performance we will grow in this fiscal '27 as well.

items.statement: Expects to maintain EBITDA margin 12-13% and PAT margin 8-9%.
items.quote: We are expecting to maintain an EBITDA between 12% to 13% and PAT margin of 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Order book of INR 621 crores to be executed over 12-24 months, average 18 months.
items.quote: Sir, generally our timeline is 12 to 24 months, so averaging it, our timeline is 18 months. So roughly it is completed in 18 months, sir.

items.statement: Win ratio of 30-40% expected to continue.
items.quote: Madam, our win ratio is 30 to 40%. Okay. We will move ahead with the same ratio, madam.

items.statement: Purchase orders have price variation clauses to pass on cost increases.
items.quote: Sir, all our purchase orders, almost all our POs have price variation calculations. The price that varies according to the scenario gets compensated for us in the price variation clause.

items.statement: H1 typically 35% and H2 65% of annual revenue.
items.quote: Generally H1 is 35 and H2 is around 65.

items.statement: Retention money around INR 66 crores as of March 2026.
items.quote: And talking about March '26 numbers, around INR 66 crores is in retention currently.

items.statement: Participated in DISCOM distribution tenders, results next month.
items.quote: Madam, we have participated in DISCOM distribution in our tender pipeline. Its result will come in the next month, madam.

items.statement: Capex to substantially reduce over next two years, less than half of past levels.
items.quote: Next capex will substantially come down. It will be less than half what we have been doing in the past.

items.statement: Price increases of 3-10% taken in Q4, similar in April, further announced in May.
items.quote: We have -- Consumer Products, our price increases have ranged from anywhere from 3% to 10% in quarter 4, and we have already taken a price increase in the same range in April.

items.statement: Lighting EBIT margin may stay close to current levels as gains reinvested in growth.
items.quote: So at the EBIT level, it may be close to where we are but whatever advantage we'll get in terms of margins or the momentum, we'll spend that behind to build momentum further.

items.statement: Consumer Products margin recovery uncertain due to war-related inflation and competitive pressures.
items.quote: Difficult to say exact margin, and I tell you why because there is another factor which is affecting the cost of our products is the war -related inflation.

items.statement: Consumer Products expected to bounce back next financial year.
items.quote: However, we expect the vertical to bounce back in the next financial year.

items.statement: Lighting Solutions momentum expected to continue into next year.
items.quote: We are confident of carrying this momentum into next year.

items.statement: Wires category launched, expected to be strong growth driver for next few quarters.
items.quote: We are confident this business will grow in future and will emerge as one of the strong growth drivers for the next few quarters.

items.statement: War sentiment, continued price hikes, and patchy summer remain key headwinds.
items.quote: However, sentiment concerns arising out of war, continued price hikes and patchy summer remains key headwinds.

items.statement: Not all cost inflation can be passed on; need to stay competitive.
items.quote: But we are using all the levers to see that we deliver a good margin. However, we do believe we have to also see we stay competitive in the market. And in that context, maybe whatever is left, not everything, we'll be able to pass on to consumers.

items.statement: Working capital expected to remain negative next year.
items.quote: So we have been operating at negative working capital for the past 2 years, and we -- the expectation is to continue on those same lines for the next year as well, and we endeavor to achieve that as well.

items.statement: Plan to bridge BLDC fan gap in next 12 months to accelerate growth.
items.quote: In the next 12 months, our plan is to bridge this gap. And this is where we believe the acceleration of growth will happen.

items.statement: Step up investment behind brands and innovations in next 12 months.
items.quote: So you will see a step up in that in the next 12 months, our investment behind brands and investment behind innovations.

items.statement: Dividend of INR 3 per share recommended for FY26.
items.quote: Further, in celebration of 100 years of Bajaj Group, the Board of Directors have decided to maintain a dividend rate same as last year and accordingly approved -- recommended a final dividend of INR 3 a share, that's 150% of face value of INR 2 each on equity shares for the financial year ending 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Management aims to return EBITDA margins to around 10% in FY27, though worst cost impact may not be over.
items.quote: So, it will be our endeavor to go back to the guided number of around 10%.

items.statement: Peak revenue at current price realizations seen at INR 1200-1250 crore excluding Mahad ramp-up.
items.quote: But that should very easily be anywhere between INR 1200 crores to INR 1250 crores.

items.statement: Mahad at current capacity to add around INR 50 crore additional revenue in FY27 on conservative basis.
items.quote: At the current capacity, it will be around INR 50 crores additional revenue.

items.statement: Mahad optimum utilization top line seen at INR 60-65 crore as Evermoss prices have increased.
items.quote: Around INR 60 crores to INR 65 crores because the prices has already increased.

items.statement: Mahad expected to reach 75-80% utilization in next one year, becoming EBITDA neutral and contributing.
items.quote: we are very confident that in the next one year, we should be in a position to achieve utilization of the plant which is anywhere between 75% to 80%

items.statement: Mahad plant capex was about INR 90 crore; capacity can be doubled with INR 12-15 crore more.
items.value: INR 90 crore; INR 12 crores to INR 15 crores
items.quote: initially we have invested around INR 90 crore approx. And this capacity can be easily doubled by adding INR 12 crores to INR 15 crores of CAPEX.

items.statement: Mahad ramp-up continues to drag consolidated EBITDA margins by 1-1.5% as previously guided.
items.quote: Mahad continues to be in its ramp-up phase and continues to be a drag on our consolidated EBITDA margins to the extent of between 1% to 1.5% as we have guided in the past few quarters.

items.statement: Input cost shock from gum turpentine, CST, alpha-pinene at all-time highs; situation may worsen before normalizing.
items.quote: Gum turpentine, CST and alpha-pinene prices continue to go up in the last two quarters and currently are at their all-time highest ever.

items.statement: Tariff overhang on India-US trade eased; gradual recovery in North America order flow expected.
items.quote: The tariffs overhang on the India-US trade has eased compared to the earlier part of FY ’25-26 and that should support a gradual recovery in order flow from North America.

items.statement: RFQ cycles for H2 FY26 constructive on volumes though pricing remains tight.
items.quote: RFQ cycles for the second half of FY ’26 are looking constructive on volumes though pricing continues to remain tight.

items.statement: Revenue split across three divisions expected to remain broadly one-third each.
items.quote: we always have a guidance that the three divisions normally have split revenues of 33%:33%:33% broadly.

items.statement: Expects consolidated EBITDA margin to exceed 10% over next three years, with mid-path by early next year.
items.quote: we are aiming right now, we have an EBITDA at around consolidated at around 3% and it will go step by step, not by way over what we are aiming is really be at more than 10% over the next three years and achieving already probably to be in the middle of the path beginning of next year.

items.statement: Expects margin improvement from next quarter as recent orders translate into results.
items.quote: So we expect from the next quarter on improvement in margins due to the fact that the orders we have registered on Q1 and also the one we got in the second half of the year in 2025 will start to, let's say, translate into positive results.

items.statement: Standalone order book at ~INR13 billion as of March 2026, up 101% YoY.
items.quote: As on March 2026, our stand alone order book stands at approximately INR13 billion and reflects a 101% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at ~INR33 billion; majority executable over three years.
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the consolidated order book stands at approximately INR33 billion.

items.statement: Secured order from JSW Steel for CGL project valued at ~INR4.4-4.7 billion.
items.quote: We have also secured an order from JSW Steel for a CGL project valued at approximately INR4.4 billion to INR4.7 billion.

items.statement: Expects positive order pipeline trend over next 24 months, driven by India, China, green steel, JVD.
items.quote: our opinion is that the trend will be positive in the next 24 months. We expect more orders coming in, especially from number one, the Indian market, which is extremely dynamic and still investing heavily to double the capacity of the country for 2030..

items.statement: Targets value services to be 30-35% of mix over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: We see that we are over the next three to five years we are looking to be at around ideally 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Investing in rolls coating facility at Taloja, expected to be commissioned shortly.
items.quote: We remain committed to investing in this segment, including the rolls coating facility at Taloja, which is expected to be commissioned shortly.

items.statement: Board still exploring fundraise options; another board meeting in 2-3 weeks.
items.quote: Board is still exploring options. So, we have another Board which is evaluating the options and we have another board foreseen in the next two to three weeks to come to better answers.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East could cause short-term volatility in industrial sectors globally.
items.quote: At the same time, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are creating uncertainty across energy markets, logistics, and commodity flows, which could lead to short -term volatility in the industrial sectors globally.

items.statement: US business consolidation may be delayed to end of year or slightly postponed due to technical issues.
items.quote: USA is we are still here also we are still investigating. There are some technical issues on incorporating, not incorporating, on consolidating USA. So, either we are able to achieve that by the end of the year or maybe it will be discussion on maybe postponing s lightly, but not so much.

items.statement: Volteron has no revenue yet; strategy under evaluation for JCIL contribution.
items.quote: So Volteron has no revenue yet due to the fact that it is ready for commercialization only since few weeks. So we are reshaping completely the Volteron strategy right now and especially we are conducting a reflection on how JCIL will contribute and benefi t from the Volteron deployment in the future.

items.statement: Cost structure aligning from West to India and China over 18 months to drive synergies.
items.quote: Going forward, the cost structure is gradually aligning from the West towards India and China, which is expected to drive operational synergies and efficiency improvements over time, improving the margin trajectory.

items.statement: Novelis long-term EBITDA/ton guidance of $600 remains intact, supported by $350-400M cost cuts.
items.quote: Importantly, our long-term guidance of $600 per ton remains intact, supported by accelerated execution of our $350 million to $400 million structural cost reduction program, which is driving sustained improvements in efficiency and margins.

items.statement: Novelis targets $350-400M permanent cost reduction by FY28 exit; current run-rate $200M.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain committed to our 3-year goal of permanently reducing our cost structure by $350 million to $400 million by FY 28 exit.

items.statement: FY27 India capex ~INR12,000 crores; Novelis capex $2.3-2.4B, mainly Bay Minette.
items.quote: In FY 27, the India capex will be about INR12,000 crores, and the Novelis capex will be between, I think, Dev has already announced on the call about 2.3 billion to 2.4 billion, largely Bay Minette.

items.statement: FY28 India capex to rise to INR15,000-17,000 crores; Novelis capex to drop sharply.

items.quote: I think that Q1, to be fair, will also be in the same range because sulfuric prices are high. But I'm not going to stick my neck out to Q2 and Q3. I would still go back to the 600, 700 per quarter there.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt peak expected at INR80,000-90,000 crores over next 2 years.
items.quote: So consolidated net debt peak should be between INR80,000 crores and INR90,000 crores over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Aditya smelter first 180 pots to commission Dec 2027, next 180 pots Dec 2028.
items.quote: So, calendar year December '27, the first 180 pots of Aditya will get commissioned. And calendar year December '28, the next 180 pots of Aditya will get commissioned.

items.statement: Captive coal: Chakla first coal from Q4 FY27; Bandha first coal FY28; Meenakshi substantial volumes FY29.
items.quote: Chakla, we are expecting to box cut in the next 2 months and the first coal may start to come from Q4 itself.

items.statement: Bay Minette full ramp-up in 18-24 months; commercial coils from FY28; EBITDA/ton >$1,000.

items.statement: Bay Minette start-up costs estimated at $100-150 million annually, below EBITDA line.
items.quote: I mean it will be -- if you ask me to say it now, it will be more like in the 100 million to 150 million range annually.

items.statement: FY27 aluminum hedges: 29% at $3,013/ton; currency 14% hedged at INR90.13/$.
items.quote: Our hedged position for aluminium in FY27 stands at around 29% of the commodity at $3,013 per ton and 14% in currency at INR90.13 per $1.

items.statement: Specialty alumina ~50% index-linked, 50% value-added; plan to move away from index-linked.
items.quote: So, in our specialty business, probably roughly 50% is index-linked and 50% is value -added, which is not linked to the index.

items.statement: Management expects sustainable PBT margin of 11-12% in the near future, with long-term focus on improvement.
items.quote: Now talking about the sustainable margin, we could be looking at 11-12% kind of margin in the near future, while obviously in long term, the focus would be on improving it further, but the sustainable margin will be that.

items.statement: Planned investment of INR 500 crores from 2026 to 2028, with about INR 200 crores in FY27.
items.quote: So, from '26 to '28, we have around INR 500 crores investment, which will go through each year. This year, '26, will be around INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Management guides for 6-8% revenue CAGR, driven by capacity expansion and localization.
items.quote: Yes, but you can consider around 6% to 8% CAGR.

items.statement: Price increases initiated in aftermarket and with some OEMs to pass through raw material cost inflation.
items.quote: So that is on the way starting with the aftermarket. And as per agreement with OEM, whatever increase in steel price and something happens, we get it. As of now, we have taken only from a couple of customers and similar discussions are happening with some other OEMs.

items.statement: EV adoption slower than anticipated; 2-wheeler EV share ~6%, PV EV share ~4%.
items.quote: Yes. I mean the current 2 -wheeler is about 6% and then the passenger vehicles is about 4%.

items.statement: Portfolio shift towards passenger and commercial vehicles, premiumization, and EV components.
items.quote: And significant portfolio shift will happen towards passenger vehicle and commercial vehicle. In proportion, these 2 segments have a high potential for us to grow and also the premiumization in the market that is happening is driving certain product value propositions that are in the sweet spot for SKF to really do wel

items.statement: Capacity constraints limit export growth; focus on domestic demand first.
items.quote: It is slightly lower with two reasons. One is India for India, our focus is first to serve our domestic customers, and there is a huge demand coming from all of our customers, so capacity is limited.

items.statement: No further demerger-related costs expected in future periods.
items.quote: We don't have much of the demerger -related costs in Q4 and going forward also, we don't see any demerger-related costs specifically to be in our future.

items.statement: Net working capital increase expected to normalize going forward.
items.quote: Moving to our net working capital. It increased by about 4.6% due to one -off factors and this same is expected to normalize as we move forward.

items.statement: Cash flow impacted by one-off demerger factors, expected to smoothen next year.
items.quote: Cash flow during the year was also impacted by certain one -off factors related to the demerger and these are expected to smoothen as we move forward, and we look forward for the next fina ncial year.

items.statement: Top 5 customers account for ~50% of sales; top 10 ~70%.
items.quote: The top 5 customers typically represent about close to 50%. If I had to name top 3 customers, basically in the 2 -wheeler segment, Bajaj is our number 1 customer, followed by Mahindra in the passenger vehicle and Tata, both the entity combined, the commercial vehicle and the passenger vehicle combined.

items.statement: No change in royalty or trademark fees post-demerger.
items.quote: Now as far as royalty is concerned, there is no change in any royalty or trademark fees from the earlier settlement. So, it remains the same, how it was pre-demerger.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for last financial year was 15.3%, expected to return to previous levels soon.
items.quote: The EBITDA margin, which you mentioned, okay, so last financial year, if you look at it, it's about 15.3%. So okay, slightly lower than the previous year, what 16%, something you were mentioning for automotive. But we hope it we should be back to the level very soon.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue of INR1,450-1,500 crores, led by Fabric and Garment momentum.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the company's growth trajectory and expect revenues between the range of INR1,450 crores to INR1,500 crores in FY 2027, this in spite of all of the headwinds.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin expected 10.5-11%; near-term may dip as raw material costs are passed on.
items.quote: At the EBITDA level, we expect margins to remain between the range of 10.5% to 11% over the medium-term. Near-term margins may go down as the raw material costs are being passed on.

items.statement: Plans FY27 capex of INR135-140 crores across segments, including sustainability and infrastructure.
items.quote: The capex has been planned around INR135 crores to INR140 crores. And so we will be utilizing this across all the segments.

items.statement: Aims to raise Fabric and Garment share of revenue to nearly 70% over medium term.
items.quote: Our strategic objective remains to further increase our contribution from the Fabric and Garment business to nearly 70% over the medium-term, which we believe will support stronger margin resilience, stickiness to the customers, and improve the overall quality of our revenues.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 may be subdued; Garment momentum expected to improve from Q2 onwards.
items.quote: While quarter one may remain relatively subdued, we do expect business momentum to improve progressively in the Garment business from the second quarter onwards.

items.statement: Targets 20% revenue growth in both Garment and Fabric businesses next year.
items.quote: And we are also targeting growth in the Fabric business next year to the extent of another 20%. So, that's aggressive targets we have set, let's see how much we can achieve.

items.statement: Middle East exposure ~INR100 crores; expects INR10-20 crores reduction in FY27.
items.quote: About INR100 crores to the Middle East. So, we expect maybe about INR10 crores, INR20 crores reduction could happen.

items.quote: The capacity utilization overall in the Garment business went up to 72% for FY26 compared to maybe 50% or so in FY 2025. items.statement: Garment division projects 18-20% growth for next year.
items.quote: Next year, we are projecting the Garment division is projecting around 18% to 20% growth.

items.statement: Labor shortages in spinning persist into Q1 FY27, impacting capacity utilization.

items.statement: D2C brand One Mile sales ~INR15 lakhs/month; plans to raise separate funds once sales reach INR1 crore/month.

items.statement: Board recommended 20% dividend on face value, total payout INR3.42 crores.
items.quote: I am very pleased to share that the Board of Directors has again recommended a dividend of 20% on face value, translating into a total payout of INR3.42 crores to the shareholders.

items.statement: Long-term debt to reduce from FY2028 onwards; no reduction in FY2027 due to planned capex.
items.quote: But from FY 2028 onwards, you will see a reduction happening in the long-term.

items.quote: And the INR958 crores capex, which we also got it cleared, that will kick in for the overall capacity of 2 million. items.quote: So we have also signed up with Andhra Pradesh government for the greenfield project that's kicking in over about 2 million capacity.

items.quote: If I have to give you some number, it is almost about 3 to 3.5 percentage on the material cost level impact is expected. And what we have done anticipating this and started working on first is before the price increase, we intensified our value engineering.

items.statement: Took a 1.75% price increase in April 2026 to offset commodity inflation.
items.quote: And we also did a pricing increase of about 1.75% in the month of April.

items.quote: Overall, because of the increase in commodity costs, we've had a total of about 90 basis points in the quarter. items.statement: April 2026 Royal Enfield sales grew 57% year-on-year to about 1.04 lakh motorcycles.
items.quote: In the month of April 2026, we sold about 1.04 lakh motorcycles, which is actually a 57% growth over the last year.

items.statement: Inquiry levels growing about 23% year-on-year; no structural correction in demand.
items.quote: Inquiry levels are growing almost about 23% compared to the previous years and the months. So there is no structural correction which is taking place in the demand.

items.statement: Started FY27 strongly with 51% growth in April 2026; medium-term trajectory expected upwards.
items.quote: we are happy to have started FY27 on a very strong note with a good momentum in April 2026 with a growth of 51%. The resilience of our growth over the past 8 quarters makes us confident that our strategies are steering us in the right direction and over the medium term, we expect the trajectory to be upwards.

items.statement: Premium motorcycle segment growing; Royal Enfield outgrew the segment which expanded from 70,000 to 1.1 lakh per month.
items.quote: the entire premium motorcycle in 2022, '23, the market size was only almost 70,000, now it has gone to almost about 1.1 lakh per month. items.quote: Basically, our intent is to set up a 50-50 joint venture for financing, leasing and other financial services business. And our investment in this will be up to INR750 crores for the 50% stake in this Volvo Financial Services India.

items.statement: Global uncertainties, geopolitical developments and supply chain volatility will continue to test ability.
items.quote: As we look ahead, the environment around us remains dynamic, global uncertainties, geopolitical developments and supply chain volatility will continue to test our ability.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 82 per share for FY26.
items.quote: the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR82 per share for the fiscal year.

items.statement: Royal Enfield capacity rising to about 1.6 million plus with 500 module kicking in from June-July.
items.quote: we mentioned our capacity is about 1.4 million with about 500 module, which we explained to you people in the last call also, that's going to kick in from June and July. It does mean the overall capacity will go up to almost about 1.6 million plus.

items.quote: So, our capacity declared was about 1.4 million, and we said with the 500 module, which we started off anticipating the growth, that's going to kick in from July because we had to be prepared for festive season.

items.statement: INR958 crores investment started, taking capacity in phases to 2 million at Cheyyar Brownfield by Q2 FY28.
items.quote: But the additional INR958 crores, which we are putting in as a capital or taking the capacity from 1.6 million to almost 2 million at our Cheyyar facility, which is a Brownfield expansion, that we are looking at Q2 FY28.

items.quote: And that's why we narrowed down on AP and we got about 261 acres of land, where we will actually be looking at further expansions.

items.quote: Typically, it will be somewhere around 24 to 30 months window, that's where we will come out with a new plant fully operational.

items.quote: So, which is expected to be in the range of 3% to 3.5% and that's in the first quarter. So that continue to be in the similar lines for the year.

items.quote: We also announced appropriate price increases for that, which is to tune of 2% various vehicles. So that has been announced from 1st April.

items.quote: I think there will be opportunity to grow the assets under management with the current infusion of money, maybe up to INR 9,000 crores, INR 10,000 crores over a period of next 5 years.

items.statement: Focus remains on middleweight 250cc to 750cc segment; Bullet 650 dispatch already started.
items.quote: A bullet 650 is on the cards. It's just going to come because that I can share it with you because the dispatch is already started.

items.statement: Flying Flea electric launched, bookings started, expanding city-by-city slowly; S6 to follow.

items.statement: April Royal Enfield grew about 37%; top 10 cities grew over 24%; rural growth continuing.
items.quote: In fact, in the month of April, we grew by almost about 37%. That's what I mentioned. And if I have to tell you about top 10 cities, in top 10 cities, we have grown almost about 24% plus.

items.statement: International markets cautiously optimistic; Europe a market adjustment year with degrowth and OBD2B pre-registered vehicles not cleared.
items.quote: So international market is -- we are cautiously optimistic as of that now.

items.statement: VECV has a reasonably good electric bus order book across 9, 12 and 13.5 meter buses.
items.quote: And we go by the current order book, our current demand, but we have a reasonably good order book business right now.

items.statement: Labour, LPG, commodity and power disturbances of 2-3 weeks now settling; production and supply improving.
items.quote: As I mentioned, it was almost about 2, 3 weeks disturbance were in both the businesses. It's all settling in down along to us even at the supplier end..

items.statement: ZEE5 at optimum investment level; may increase but won't significantly impact EBITDA.

items.statement: Board approved INR20 crores investment in CORE Private Limited for live business.

items.statement: Board approved up to INR116 crores investment in Phantom Digital Effects Limited for VFX capabilities.
items.quote: Secondly, an investment of up to INR116 crores was also approved, as Punit mentioned, in Phantom Digital Effects Limited, which happens to be a listed company as well.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 6.9% in Q4 FY26.

items.quote: We've had a look at the various patterns of consumption, and we have changed that estimate to make it more front-ended to increase it to 50% in the first 2 years and then the balance in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Advertising environment challenging near term due to West Asia crisis; medium-term outlook positive.
items.quote: While the advertising environment looks challenging in the immediate near term amidst the prolonged West Asia crisis, we do believe that the investments in strategic levers during the financial year '26, along with our digital proposition, positions us well from a medium-term perspective.

items.statement: Middle East conflict impacted March advertising; overall ad revenues declined 4% YoY.
items.quote: As a result, our overall advertising revenues declined 4% year -on-year.

items.statement: ZEE5 FY26 revenue growth 53% YoY.

items.statement: Network share increased 80 bps to 17.4% in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Zee TV GRP growth 40% YoY.

items.statement: Publication EBIT margin expected at least 200 bps better than last year on double-digit revenue growth.
items.quote: So there will be at least 200 basis points better margin than the current year -- than the last year.

items.quote: So it would be just hardly INR25 crores, INR30 crores of investments.

items.statement: South Gujarat plant total investment INR65 crores including land; asset turnover 1x first year, 2x second, 2.5x thereafter.

items.quote: But for the year, it will be hardly impacted in not even 100 basis points. It will be more or less lesser than that.

items.statement: Paper prices up ~8% from lowest level; no further increases expected for 3-4 months.
items.quote: So the paper that we use in last 1 quarter, we have seen around 8% jump from its lowest level that it had gone down last year.

items.statement: Internal target of 20-30% growth in FY27, with 30%+ over 5 years.
items.quote: our targets internally are to remain in this, you know, on the lower side also, upwards of 20, and closer to 30, if all goes well.

items.statement: Busbar/CCS unit expected to generate ₹250-350 crore revenue in 2-3 years.
items.quote: we expect that this standalone unit, this new standalone unit could bring in revenues, you know, anywhere in the 250 to 350 crore, range.

items.quote: we expect the business to come back to those levels, or almost back to those levels, at least in this year, and then probably surpass it next FY27-28.

items.quote: maybe by sacrificing 1% or 2% margin, but adding that capacity and getting that added revenue in bimetal will anyway overall be, really good for our bimetal-related numbers.

items.quote: we consider any growth coming from smart meters good, or bad,- we consider it to be more of a bonus for us, and we don't want to rely or make our growth story

items.quote: As of March 2026, our order backlog stood at approximately INR593 crores, and we recorded an order inflow of almost INR990 crores in FY’26.
