items.statement: Bathware business targets 15-20% growth in FY27 with margin improvement.
items.quote: Based on the business momentum we are witnessing over the last couple of quarters and improving market conditions, we remain confident of delivering growth in the range of 15% to 20% in FY27, along with an improvement in margins.

items.statement: Consumer appliances business targets 15-20% growth.
items.quote: In consumer appliances, we are also targeting 15% to 20% growth.

items.statement: Pipes business expects 14-15% volume growth.
items.quote: Therefore, we are expecting an increase of around 14% to 15% in volume.

items.statement: Console margins to expand 1.5-2% annually for next two years.
items.quote: our plan is to expand our overall margins of the business, on a console basis ranging 1.5% to 2% systematically at least for the next 2 years.

items.statement: Bathware EBITDA margin to improve 1-2% in FY27 and another 1-2% next year.
items.quote: We're confident of delivering about between 1% and 2% improvement in the EBITDA margin in this financial year and another 1% to 2% in the next year as well.

items.statement: Consumer appliances targets 8-10% EBITDA margin within two financial years.
items.quote: We are targeting the 8% to 10% EBITDA margin in the consumer appliances business within the next two financial years.

items.statement: Faucets price increased 15% mid-January and 3% on May 1.
items.quote: mid-January, we took a 15% price increase in faucets because there was a substantial increase in brass price from about INR600 to about INR800. So 15% hike we took mid-January and then on 1st May, we've taken another price hike of about 3%.

items.statement: Sanitaryware price increased 6% on Feb 1 and 7% mid-April.
items.quote: In sanitaryware, on 1st February, we took a 6% increase and then gas prices obviously went up significantly in March and April. So mid-April, we took another 7%.

items.statement: Pipes business sees strong April growth of 50% and year-to-date growth of 30%.
items.quote: we recovered that in April and recorded growth of around 50% last month. We continue to see momentum, with year-to-date growth of around 30% this month.

items.statement: Focus on premiumization with smart toilets, thermostats, and differentiated designs for higher margins.
items.quote: So between smart toilets, between thermostats, and between these better and differentiated design and aesthetics products with better raw materials, these are the categories where we're seeing higher gross margin.

items.statement: Tiles supply disruption impacted Q4 sales by INR10 crore; April-May impact INR4-5 crore.
items.value: INR10 crore and INR4 to INR5 crore
items.quote: We had an impact in March of roughly about INR10 crore in terms of non-supply of planned material that we had for tiles. In Q1 of this year, there has been improvement in terms of supplies in May. April still got impacted. So, if I were to quantify the April plus May impact, then it would be about INR4 to INR5 crore in

items.statement: Net debt to reduce by 30-40% in next two years through repayments.
items.quote: I'm not saying we'll make it debt-free in the next two to three years, but definitely a substantial reduction by almost 30% to 40% should happen in next two years.

items.statement: Demerger process expected to complete in 2-3 months for court order, then 1-1.5 months for listing.
items.quote: We feel that this may take another two to three months, in terms of getting the final court order. And after which we'll approach stock exchanges for the listing, which is another month, month and a half process based on our past experiences.

items.statement: Consumer appliances to hit INR100 crore quarterly revenue run rate in Q1-Q2 FY27.
items.quote: In terms of the target, basically we will hit the INR100 crore target within Q1 and Q2 of this year. So, we continue on that path of INR100 crore in a quarter.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 11-13%, including Bathware losses.
items.quote: I think EBITDA should be closer to our normal guidance of in the band of 11% to 13% for the full year.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guidance 12-15%.
items.quote: we see 11% to 13% kind of operating margin and 12% to 15% kind of a volume growth.

items.statement: FY27 capex plan INR200-210 crores, including Bhuj second tranche.
items.quote: Around INR200 crores to INR210 crores is the planning for FY 2027. That includes the second tranche of Bhuj as well.

items.statement: Steady-state annual operating margin 11-12%.
items.quote: At an annual level, 11% to 12% kind of operating margin.

items.statement: Value-added share to rise from 23-24% in FY26 to 27-28% next year.
items.quote: So, this would be in the range of 23%, 24% in FY '26, and this has to move towards 27% to 28% next year.

items.statement: Inventory days guidance 65-75 days, currently within range.
items.quote: We have guided for 65 days to 75 days of inventory. And we are in that range as we speak.

items.statement: Bathware breakeven targeted at INR20-25 crores quarterly run rate in Q2/Q3 FY27.
items.quote: And at around INR20 crores, INR25 crores, we will hit that breakeven mark.

items.statement: FY27 capacity utilization expected 58-60% if 15% volume growth achieved.
items.quote: So, of the production capacity, we intend to have around 58% to 60% if the guidance of 15% we achieve to get the volume.

items.statement: May sees strong demand revival across plumbing and agriculture after April destocking.
items.quote: But in May, we have seen a strong primary pickup because dealers have been able to liquidate their material.

items.statement: Q4 inventory gains fully passed to channel; no inventory gain retained.
items.quote: We have had no inventory gain in quarter four. It has been passed on to the channel to improve our competitiveness...

items.statement: CPVC highest growing polymer, followed by PVC, PPR, HDPE; trend to continue.
items.quote: CPVC continues to be our highest growing polymer, followed by PVC, PPR, and HDPE. And we see that trend going forward in the current financial year as well.

items.statement: PVC price volatility continues; April weak for industry due to high channel inventory.
items.quote: Volatility in PVC continues. April was weak for the industry, because channel partners had high inventory.

items.statement: Gross asset turnover target ~2.5x over long term.
items.quote: So once -- so if we consider that to reach at an optimal level, our turnover should be around 2.5x of the gross block, that should be the decent enough.

items.statement: April and May growth momentum good, but global inflation and currency concerns make management cautious for next year.
items.quote: I have to admit that April and May have been good overall for the business in terms of the growth momentum. However, you are right that the global concerns, which are being translated to high currency and oil prices, I mean, high oil prices and depreciating currency and its impact on inflation and through that consumpt

items.statement: Beauty categories are small luxuries, so consumption less impacted during tougher times.
items.quote: But there, I would like to remind everyone of our consumption categories are small luxuries. And as a result, their consumption is not as impacted during tougher times.

items.statement: Sees AI-led growth benefits on both top line and costs.
items.quote: But I have to admit that we are definitely seeing benefits of AI-led growth in our business for sure. So, it will be a combination of the two. There will be some general global concerns, but we also do see opportunities for businesses like us to benefit from current developments on AI. And the benefit is both on top li

items.statement: Marketing funnel improving at all levels from visits to cost per visit to conversions.
items.quote: Yes. So I think best to say that we are seeing improvement in marketing funnel at all levels on visits or cost per visit to conversions to more engaged users. So I think across the board there are benefits.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 132 bps in FY26 led by House of Nykaa and service income.
items.quote: That's what you see on this slide, with gross margin improving by 132 basis points in FY '26, led by strong performance of House of Nykaa and improved service income across businesses.

items.statement: Beauty improved margin 70 bps; Fashion improved 570 bps in FY26.
items.quote: Beauty improved its margin by 70 basis points led through productivity gains and scale efficiencies. While Fashion has seen strong improvement of 570 basis points as Abhijeet covered as well, with strong improvement across marketing in S&D and other expenses.

items.statement: Fashion reported positive 0.3% EBITDA in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Again, the key highlight here being that, as Abhijeet again mentioned, Fashion has become profitable and we reported a 0.3% EBITDA for quarter 4.

items.statement: ROCE improved sharply to 21.2% in FY26 versus 11.3% a year ago.
items.quote: And all of this, high profitability as well as better efficiency on both fixed capital as well as working capital has resulted in ROCE seeing a sharp improvement in FY '26 and moving up to 21.2% versus 11.3% a year ago.

items.statement: Completed Earth Rhythm acquisition by acquiring additional 24% stake at pre-agreed terms.
items.quote: We had acquired 76% stake in Earth Rhythm over a couple of tranches between FY '23 and FY '25, as you are aware, and we now completed the acquisition by acquiring an additional 24% stake and which happened at pre-agreed terms.

items.statement: Korean beauty brands grew 58% YoY; dermacosmetics GMV grew over 40% YoY.
items.quote: For us on the platform, Korean brands have shown phenomenal growth at 58% growth year-over-year. And I would say, Nykaa has been ahead of the curve when it came to identifying and capitalizing on the Korean beauty wave early.

items.statement: Beauty vertical margins to continue improving, similar trajectory to past years, despite reinvestment in growth.
items.quote: So yes, I think you could assume that all else remaining constant, you can see similar trajectory in the coming years.

items.statement: Fashion business margins expected to improve going forward.
items.quote: So we feel confident that the trajectory should be positive on margins for the fashion business from here on.

items.statement: Offline store expansion of 50-60 doors per year, on track to reach 500 stores in 3-4 years.
items.quote: So, you can say about 170 or 180 doors more over the next 2 to 3 years, averages out to about 50-60 doors a year.

items.statement: Brands may take price increases due to freight and currency pressures, but not yet and not likely near term.
items.quote: I would say it's not likely in the near term, but yes, it can happen.

items.statement: Headroom for customer acquisition growth in beauty; AUTC growth can continue at current rate for 2-3 years.
items.quote: Yes. As I said, I think there is headroom for growth on customer acquisition for sure.

items.statement: Owned brands growth may slow but won't impact beauty vertical margins; retail business has highest margin.
items.quote: So even if the owned brands business does slow down, I don't think you're going to see an impact on the overall margin profile for the Beauty vertical.

items.statement: Nykaa Now to be marketed more actively in FY27, expecting meaningful order contribution.
items.quote: And now in FY '27, the plan is to really start to market Nykaa Now more actively to our consumers, given that we have the assortment and the speed buttoned up.

items.statement: Brands may pull back ad spends due to inflation, but low revenue concentration mitigates risk.
items.quote: So, to answer your first question, it is a possibility that certain brands pull back on ad spends or on marketing on digital platforms, including ours, that is a possibility.

items.statement: Each beauty sub-business improving margins; B2B single-digit, owned brands higher than multi-brand retail.
items.quote: But what I can tell you is, and based on the commentary you heard from the various business leaders, each business is independently seeing improvement in their margin profile.

items.statement: Fashion growth driven by customer acquisition and assortment addition; positive trajectory expected.
items.quote: And that's why we remain confident that we should continue to see positive trajectory.

items.statement: Owned brands strategy focuses on building independent brands, not targeting specific share of Nykaa platform.
items.quote: We're truly trying to build an independent unit within Nykaa which is truly a house of brands.

items.statement: AI improving marketing efficiency and personalization for new and existing customers.
items.quote: And AI has only allowed us to be more efficient in terms of how we spend that additional dollar on some of these other platforms.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining long-term sales growth in the 15% range year on year, with possible quarterly hiccups.
items.quote: When we look to the future, we are pretty confident that on a long-term basis we can continue to grow our business in that (+15%) range year on year, as we have done and shown over periods of time.

items.statement: FY26 delivered metrics within guidance: PAT mid-teen, EBITDA high 20s to low 30s, sales growth 15%.
items.value: PAT mid-teen, EBITDA high 20s to low 30s, sales growth 15%
items.quote: delivered metrics in our guidance range, which has been PAT in the mid-teen percentage range, EBITDA in the high 20s to low 30s, and of course, a sales growth of 15%.

items.statement: Full-year pre-IndAS EBITDA around 21% and pre-IndAS PAT 15.5%.
items.quote: So, pre-IndAS EBITDA among would be around 21%.And I think we have already given pre-IndAS PAT. So, for the full year, it is 15.5 percent.

items.statement: Overall input cost inflation seen at about 10%, with some categories spiking more; no immediate price hikes planned.
items.quote: Overall, if it does impact us, in those items that it impacts us, I think we have seen overall input costs of 10%, maybe, so it's not significant in spike, though there are certain categories that spike a little bit more than the others.

items.statement: Mitigating input cost inflation via forward buying and six months of inventory; no knee-jerk pricing action.
items.quote: There's two ways that we plan on mitigating this. First of all we are looking at forward buying a lot of the raw materials that we can buy in bulk to make sure that we don't see significant price hikes there.

items.statement: E-commerce expected to represent 12% to 15% of business in the near term.
items.quote: And it's going to represent somewhere between 12% to 15% of our business in the near term.

items.statement: New distribution center adds 200,000 sq ft of storage capacity to support growth.
items.quote: In March of 2026, we also opened a new DC that increases our storage capacity by 200,000 square feet, ensuring that we have the capacity to cater for our growth.

items.statement: Aggregated opportunity to open 50 stores across Fila, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv this year.
items.quote: I think the opportunity to open, I am just going to say an aggregated number in those brands that you mentioned, option open 50 stores exist.

items.statement: BIS import challenges persist for Foot Locker and MetroActiv, limiting store expansion; timing unpredictable.
items.quote: All I can tell you as of today, we still don't have 100% comfort that BIS challenges, for whatever reason, have been mitigated.

items.statement: FILA repositioning underway with local manufacturing; expected to become meaningful to numbers in next 18 months.
items.quote: But I have got to believe that in the next 18 months, it becomes meaningful to our numbers.

items.statement: Monitoring Gulf crisis impact on raw material and input costs, though most can be mitigated near term.
items.quote: As we look to the future, we are closely monitoring the Gulf crisis to see the impact that it could potentially have on our raw materials and other input costs, though we believe we can mitigate most of it for the near term.

items.statement: Premium customer base relatively insulated from inflation; Walkway has large growth opportunity from unorganized shift.
items.quote: What I where we feel a little bit more insulated is twofold. One is our customer for the most of our business tends to be a premium customer.

items.statement: Technology upgrades planned: new POS system starting June, SAP upgrade later this year, in-house AI agents.
items.quote: So, we have started that tech upgrade to the new POS system that will start in June. And by the end of the year, we hope to have that rolled out.

items.statement: Three significant senior hires in last 12 months: new CTO, CMO and Chief Product Officer.
items.quote: We have had three significant hires in the last 12 months. Some of them are role replacements and some of them are new. But we had a new Chief Technology Officer. We have had a new chief marketing officer.

items.statement: Plans to open 800 net new stores in FY27, including franchisee outlets.
items.quote: For FY27, company plans to open 800 net n ew stores, including franchisee outlets.

items.statement: Aims to maintain current 5.7%-5.8% operating EBITDA margin for next year, then grow.
items.quote: we would first try to stabilize this and maybe deliver again the same 5.7% to 5.8% and then keep growing.

items.statement: Expects to maintain same gross margin level; private label growth should be accretive.
items.quote: We do not give any specific guidance, but we expect at least to maintain the same level of gross margin. And as and when we see further improvements in the share of private label that should be accretive to our gross margins.

items.statement: Targets 9%-10% annual SSSG for stores older than 12 months.
items.quote: we still believe that we will be able to continue to clock at least 9% to 10% on an annual basis.

items.statement: Private label growth guidance of 20-30 bps per quarter remains intact.
items.quote: So I think that guidance continues to be intact.

items.statement: Every 0.3% private label mix increase gives 0.1% gross margin impact; guidance remains.
items.quote: we had earlier indicated that for every 0.3%, we will have a 0.1% impact on the gross margin. For that, I said, yes, that guidance still remains.

items.statement: Private label non-pharma gross margin is 23%-25% vs branded non-pharma 9%-10%.
items.quote: The private label non-pharma margins are in the range of 23% to 25% at the gross margin level, which are significantly better than the non-pharma branded products, which are in the range of maybe 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Plans to modernize 600-plus stores this year to accommodate more private label non-pharma products.
items.quote: even during the current year, we have a project to, I would say, upgrade or modernize at least 600-plus stores to accommodate more and more.

items.statement: Franchisee store setup capex of about INR10 lakhs per store, invested by company.
items.quote: we spend INR10 Lakhs per store for setting up the complete capex, including the EBITDA.

items.statement: Franchisee model: MedPlus retains 9.5%-10% gross margin, no other costs, accretive to company margin.
items.quote: And we would be making that delta margin of 9.5% to 10% when we sell the inventory to the franchisee.

items.statement: Online is 5-plus percent of total sales; growth focus remains Tier 2 and Tier 3 physical stores.
items.quote: It is five-plus percent of our current total sales.

items.statement: Private label inventory expiry and write-off risk is entirely on company's books.
items.quote: On the private label, the entire inventory risk of expiry and write-off is on our books.

items.statement: Company is zero-debt; INR120 crore interest is lease accounting, not external loans.
items.quote: So this interest that you are seeing in P&L, so this is all related to lease accou nting. And there is no external loan in our book.

items.statement: Warehouse inventory sustainable at 30-33 days; may reduce tail brands if private label reaches 40%+.
items.quote: I think, Govind this would be in the range of 30 days to 33 days.

items.statement: Core states to grow ~13%, focus states 20%+; 15% growth not sustainable.
items.quote: So 15% growth would not be sustainable. What we look at it is that's about 13 plus/minus kind of growth we'll look at from core states and from focus states would be, of course, up 20%.

items.statement: Target to maintain same consolidated gross margin percentage in FY27.
items.quote: So, from that perspective, gross margin, the target of gross margin at consol should be same for us. We need to maintain the gross margin this year.

items.statement: Ad budget for FY27 to be ~2% of sales, same as last year.
items.quote: So, from ad perspective, ad budget this year will be close to 2%, which is same from last year.

items.statement: Plans ~INR100 crores capex this year, mainly for new sweet factory in Bikaner.
items.quote: So, capex largely what we'll be doing, there's 2 capex, the sweet factory, which is coming in Bikaner. And so, this year, we'll be doing close to INR100 crores of capex.

items.statement: Took ~3% price hike in April to offset raw material and packaging inflation.
items.quote: Overall, the price rise was close to 3%, which will be manageable, which can manage this increased RM PM price.

items.statement: Edible oil prices up 12-14%, packaging material up 25-30% due to war.
items.quote: We have seen a significant increase in our packing material and edible oils -- largely edible oil has increased to the tune of close to 12% 13%, 14% in fact, and packaging material has increased to close to 25%, 30%.

items.statement: Continued strong demand momentum post-November, no slowdown despite price hikes.
items.quote: So, momentum, what we are seeing is it's a continued momentum. So , post November, the way of the trajectory we are on, this continues.

items.statement: Western snacks to grow 20%+ annually; contribution to rise to 11% in 3 years.
items.quote: But yes, Western snacks will continue to grow in double digit, 20% plus kind of a growth year -on-year, Western should do. And thi s is what we are talking of also that in next 3 years, currently, what it is 8.5% Western contribution should move to about 11% in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Production loss of 4-4.5 days in Q1 due to labor migration for Bengal elections and Chairman's demise.
items.quote: So overall, close to 4 to 5 days, 4, 4.5 days loss of production was there in -- and now like it's close around 16 -- from 16, 17 from this Month, all the labours have come back and our production is in full swing.

items.statement: THF retail to grow 50-60% YoY for next 3 years, opening 8-10 stores annually.
items.quote: Intent is to open 8, 10 stores every year for next 3 years and to grow our business at 50%, 55% top line growth.

items.statement: E-commerce and quick-commerce now 3% of business, targeting ~100% growth this year.
items.quote: E-com Q-com has now became 3% of overall business, which is significant and growth has grown over close to 100%. And that's the target what we're taking for this year also.

items.statement: New warehouse to be fully operational by mid-June, improving supply chain and storage capacity.
items.quote: Trials has started 2 weeks back early. And it will start completely in -- by 15th of June. So, by end of this quarter, so by next quarter, we'll see a benefit in this.

items.statement: Export business crossed INR100 crores for first time, growing 50-60%.
items.quote: And from export perspective also, we have crossed INR100 crores first time this year.

items.statement: FY27 top line growth to be double digit, better than FY26, aspiration to outperform IQVIA.
items.quote: So I can say only one thing that growth would be better -- top line growth will be better than the last year, double digit. And also, we'll try to outperform IQVIA. That's the aspiration actually.

items.statement: FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance 25.5% to 26.5%, better than FY26.
items.quote: And as far as the bottom line is concerned, EBITDA is concerned, that too would be better than this year '26. We can expect -- I mean, the guidance has been given 25.5% to 26.5% in the range of that.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance 6% to 7% of FY27 revenue, up from 5.2% in FY26.
items.quote: Accordingly, our capex guidance for FY '26 is expected to be in the range of 6% to 7% of FY '27 revenue.

items.statement: INR500 crore investment in Mankind Medicare subsidiary for new Vadodara biotech facility.
items.quote: So Medicare is basically the manufacturing arm of Mankind. So this investment is towards setting up of best-in-class Vadodara biotech facility.

items.statement: FY27 effective tax rate to rise to 25-26% as Sikkim exemption ended in FY26.
items.quote: Sir, this year for FY27, the expec ted tax rate will be in the range of 25% to 26% because the Sikkim exemption what we have been enjoying , FY26 has been the last year.

items.statement: On track to repay acquisition-related debt by FY28; FY27 net debt/EBITDA guided at 0.5x.
items.quote: And we have given a guidance also that for FY27, the net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio will be 0.5x. So, we are on track.

items.statement: International business expected to grow high double digits in FY27, with BSV international high teens to 20%.
items.quote: But next year, we see a revival. We are expecting high double-digit growth in both these international business units.

items.statement: Acute therapy growth in FY27 expected to match IPM after muted FY26.
items.quote: Acute therapy would be in the line of IPM growth. So last year, our acut e growth was muted, but this year, it would be matching the IPM.

items.statement: GLP-1 pen launched about a month ago targeting endocrinologists; no rush on vials or price cuts.
items.quote: We have already launched around a month ago. We are targeting - endocrinologists are on the top.

items.statement: FY26 price hike 4.2% per IQVIA, in line with industry 4.4%.
items.quote: So for the year, our price hike as per IQ VIA has been 4.2%; Industry is around 4.4%. So we are in line with the industry price hike.

items.statement: Employee cost targeted at ~22% of sales long term, plus/minus 0.5%.
items.quote: And secondly, long story short, what our endeavor is that the employee cost should be in the vicinity of 22% of the sales, plus/minus 0.5% here and there.

items.statement: OTC modern trade and e-commerce growth to normalize to high teens, not 50-60%.
items.quote: And hopefully, better growth, double -digit growth, I mean high teens growth would be there. But we don't expect, I mean, 50 - 60% kind of a growth. So high teens would be there.

items.statement: Raw material, packaging and excipient disruption from Middle East war; precautions taken.
items.quote: Tushar, you cannot deny that some kind of a disruption is there as far as the raw materials are concerned, packaging material is concerned, and excipients are concerned. But whatever precautions we had to take, we have taken.

items.statement: FY27 expected to be much better year than FY26 for all businesses.
items.quote: and we remain confident that financial year '27, will be much better year as compared to year '26 for all our businesses.

items.statement: On track to achieve 1 million laden TEU volume by FY28.
items.quote: So we are on course to achieve the 1 million laden TEU number in FY28.

items.statement: Capacity ambition of 12.5-13 lakh laden TEUs by FY30.
items.quote: So our capacity ambition by FY 2030 would be in the range of around 12.5 lakh to 13 lakh laden TEUs.

items.statement: Target EBITDA per TEU of INR2,800 by 2030.
items.quote: from existing INR2,300, INR2,400 level per TEU, we are looking to go up to INR2,800 level.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR400 crores for expansion projects.
items.quote: overall, we are looking for INR400 crores capex spend for various expansion projects we are talking about.

items.statement: Farrukhnagar project capex outlay of INR226 crores.
items.quote: For overall Farrukhnagar project, we have allocated a capex spend of INR226 crores.

items.statement: JNPT Speedy facility upgradation capex of INR20 crores.
items.quote: we are planning an upgradation of JNPT Speedy facility. That would be an outflow of around INR20 crores.

items.statement: Target EBITDA per TEU of INR2,200-2,300 going forward.
items.quote: our targeted EBITDA per TEU is in the range of INR2,200 to INR2,300.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA per TEU expected at INR2,200-2,400.
items.quote: What we would like to be is in the range of INR2,200 to INR2,400.

items.statement: INR80 crores remaining to be called from rights issue and private placement.
items.quote: around INR80 crores is yet to be called on totality of rights issue and the private placement, which will happen in the current year.

items.statement: Looking to raise INR300 crores for project financing.
items.quote: we are looking to raise INR300 crores for the project financing.

items.statement: Current disruptions from terminal congestion and transport fleet shortage.
items.quote: We are passing through one of them currently because of a bit of terminal congestion, shortage of transport fleet.

items.statement: Expected market growth of 5-6% annually in container volumes.
items.quote: expected market growth, which is in the range of 5% to 6% annually, which we will participate in.

items.statement: Farrukhnagar rail-linked ICD to have higher realization per TEU.
items.quote: the realization per TEU in Farrukhnagar would be higher as compared to our existing business.

items.statement: Lease outgo expected at INR95-100 crores for next year.
items.quote: the outgo for the year would be in the range of INR95 crores to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Aim to improve margins significantly over next 2-3 years, with margin improvement each passing quarter.
items.quote: We endeavour to improve our margins significantly in next 2-3 years.

items.statement: All 190 Aadhaar Seva Kendras to go live by September-October 2026; full revenue from Feb-Mar 2027.
items.quote: Our plan is to go live with all 1 90 Aadhaar Seva Kendras by September or by October 2026 max.

items.statement: Employee cost to increase in FY27 due to deploying staff across 190 Aadhaar Seva Kendras; ~2,000 employees to be added.
items.quote: we will add about 2,000-odd employees for these Aadhaar centers.

items.statement: Processing charges to remain in 35-38% range going forward.
items.quote: I guess processing charges will remain in this range only between 35% to 38%.

items.statement: CRA margin to dip in short run due to revised PFRDA charges, but become accretive in long run.
items.quote: In short run, no. In long run, yes.

items.statement: Timing mismatch between Aadhaar Seva Kendra costs and revenues will affect margins in the interim.
items.quote: There will be a timing mismatch, I would say, wherein we will be in building phase as well, and we will be in revenue phase for some centers. So there will be definitely a timing mismatch. To that extent, the margin will be affected.

items.statement: Total outstanding order book as on date stands at more than INR 1,500 crores.
items.quote: The total outstanding order book as on date stood at more than INR 1,500 crores.

items.statement: Storage charges of INR 44 crores in Q4 FY26 relate to 2.5-3 years; next year will be lower.
items.quote: No, this is for 2.5-3 years. This will not be the run rate for next year. Next year will be a lower than this

items.statement: Bima Sugam implementation revenue to start significantly this year; total project revenue ~INR 100 crores over 4-5 years.

items.statement: Capex per new store is INR40-45 lakhs.

items.statement: Comfortable achieving 35-40% growth from current infrastructure.
items.quote: we are comfortable to do at least 35-40% growth from the current infrastructure.

items.statement: Can do above INR 100 crores revenue with current infrastructure.

items.statement: No major capex planned; comfortable with current capex.
items.quote: currently, we are quite comfortable with the CapEx. And if there will be anything, then, of course, we'll discuss.

items.quote: we have three orders lined up of the airport. One is Lucknow, one is Mumbai, and one is Visakhapatnam, which comprises approximately INR 1.5 crores.

items.statement: Aims to maintain margins despite raw material inflation.
items.quote: we are trying to maintain the margin, but I cannot really put the whole, amount on my customer because they'll run away.

items.quote: the prices of the raw material has been hiked by 60%.

items.statement: Solar panels to save INR 10-15 lakhs per month on electricity.

items.quote: We can expect approximately 10-20% growth from what we did last year.

items.quote: So, the contribution from the new stores is around 12% to 15% of the overall business.

items.statement: Export revenue was ~INR 3 crores in FY26; no overseas personalization bureau planned this year.
items.quote: Revenue from exports has been about INR 3 crores in FY '26.

items.statement: Payment cards market share 31.6% in FY25 per industry analysts.
items.quote: Basically, the market share data which was last published was for FY '25 by the leading industry analysts, and there we had a market share of 31.6% of the payment cards market in India.

items.statement: Took ~4% price increase in Q4; another round planned in Q1 FY27, calibrated to input costs.
items.quote: We did start to take up price increases in quarter four. We expect to take another round of price increases in quarter one of FY27.

items.statement: Kerala distribution restructuring impact to last at least two more quarters; project complete by Jan 1, 2027.
items.quote: We do see that by 1st of January 2027, this project should be complete and the new distribution system should be working seamlessly in the business.

items.statement: Aims to continue double-digit growth in near term despite West Asia conflict and restructuring.
items.quote: our goal is to continue to work towards a double-digit growth performance, and we are pretty confident that we will move towards that in the near-term.

items.statement: GCC grew 11.5% in Q4; expects to continue double-digit growth in Gulf.
items.quote: Gulf markets, we have grown at about 11.5%, despite the West Asia challenges that are there. We do expect to continue to track a growth rate going ahead.

items.statement: Spice prices up 6.5% in Q4 vs lows; chili up 20-30%, coriander up 10-15%.
items.quote: we are seeing a recovery in spice prices, with quarter 4 showing an 6.5% uptick versus the lows that we were seen earlier in the years, indicating the beginning of an inflationary cycle.

items.statement: Q4 margin hit 200 bps by higher freight and Project BOLT investment.
items.quote: The marginal decline in quarter 4 margins is attributed to higher freight costs driven by West Asia conflict and investment in Project BOLT, which is a digital commerce project I will speak about later. This impact is to the tune of 200 basis points on our margin.

items.statement: No PLI income in FY26 due to deflation; FY27 is last year of scheme, recognition uncertain.
items.quote: FY27 is the last year of the PLI scheme. It is still early days, so clearly if we meet the threshold, we will start to recognize it, but it's early days and difficult to comment at this stage.

items.statement: Pure spices ~26% and blended spices ~39-40% of spice segment.
items.quote: It's about roughly 26% pure spices and about 39%, 40% is blended spices.

items.statement: Digital commerce grew 38% in FY26, now 8.7% of domestic revenues.
items.quote: on a full-year basis, we've achieved a strong 38% growth in FY26, clearly reflecting the structural scaling of this channel.

items.statement: Project BOLT launched to accelerate digital commerce with external agency.
items.quote: we have now launched Project BOLT, a focused initiative to accelerate our digital commerce trajectory with the help of an external agency.

items.statement: West Asia conflict causing input cost pressures and supply chain disruptions.
items.quote: The West Asia conflict has introduced volatility, leading to input cost pressures and intermittent supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: US growth soft due to tariff-related inventory issues; normalization expected after inventory flush.
items.quote: The growth in the US markets has been very soft.

items.statement: Eastern convenience food profitability improved with new value-added products.
items.quote: the profitability is much, much better than what it was earlier.

items.statement: Operating margin guidance raised to 7-10% from earlier 6-8%, depending on external scenarios and demand.
items.quote: But given our focus on reducing cost and also reducing our power rates through hybrid power and renewable power, we now feel that depending on the external scenarios and demand, our operating margin could be in the range of 7% to 10%.

items.statement: FY27 capex outlay over Rs. 100 crores for value-added products, Mother Yarn expansion, power reduction, waste reduction, and fire risk mitigation.
items.quote: As far as other projects are concerned, we are expecting a total CAPEX outlay of over Rs. 100 crores, primarily going into value-added products, expansion of Mother Yarn project capacity, and also for various reduction of our power consumption as well as reduction of waste for improvement of our operating margins and e

items.statement: PTCF commercial sales expected from FY27, most likely second half.
items.quote: We are hopeful that the commercial sales would start in FY '27, most likely second half of FY '27.

items.statement: Raw material price increases passed through to customers, with rare exceptions where production was declined.
items.quote: So the pass-through to a large extent, which started in March, has continued based on the pricing of raw materials which prevailed in the, up to, I mean, April and May.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on demand growth due to geopolitical situation, elevated crude prices, and inflation.
items.quote: Due to continuously changing geopolitical situations, elevated crude oil prices and persistent inflation, we continue to remain cautiously optimistic about demand growth in coming quarters.

items.statement: Chinese imports at low prices persist in commodity products; favorable anti-dumping ruling received, awaiting Finance Ministry notification.
items.quote: While Chinese import at very low prices persists in commodity products, we are encouraged that the DGTR has issued a favorable anti-dumping ruling. We now await final notification from the Finance Ministry.

items.statement: Renewable energy share to increase from 36% in FY26 to 48% post additional capacity commissioning in FY27.
items.quote: I can give you an estimate of our current, for the FY '26, our renewable content on the total power consumption was about 36%. Post our commissioning of additional renewable power, it should go up to about 48%.

items.statement: Value-added products yield about 20% additional margin over commodity products after conversion costs.
items.quote: Since we report all, I mean, in a single segment, I will not be able to give volumes, but on an average, about 20% additional margin we realize after the additional cost that we do in converting these into value-added products.

items.statement: FY27 volume target to repeat Q4 plus volumes, dependent on external factors; focus on maximum capacity utilization.
items.quote: We would ideally want to have repeat our Q4 plus volumes, but this is all dependent on so many external factors. But the focus is to keep on utilizing maximum capacities, and that also improves our margin because it helps in better spreading of our fixed costs.

items.statement: Capacity to increase by 2 to 2.5 KT from FY27 capex; other investments add value but not capacity.
items.quote: So, c apacity would go up by about 2 to 2.5 KT, you can say, for the project that would get commissioned. Others are mostly adding value, so the capacity will not go up, but the value addition will go up.

items.statement: Radialization in truck and bus segment has stabilized at 60%; nylon reinforcement growth expected marginal at 1-2%.
items.quote: We expect only marginal growth of maximum 1 % to 2%. But we also do not expect a significant fall now, since it is now reaching a level where normally it is more stabilized.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on NFY could impact prices by 10-30% of current FOB value, favorable for domestic industry.
items.quote: So, what has come out as a notification talks of between about 70 cents to, I mean, depending on the product and the country, it is varying from about 20 cents to 80 cents. So, it will have a multiple, I mean, so, it is fair to assume that it is about between 10 % to 30% of current FOB value and that could be the impac

items.statement: Exports are 4-5% of revenue; focus on increasing value-added filament yarn exports.
items.quote: That is about 4% to 5% is our exports, but we are focusing on increasing our exports particularly of the value-added filament yarn.

items.statement: Cash to be used for growth in current and new segments; buyback decisions based on merits.
items.quote: So, I mean, the discussions at the Board are mainly at growth and we intend to utilize this cash for growth of the business in current and possibly also into the new segments.

items.statement: Targets 36 million pens in FY27 and roughly 50 million in FY28.
items.quote: Look, our projections are, what, 36 million pens this year, roughly 50 next year.

items.statement: By end FY28, 35-40 million pens from new capacity to be in supply.
items.quote: By FY28, I think what we're targeting is 35 million to 40 million pens from that capacity should more or less be in supply by end of FY28.

items.statement: By end of year, both new lines to produce 65-67 parts per minute, combined 40-42 million pens.
items.value: 65 to 67 parts per minute, 40 million to 42 million pens
items.quote: See, what our target is that by the end of the year, both lines should be able to produce at 65 to 67 parts per minute effectively, which gives us a combined capacity of both these 2 new lines of around 40 million to 42 million pens combined.

items.statement: Semaglutide capacity of about 50 million by year-end, to be fully utilized over next 2 years.
items.quote: So on semaglutide, for example, by the end of the year, we'll have about 50 million capacity. So we intend to fully or as fully as possible, utilize that over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Total pen capacity 40-60 million at end of FY28, 30 months from now.
items.quote: So you can look at it as a range of somewhere between 40 million to 60 million kind of pen at the end of ‘24, 30 months from now.

items.statement: Initial capex of about INR100 crores for new consumer electronics plant down south.
items.quote: So we have said that we would need to set up a plant down south. We are evaluating. But our estimate is we will need an initial capex of somewhere around INR100 crores when we set up the plant.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to raise up to INR500 crores, annual affair, no immediate plan.
items.quote: Reflecting the confidence in Shaily's next phase of growth and the multiple new opportunities ahead of us, the Board of Directors have approved an enabling resolution to raise up to INR500 crores.

items.statement: Margins sustainable and improving year-on-year, no specific numbers given.
items.quote: I think what we've been saying is if you look at more on a year -on-year basis, margins will be sustainable and we see margins improving. We do not want to get into numbers.

items.statement: Customers asking for more Semaglutide pens after Canada launches; installing more capacity.
items.quote: Yes. Given only 2 launches in Canada, we are asked for more product. And we're doing what we can to install more capacity as fast as we can to supply that product. So, there are instances being asked for more, certainly.

items.statement: Consumer segment weak due to soft US/Europe home furnishing demand; expects recovery when global situation improves.
items.quote: I think as and when the global situation improves, you would see that demand coming back. At the same time, as we have mentioned in the presentation also and earlier, we continue to add more products on the consumer space, and we will continue to do that. Growth will depend on how the global situation pans out.

items.statement: Healthcare and consumer electronics are largest opportunities; semiconductor second; industrial and consumer together.
items.quote: I would say health care and consumer electronics represent the 2 largest opportunities. which scales faster is a very difficult question. And as you can imagine, the consumer electronics market is significantly larger than the pen market.

items.statement: Production ramp-up risk: if lines don't run at specified speed, supply to customers at risk.
items.quote: If we can't supply enough, then there is a risk, right?

items.statement: Semiconductor tray supplies to start Q4 of current financial year.
items.quote: Quarter 4 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Eye-applicator commercialization factored in current financial year.
items.quote: And we have factored the commercialization of the eye-applicator in the current financial year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of approximately 12%.
items.quote: FY27, we look at an approximate guidance of about 12% of revenue growth for this coming year.

items.statement: Maintains ~14% EBITDA margin guidance, with 150 bps drop due to retail.
items.quote: We will continue with our guidance of approximately 14% of EBITDA with the 150 basis points of drop due to retail.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR 100 crores: INR 50-60 crores maintenance plus INR 40 crores for new stores.
items.quote: So that would be about INR100 crores of capex.

items.statement: Residential project total spend ~INR 45 crores, INR 25 crores this year, balance next year.
items.quote: We estimate a spend of about INR 45-odd crores. So about INR 25 crores will be spent this year and the balance will be probably spent next year.

items.statement: Plans to reach ~70 stores across ZECODE and DEVO by end of FY27.
items.quote: As part of our expansion plans, we intend to reach a total of approximately 70 stores across both ZECODE and DEVO by the end of the coming financial year.

items.statement: FY27 store additions: ~8 DEVO stores, remaining ~18 ZECODE stores.
items.quote: There are approximately 8 stores of DEVO approximately, and the rest of them are ZECODE.

items.statement: Residential project: 77,000 sq ft, INR 60 crores cost, INR 80 crores revenue, 24 months.
items.quote: We estimate to complete this project within 24 months, with an expense of about INR 60 crores in total, including the land cost and the revenue estimation would be around INR 80 crores.

items.statement: Residential project gain ~INR 20 crores over two years.
items.quote: And therefore, there is a gain of about INR 20 crores, which will be not in three years, but in two years.

items.statement: Brand can pass on input price increases to consumers, but gradually to avoid demand disruption.
items.quote: Now as a brand, we are able to pass on prices to the consumer, but that happens in a very gradual manner because we also want to make sure that demand is not disrupted and market share keeps growing.

items.statement: Q1 is generally weakest quarter; business is seasonal, guidance is annual.
items.quote: Now this first quarter generally is the weakest quarter for the company.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: fabric 80%, garments 15%, others 5%.
items.quote: Our revenue mix comprised of fabric at 80%, garments at 15% and others at 5% in the financial year '26.

items.statement: Export contributes ~10% of revenue, stable; domestic growing faster.
items.quote: Export right now contributes about 10% of the overall revenue. For this year, it is about 10%.

items.statement: Preferential issue: NCLT order expected first week of June; RPS issuance 3-4 months after.
items.quote: We expect that by first week of June, when they will pronounce the order and thereafter, we will get the order copies. After that, it will take another three, four months to complete the order spread and issue the RPS.

items.statement: Net debt ~INR 40 crores; internal accruals sufficient for capex and expenses.
items.quote: So right now, the net debt is about INR 40-odd crores. And this is something , so the cash flow for the year should suffice the expansion plan that we have, the capex plan that we have in place.

items.statement: Management guides 15-20% year-on-year revenue growth for FY27, with demand strong in Q1.
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering a 15% to 20% year-on-year growth in '27.

items.statement: Management targets maintaining EBITDA margins between 17% and 18% through product mix, operational leverage, and cost management.
items.quote: Our focus will be to maintain EBITDA margins between 17% to 18% through product mix and operational leverage as well as cost management.

items.statement: Plans to invest about INR103 crores in FY27, following INR51 crores in FY26.
items.quote: In line with this growth visibility, we are going to invest INRS1 crores in '26 and plan to invest about INR103 crores in '27.

items.statement: New orders worth INR500 crores secured in Forging business, with significant portion from a new European car maker.
items.quote: New orders worth INR500 crores have been secured in the Forging business with a significant portion from new onboarded major European car maker in Europe as well.

items.statement: New domestic orders worth INR170 crores secured for hoses and anti-vibration products.
items.quote: New domestic orders worth INR170 crores have been secured for hoses and anti-vibration products, showing good growth in the coming new years.

items.statement: Management expects to pass on inflationary cost pressures to customers, recovering majority of price increases.
items.quote: As you all know, there are inflationary pressures that are coming our way, but we have to 'manage that, and we'll try and pass on the cost to the customers.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 top line expected to be in line with Q4 FY26, with H2 significantly better than H1.
items.quote: Quarter 1, top line should be in line with last quarter, should be.

items.statement: Marelli JV expected to grow 35-40% and Marugo JV around 15% in FY27.
items.quote: Next year, I'm expecting Marelli maybe should to grow between 35% to 40% and Marugo should be around 15%.

items.statement: Heat Shield segment FY26 revenues at INR58 crores, high-margin and high-growth business.
items.quote: The Heat Shield segment continues to scale meaningfully with FY26 revenues at INRS8 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia may cause temporary cost pressures, shipment delays, and supply chain disruptions.
items.quote: Geopolitical tensions in the West Asia region led to an increase in raw material and freight costs. The ongoing situation may also result in temporary shipment delays and supply chain disruptions across certain export matkets.

items.statement: FY27 capex split: INR16 crores Gasket/Heat Shield, INR60 crores Forging, INR20 crores Marelli, INR7 crores Marugo.
items.quote: So this year, we are expecting to invest INR16 crores capex in Gasket and Heat Shield, primarily for the new business, plus the new business we are expecting from Cummins USA and to take growth of --

items.statement: Management expects to cross INR1,000 crores consolidated top line in FY27.
items.quote: We are targeting for crossing INR1,000 crores this year, definitely.

items.statement: 70% of total order book expected to be commercialized by end of FY27.
items.quote: I can say that by the end of this year, 70% order will be commercialized, our total order book

items.statement: Lohum Talbros JV expected to commence operations between July and October 2026.
items.quote: The IV is expected to commence operations from July to October 2

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 40-50% YoY for FY27.
items.quote: in the last concall also we have for this financial year we have given a guidance of 40% to 50%.

items.statement: Aspire to reach INR 5,000 crore AUM by 2029.
items.quote: we aspire to reach maybe in next five years by 2029, we are aspiring to reach about INR 5,000 crore, that is our immediate target.

items.statement: Long-term ROE target of 17-18% and ROA of 3.5-4%.
items.quote: we would like to have an ROE of 17% to 18% with an ROA of 3.5% to 4%.

items.statement: Branch network to expand by ~50% in FY27, from 105 to ~150-160 branches.
items.quote: We have given a guidance of around 50% of expansion in this financial year.

items.statement: Co-lending to reach 20% of AUM by end of FY27.
items.quote: We aspire to achieve a 20% of the overall portfolio in co-lending by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Capex per branch INR 14-15 lakh, opex INR 2.5-3 lakh.
items.value: INR 14 lakh to INR 15 lakh capex, INR 2.5 lakh to INR 3 lakh opex
items.quote: Typical capex is around INR 14 lakh to INR 15 lakh. And opex is around INR 2.5 lakh to INR 3 lakh.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing to remain around 11.2% in FY27.
items.quote: 11.2% was the number of last financial year, the average cost of borrowing that we have had. In this financial year, we are aspiring to maintain the same numbers

items.statement: Expect to bring down cost of funds via borrowing mix and co-lending.
items.quote: we should be in a position to bring down our cost of funds in this financial year.

items.statement: Average LTV ~72%, comfortable with 15-20% gold price correction.
items.quote: As of the year-end, our average LTV was around 72%, that we have displayed in our presentation as well. So, we are comfortable in terms of stress test of even 15% to 20% as well.

items.statement: No equity raise planned for FY27; CRAR at 31% provides headroom.
items.quote: For this financial year at least, as of now we are not envisaging any capital raise.

items.statement: Focus on South India; may explore Odisha, Goa, Maharashtra in FY27.
items.quote: we are looking in this financial year, we will explore other opportunities which are nearer to our branch, our catchment areas, for example, Odisha and from Karnataka if you move out then maybe Goa or Maharashtra.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity target of 4x to 4.5x on steady-state basis.
items.quote: we would like to see ourselves anywhere between 4x to 4.5x.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected at approximately INR 6,000 crores, plus/minus 10%, split equally growth and maintenance.
items.quote: For FY27, we expect capex of approximately INR 6,000 Crores plus/minus 10%, of this 50% will be growth capex and 50% maintenance capex.

items.statement: Consumer electronics third facility on track for commissioning in Q3 FY27, adding upstream integration.
items.quote: The third facility remains o n track for commissioning in the Q3FY27 and will include additional upstream integration capabilities, which should support both growth and the margin enhancement.

items.statement: Aerospace order book increased over 20% to USD 1.6 billion, providing long-term visibility.
items.quote: The order book increased by over 20% to USD1.6 Billion, providing strong term -- strong long -term visibility

items.statement: Yutaka Giken acquisition on track for completion by end of first half FY27.
items.quote: The acquisition of Yutaka Giken will mark our third Honda San related acquisition and remains on track for completion by the end of first half FY 27.

items.statement: Nexans automotive harness acquisition expected to close end June/early July, then consolidate.
items.quote: We expect the closure sometime in the end of June, beginning of July. And that's the time when it should get consolidated with the regulatory approvals being in place.

items.statement: 13 of 16 facilities under development scheduled to come on stream during FY27.
items.quote: Currently, 16 facilities are at various stages of development globally, with 13 scheduled to come on stream during fiscal '27.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margins improved 200 bps year-on-year, driven by emerging businesses.
items.quote: EBITDA margins impro ved by 200 basis points year -on-year in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Long-term pass-through arrangements for raw material price variations, with one to two quarter lag.
items.quote: We have long-term pass -through arrangements with our major customers for raw material price variations. While there may be a timing lag of one or two quarters before settlements are realized, these mechanisms provide structural protection over the medium term.

items.statement: Bullish on commercial vehicle outlook for FY27.
items.quote: We continue to remain constructive and bullish on the CV outlook for FY 27.

items.statement: Leverage ratio at all-time low 0.8x, within policy of below 2.5x and aspiration below 1.5x.
items.quote: Despite continuous investment in growth, our leverage ratio improved further and reached an all -time low of 0.8x.

items.statement: Vision 2030 aspiration of USD 108 billion gross revenues and 40% ROCE.
items.quote: We continue to move steadily towards our Vision 2030 aspiration of reaching USD 108 billion in gross revenues, while simultaneously improving diversification, strengthening returns and maintaining financial discipline.

items.statement: Copper prices up 16% sequentially and 38% year-on-year, with polymer and freight costs also rising.
items.quote: Copper prices increased sharply by about 16% sequentially during the fourth quarter and were nearly up 38% year-on-year.

items.statement: EV programs 22% of order book; EV revenue around 11%; powertrain agnostic strategy.
items.quote: Around 22% of the book business comes from EV programs, while non-automotive contributes around 3% and continues to grow steadily.

items.statement: Management reiterates FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crores, confident despite footwear headwinds.
items.quote: we remain confident in sustaining profitable growth and delivering FY27 PAT guidance in range of INR200 crores to INR220 crores.

items.statement: Gross block expected to reach INR2,150 crores by FY27, with 60% dedicated and 40% shared.
items.quote: we believe that currently, the gross block is distributed as mostly around 61% and 39%. We believe it will be on the same range in INR2,150 crores also.

items.statement: Footwear order book visibility for FY27; expects turnover of INR700-800 crores.
items.quote: we have an order book visibility for the end of the year. We do believe that we will be well above the growth rates that we had targeted last year. So we should be about INR700 crores to INR800 crores of turnover as far as shoes is concerned in this FY27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 10% achievable on like-to-like basis.
items.quote: EBITDA 10% is definitely achievable, Jaiprakash. I mean that's not even a question actually.

items.statement: Raw material cost increases passed on in all verticals except footwear, where discussions ongoing.
items.quote: we have been able to pass on the increased cost of our raw materials across all our verticals, our footwear division did face the brunt of rising petrochemical prices in this quarter.

items.statement: Strong engagement in home care, beverages, and ice creams.
items.quote: Currently, we continue to see a lot more engagement in home care, in beverages and in ice creams.

items.statement: Entering Greek yogurt segment to expand into higher-value dairy categories.
items.quote: HFL is also entering the Greek yogurt segment as a part of its strategy to expand into higher value and wellness-oriented dairy categories.

items.statement: Footwear division impacted by geopolitical conditions and petrochemical price hikes; Q1 FY27 also affected.
items.quote: that's the one division which has been affected in this last quarter and continues to be affected in Q1 as well as far as the P&L is concerned.

items.statement: Net debt to equity at 0.84x, within comfort level; sufficient buffer for capex.
items.quote: Overall, net debt to equity as on March '26 stood at 0.84x, which is well within the company's internal comfort level of 1x.

items.statement: Transition from gross to net revenue recognition for certain food businesses from Q3 FY27.
items.quote: we are in discussion with our customer to transition certain businesses from the gross to net revenue recognition from Q3 FY27 onwards.

items.statement: Mandate for each business unit to grow EBITDA at 20% and deliver 20% ROE.
items.quote: all of them have been given a simple mandate, which is to grow the EBITDA at 20% and to continue delivering 20% ROE numbers.

items.statement: Expects to become largest independent bottler of beverages in India by end of FY27.
items.quote: We will probably, at the end of FY27, become the single largest independent bottler of beverages in the country.

items.statement: Healthcare segment signed 3-4 new customers; focus on exports with US modern trade.
items.quote: We've signed on 3 or 4 new customers for that facility. And as a result, I think that segment will start contributing very well for us.

items.statement: Surcharge is mainly to cover additional costs already incurred, not expected to add to bottom line but prevent it from getting affected.
items.quote: It's not, or are incurring on account of the depreciation at the whatever this Iran thing. I don't think it's going to necessarily add to our bottom line, but it will prevent it from getting affected.

items.statement: V-Shapes losses could reduce this year; breakeven possible this year, with no further fund infusion needed after current round.
items.quote: So it could be this year also. So what happened was, you know, we had predicted about a EUR 1 million something loss, this like an reduction from about EUR2 million, EUR 2.5 million last year to about EUR1.5 million this year.

items.statement: No further funds needed for V-Shapes after current infusion; most funds not going to be infused there.
items.quote: I don't think that we need to put more funds in after this -- since we purchased the technology and shipped it to India. I think this will be the last, like you said, someone said, part of it is to feed some loans that we have provided to get them back.

items.statement: Coding and marking business steady; Track and Trace expected to add to sales and hopefully profitability this year.
items.quote: So that's going steadily. I think that's steady so far. Last quarter, last year was good. This year should be also reasonably good. And like I said, we expect the Track and Trace to be one of the things that we add to sales, hopefully profitability this year.

items.statement: Track and Trace business is at breakeven or profitable in conventional part; gross margin similar to coding and marking business.
items.quote: In general, whatever we do in terms of any business is at a similar gross margin level to what we do in our coding and marking business, at least.

items.statement: Pilots with two top-5 to top-10 Indian pharma companies nearing completion; successful pilots could lead to bigger rollout.
items.quote: And I had mentioned that, we are doing some pilots with two of the top five to ten in size pharmaceutical companies in India. And we're coming to the end of those. And if everything goes and everything is successful, then we should get a bigger rollout of these companies.

items.statement: Employee cost increase largely due to new wage code impact on leave encashment and gratuity (~INR3.5 crores), plus incentives and loyalty bonuses.
items.quote: So, the last one, basically in terms of keeping the business ahead and having the right people and the first impact of more or less about INR3.5 crores was because of that leave encashment and the gratuity entitlements.

items.statement: Major growth last year was from volume; some small part from cost increase; this year surcharge mainly to cover additional costs.
items.quote: So most of the growth last year was volume. Some small part is a cost increase. And, yeah, this year there's a surcharge, but I don't think it's going to -- it's mainly to cover the additional costs that we've already incurred.

items.statement: Packaging sector (pharma, beverage, food, FMCG) demand stable; industrials like cable, wire, pipe, steel fluctuate more.
items.quote: Normally the packaging sector which is pharmaceutical, beverage, food, and FMCG, whatever you call it, is stable. And we see more ups and downs in the industrials, which is like cable and wire, pipe, steel, those are the ones which fluctuate more.

items.statement: V-Shapes R&D costs about EUR100,000 per month; about half of V-Shapes expense is R&D.
items.quote: So I would say like, if the R&D costs of something like a EUR100,000 a month.

items.statement: Track and Trace market size estimated at INR500-600 crores currently.
items.quote: And like you said, yeah, it is a INR500 crore, INR600 crore business currently.

items.statement: Coding and marking total India market estimated at INR2,000-2,200 crores, growing about 10% on average.
items.quote: We have felt that our coding and marking business has a certain limit because the total business in India is still, like somewhere between INR2,000 crores, INR2,200 crores was our last calculation when we had the fall of us, plus assume something for all the other parts of the market.

items.statement: Expects 15-20% top-line growth in CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT subsidiaries.
items.quote: So again we expecting some growth there in a similar 15%, 20% growth rate . I think that's what one would expect there in both CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT.
