items.quote: So as we move ahead, we will see more improvement in consolidation moving forward, and we may continue to outgrow the market by 3 to 4 percentages.

items.statement: Particle Board old plant shut down and will be scrapped; no revival plans.
items.quote: The old plant, which is a multi -daylight, fairly older technology, that we have shut down. And as of now, there are no plans to revive it. So we will most likely scrap it.

items.statement: Plans 9,557 MW capacity addition in FY27, mostly renewables.
items.quote: as far as FY27 is concerned, on a totality basis, we are planning around 9,557 MW of capacity.

items.statement: Plans 10,039 MW capacity addition in FY28.
items.quote: The year next, FY28, the total plant capacity addition is 10,039 MW

items.statement: Plans 11,478 MW capacity addition in FY29.
items.quote: In a similar way for FY29, we are planning 11,478 MW total capacity.

items.statement: NGEL capex: INR35,800 crore in FY27, INR46,000 crore in FY28, INR48,000 crore in FY29.
items.value: INR35,800 crores; INR46,000 crores; INR48,000 crores
items.quote: For NGEL, for current year it would be c apex of INR 35,800 crores. Next year, it would be INR46,000 crores and the year next, it would be INR48,000 crores.

items.statement: Group capex target INR6,22,000 crore till FY32; half for renewables.
items.quote: We have a broad c apex for the group of INR 6,22,000 crores till the financial '32 and we have allocated roughly half of that, around INR3 lakh crores for renewable energy

items.statement: Plans to add around 8 GW renewable capacity in FY27.
items.quote: In the Renewables segment, we are planning to add around 8 GW capacity.

items.statement: 34 GW under construction: 16.5 GW coal, 2.6 GW hydro, 15 GW renewables.
items.quote: NTPC Group currently has over 34 GW of capacity under construction, comprising 16.5 GW of coal-based capacity, about 2.6 GW of hydro capacity and 15 GW of renewable energy capacity

items.statement: NGEL grid curtailment impact ~INR90 crore; TRAS compensated.
items.quote: as regards the grid curtailment where we are experiencing because of the temporary GNA , it would have an impact close to INR90 crores.

items.statement: FY27 renewable firm connectivity 57%, T-GNA 38%; FY28 88% firm, 3% T-GNA.
items.quote: as far as FY27 is concerned, we have the firm connectivity of 57% and T-GNA of 38%. As far as FY28 is concerned, whatever CODs are expected in FY28, we have a projected firm connectivity of 88% and 3% would be coming from the T -GNA

items.statement: PPA coverage: 79% FY27, 71% FY28, 66% FY29.
items.quote: For FY27, it is 79%. FY 28 CODs of 8,069 MW we are already covered with 71% PPA. And the year next around 8,400 MW, it is 66%.

items.statement: FY27 8 GW renewable addition: 1.9 GW via JVs; FY28: 624 MW via JVs.
items.quote: in FY27, out of the 8 GW around 1.9 GW would come through JVs, primarily through Ayana and a part of that would come through a JV with IOCL that is INGEL. And in FY 28, out of the 8 GW around 624 MW would come through the JV route.

items.statement: Mahi Banswara nuclear: first concrete Aug 2027, first unit sync Nov 2032.
items.quote: The first pour of concrete is anticipated by August 2027. And first unit synchronization we are planning in November 2032.

items.statement: Pump storage: 3-5 GW expected commercialized by 2032-33.
items.quote: Another 3 GW to 5 GW, you can expect to be commercialized by 2032 to '33.

items.statement: Coal gasification pilot at Talaipalli: 4 lakh tonnes per annum synthetic natural gas.
items.quote: we have taken up a pilot project at one of our mines, Talaipalli. And we are going to EIL, and this has a capacity of 4 lakh tonnes per annum.

items.statement: Aims to maintain CASA ratio at 33% plus and CD ratio at 80%.
items.quote: While focusing on CASA, we have assured that 33% plus, we want to maintain 33%-plus of CASA percentage. And all these ratios, once we do that with the CD ratio of 80%...

items.statement: Holds ROA guidance at 1% plus, expected to trend toward improvement.
items.quote: ROA, I was telling 1% plus. 1% plus may be anything. So 1% plus, I will still hold on to it.

items.statement: Plans to increase provision coverage ratio by about 1% every quarter.
items.quote: We want to increase 1% every quarter. That number still I'm holding on.

items.statement: NIM has bottomed out; will work on sustaining 3% plus NIM going forward.
items.quote: As I was telling in the beginning, if you have seen, I am working on that 3% plus NIM. I will be working on it.

items.statement: ECL guidelines impact estimated at 1-1.5% of net worth, spread over 4-5 years at 25-30 bps annually.
items.quote: I believe the guidelines which has now come, which is available to spread over to the next 5 years and we have studied the impact also maybe around 1% to 1.5% overall will be there. Even that also available for the next 4 years or 5 years, that will be spread over to 25 basis points, 30 basis points.

items.statement: Will consciously reduce bulk advances and grow retail and mid-corporate portfolios.
items.quote: Going forward, consciously, we will reduce the bulk advances and we will grow in retail and mid-corporate.

items.statement: Had INR2,000 crores of sanctioned but undisbursed advances as of March; disbursements started post April.
items.quote: And as of March, we had INR2,000 crores of sanctioned but pending for disbursal. It has not happened for various reasons. It started happening post April.

items.statement: Aims to recover 50% of NPA book and 50% of technically written-off book.
items.quote: What quantum, what number, our aim is always to recover 50% of the book of NPA, 50% of the technical written-off.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia and rising input costs could weigh on growth and inflation.
items.quote: However, the war in West Asia, along with the rising input costs driven by higher energy prices and supply chain disruptions, could weigh on the growth.

items.statement: Plans FY27 technology projects: loan origination system revamp, DevSecOps, HRMS and Treasury revamp, BHIM 3.0.
items.quote: A few major solutions that are planned for completion in FY '26-'27 are loan originating system revamp with collateral management, implementation of DevSecOps, HRMS revamp, Treasury revamp and BHIM 3.0.

items.statement: Middle East NRI deposit exposure is not sizable; bank expects limited impact from regional conflict.
items.quote: But with regard to your specific question of the deposits from Middle East, it is not sizable one and we will not be affected much.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% year-over-year.
items.quote: So, from a guidance perspective, I would try to give anywhere between 20% to 25% growth.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin 12.5-13% in short term, 15% long term.
items.quote: So short term, we should be able to do 12.5%, 13% and on the longer term, we should be able to be 15%.

items.statement: Won Mumbai government contract worth Rs 150-200 crore, announcement in 2-3 weeks.
items.quote: It should be to the tune of about anywhere between Rs. 150 crore to Rs. 200 crore.

items.statement: Maharashtra pipeline over Rs 2,000 crore; two large contracts worth Rs 600 crore each upcoming.
items.quote: If I look at Maharashtra as a state, we have close to about Rs. 2,000 crore plus worth of pipeline coming up only in the state of Maharashtra, for which we are very keen on bidding and getting major contracts out of this.

items.statement: Q4 new orders and renewals secured around Rs 166 crore.
items.quote: We secured around Rs. 166 crore in new orders and renewals during this period, reflecting continued demand for our capabilities across digital transformation, infrastructure modernization, managed Services and AI-led Solutions.

items.statement: Government business expected to rebound in FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: At the same time, Government business continues to remain an important and strategic component of our revenue mix, and we anticipate a meaningful rebound in this segment during FY '27, '28.

items.statement: Aim for Services to be 75-80% of revenue for consistency.
items.quote: But if you ask me personally, I would want our Services business to keep on growing and take about 75% to 80% of our top line revenue because that gives a lot of consistency from a growth perspective because most of the Services contracts are signed for 5 years.

items.statement: Western Railway project dropped due to 25-30% equipment cost increase; retender expected mid-July.
items.quote: So that Western Railway project , unfortunately, we had to let it go because by the time the pricing was about to open, the equipment procurement cost went up by 25%, 30%.

items.statement: Audit qualifications to be fully resolved in next 2 quarters after RBI approval.
items.quote: So in next 2 quarters, we should be able to get a clean sheet coming in from everywhere.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to scale business 10x over next decade, implying 20-25% CAGR.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aspire to scale the business 10x over the next decade, which would imply a compounded annual trajectory growth of approximately 20% to 25%.

items.statement: FY27 tax rate expected around 25%, with some deferred tax benefit.
items.quote: It should be 25%, maybe 1%, 2% or 3% here or there, depending upon the deferred tax we get.

items.statement: AI implementation reduces resource count by 20-25% in 6-12 months.
items.quote: So, we see definitely a reduction on the resource count for any customer close to 20%, 25% in a matter of 6 months or a year.

items.statement: Long-term like-for-like growth guidance of 5% to 7% remains; Q1 FY27 already better than Q4 FY26.
items.quote: So SSSG, we've given a commentary already, right, on Q1 and the longer term or the annual number, 5% to 7% remains. The quarter 1, we've already done better than Q4.

items.statement: Long-term margin guidance of 200 bps expansion holds, but short-term margin pressure expected.
items.quote: In the letter also we have said the long -term margin guidance on 200 bps holds and we'll try as quickly to get to that elevated number. But short-term pressure exist.

items.statement: Plans to open 230 to 250 restaurants this year; capex per store down 20% for nearly 3 years.
items.quote: So from all accounts, right, store addition and expansion is not a worry, we would open similar to about 230 to 250 kind of restaurants this year.

items.statement: Took 120 bps of pricing to offset energy cost inflation of 100-120 bps.
items.quote: We've already passed on the pricing to the tune of 120 basis points to the customers.

items.statement: Energy cost inflation of 100-120 bps already hitting P&L; LPG and PNG costs up.
items.quote: To some extent it's been very hard to calibrate Avi, but the energy is definitely the tune of 100 to 120 basis points, that hit we are already beginning to see come into the P&L.

items.statement: Labour Code adds ~20 bps; state minimum wage hikes add 20-30 bps; delivery mix adds further labor inflation.
items.quote: One is, of course, Labour Code is absolutely write-up of about 20-odd bps. But the minimum wage increases that we have seen across some of the states that have already gone live over 11 states out of 29 have already announced, and we'll wait and see some more, but that's another 20, 30 bps, which is there.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement is sustainable, driven by wastage reduction, premium products, mix changes and calibrated price increases.
items.quote: Actually, gross margin is sustainable. I think we answered that before.

items.statement: Will tighten belts first and not pass on all inflation; calibrated price increases to consumers later.
items.quote: What we are doing is, of course, first tighten our belts and not pass on everything to the consumer and the resul tant will have to pass on to the consumer after doing a thorough calibration of price increases.

items.statement: Domino's gained market share in pizza category and QSR space per Nielsen panel of 50,000 customers.
items.quote: And we have a separate panel of 50,000 customers run by Nielsen. They are also indicating that we have gained share, and we have gained share materially in pizza as a category.

items.statement: Consciously reduced minimum order value from Rs.149 to Rs.99 to gain share and acquire customers, lowering average ticket size.
items.quote: We have very consciously taken a call to reduce minimum order value from Rs.149 to Rs. 99. And as a result, there was a drop in the average ticket size.

items.statement: Near-term inflation pressure high across energy, labor and commodities; hard to predict duration.
items.quote: We're entering an inflationary environment; at least near-term inflation pressure is high. To some extent it's been very hard to calibrate Avi, but the energy is definitely the tune of 100 to 120 basis points, that hit we are already beginning to see come into the P&L.

items.statement: Launched premium products (Big Big Pizza, Sourdough Pizza) with better margins; supply chain cost lowest ever.
items.quote: We launched Big Big Pizza, we launched Sourdough Pizza, we launched some of the more premium products.

items.statement: Converting LPG ovens to electric and piped natural gas; large part of delivery fleet is electric, an advantage.
items.quote: Where the teams have done an amazing job of converting LPG to electric, we have developed our own solution kits. We've also been able to import quite a lot of electric ovens. And we are also converting very quickly to pipe natural gas, and there is a mandate from the government to convert to pipe natural gas.

items.statement: No major price increases planned; will not do major price increases.
items.quote: We will not do major price increases that is out of the table. Otherwise, we know what needs to be done on the margin front.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20% for FY27.
items.quote: As we have said, we are targeting 20% of revenue growth we are looking at.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance of INR8,000-10,000 crores for FY27.
items.quote: So order book guidance, as I said, it is INR8,000 c rores to INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 9.5-10.5% for FY27.
items.quote: Our estimation for FY '27 based on the order book which we have, we will be in the range of 9.5% to 10.5% for next year.

items.statement: Capex plan of approximately INR100 crores for FY27.
items.quote: We're planning approximately around INR100 crores o f capex, which includes certain capex on the international projects also.

items.statement: Monetization of 4 HAM assets by June 2026, expecting INR750+ crores.
items.quote: So to continue on that, out of the 6 projects, 4 we are definitely targeting by June end, which will typically bring in cash of around INR750-plus crores.

items.statement: Monetization of remaining 2 HAM assets by December 2026, expecting INR400 crores.
items.quote: And the balance we expect by December, which should bring in another INR400 crores.

items.statement: Working capital expected to normalize to 110-120 days post September.
items.quote: we believe that we should go back to the old norms of 110 to 120 days, this is more of a transitory as in the last call also, we had said there was some buildup of receivables in our Power division, which probably by end of June and September quarter, most of things would get cleared.

items.statement: Debt level expected to be INR500-600 crores by March 2027.
items.quote: And we believe that the debt level will be in the range of INR500 crores to INR600 crores by March '27 also, keeping all almost similar kind of turnover with a 20% jump.

items.statement: Balance HAM equity investment of INR325 crores, with INR175 crores in FY27.
items.quote: So on the equity side, the balance investment to be made in the HAM projects is around INR325 crores.

items.statement: Deferred consideration of INR550 crores expected in 24-36 months.
items.quote: And there are certain deferred consideration, which is based on toll extension, which is approximately INR550 crores, which will come in the next 1 or 2 years' time.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 was INR67 crores, with Q4 at INR16 crores.
items.quote: Q4, so total capex for the year was, INR67 crores, of which Q4 was INR16 crores.

items.statement: Effective tax on HAM asset sales expected at 6-7%.
items.quote: So effective tax on al l the put together would be in the range of 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Long-term vision to deliver INR 17,500 crores top line with 12.5% EBITDA margin by 2030.
items.quote: Yes. So we have kept the long-term vision in mind for 2030 to deliver INR 17,500 crores top line with 12.5% EBITDA margin. And the whole group is working towards achieving those stated numbers.

items.statement: Guiding principle to grow at least 50% more than industry growth; if industry grows 10%, revenue growth 15%+.
items.quote: While we don't give future outlook in terms of revenue guidance, but our guiding principle has been that we want to grow our business at least 50% more than the industry growth. So if the industry grows about 10%, so we should look at revenue growth in Minda Corporation to the tune of 15% plus.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected INR 400-450 crores, up from INR 350-400 crores range.
items.quote: So our capex has been in the range of INR 350 crores to INR 400 crores. And this year also, we expect to be in that range, maybe 10% plus of that, close to about INR 400 crores, INR 450 crores capex we are expecting for fiscal year 2026-27.

items.statement: Lifetime order book of INR 10,000 crores with execution timeline of 48-60 months.
items.quote: Now our order book is INR 10,000 crores, which we have registered throughout the year, and different product, different customer will have a different life cycle. Some maybe order for 5 years, so maybe for 6 years. But by and large, you can say it ranges anywhere between 48 months to 60 months.

items.statement: Commodity inflation passed through to customers, but no profit element, so some EBITDA margin impact.
items.quote: So any escalation should not necessarily eat up our margin. But definitely, since there is no profit element attached to the escalation, you would see some bit of impact on the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Commodity prices (copper, zinc, aluminum) escalated 30-40% throughout the year; contracts on pass-through basis.
items.quote: And when I look at across our main commodity, whether it is copper, zinc and aluminum, throughout the year, we saw escalation anywhere between 30% to 40% and most of our contracts with our customers are on pass-through basis.

items.statement: Passenger Vehicle segment at overall Minda Corporation level will grow north of 20% in FY27.
items.quote: So, the Passenger Vehicle segment at the overall Minda Corporation level will grow north of 20%.

items.statement: Instrument cluster and wiring harness to see maximum product launches in FY27, followed by die casting for exports.
items.quote: However, in terms of the products wise, you can say the instrument cluster business as well as the wiring harness business will see the maximum amount of product launches, followed by the die casting for exports will be the top 3.

items.statement: Minda VAST consolidation from FY27 to accelerate vision of 25% revenue from Passenger Vehicle segment.
items.quote: With the consolidation of Minda VAST business with Minda Corporation from FY 27 onwards, it will certainly accelerate our vision to achieve 25% revenue from Passenger Vehicle segment, which currently stands at about 14%.

items.statement: Sunroof JV received lifetime order of INR 350 crores; mass production in next 4-5 months; FY28 first full year.
items.quote: So yes, for sunroof, we have received the lifetime order of about INR 350 crores last year. We are getting into the mass production in the next 4 to 5 months. So yes, FY28 will be the first full year revenue.

items.statement: Switches JV mass production by March; FY28 ramp-up year, FY29 first peak year.
items.quote: When it comes to the switches, which is coming again into the mass production by March this year, so the FY28 will be the ramp-up year, I would say. So the first peak year would be, let's say, FY29 for the switches joint venture.

items.statement: Commodity inflation expected to continue at least next quarter due to geopolitical situation.
items.quote: So unless and until the geopolitical situation improves, we don't see this cooling off at least in the next quarter or so.

items.statement: Turntide JV orders for motor controllers to start SOP in 5-6 months; motors under advanced discussion.
items.quote: Number two, when it comes to the Turntide joint venture. As I mentioned, we've already won orders when it comes to the motor controllers as well as the other electronic space. So that is going to start SOP in about 5 to 6 months.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 outlook positive with several high-profile releases; confident of continuing last year's momentum.
items.quote: The outlook for the upcoming quarter remains positive, with several high-profile releases, including “Peddi”, “Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai”, “Welcome to the Jungle”, “Sarpanch”, “Cocktail 2” etc. With this robust lineup, we remain confident about continuing with the momentum of last year.

items.statement: Caravan business fully shut down; assets already disposed, realizing about INR 2-3 crores.
items.quote: We have already disposed of the assets, and these vans were quite old, more than 10 years old. So the amount of realization on that front totally would have been around INR 2 crores to INR 3 crores.

items.statement: Caravan business discontinued due to inconsistent pipeline; may operate via third-party tie-ups with no cost.
items.quote: Secondly, on the Caravan front, we have discontinued the Caravan business operations because there was significant inconsistency in the business pipeline.

items.statement: Ad revenue-sharing ratio should gradually decline as revenues scale up; ~80% of sharing expense is minimum-guarantee based.
items.quote: Therefore, nearly 80% of the revenue-sharing expense falls into this category, and that is the reason why, as revenues scale up, the sharing ratio should gradually decline.

items.statement: Ad-sharing with theatres rose to 50-60% from legacy 30-35% due to multiplex-heavy network; not losing pricing power.
items.quote: So, I think that’s a very valid observation regarding ad-sharing increasing from the earlier 30–35% range, which used to be our legacy percentage, to now being in the 50% –60% range.

items.statement: Where UFO invests in infrastructure, sharing percentage is lower, typically 35% to 45% depending on revenues.
items.quote: One, where we invest in the infrastructure, in which case the sharing percentage is relatively lower and typically ranges between 35% to 45%, depending on revenues.

items.statement: Consolidated DSO rose to 147 days in FY26 from 121 days in FY25, largely due to Dhurandhar receivables.
items.quote: To give you some perspective on DSOs, or Days Sales Outstanding, the consolidated DSO for the current year stands at 147 days, compared to 121 days in FY25, and this increase is largely attributable to the reasons I just mentioned.

items.statement: Net cash improved from INR 48.3 crores to INR 59 crores during the year despite working capital getting tied up.
items.quote: Our net cash has improved from INR 48.3 crores to INR 59 crores during the year, despite nearly INR 11 crores getting further tied up in working capital.

items.statement: Company will maintain both cash and debt on books; debt funds theatre equipment via LC converted to loan.
items.quote: The debt is taken specifically to fund the expensive equipment installed in theatres. Typically, we open a n LC, which subsequently gets converted into a loan.

items.statement: Company may reward shareholders with excess cash again once profitability turnaround sustains.
items.quote: And obviously, whenever excess cash is not required and there is an opportunity to reward shareholders, as we have done in the past, we will continue to ev aluate that.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 saw improving theatrical momentum; March strongest led by Dhurandhar: The Revenge.
items.quote: March was clearly the strongest month of the quarter, led by the exceptional success of “Dhurandhar: The Revenge”, which emerged as one of the biggest box office successes of the year.

items.statement: UFO network contributes 40-45% of footfalls for major blockbusters; got ~30% ad revenue share for Dhurandhar.
items.quote: For example, for any major blockbuster movie, the UFO network contributes nearly 40 –45% of the overall footfalls. However, historically, we were not receiving a proportionate share of advertising revenues associated with those movies.

items.statement: Employee cost rise largely due to ~INR 9 crores variable payouts after better profitability; costs under continuous monitoring.
items.quote: If you refer to Slide 18 of the investor presentation, we have highlighted that, on a full -year basis, there has been a variable payout of around INR 9 crores during the current year.

items.statement: VPF and CDC revenues declined in Q4 due to blank February and blockbuster clustering; full-year both grew.
items.quote: CDC and VPF revenues have gone down . So, that observation is correct for Q4. However, if you look at the full -year performance, revenues in both the CDC as well as VPF categories have increased.

items.statement: Expects 10-12% cement volume growth in FY27, excluding clinker sales.
items.quote: What we are looking for in the coming year is about 10% to 12% growth.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR600-700 crore, FY28 at INR1,500 crore.
items.quote: I think the estimate for FY27 will be about INR600 crores to INR700 crores given we follow these timelines.

items.statement: FY28 capex estimated at INR1,500 crore.
items.quote: In FY28, I think the estimate would be about INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton expected INR1,500-1,700 for next 2-3 years until Rajasthan project.
items.quote: I think for the next 2, 3 years till when we get the Rajasthan project, I think the EBITDA is -- because it is only in Northeast sales, the EBITDA should be between INR1,500 to INR1,700, right, at least.

items.statement: Long-term blended EBITDA per ton expected INR1,300-1,400 after Rajasthan ramp-up.
items.quote: But I think in the long run, we should be able to maintain it at about INR1,300, INR1,400 blended.

items.statement: Fuel cost to increase by INR0.10-0.15 per GCV in Q1/Q2 due to rake shortage, normalizing by Q3/Q4.
items.quote: So, I think there would be an impact of, I think, about INR 0.10 to INR0.15 per GCV cost in coal.

items.statement: Price increase of INR6-7 per bag in Northeast and INR10 per bag outside Northeast in April-May.
items.quote: Northeast, I think it may be about INR6 to INR7. Outside Northeast was about INR10.

items.statement: Demand sluggish in April due to elections, pickup in May; too early to predict full year.
items.quote: So, the current scenario right now, because of April, there was elections in April and May in Assam and also West Bengal. So, I think the demand was a bit sluggish because of that. I think we do see a pickup in May.

items.statement: New entrants to Northeast may pressure pricing for 1-2 years, but rationality expected to normalize.
items.quote: So, I think it's something that probably may happen for a year or 2, but then I think it should normalize because everyone is there to earn, right?

items.statement: Premium cement share was 15.1% in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: The premium cement share for this quarter was 15.1%.

items.statement: Trade share decreased to 78% in Q4 FY26 from 81% last year.
items.quote: So, trade share is about 78%. Last year, same quarter, it was 81%.

items.statement: QIP decision not yet taken at Board level; will inform in advance when planned.
items.quote: I think that decision we still not have taken at the Board level. We have, of course, taken the permission for raising money in the Board. I think in quarter 3, we did that. But we haven't planned it also because the markets were, of course, a bit weak as well, right?

items.statement: Subsidy expected to reduce by INR40-50 crore per quarter in FY27, totaling INR145-150 crore.
items.quote: So current year, we have done INR184 crores of subsidy. So what Tushar ji is saying INR40 crores to INR50 crores, somewhere in the INR145 crores to INR150 crores sort of thing you can estimate for the coming year.

items.statement: Targets 8% store EBITDA for Spencer's in FY27.
items.quote: And we are quite confident that going forward in FY'27, we will be able to achieve that 8% store EBITDA.

items.statement: Plans to break even on offline business this year.
items.quote: The plan is that this year, we will be able to break even on the offline business, definitely.

items.statement: Aims to reduce online business loss to low double digit or single digit.
items.value: low double digit, ideally in single digit
items.quote: we want to reduce this to low double digit, ideally in single digit.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA breakeven at operational level in FY27.
items.quote: the management ask is that in FY'27, we breakeven at an EBITDA level, at an operational EBITDA level.

items.statement: Will add 3-4 Spencer's stores this year, not as growth basis.
items.quote: you will see 3 -4 stores of Spencer's coming up in this year.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to remain 9.5-10.5% in FY27.
items.quote: Right now, we are in the range of 9.5 - 10.5%, and we expect that to continue in the financial year as well.

items.statement: Confident to sustain growth in Q1-Q4 of current year.
items.quote: I'm quite confident that we'll be able to sustain this in Q1-Q4 of the current year.

items.statement: Online business to grow from INR200 crores to INR250 crores next year.
items.quote: The idea is for it to go from INR200 crores to INR250 crores next year

items.statement: Nature's Basket faces internal challenges; next 2 quarters critical.
items.quote: Nature's Basket is, I would say, next 2 quarters are going to be critical, and we will demonstrate and drive growth over the next 2 quarters on that.

items.statement: Membership program has ~100,000 members, 20-22% of monthly sales.
items.quote: we closed the year with close to 100,000 members who had not only bought into the membership, but had also used the membership.

items.statement: Online business grew 37% YoY to INR200 crores in FY26.
items.quote: The online part of the business grew by 37% YoY. So closed at INR200 crores for FY'26, which was 37% increase over the previous year.

items.statement: SPSF improved from INR1,400 to INR1,700 per month per sq ft; target INR2,000.
items.quote: On Spencer's, in FY'25, we were at around INR1,400 per month per square foot. That number has gone up to close to INR1,700.

items.statement: Membership cash back impacted Q4 margins by 120 bps; real margin 18.6%.
items.quote: the 17.4% margin in Q4 on Spencer's is actually there is a 120 -basis point impact of the membership cash back. So, the real margin delivered on the category intake side is 18.6%.

items.statement: Eye tests growing 50%, volume growth 25%, focus on improving conversion post eye test.

items.statement: FY27 priority: transform into consumer AI company, step up R&D investments.

items.statement: Ambition to scale to 100 million eye tests, eventually a billion.

items.quote: we continue to aspire to do 40 to 50 clinics in India. We try to do 10 to 15 in Philippines.

items.quote: from a guidance point of view, we are not giving any guidance on the capex amount, but suffice to say that we have we have the cash and we have a approach in place and we will follow that.

items.statement: Platform costs in India during international ramp-up; best to view at consolidated level.

items.quote: So, in this coming year, we are not expecting any large price increase, but RPT change will be a factor of geography mix.

items.quote: Saudi, as we mentioned, we are on the in the investment phase and there is just recently a new contract or new tender which has been just released and it's at the EOI stage, which will take couple of quarters to take shape.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected mid-to-high teens; EBITDA margin 14-14.5%.

items.quote: So this is around mid -teen revenue growth we foresee we will be achieving, coupled with the EBITDA around something 14% to 14.5% for FY 2027.

items.statement: Greenfield project total outlay INR1,200-1,400 crore over 4-5 years, annual capex INR200-250 crore.
items.quote: Broad mind set is around INR1,200 crores to INR1,400 crore.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR200 crore, 60% growth, 40% infra/automation, mostly pharma.
items.quote: So generally, we are doing 60% growth and 40% for development of infra and automation and land procurement. So generally 60% on growth activities.

items.statement: Paracetamol capacity utilization to rise from 55% to 75% in FY27, full by FY28.
items.quote: We are hopeful that we will be reaching to around 70% to 75% capacity utilization in FY 2027 itself. And I think in FY 2028, we will be having the full capacity utilization by that time.

items.statement: Non-ibuprofen exports to regulated markets targeted at 25% of segment in FY27.
items.quote: So we are expecting that we should achieve around 25% in this FY 2027.

items.statement: Ibuprofen demand expected stable for next 4-6 quarters; annual growth 3-4%.
items.quote: And we anticipate that this level will maintain upcoming four to six quarters.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by operational efficiency, product mix, capacity utilization, not inventory gains.
items.quote: This is mainly because of the operational efficiencies from our side and good traction in the non-Ibu.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues and logistics delays impacting raw material prices, but no major supply disruption.
items.quote: I think not much issue, but the prices across the board of the -- all the raw materials has gone up to the extent that crude is having the impact. Logistics has also gone up and is going up. And some delays in the logistics across the globe.

items.statement: No buyback planned; funds prioritized for growth projects.
items.quote: As of now, no, because as of now, this has not been discussed in the Board. But I think whenever this is discussed, we will -- as of now, we are focusing on the growth.

items.statement: R&D expenses 2-3% of revenue annually, focused on process development.
items.quote: Sachinji, in R&D, we are having around 2% to 3% expenses annually.

items.statement: Employee benefit expenses expected at 9-10% of turnover.
items.quote: on turnover, we are having around 10%.

items.statement: Maximum revenue potential from existing capacity INR3,200-3,300 crore at 100% utilization.
items.quote: So I think having -- considering the -- if we achieve 100% for all, this will be around INR3,200 crores to INR3,300 crores.

items.statement: Expects 20-25% revenue growth in FY27 over previous year.
items.quote: What I can tell you on overall revenue is we are expecting about 20% to 25% growth in revenue in FY27 from the previous year.

items.statement: Targets revenue of INR1,000 crores with EBITDA margin over 18% by Vision 2029.
items.quote: We aim to achieve revenue of INR1,000 crores while maintaining EBITDA margins of over 18%.

items.statement: Saudi plant capex expected at INR20-25 crores.
items.quote: The Saudi plant for us, we expect to spend approximately INR20 crores to INR25 crores.

items.statement: Pyrolysis and rCB capex approximately INR40 crores, largely completed.
items.quote: The pyro, RCB capex is approximately INR40-odd crores, and that's largely completed.

items.statement: PCMB contribution expected to rise to 8-10% of turnover in FY27 from 4%.
items.quote: We expect the contribution from the PCMB business to increase to 8% to 10% in FY27, supported by strong business momentum.

items.statement: PCMB revenue projected at approximately INR75 crores in FY27.
items.quote: for FY '27, our projection of revenue contribution from PCMB is about INR75 crores.

items.statement: rCB and TPO plants expected to contribute INR50-55 crores top line in FY27.
items.quote: our projection for this RCB and TPO plant for the FY27 is somewhere around INR50 crores-INR55-odd crores for the FY27.

items.statement: Expects to maintain ~18% EBITDA margin achieved in Q4.
items.quote: we have achieved about 18% EBITDA in Q4. We expect to maintain that.

items.statement: Pyrolysis and rCB plants expected at 15-19% EBITDA margins.
items.quote: Our expectation is maybe 15% on the low side and 18% or 19% on the high side.

items.statement: Infra business may see reduction in Q1-Q2 FY27 due to bitumen shortage, but normalize later.
items.quote: we expect some reduction possibly in the infra business during Q1, Q2 of this year. And that is probably, it will be because of less availability of bitumen.

items.statement: Industrial segment expected to see very strong growth in FY27.
items.quote: We absolutely see very strong growth in the Industrial segment.

items.statement: Plans to finance capex mostly from internal accruals, may take up to INR20 crores debt.
items.quote: We may opt to take up to about INR20 crores of debt also, but I don't expect it to be any more than that.

items.statement: Expects 15-20% top-line growth in FY27, with at least 10% volume growth, assuming stable metal prices.
items.quote: assuming that the current metal prices levels have stayed over the year, we should be achieving some 15-20% growth in top line. That should be around minimum 10% of volume growth.

items.statement: Aims to return to pre-U.S. tariff margin levels by end of FY27.
items.quote: by end of FY27, we hope to achieve the pre-tariff, you know, pre-U.S. tariff levels of margin also.

items.statement: Narmadapuram greenfield project to invest ~INR 300 crores by FY28, operations start Q1 FY28.
items.quote: The project at Narmadapuram envisages an investment of approximately INR 300 crores by FY28, with operations expected to partly commence in Q1 FY28 and ramp up through FY28.

items.statement: Targets INR 500 crores sales from Narmadapuram in FY28, scaling to INR 1,200 crores in FY29.
items.quote: We are targeting sales of approximately INR 500 crores from Narmadapuram in FY28, which will scale up to INR 1,200 crores in FY29.

items.statement: Narmadapuram plant margins expected at 9-10%.
items.quote: And margin from this Narmadapuram plant are expected to be between 9-10%.

items.statement: Aims to achieve INR 5,000 crores revenue by FY31, doubling sales every 3-4 years.
items.quote: we will begin to achieve the revenue milestone of INR 5,000 crores in the next five years, that is by FY31, which shall mean that we will be having to double our sales every three to four years.

items.statement: Order book as of March 31, 2026: INR 583 crores total, INR 508 crores domestic, INR 76 crores exports.
items.quote: Our order book as of 31st March 2026 stood at INR 583 crores, comprising INR 508 crores of domestic orders and INR 76 crores of exports.

items.statement: Expects strong U.S. demand recovery from Q2 FY27 onwards.
items.quote: we are expecting that Q2 onwards, actually, we should be seeing a very good demand pull out of the U.S.

items.statement: Policy to avoid firm-price orders beyond 3-4 months to mitigate metal price volatility.
items.quote: Paramount continues to follow a deliberate policy of not accepting firm-price orders with delivery horizon beyond three to four months, a discipline that protects our margins from copper and aluminum price volatility.

items.statement: Narmadapuram to focus on EHV cables up to 132 kV, specialized conductors, and elastomeric cables.
items.quote: The product focus for Narmadapuram will be extra high voltage cables up to 132 kV, specialized conductors and cables for the transmission sector, elastomeric EBeam cables, and EPR cables, etc., EPR, lead-sheathed rubber cables.

items.statement: U.S. tariffs caused significant disruption in FY26, but recovery expected.
items.quote: Such huge increases in U.S. tariffs over a very short period of time, without any notice at all, caused a significant disruption for our export business in FY26.

items.statement: Equity raise of INR 122 crores for Narmadapuram project, with promoters contributing INR 30 crores.
items.quote: Out of the overall project of INR 300 crores, around INR 122 crores out of this INR 30 crore, of course, the promoters we ourselves are putting in, INR 92 crores all is coming from investors.

items.statement: Targets double-digit margins within 3-4 years.
items.quote: we are looking at double-digit margins within the next three to four years at the minimum.

items.statement: With Phase 1 and existing capacity, peak revenue potential of INR 3,600-4,000 crores.
items.quote: from the Phase 1, I think from Phase 1, we should be able to touch around INR 3600-4000 crores.

items.statement: Thousand crore turnover target is for 2030, not FY27.
items.quote: This is in terms of numbers the thousand crore is not for the next financial year. It is the target of 2030 for which we are gearing up in terms of capacity expansion in powder as well as egg production.

items.statement: 400 crore capex to expand layer birds from 20 lakh to 40 lakh by 2029.
items.quote: This 48,4400-crore investment where currently we are at 20 lakh birds and by 2029 we will be at 40 lakh birds.

items.statement: Plan to increase egg powder capacity from 7,000 to 10,000 tons over five years.
items.quote: We are looking to do 10,000 tons. The capex is analyzed be able to give a better picture by end of next quarter or after that. But definitely there is plan to invest to enhance our capacity to about 10,000 tons and when we will realize this is the next question. Maybe you can take five years’ time to achieve some 7,000

items.statement: Capex to add at least 50 paisa per egg gross margin by replacing market purchases.
items.quote: There is a gross margin of at least 50 paisa market price and oil production at this stage.

items.statement: Average realization is about 722 on powder terms, expected to continue next quarter.
items.quote: So, our average realization is about 722. This is on powder terms which I expect to continue for the coming quarter because the international market situation there are some changes, but it is not going to affect us very hugely.

items.statement: FY27 capacity fully utilized, no big increase in powder top line expected.
items.quote: So, for 26 - 27 we don't foresee a very big increase in capacity.

items.statement: Q4 realization dip due to product mix, not a concern.
items.quote: So, quarter four was a slight dip, but it's because of the product mix that goes on.

items.statement: Bird flu is the biggest disruptor, causing supply fluctuations and price volatility.
items.quote: Price trend Bird flu so bird flu is the biggest disruptor in our industry.

items.statement: Acquiring remaining 74% of SKM Universal for 27.75 crores, total valuation 37 crores.
items.quote: I think the valuation number that is about 37 crores for the entire company. Since our company already holds 26%, the 74% is 27.75 crores is the out pay that will go.

items.statement: Japan branch expected by July end, will increase market share.
items.quote: Japan is under the establishment hopefully within two to three months we will have our Japan branch by July end of something.

items.statement: Realize at least 5% more than competition in key markets due to quality and reputation.
items.quote: I can tell you we realize at least 5% more than our competition in these markets.

items.statement: Forex hedging: currently 30% covered, usually 70% covered, due to high volatility.
items.quote: We are currently at 30% coverage because of the high volatility we see now. So, we have not done the 70%. We have gone down. We have kept the open 70% and 30% covered.

items.statement: Contracts: 70-75% on contractual basis, 20-30% spot, typically 3-6 months.
items.quote: And about 70% of our business, 75% of our business is on contractual basis. About 20, 30% is on spot basis.

items.statement: New value-added Egg Pro drink reformulated, launching this week from June.
items.quote: We have already reformulated our Egg Pro drink which will be put into market this week from June.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected 9-11% with EBITDA margin improvement of 50-100 bps.
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY '27, we remain confident in our growth trajectory and currently expect revenue growth of 9% to 11%, along with an improvement in EBITDA margin of 50 to 100 basis points.

items.statement: Margin improvement to come from gross margin and employee cost, targeting peak 15% gradually.
items.quote: we have guided 50 to 100 basis point year-over-year improvement next year, we have given a guidance.

items.statement: Digital mix on track to reach 50% by end of FY27.
items.quote: We remain on track to reach 50% digital mix towards the end of FY '27.

items.statement: Lifestyle products currently 35% of sales, targeting 50% medium-term.
items.quote: Our product mix, lifestyle products now contribute around 35% of total sales, and we continue to target a medium -term share of 50%.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds contribute 11% of retail revenue at average selling price ~$250.
items.quote: Lab- grown diamonds are another important new lever. LGD now contributes 11% of retail revenue at an average selling price of around USD 250.

items.statement: Germany achieved EBITDA breakeven in FY26, expected to contribute to group profitability from FY27.
items.quote: Germany is now well placed to contribute to group profitability from FY '27 onwards.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to be steady around 22% for upcoming years.
items.quote: So our tax rate will be steady around 22% for the upcoming years.

items.statement: TV broadcasting and content costs to remain around 20% of revenue.
items.quote: We expect that this will continue to be around in 20-odd percentage that line.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty remains but company agile with multi-country operations.
items.quote: With the current administration, Mehul, we can never be certain. -- but I can only say that is whatever the circumstances, we are very agile and pretty multi-country operations and logistics that we'll deal better than competitors.

items.statement: Mindful Souls impairment of INR25 crores due to conservative testing; potential reversal if performance improves.
items.quote: But for now, because of the initial year, we haven't converted well from Mindful souls, that is why the write-off is coming INR25 crores.

items.statement: New U.K. lease signed, ROU assets increased; operational efficiencies expected from consolidating buildings.
items.quote: So ROU increase is mainly related to the new lease we have signed for the U.K. premises.

items.statement: AI integrated across marketing and operations, improving conversion and customer spend.
items.quote: So from product identification to creative angles to making the creative AI and the landing pages and analytics. Completely this is on the marketing side. Now we are also using AI in our operations to -- for the supply chain demand forecasting into the back-end supply chain analysis and optimization.

items.statement: 99acres aims to double billings over 3 years and reach 25-30% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: We should aim to at least double our business, if you ask me, over the next 3 years. If we are able to do that, then we should be able to generate at least a 25-30% EBITDA margin as well.

items.statement: Naukri margins to remain stable if topline grows double digits; may dip if growth slows to 7-8%.
items.quote: If you're able to grow at 10% or more, you should be able to maintain margin in Naukri. If we grow faster than that, then margins could get better going forward. If we, on the other hand, if the economy slows down further and Naukri grows at 7-8%, then we may sort of lose a little bit of margin in the short term.

items.statement: JobHai to grow 100% YoY for next few years; expand to Mumbai and Bangalore.
items.quote: We would like to grow it 100% year on year for the next few years.

items.statement: AI-Rex and Talent Pulse aim for few hundred crores incremental revenue over 3 years.
items.quote: over a three-year period, it'd be great if we can make a few hundred crores of incremental revenue from these offerings.

items.statement: 99acres billings growth to recover in Q1 after Q4 transitional impact.
items.quote: We expect billings growth to recover in Q1 once again.

items.statement: Shiksha AI headwind to persist near term; initiatives to progressively offset.
items.quote: We expect this headwind to persist over the near term.

items.statement: Continue investing in JobHai and AI without starving them.
items.quote: We don't want to starve these two areas of investment. We'll continue to invest in both JobHai and AI, important for us for the long term.

items.statement: 99acres Q4 revenue boosted by Rs.20.5 crore one-time warranty provision reversal; not recurring.
items.quote: a portion of the accumulated provision over the last 8 quarters has been reversed and revenue for the quarter as well as for the year stands increased by Rs. 20.5 crores as a result.

items.statement: Jeevansathi faces pricing pressure from competitors' discounts, but ability to withstand improved.
items.quote: The market continues to be comparative with leading matrimony platforms investing in marketing and offering higher than usual discounts. This has led to some pressure on pricing.

items.statement: Hiring sentiment subdued and stable; non-IT slowed; AI/ML roles growing.
items.quote: See the overall job market, I think the sentiment continues to be subdued. It's not a hot market. It's a lukewarm market.

items.statement: Premium hiring segment growing faster than mid-level; Naukri strong there.
items.quote: The premium segment and when I say premium, I mean, people who earn more than, let's say, Rs.25-30 lakhs a year. That segment has been growing faster than the mid-level segment for the last few quarters.

items.statement: AI-driven search changes affecting Shiksha traffic and billings.
items.quote: AI-driven changes in search behaviour have been affecting Shiksha's traffic for several quarters. In Q4, this translated into a more direct billing impact as reduced referred search traffic from Google affected client deliveries.

items.quote: As stated, we are planning to utilize it INR1,000 crores in FY '26, INR600 crores in FY '27 and INR500 crores in '28, post which we aim to be FCF positive in FY '29.
