items.quote: We expect Receivables and Inventory to normalize during the 1H of FY27.

items.statement: Higher education share fell from 20% pre-COVID to 8% currently; school segment grew 20-25%.
items.quote: Just to add to that, pre -COVID, higher education constituted almost 20% of our market. Currently, it's about 8%. So, the degrowth has happened in the higher education segment. The school segment continues to still grow. So, we are higher by about 20% to 25 % in the school segment.

items.statement: Considering buyback but waiting for war situation to settle; cash position expected at Rs130-135 crores next year.
items.quote: Yes, yes, we are considering that. Unfortunately, because of the war situation, we are waiting for things to settle down because it's best to have cash in books for this uncertain period.

items.statement: Plans small capital investment of Rs5-7 crores over next 2-3 years for international business expansion.
items.quote: So, we are not going to spend too much of money, maybe a small capital investment in the next 2 to 3 years of maybe Rs5 crores to Rs7 crores, nothing large, nothing major.

items.statement: Management guides over 15% revenue growth for FY27, excluding potential price retrigger benefits.
items.quote: I do expect that even on a conservative level, I am happy to give a guidance of over a 15% growth in the overall revenue.

items.statement: Company aims to double revenues every three to four years with improving margins and returns.
items.quote: we expect to double our revenues every three to four years with consistent improvements in margins and return on investments.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected at INR 275-310 crores, 5-7% of revenues, including growth, maintenance and upgradation.
items.value: INR 275 crores to around INR 310 crores
items.quote: you can expect somehow capital outlay of INR 275 crores to around INR 310 crores for the upcoming financial year, which will include a part of growth CapEx, part of maintenance CapEx, part of upgradation CapEx

items.statement: Existing projects expected to improve EBITDA margins by about 0.25% in FY27.
items.quote: yes we could expect a growth of 0.25% in EBITDA margins.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain around 11% while absolute returns and ROCE improve with volumes.
items.quote: while EBITDA levels will remain constant around 11%, but with the volumes coming up and the revenue going up, automatically in terms of absolute returns, our multiplier will be giving us a more return on capital employed.

items.statement: Targets post-tax ROCE improving from 15% to a peak of 20%.
items.quote: we are targeting an improvement return on capital employed starting with a post-tax return of 15%, going something at a highest peak of 20%.

items.statement: At INR 10,000 crores revenue, expects PAT of around INR 450 crores.
items.quote: on a INR 10,000 crores of revenue, we could be in a position to generate a PAT of around INR 450 crores

items.statement: New projects with INR 342 crores investment generated INR 468 crores revenue; expected to reach around INR 750 crores in FY27.
items.quote: around INR 750 crores of revenue these projects can do. 468 they have already delivered.

items.statement: EV business revenue expected to double in FY27 but remain loss-making until FY28 turnaround.
items.quote: This year, we expect the revenues to approximately double, but there would be losses again as we are trying to develop more new products also and capturing new markets.

items.statement: Overseas business faces aluminum price pass-through lag; Q1 FY27 may see dip before recovery.
items.quote: with the recent increase in aluminum prices, we might find a little bit of a dip in Quarter 1, but once the regenerative cycle of the pass-through of aluminum prices comes through, we are back on track

items.statement: Pricing retrigger mechanism likely activated due to rising input costs, benefiting company versus older customer pricing.
items.quote: there will be a pricing retrigger mechanism that will be activated, and sometimes this becomes positive for the company because many costs or pricing that has been done by the customer was done years ago

items.statement: Demand outlook very positive, especially two-wheelers; industry lost 200,000-300,000 vehicles in April due to manpower issues.
items.quote: the entire industry, according to my understanding, would have lost somewhere in the region of almost 200,000 to 300,000 vehicles.

items.statement: Manpower availability and rising state minimum wages (30-50%) pose significant industry-wide risk.
items.quote: various state governments increasing the minimum wages by almost 30% to 40%. And yesterday, Karnataka giving an indication that that could be even higher than 50%

items.statement: Term loans of INR 384 crores to be repaid over 3-4 years; FY27 repayment commitment around INR 103 crores.
items.quote: This year we have a repayment commitment of around close to INR 103 crores with various banks.

items.statement: Committed to 15-20% YoY revenue growth and ~20% EBITDA margin in medium term.
items.quote: So we are, as a team, fully committed to enhancing the revenue by 15% to 20% year-on-year, and achieving EBITDA of closer to 20-odd percent in the medium term, and we continue to work on that journey.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected around INR110 crores, including announced projects and maintenance.
items.quote: Yes. INR110 crores -- I mean, broadly, yes. Yes, broadly. It can go -- maybe it can go up depending on more projects through the year. But at the moment, yes, that's correct.

items.statement: Two approved expansion projects total about INR90+ crores; maintenance capex INR20-25 crores annually.
items.quote: Yes. So capex, these 2 capex, which I already said earlier, is about INR90 plus crores. There's maintenance capex of roughly INR20 crores, INR25 crores a year, which should continue.

items.statement: INR75 crores solar plant with battery storage to be commissioned in Q1 FY27, covering 61% of power needs.
items.quote: The company is further investing INR75 crores towards setting up a 20-megawatt ground-mounted solar plant with a battery energy storage system, which will further reduce the overall power cost, and the same is expected to be commissioned in this quarter, Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Solar plant expected to deliver about INR28 crores EBITDA-level cost savings in FY27.
items.quote: Yes. So that will be -- that is estimated to be about INR28 crores at EBITDA level, for FY27.

items.statement: Price hikes of 8-10% taken in glassware and opalware to cover cost inflation; full benefit may take 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: It's more because to get customers to accept substantially higher pricing, let's say, 8% to 10%, which is what prices we have taken, that takes a bit of time.

items.statement: Direct gas cost increased from INR20 crores to INR50 crores per annum due to West Asia crisis.
items.quote: Increased to INR50 crores.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing of vacuum bottles expected to improve gross margin by at least 10%, but not in first couple of quarters.
items.quote: But my sense is on the gross margin side, 10% at least we should get an increase. Otherwise, there's no benefit of manufacturing in India, so -- but I don't think that will be realized in like the first couple of quarters.

items.statement: Opalware demand growth muted; expects muted growth for next year or so.
items.quote: And we are working on that, but at the moment, I think we are -- for the next year or so, I think we are going to expect to see muted growth.

items.statement: Chinese dumping in borosilicate glass continues to pressure margins despite rupee depreciation.
items.quote: So that will, over a period of time, definitely cause some pressure on the margins. We can only keep working on innovation and petitioning the government to kind of create a level playing field, which we're trying to do.

items.statement: Anti-dumping investigation on borosilicate glass may take 6-9 months for outcome.
items.quote: At present data is under the investigation, but we hope that it at least it will take 6 to 9 months from now

items.statement: Debt may increase in short term but no major fundraising planned; operating cash flow sufficient for capex.
items.quote: Not much debt, right? I mean, it may go up in the short term, but we also have reason -- I mentioned our operating cash flow was about INR120 crores.

items.statement: Hydra inventory largely depleted; appliance inventory built up due to QCO, expected to correct.
items.quote: The Hydra inventory, whatever we built up last year is more or less all depleted. But on the flip side, we had to build up a lot of appliance inventory this year because of this QCO, which has come on a large range of appliances.

items.statement: Expects some challenges in next quarter or two before stabilizing.
items.quote: I do expect the next quarter or 2, we are still settling or still reaching lever, there are to be some challenges in the short run.

items.statement: Expects revenue growth of 15-20% for FY27, maintaining earlier guidance.
items.quote: Sir, we are expecting a revenue increase of about 15% to 20%, as we have given the earlier guidance also. So that expectation we are having even for this year.

items.statement: Reiterates target to achieve INR 3,000 crores revenue by March 2031.
items.quote: No, no. We are very much intact, and we have a plan to achieve this INR 3,000 crores by March 2031. So that plan is already in place, and we are working very rigorously on that plan.

items.statement: Projects EBITDA margin of 18-20% for FY27.
items.quote: Our margin ranges we have projected 18% to 20% EBITDA margin. So margin will be in that range only.

items.statement: Plans capex of INR 45 crores for India Pesticides and INR 90 crores for subsidiary in FY27, funded via internal accruals.
items.quote: Our capex plan for India Pesticides is INR 45 crores and for our 100% subsidiary, it is INR 90 crores. And mainly, it will be funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Expects Shalvis facility revenue of INR 70-80 crores in FY27, including new block.
items.quote: No, just now we answered, the revenue from the Shalvis facility will be around INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores in this financial year, FY27, including the new block, what we are going to construct.

items.statement: Successfully passed on some raw material cost increases to customers, aiming to maintain prices.
items.quote: But we also have discussed with our customers, and we have tried to pass on the cost differential to our customer, and we have been successful in convincing them for some of the products. And we feel that we should be able to maintain these prices in the coming months.

items.statement: Japanese partner forecast for this year and next is 30% higher than last year; discussing new molecule.
items.quote: That is going on well, sir. Actually, we are having regular discussions with our Japanese friends, and they have given the forecast for this year and for the next year, which is almost 30% more than last year.

items.statement: Expects full capacity utilization of PEDA and Pretilachlor in FY27 after capacity expansion.
items.quote: Sir, FY27, I think we will be utilizing the full capacity of the products because we increased the capacity last quarter, which was commissioned only in March. So we hope that this year, we should be able to utilize fully.

items.statement: Monsoon forecast 6-8% below normal may not significantly impact production, but El Niño uncertainty remains.
items.quote: Yes. See, we know that IMD has given a forecast of reduced rainfall this season from 6% to 8%. But the previous history, what we have gone through, there was news item in the papers that in the past also, there has been occasions where the rainfall was less, but the overall production did not get suffered.

items.statement: Net working capital days expected to improve by 10-12 days by FY27.
items.quote: And our net working capital days has now improved to 223. There is a slight scope for further improvement, maybe by 10 to 12 days less by FY27.

items.statement: Shalvis expected to contribute INR 1,000 crores revenue by March 2031; rest from existing plants.
items.quote: Yes. By March 2031, we expect to reach INR 3,000 crores. And thereby, we have got plans already in place. In Shalvis, we expect the total revenue by March 2031 to be about INR 1,000 crores. And rest, we will be generating from our existing plants at Dewa Road, Sandila and our formulation facilities.

items.statement: Supply chain critical; long-term supplier arrangements and customer discussions mitigate price increases.
items.quote: Sir, you are absolutely right. The situation in terms of supply chain is very critical. We have done some long-term arrangements with some of our suppliers who are able to bring the material to us in time.

items.statement: Dividend policy provides 5-15% of net profit; retaining funds for capex and working capital.
items.quote: I mean we have a dividend p olicy, which is providing 5% to 15% of net profit. As you know, we have a lot of capex plan for our subsidiary, and our turnover is growing, so we have to fund a lot of increased working capital through our internal accruals.

items.statement: Plant 6 mechanical completion achieved; commercialization on track by H1 FY27.
items.quote: Meanwhile, Plant 6 has achieved mechanical completion, and we remain on track for commercialization by H1 of FY '27.

items.statement: No organic capex in FY27 beyond maintenance; additional capacity possibly in FY28 if growth strong.
items.quote: So FY '27, we'll keep judging, but we don't expect FY '27, any organic capex other than the maintenance capex. And if we are able to deliver very good numbers, maybe FY '28, we go for additional capacity, which everyone would love.

items.statement: Plant 6 enables ~INR1,000 crore revenue excluding injectables; further 10-15% capacity efficiency expected.
items.quote: So about -- excluding injectables, which is about 100 cr, we can deliver about 1,000 cr revenue with Plant 6.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA improved excluding ESOP; overall EBITDA level expected to grow long term.
items.quote: Yes. So the operational EBITDA, as you must have seen, if we exclude the ESOP expenses has actually improved a lot. And in the long run, we maintained that we expect the overall EBITDA level to grow.

items.statement: Trade generics and institutional long-term growth positive; near-term affected by codeine discontinuation and lumpy institutional orders.
items.quote: So we remain positive, very, very positive about the long-term growth potential of trade generics and institutional verticals also going forward, which is supported by favourable macroeconomic factors, increasing demand for affordable health care, our own AAA strategy.

items.statement: Exports positive traction; no guidance but confident in high-margin vertical.
items.quote: Yes. In terms of run rate, we do not -- as you are aware, do not give guidance. But we have seen positive traction in exports.

items.statement: Dosage form expansion planned across ointments, steroids, beta-lactams, soft-gel hormones, eye drops; no immediate plans.
items.quote: So there are several dosage forms where we currently are not present, right? We don't have anything in ointment. We don't have anything in steroids, beta-lactam antibiotics. We don't have anything in soft-gel hormones. And even on the protein powders and nutra side, our capacities are very, very small. So there is a lo

items.statement: GLP-1 opportunity: injectable facility can fill vials; watching space; no trade generic plans yet.
items.quote: GLP-1, we -- so with respect to the vial format for GLP-1, our facility can fill those vials already, okay? So that is one important thing. And our question is that as the volume picks up and the people who have done the launches so far have done it from their in-house facilities. And as the volumes pick up, they have

items.statement: EU GMP approval timeline not commented; readiness on track.
items.quote: No, this is something that we don't want to comment.

items.statement: Inorganic strategy: avoid troubled assets; willing to pay premium for good established businesses.
items.quote: On the inorganic side, while we keep looking at ideas and units and businesses, one of the things that has been very important discipline for us has been that we don't want to walk into somebody else's problem. Even if it is coming for a very cheap price because a lot of effort goes into fixing something that is really

items.statement: ADS revenue guidance for FY27 retained at INR 550-600 crores.
items.quote: we have given a guidance for next year, which we retained roughly INR 550 crores to INR600 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected similar to FY26 capex of INR 5,097 million.
items.quote: during FY '26, we incurred a capex of INR5,097 million, and we expect a similar level of investment in FY '27 as well.

items.statement: Additional INR 250 crores capex in ADS to clear current order backlog.
items.quote: we would be incurring another INR 250 crores of capex, more or less to clear the current order backlog of INR4,500 crores.

items.statement: ADS cumulative unexecuted lifetime order backlog for 5 years stands at INR 44.6 billion.
items.quote: If we look at the cumulative unexecuted lifetime order backlog for 5 years, especially for the ADS business, it stands at INR 44.6 billion.

items.statement: Peak annual revenues for new business at INR 19.2 billion as of March 2026.
items.quote: As of March 2026, our peak annual revenues for new business stood at INR 19.2 billion post our annual reset exercise.

items.statement: ADS margin expected to move towards 25-30% with full facility utilization.
items.quote: the margin profile should move towards the number that you indicated.

items.statement: Auto business FY27 H1 expected stronger than H2 due to favorable base effect.
items.quote: Within the Auto business, FY '27 H1 is expected to be relatively stronger than the H2, aided by favorable base effect.

items.statement: Exports expected to gain momentum this year, but order inflows may take 1-2 quarters to convert.
items.quote: we expect that business-wise, there will be good momentum in the exports this year, but order inflows could take 1 or 2 more quarters to see the conversion that is happening.

items.statement: Non-auto and xEV mix may exceed 20% target, with non-auto potentially higher.
items.quote: we may have some change in this mix of non-automotive could go up higher than 20%.

items.statement: Labor availability and attrition are key challenges for execution efficiency this year.
items.quote: the availability and the attrition of the labor workforce is going to be one of the key challenges in this year for our execution efficiency.

items.statement: Inflationary pressures across steel, aluminum, energy, tooling, consumables, and freight; proceeding with caution for FY27.
items.quote: the operating environment remains fluid with inflationary pressures across steel, aluminum, energy, tooling, consumables and freight, et cetera. We are proceeding towards FY '27 with caution.

items.statement: Order book visibility supports INR 8,000-8,200 crores revenue, targeting INR 10,000 crores.
items.quote: we already have a visibility of closer to, as you said, about INR 8,000 crores, INR 8,200 crores on the order book front for the execution. We still have a couple of years where we can fulfill the order book and take the company towards INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: Energy storage program expected to generate INR 80-100 crores annual revenue.
items.quote: Currently, for this program, it is anywhere between INR 80 crores to INR 100 crores is the annual revenue that we expect out of this program that has come to us.

items.statement: Nichidai JV capex contribution of INR 50 crores this year; facility to be ready by Q3 FY27.
items.quote: This year, we have kept about 50 cr as our contribution, the thing towards the JV. That would -- we have already procured one forging press, which has come into India currently on part of that -- as a part of that capex. So we expect that this year, Sansera, from our side, we may have to invest about INR50 crores.

items.statement: FY27 volume guidance of 350,000-360,000 tonnes, implying 20-25% growth.
items.quote: For this year, we are having around roughly you can take 3,50,000 to 3,60,000.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 12.5-12.6% is sustainable and will continue.
items.quote: EBITDA margins are sustainable, basically, whatever is being shown in the numbers are there. So, these are the sustainable things and this will continue as we are focusing only on our profits.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA per tonne expected to be at least current level, with continuous efforts to grow.
items.quote: So, if at all everything goes well without the geopolitical issues and the scenario on the pricing hit and other things. So, we feel that this will be the minimum one and this should continue.

items.statement: Solar project to be completed by FY27, with 10 MW production starting next month.
items.quote: For us '27 is the last deadline to complete our entire 13 locations, 60 megawatt AC projects. So, out of 13 locations, we have almost of start of the project, 8 locations, 2 are yet to be coming for commencement and remaining will be completed within this financial year.

items.statement: Backward integration benefits quality and security of raw material, not major margin impact.
items.quote: So, the margins would not be a very big thing, but only the quantity and the quality and the consistency of the supply for the raw material will get improved.

items.statement: B2B contribution increased from 15% to 20%, targeting further increase.
items.quote: Earlier it was 15% now it has become increased up to 20%.

items.statement: Current quarter demand is good, but no specific growth guidance provided.
items.quote: Current quarter is good, sir. So far it is absolutely good.

items.statement: Solar power per unit price fixed at INR3.21, with fixed revenue stream.
items.quote: So, per unit we are getting around INR3.21paise, apart from capital subsidy. So, as and when it will be generated that is the fixed tenurity and fixed revenue will be coming.

items.statement: Metal Mart subsidiary awaiting GST registration in Maharashtra and South India to start operations.
items.quote: We have registered our supply for GS T registration in Maharashtra in 2 to 3 places. We are waiting for the GST registration from Maharashtra and similarly we are doing in southern part like Tamil Nadu and Telangana also, the GST registration process and we are also tie up with the suppliers as well as the customers.

items.statement: No impact from gas supply disruptions, own suppliers and storage intact.
items.quote: Touchwood we have not been impacted by the gas which means we were having our own the suppliers and other things are intact basically. So, we have not faced any shortage or any disturbance in the supplies.

items.statement: Expects VNB margins to further improve, but no specific target; focus on VNB growth.
items.quote: So our ultimate strategy, as you mentioned rightly, yes, we expect margins to further improve, but that all depends upon various factors, and that will have to be seen over a period of time.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio expected to be sustained in future.
items.quote: We expect it to be sustained in the future also, that also has been kept in mind before the board decided the amount of dividend to be declared.

items.statement: VNB margin improved 360 bps YoY to 21.2% in FY26.
items.quote: Further, net VNB margin has improved by 360 basis points on a year-on-year basis to 21.2% for the year ended 31 March, 2026 from 17.6% for the previous year.

items.statement: Operating assumption changes (persistency, expense, GST) negatively impacted VNB margin by 2.8%.
items.quote: So the combined effect of the persistency and expense in some line of business adjustments based on the experience along with the GST impact, which has been taken as part of the policy expenses, the contribution is negative 2.8%.

items.statement: Business mix shift to non-par contributed 3% to VNB margin.
items.quote: So this business mix which has gone up has contributed to 3% to the VNB margin.

items.statement: RFR changes contributed 3.4% to VNB margin.
items.quote: So this RFR has contributed to 3.4%.

items.statement: Non-par share of individual APE settled at ~35% for last three quarters.
items.quote: Our non-par share of individual APE business has now consistently settled at about 35% sequentially over the last three results performance updates.

items.statement: Aims to increase guaranteed business (non-par savings, protection, annuity) while maintaining margins.
items.quote: We would naturally like to increase our contribution from guaranteed business, both in terms of non-par savings as well as protection as well as tap the market in full in terms of annuity business that is possible.

items.statement: Cautious on dividend due to expected risk-based capital (RBC) regime; building reserves.
items.quote: We are not sure when it is going to be introduced, so we need to build some reserves so that we remain at a comfortable level of solvency throughout.

items.statement: High equity exposure may impact RBC; monitoring regulatory developments.
items.quote: But the point here is sensitivity to the volatility in equities is a significant factor for -- which will impact the risk-based capital.

items.statement: No immediate plan to increase non-par IRR; will balance investment opportunities and competition.
items.quote: So we'll continue to watch and see whether there is a possibility of -- also added to it the hedging possibilities, particularly in the non-participating portfolio, how much of the risk can be hedged, because as of now, these hedging instruments are not available for very long duration.

items.statement: April 2026 saw good growth in both par and non-par, number of sales and premium.
items.quote: We are seeing a good growth in terms of both the number of sales as well as the premium that is being accumulated. Particularly, the April figures have been a testimony to that.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR10 per share (pre-bonus INR20) for FY26.
items.quote: I would like to share that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR10 per equity share of INR10 each equivalent to INR20 per equity share, pre-bonus issue basis, for the financial year 2025-26 subject to approval of shareholders in the 5th Annual General Meeting of the Corporation.

items.statement: FY27 volume target 231,000 MT, capacity utilization 73%, revenue growth 13% YoY, EBITDA margin ~11%.
items.quote: Looking ahead to financial year 2027, we are confident of sustaining our growth trajectory, targeting a volume of 231,000 metric tons per annum with a capacity utilization of 73% and a year-on-year revenue growth of 13% alongside top line expansion.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin anticipated at approximately 11%.
items.quote: We remain equally focused on margin quality with EBITDA margins anticipated at approximately 11%, reflecting our continued emphasis on operational efficiency and value-accretive business.

items.statement: FY27 capex plan of INR175 crores, including BESS, primarily for XLPE expansion.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we plan to invest further INR175-odd crores in financial year 2027, primarily towards expanding our XLPE compound capacity with investments earmarked for our diversification into BESS as well.

items.statement: FY27 capex split: INR70+ crores for BESS, remaining ~INR100 crores for capacity expansion.
items.quote: Total outlay for this financial year is INR175 crores, including BESS. And out of the INR200 crores of BESS, there is a phased manner of implementation, which will be happening. So, this year, we are allocating close to INR70-plus-odd crores for BESS.

items.statement: BESS: 5 GW capacity planned, each GW generating INR800-900 crores revenue; FY27 BESS revenue ~INR200-250 crores, breakeven expected.
items.quote: We aim to develop 5 gigawatt of installed capacity in a phased manner with each gigawatt projected to generate approximately INR800 crores to INR900 crores in revenue.

items.statement: BESS FY28 target: 1 GWh sales, INR800-900 crores revenue, 10%+ EBITDA margin, INR80-90 crores EBITDA.
items.value: 1 GWh, INR800-900 crores, 10%+ margin, INR80-90 crores EBITDA
items.quote: We are targeting 1 gigawatt hour of sales and close to INR800 crores to INR900 crores of revenue, expecting EBITDA margins of 10-plus. So, INR80 crores to INR90 crores of EBITDA, which we are anticipating is something which we have also factored in our estimates.

items.statement: Fixed EBITDA margin per kg maintained despite price volatility; pass-through lag 7-15 days, instant for sharp hikes.
items.quote: Yes. See, we are able to pass-through the price increases, which means we are able to maintain our fixed margins per kg basis.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased over 50%, now stabilized; supply normalized from mid-April.
items.quote: As far as the price is concerned, there has been substantial volatility and the prices have gone up beyond 50% inflation. And now the prices are comparatively stabilized.

items.statement: Export demand strong in MENA and Europe; Q1 FY27 growth continuity expected, but Q2/Q3 uncertain due to geopolitics.
items.quote: First quarter visibility is already there. So, we say that first quarter will see the continuity of the growth, which we have seen in the last quarter.

items.statement: XLPE capacity addition of 48,000 MT operational from April 2026; total capacity to exceed 315,000 MT.
items.quote: This capacity addition will take our overall capacity to a level beyond 315,000 tons per annum.

items.statement: Backward integration by customers is a theoretical risk, mitigated by scale, skill, and product range.
items.quote: Yes. See, it is a risk which is attached to our business, and it will always remain. That customer can go for backward integration.

items.statement: BESS working capital for 1 GWh: INR200-250 crores, funded by existing limits and free cash flow.
items.quote: For the first phase of 1 gigawatt hour, we have plans that the total working capital requirement will be in the range of INR200 crores to INR250-odd crores, and we have sufficient limits available with us for that funding the same as well as the margins for them are also similarly available with us as a free cash flow.

items.statement: FY28 volume growth expected at 15% over FY27 base of 230,000 MT.
items.quote: In 2026, 2027, if we are targeting a polymer compound volume of 230,000 tons, then in 2027, 2028, you can add on another 15% on that 230,000 tons.

items.statement: BESS initial phase: import from China, assembly line; plan to develop own BMS/EMS IP in future.
items.quote: Yes, initially for the initial period, we are going to import it from China. And over a period of time, we will be working on backward integration or just a suggestion of many components, which are easily available in the country.

items.statement: Company plans high-teens revenue CAGR over next 5 years.
items.quote: But overall, we'll grow at a high-teens CAGR from the next 5 years' perspective.

items.statement: Plans 500 bps EBITDA margin expansion over next 5 years.
items.quote: And from an EBITDA profile perspective, over the next 5 years, we want to get 500 basis points better.

items.statement: Mamaearth brand expected to grow at double-digit CAGR over next 5 years.
items.quote: So, we're fairly confident of delivering a double-digit CAGR on the brand from the next 5 years perspective.

items.statement: Mamaearth distribution to expand from 200,000 to 0.5 million outlets in 3-5 years.
items.quote: We also see distribution gain opportunities given the brand is only 200,000 outlets and potentially can get to 0.5 million outlets over the next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Calibrated price increases already executed in Q1 to offset crude-driven COGS inflation; no further hikes expected.
items.quote: And those have already been sort of executed as we speak in Q1. So we don't impact at least at this point of time with where crude is at this point of time. We don't expect any further price increases.

items.statement: Mamaearth and Derma Co. are double-digit EBITDA positive and expected to improve margins.
items.quote: So, from a margin standpoint, Mamaearth and Derma Co., both are double-digit EBITDA-positive now. And we foresee them to continue improving their margin trajectory in future, as they have done in the past, along with growth.

items.statement: Focus categories grew 35% YoY, contribution up 500 bps in one year.

items.quote: Our order book plus confirmed and expected, i t may be around just over INR300 crores. It is executable. Out of it, the technology services alone, it will be INR175 crore s.

items.statement: US nearshore team of 30 consultants costs INR8.5 crores per quarter, annualized INR34 crores.
items.quote: So we wanted to set up a team anyway, came across an opportunity in January where we could hire a team of about 30 people, and we went about doing that and incurred the expense for the first three months of about INR8.5 crores.

items.statement: US nearshore team already generating 30% gross margin, expected to scale to 54%.
items.quote: At this point in time, we already have a 30% margin from this team. So like what we explained, it will grow beyond the 30% and will be in the range, the same range of about 54% gross margin when we are able to scale other businesses beyond what we have alr eady been doing with this team.

items.statement: April revenue INR23 crores vs INR15 crores last year, aided by new US team business.
items.quote: Typically we did last year about INR15 crores in April and we were able to do INR23 crores in April, one of the reasons where we had new business coming in because of this.

items.statement: AQA engagement concluded, announcement in one or two days; very large business.
items.quote: We have concluded everything from that aspect. In the matter of one or two days, we will be announcing about our larger engagement with AQA.

items.statement: Acquisition strategy paused for new CEO review, due diligence rehashing, progress soon.
items.quote: So rightfully so, we said we will pause whatever we have done till then until such time that Doreswamy takes a look at what we have done and then progress it further.

items.statement: Intangible assets investment INR12.2 crores last year; book value INR100 crores, amortization INR18 crores.
items.quote: Sir, this is intangible assets for INR12.2 crores in the last financial year.

items.statement: Assessment and proctoring 27% of FY26 revenue; EdTech services 56%.
items.quote: FY26 educational technology services contributed 56%, while assessment and proctoring solutions contributed 27%. Learning and student success solutions 12%, and learning design and content solutions is 5%.

items.statement: Demand for domain-based AI tech services rising in USA and Europe.
items.quote: Demand for domain -based AI tech services are on the rise, particularly in the markets where we mainly operate, that is USA and Eu rope.

items.statement: Client concentration high: top 5 clients 68%, top 10 78% of FY26 revenue.
items.quote: In terms of client concentration, our top five clients contributed approximately 68% of full-year revenue, while the top 10 contributed approximately 78%.

items.statement: Added 14 new clients in FY26; hired 3 US salespeople, 1 Middle East, 1 UK.
items.quote: We added 14 new clients during the year and continue to strengthen our sales pipeline across education, certification, publishing, and public sector markets.

items.statement: AI capabilities: 38 concepts, 16 prototypes, 9 pilots, 4 commercial products; 60% database optimization.
items.quote: To date, we have developed 38 AI-driven concepts, 16 working prototypes, nine active customer pilots, and four commercially deployed AI products.

items.statement: Pharma food and nutrition expected to grow faster than FY26's 10%; specialty to maintain similar growth.
items.quote: Both verticals, we expect actually pharma food nutrition to grow faster than it has grown in FY26 of 10%. And specialty ingredients will continue to track similar growth to what we have done over the last two, three years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to return to FY24/FY25 levels of 37-38% in FY27.
items.quote: So once that happens, I think in the next couple of quarters, you will see the margin kind of tracking back to what we were delivering maybe in FY24 and FY25.

items.statement: Total capex for 100,000 tons battery material capacity approximately INR600 crores.
items.quote: I had mentioned previously as well that to achieve our target of 100,000 tons, we are looking at a capex of approximately INR600 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex: ~INR10 crores greenfield completion, INR15 crores maintenance, plus SAM capex.
items.quote: In FY27, we'll see major greenfield expansion is over. So maybe there would be around INR10-odd crores for completing the greenfield project and a maintenance capex of INR15-odd crores.

items.statement: Received 700 metric tons battery material orders in last month; 42 customers engaged, 6 completed validation.
items.quote: Encouragingly, we have also started receiving initial commercial purchase orders, including approximately 700 metric tons over the last month alone, supporting customer efforts to diversify sourcing away from China.

items.statement: Bisglycinate has four times realization of current portfolio; higher margin contribution expected from FY28.
items.quote: So, realization, as I mentioned, it would not be fair to compare because the -- like the bisglycinate product they were talking about has four times the realization of our current portfolio, right?

items.statement: Phosphoric acid price increase passed to customers; benefits to reflect in Q1 and more in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: You will see the partial benefit reflecting Q1 and more importantly in Q2 going forward.

items.statement: Battery materials Phase 1 capacity 25,000 tons on track for commissioning by April 2027.
items.quote: During FY26, we successfully conducted the groundbreaking ceremony for our battery materials project at Dahej, which remains on track for commissioning of Phase 1 capacity of 25,000 metric tons per year by April 2027.

items.statement: Specialty ingredients revenue grew 62% to INR280 crores; contribution increased to 44% in FY26.
items.quote: Revenue for the vertical grew from INR172 crores to INR280 crores during the year.

items.statement: Working capital days increased to 213; targeting 150-160 days within FY27.
items.quote: We are internally focused on managing our net working capital cycle and targeting to come around 150 to 160 days within this financial year.

items.statement: Battery materials sales expected around 2,500 metric tons in FY27.
items.quote: So, next year it is fair to assume that we will be selling say 2,500 metric ton here or there in terms of the battery chemical, in terms of volume, right?

items.statement: Excluding battery, business can scale to INR1000-1200 crores without incremental capex.
items.quote: So excluding battery, once this greenfield now that is commissioned, the business can scale to approximately INR1000 crores to INR1200 crores without any incremental capex in the existing product portfolio.

items.statement: Global demand for bisglycinate ingredient approximately $1 billion; North America 40-50%.
items.quote: I mentioned, I think the current global demand for this ingredient is around $1 billion for the ingredient alone. North America would be 40% to 50% of that global demand.

items.statement: Received 51 new customer approvals in FY26, expected to contribute to FY27 growth.
items.quote: Compared to FY25, we received around 51 new customer approvals in FY26, which are expected to meaningfully contribute to the growth of the business in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Aspires to grow at least 20% at company level, but no formal guidance due to inflation and geopolitical headwinds.
items.quote: But like I said, at a company level, given all these variables of multi-channel and multi-category, we aspire to grow at least about 20%. We will do our best to achieve that.

items.statement: Plans capex of INR120-140 crores in FY27, mostly for retail including Jumbo store and 80 new stores.
items.quote: But with the Jumbo store coming in and the new stores we are talking about, we should be somewhere around INR120 crores to INR140 crores of the capex we will be spending in this year.

items.statement: Targets net addition of more than 80 stores in FY27, focusing on Tier 2 cities.
items.quote: But the target for this full year is to deliver more than 80 stores net addition.

items.statement: Expects no material change in margin structure in Q1 FY27, but full year may see pressure if raw material prices persist.
items.quote: On a near-term basis, we do not expect any material change or dilution in the margin structure in Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Implemented two price increases of 7-8% each in March and April 2026 to offset raw material inflation.
items.quote: And to pass this on, we have done two measured calibrated price increases of about 7% to 8% in March and 7% to 8% in April.

items.statement: Raw material prices increased 30-160% between February and May, but procurement managed at 5-30% increase.
items.quote: Between February and May, the prices have seen a lot of volatility. They have gone up between 30% to 160% at some point.

items.statement: April 2026 growth was better than Q4 FY26, but too early to confirm trend; Q1 FY27 results will provide clarity.
items.quote: But in short, April definitely has been way better than JFM.

items.statement: Expanding into adjacent categories like live plants and fertilizers to complete home solutions portfolio, with no meaningful financial impact in medium term.
items.quote: While we continue to prioritise our three core categories, these amendments are not anticipated to entail any meaningful financial impact in the medium term.

items.statement: Advertising and marketing spend expected to be 7-8% of sales over medium term, up from 5.7% in FY26.
items.quote: As mentioned in our last call as well, we reiterate that over the medium term, we anticipate a ramp-up in our brand building efforts from the A&P spend expected to be around 7% to 8% of the sales with continuous monitoring on the success metrics.

items.statement: ESOP expenses expected to be around INR12 crores in FY27, up from INR33 million in FY26.
items.quote: However, for the next year, we anticipate these expenses to be estimated at around INR12 crores.

items.statement: Jumbo store expected to break even in 18-24 months, first store to open in early FY28.
items.quote: So in about 18 months or so, we should aspire to breakeven. And think of it as a standard asset-heavy retail company, which would break even in 18, 24, 36 months. So we are trying to beat that benchmark by doing it in 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: 100-day return policy return rate remains stable below double digits, with no cost to customer.
items.quote: To answer your question on the returns percentage, I can tell you that it has always remained in the same stable percentage range, most of the 10, 11 years that we had this policy, and that number is stable at -- it's below double digits.

items.statement: Launching large capacity frost free refrigerators in Q2 FY27, filling a significant portfolio gap.
items.quote: Many of you have asked us when are we launching into the frost free large capacity space? Well, the answer is in Q2 of 2026-2027, thereby filling a significant gap in our frost free portfolio.

items.statement: Energy upcharge is a permanent BOM cost increase; next energy upgrade expected in three years.
items.quote: The energy upcharge is here to stay. I think the next energy upcharge is supposed to be three years from now. So, every time there is an energy upcharge, there will be a cost upcharge.

items.statement: Energy cost upcharges not yet compensated by pricing as of March 31.
items.quote: One is the energy cost upcharges because of the refrigerator and air conditioning, which has not yet been compensated by pricing as of March 31.

items.statement: Full year PBT margin would have held flat excluding incremental e-waste provision.
items.quote: If you just take out the incremental e-waste provision we have made versus last year, we would have held our margin.

items.statement: Gross margin fell to 29.9% in FY26 from 30.6% prior year due to AC mix.
items.quote: This year, we've arrived at a 29.9% margin, driven by basically the air conditioner mix in our margin.

items.statement: Core refrigerator and washer business margins improved versus last year on P4G cost program.
items.quote: And because of this P4G program, our core T2 business margins, which is ref and washers business, improved versus last year.

items.statement: Industry grew low single-digits in Q4; refrigerator industry declined for full year.
items.quote: But the industry continued to basically grow with very low single-digits in Jan 2026 to March 2026, so subdued industry growth. Decline in refrigerators so far for the whole year, driven by decline in direct cool refrigerators.

items.statement: Expects to recover market share in April-June as phase-in phase-out completes.
items.quote: But as we recover our phase-in phase-out, as we move faster than others on the phase-in phase-out in the month of April, May, June, I hope to be able to recover that market share back again as we ramp up our display shares and our stock.

items.statement: Middle East war causing supply and cost concerns for components and products across industry.
items.quote: As everybody knows, the supply situation arising from the Middle East war is of concern to not only us but all industries across the country. Both with respect to cost and supply of components, products, etcetera, it is quite challenging and we continue to work on that very, very seriously and diligently.

items.statement: 20-35% of components imported, exposed to forex; monitoring oil and currency daily.
items.quote: So, typically between, depending on the company, between 20% and 35% of products components may be imported, right, depending on the company. And so that part of it is subject to forex.

items.statement: Will balance pricing between volume/market share and profitability; may act if outpriced.
items.quote: So, if it comes to a place where we're outpriced and we start having an impact on volumes in a material way, then we will have to do what we need to do to protect our business.

items.statement: Air conditioner business grew over 40% in FY26 after ~80% growth prior year.
items.quote: Our air conditioner business, even in a relatively tough year, has gone up by more than 40% versus last year, following quite a strong 80%-odd growth in the previous year.

items.statement: Front load washer business grew about 60% versus last year with triple-digit market share gains.
items.quote: The front load washers accelerated for us in 2025-2026. Our total business has grown about 60% more than last year.

items.statement: E-waste provision made at highest possible rate; potential rationalization would benefit company.
items.quote: On e-waste, we are providing at the highest possible rate that we can provide for.

items.statement: FY27 will be financially difficult for the industry and Whirlpool due to energy changes and war impacts.
items.quote: I have already said to you that 2026-2027 will be difficult financially for the entire industry and also for Whirlpool because of all the energy changes, because of all the war impacts that are happening, which are very, very significant and kind of continuing to be not so clear as we go along.

items.statement: Long-term revenue growth ambition is early double-digits, up from high single-digit.
items.quote: I had said even two years ago, our intent over the long run would be to grow the business high single-digit, you know, year-on-year compound growth rate. I think maybe we can up that a little bit and go into early double-digits as we think about the future.

items.statement: Long-term margin for refrigerator, washing machine, AC space likely high single-digit.
items.quote: And therefore, over a long span of time, I think to get to a high single-digit margin is probably what is likely in the refrigerator washing machine air conditioner space, right?

items.statement: Elica to remain in double-digit margin range, but may invest some margin in growth over 5-7 years.
items.quote: I would always hope to keep it in the double-digit margin range, but over the next maybe five to seven years, I would love to take a little bit of that margin and put it into driving revenue growth because I think there is a significant opportunity to drive that category whose penetration is probably less than 5% today

items.statement: Premium refrigerator capex in CWIP, to be capitalized next quarter.
items.quote: The CWIP right now pertains to the premium refrigerators we spoke about. Since we've not started -- since it's going to come in the next quarter, so the capex is still lying in CWIP and has not got capitalized.

items.statement: AC manufacturing capex decision depends on volume and 3PL economics; continuously evaluating.
items.quote: In terms of the air conditioning investment into capex, this will be a commercial and strategic decision. The reason I'm saying that is because there is quite a bit of capacity in the country available with 3PL players who can supply air conditioners to you with your design, to your specification, to your technical req

items.statement: No buyback considered; cash to be used for organic or inorganic growth opportunities.
items.quote: So, buyback is something that we've not looked at, at this point in time because we think there is lot of opportunity that we can actually take.

items.statement: Cash sufficient to acquire a company of similar size; evaluating inorganic opportunities.
items.quote: And probably just from a sheer cash point of view, it is just sufficient enough to look at a company of a similar size.

items.statement: Focus on growing AC responsibly, targeting offtake not inventory loading.
items.quote: We would like to grow this business very responsibly. We would like to grow this business very strongly, but focused on offtake, focused on making sure our products are selling out and we are putting in as much products as are selling out.

items.statement: Entry-level refrigerator demand weak post-COVID, but expected to recover in 3-18 months due to government measures and pent-up replacement.
items.quote: Now, is it three months, six months, 12 months, 18 months from now, I do not know, but it's certainly not three years away where penetration should start growing again.

items.statement: Energy rating increases will raise costs and potentially prices, risking demand pull-down.
items.quote: So, energy rating cannot increase without a commensurate increase in cost. And if there is a commensurate increase in cost, then over time there has to be a commensurate increase in pricing.

items.statement: Vision to become number one in refrigerators and washing machines, may take more than five years.
items.quote: It will not be five years, it will probably be more than five years to get to the leadership position in refrigerators and washers, we know that, but one day we hope to get there.

items.statement: Aggressive investment planned over next 12-24 months to drive growth.
items.quote: But we do believe that we are at that type of -- at that time of our existence where aggressive investment across the next 12 to 24 months can really take us into a different level of growth on both revenue and profitability.

items.statement: Board proposes final dividend of Rs. 15 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the Board proposes a final dividend of Rs. 15 per share for FY26 subject to approval by the shareholders in the forthcoming AGM.

items.statement: New tax regime may enable significantly higher dividends in the near future.
items.quote: As you can see, we have moved to the new tax regime which has enabled us to distribute, which will hopefully enable us to distribute significantly higher dividends in the near future potentially.

items.statement: No concrete plans to repay debt from existing cash balances; will follow HSBC agreement terms.
items.quote: As of now, there is nothing concrete or no concrete plans to pay back any debt from the existing cash balances.

items.statement: HSBC loan: 5% repayment in May 2027, then 5% annually for five years, with bullet payment at end.
items.quote: As per the terms of the agreement, 5% in May 2027.

items.statement: No significant lease renewals expected in 2026-27.
items.quote: After that, there is nothing significant because there are not many renewals coming up in 2026-27.

items.statement: No significant early tenant exits currently anticipated.
items.quote: No, not right now. Not anything significant that we have been told.

items.statement: No data center plans or FSI increase to comment on now.
items.quote: Nothing that I can make a comment on now, no. I can't comment on that. Nothing significant or concrete.

items.statement: Moved to new tax regime for efficiency; no significant new structures being pursued.
items.quote: We just felt that the best thing to do would be to move to the new tax regime at this point and optimize whatever, to the best possible extent, whatever efficiencies we had at this point in time.

items.statement: Buyback not considered at this point in time.
items.quote: Not at this point in time, for various reasons.

items.statement: Property valuation increased from approximately Rs. 6,500 crores to Rs. 6,650 crores year-over-year.
items.quote: Yes, okay, so I think last year March 25 was 6,500, and this year it's 6,650, approximately.

items.statement: Growth driven by contracted license fee escalations and new licenses at higher prices; marginal reduction in finance costs.
items.quote: This is the real reason for the growth in the license fees, which basically translates into higher margins. There was a marginal reduction in finance costs in 2026 as compared to March 25 as well.

items.statement: No significant capex outside the park; will continue maintenance and incremental capex to maintain A-grade asset.
items.quote: Nothing significant to say, the capex is of course to ensure that the park is in the best possible condition, the maintenance is to the best possible extent, whatever additional and incremental capex and capex-related modifications we have to do to maintain an A-grade asset, we are happy to do and we are going to keep

items.statement: Fixed deposits of Rs. 287 crores mature between 6 months to 1 year.
items.quote: It is between 6 months to 1 year. All FDs will mature between 6 months to 1 year.

items.statement: Management commits to 20% PAT growth for FY27.
items.quote: So, let me say, a PAT growth of 20% is what we are committed to it, we will ensure we achieve that.

items.statement: Expects PAT margin to continue increasing quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year.
items.quote: And over quarter-on-quarter, year-on-year, the PAT margin percentage also will increase as it has over the past 4 years.

items.statement: Targets PEB India capacity utilization around 80% in FY27.
items.quote: I think around 80% is certainly achievable for this financial year, and that will be goal.

items.statement: Aims to reduce working capital days to 75 in next few quarters.
items.quote: we are focused on reducing working capital days to 75 in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Targets debt-equity ratio of 0.8 by end of FY27.
items.quote: Our stated goal is to get to 0.8 debt -equity. I think we can say that by the end of the year we'll get there

items.statement: Guides consolidated tax rate of 25% to 26%.
items.quote: We continue to guide you to a consolidated tax rate of approximately 25.5%, which is 25% to 26% -- in the range of 25% to 26% overall.

items.statement: Finance cost to remain below 4% of revenue.
items.quote: we continue to guide you based on the revenue, we will be at below 4%.

items.statement: FY27 capex plan of close to INR100 crores, mainly for BIW Hyundai plant completion and automation.
items.quote: Close to INR100 crores and our cash generation would be much higher than that.

items.statement: PEB India order backlog at INR810 crores, expected to grow quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: The order book stands healthy for PEB India at INR810 crores, PEB U.S. at $63 millions and Boiler at INR128 crores.

items.statement: PEB U.S. order backlog at $63 million including Ascent Structural.
items.quote: The current order backlog stands at about 63 million when you include Ascent Structural.

items.statement: Boilers order backlog increased to INR145 crores.
items.quote: Boilers and process equipment, building on our strong order backlog, we have now increased the order to INR145 crores

items.statement: Gross margins sustainable at 42-43%.
items.quote: But overall, the margins we guide you would remain at the similar 42%, 43% kind of a thing.

items.statement: Passing on increased steel and energy costs to customers.
items.quote: So our costs have gone up a little bit. We have passed on to our customers.

items.statement: Strong demand in U.S. data centers and industrials; India process industries and solar.
items.quote: In the US, it's dominated by data centers and in dustrials. That's what's growing right now.

items.statement: Presales target of around INR 2,200 crores for FY27.
items.quote: building on FY26 performance momentum, we are setting a presales target of around INR 2,200 crores for FY27.

items.statement: Targeting INR 1,800 crores of project additions in FY27.
items.quote: To maintain this growth, we are targeting INR1,800 crores of highly selective project additions.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity guidance to move to 1.00x.
items.quote: As a result, you will see our debt-to-equity guidance move to 1.00x.

items.statement: FY27 launch pipeline of INR 6,324 crores.
items.quote: a coupled with a robust FY27 launch pipeline of INR6,324 crores

items.statement: Overall revenue visibility of INR 10,432 crores from upcoming launches and existing projects.
items.quote: taking our overall revenue visibility to a robust INR10,432 crores

items.statement: Estimated net cash flow from OC received and ongoing portfolio around INR 3,150 crores.
items.quote: The estimated net cash flow pretax cost debt from our OC received and ongoing portfolio is expected to be estimated to be around INR3,150 crores.

items.statement: Manhattan project selling at INR 30,000-35,000 per sq ft; expect 10-15% annual price increase.
items.quote: Currently, in Manhattan, we are selling on an average of INR30,000 to INR35,000 a square feet depending upon the floor and the view and everything. Going forward, we are looking to launch different, different projects or different towers within Manhattan at an incremental rate of at least 10% to 15% plus year-on-year.

items.statement: Customers cautious due to geopolitical scenario; conversion timeline pushed from 30-45 days to 40-60 days.
items.quote: Right now, people have become cautious with the current geopolitical scenario. It has got nothing to do with AI, but it is more with the current geopolitical scenario, people have become cautious and they are trying to analyze and assess and take their decisions accordingly. But we are seeing inheritant demand. Let's s

items.statement: Vann project average carpet size 1,700-1,800 sq ft, mostly 4BHK; luxury segment with steady sales.
items.quote: The average carpet size in Vann is around 1,700 square feet. We have larger 4 bedrooms around 2,000-odd square feet, but we also have some 3 bedrooms. But overall, it's about 1,700 to 1,800 square feet flats.

items.statement: In discussions with funds for SPV-level tie-up for Kanjurmarg conversion; positive approvals.
items.quote: Well, we are already in discussions with some funds and other people where we are trying to do a tie-up for the conversion process and we are having positive approvals for the same. So, we are not too worried on the requirement of funds, which is already almost on the verge of tie-up.

items.statement: Unsold inventory as of March 2026: INR 2,200 crores.
items.quote: So as on March '26, we have about INR2,200 crore s worth of the unsold inventory, both from OC completed projects and as well ongoing projects.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected 30-35%, PAT margin ~25% due to high-margin Imperia 2 recognition.
items.quote: EBITDA margin should be in the range of about 30%, 35%. Profit after tax should be about 25% next year, but that will be because of Imperia 2.

items.statement: Imperia 2 revenue recognition of INR 130-150 crores expected in FY27.
items.quote: But according to our projection, about INR130 crores, INR150 crores, between that number should be the recognition of Imperia 2 next year.

items.statement: Total GDV of unsold inventory and tied-up projects is INR 4,000 crores, to be sold over 5-7 years.
items.quote: All of them put together should have a value of about INR 4,000 crores. Now that will get recognized on completion as and when the projects get completed over the next 5-6-7 years

items.statement: Construction spend in FY27 expected 15-20% higher than FY26, around INR 200 crores.

items.quote: the total saleable area would be about 2 million square feet, between the 3 projects put together. And total GDV would be about INR 2,000 crores.

items.statement: Plotted development margins are 50-60%, but Solano Gardens weighted average margin is 35-40% including villas.
items.quote: I think you should please take it at about 35% to 40%, including villas. 50% to 60% is the plotted component, but the weighted average will be 35%-40%.

items.statement: Demand in Lucknow is strong and organic, not impacted by geopolitical factors or interest rates; supply is the constraint.
items.quote: No great impact in Lucknow. The demand is very organic. It does not depend so much on the linkages. The geopolitical factors are not that great.

items.statement: Construction cost inflation expected to be a bigger impact, with transmission not yet fully passed through.
items.quote: The bigger impact that we think will come will be on the cost of construction side. That transmission is still not there fully. So, I think that will be the bigger impact.

items.statement: INR 14 crores one-time expense in FY26 (GST write-off and prior project costs) unlikely to recur.
items.quote: around INR 14 crores is onetime kind of expense in the other expenses, which is hitting our EBITDA and the PAT for this quarter and the financial year.

items.statement: Latitude 27 handover officially November 2027, but may be earlier, possibly within FY27.
items.quote: Our official position remains November '27, but hopefully, because the way the site is working, we may do it much earlier than that, even so early that it could be within this financial year.

items.statement: New land parcels in Shaheed Path and LDA auctions to be launched towards end of FY27 after approvals.
items.quote: it will be towards the end of this financial year, the launches. It does take that kind of time to get the designs right and get the approvals and then get the RERA registration.

items.statement: Expects 15-20% volume growth in FY27 for ATBS.
items.quote: we have witnessed a recovery and expect approximately 15% to 20% volume growth in FY 2027.

items.statement: Targets ~15% overall volume growth in FY27.

items.statement: Plans INR200-250 crores capex for FY27.

items.statement: VOPL revenue expected INR100-120 crores in FY27 from Q3.
